semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مِّن طِينٍ}: there are two views on it. The more evident of them: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَلَقكم», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Does this statement need the omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) or not? There is a disagreement: a group, such as al-Mahdawī, Makkī and others, held that there is no omission, and that the human being is created from clay; and it is narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «There is no child born except that some of the dust of his grave is sprinkled upon the sperm-drop.» It was also said: the sperm-drop's origin is clay. Most of the exegetes said: there is something omitted there, i.e. He created your origin, or your father, from clay — meaning Adam and his well-known story. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
185 - 9- إلى عِرْقِ الثَّرى رَسَخَتْ عُروقي ... وهذا الموتُ يَسْلُبُني شبابي
(My roots are firmly set down to the root of the moist earth, and this death is robbing me of my youth.)
They said: by "the root of the moist earth" he meant Adam, peace be upon him, because he is his origin.

His saying: {ثُمَّ قضى}: if «قضى» means "He made manifest", then «ثُمَّ» is for temporal sequence, according to its basic meaning, because that comes after our creation, and it is an attribute of action. If it means "He wrote and decreed", then it is for sequence in mention, because it is an attribute of essence, and that precedes our creation.

His saying: {وَأَجَلٌ مُّسمًّى عِندَهُ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Two things permitted beginning with it (an indefinite) here. One of them: its being qualified (by an adjective); the second: its being conjoined; and mere conjunction is among the things that permit it. [The poet] said:
186 - 0- عندي اصْطِبارٌ وشَكْوى عند قاتلتي ... فهل بأعجبَ مِنْ هذا امرؤٌ سَمِعا
(With me is patience, and complaint is with the woman who is killing me — has any man ever heard of anything more wondrous than this?)
The indefiniteness of the two terms (أجلين) is for vagueness (ibhām). There is another permitting factor here, which is subdivision (tafṣīl), as in his saying:
186 - 1- إذا ما بكى مِنْ خلفِها انصرفَتْ له ... بشِقٍ وشِقٌ عندنا لم يُحَوَّلِ
(Whenever he cried behind her, she turned to him with one half, while one half remained with us, not turned away.)
Putting the khabar first was not obligatory here, even though the mubtadaʾ is indefinite and the khabar is an adverbial (ẓarf). Al-Zamakhsharī said: because it has been specified by the adjective, so it approaches the definite. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What he mentioned — that its permitting the indefinite to be a mubtadaʾ is due to its being qualified — is not the only possibility, since the permitting factor could be the subdivision"; then he quoted the verse «إذا ما بكى». I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not say that this is the only possibility, so that he could be held to it; he merely mentioned the best-known of the permitting factors, for few mention conjunction and subdivision among the permitting factors.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: the common usage is to say «عندي ثوب جيِّدٌ، ولي عبدٌ كيِّس» (I have a fine garment, and I have a clever slave) [with the khabar first], so what made the fronting [of the mubtadaʾ] necessary? I say: what made it necessary is that the meaning is: and what a term appointed with Him!, in magnification of the matter of the Hour; so since this meaning ran through it, it necessitated the fronting." The Shaykh said: "This is not permissible, because if the implied form is «وأيُّ أجل مسمَّى عنده», then «أيّ» would be an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being «وأجلٌ أيُّ أجلٍ مسمَّى عنده», and it is not permissible to omit the adjective when it is «أيّ», nor to omit its qualified noun and keep it: if you said «مررت بأيِّ رجل», meaning «برجلٍ أيِّ رجل», it would not be permissible." I say: I do not know how one can be held to account who explained a meaning with a wording without claiming that this wording is the underlying form of the explained speech; rather he said: its meaning is such-and-such. So how can he be bound to the claim that the speech he explained with is the underlying form of what is explained? Besides, the omission of the qualified noun of «أيّ» while keeping it has occurred, as in his saying:
186 - 2- إذا حارب الحَجَّاجُ أيَّ منافقٍ ... عَلاه بسيفٍ كلما هَزَّ يقطعُ
(Whenever al-Ḥajjāj fights some hypocrite — what a hypocrite! — he strikes him from above with a sword that cuts whenever he brandishes it.)

His saying: {ثُمَّ أَنتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ}: the discussion of this «ثم» has preceded. «تمترون» is of the form taftaʿūn from al-mirya (doubt), and its meaning preceded in al-Baqara at His saying {مِنَ الممترين} [verse 147]. The Shaykh made this a case of iltifāt (shift of person), I mean His saying «خَلَقَكم ثم أنتم تَمْتَرون»; he means that His saying {ثْمَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ} is in the third person, so He turned from it to His saying «خلقكم ثم أنتم». Then it is as though he raised an objection against himself, that "your creation" and the decreeing of the term are not specific to the disbelievers; rather the believers are like them in that. He answered that He intended only the disbelievers, to alert them to His creating them, His power, and His decreeing of their terms. He said: "I made it a case of iltifāt only because this address, namely {ثُمَّ أَنتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ}, cannot include those whom Allah has chosen for prophethood and faith."

The origin of «مُسَمَّى» is «مُسَمَّوٌ», because it is from the root of «الاسم», and that has preceded; the wāw was changed into yāʾ, then the yāʾ into alif. «تمترون»: its origin is «تَمْتَرِيُون», and it underwent weakening (iʿlāl) like its counterparts that have preceded.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَهُوَ الله فِي السموات}: there are many views on this verse, all of which I have summarised in twelve aspects. That is because there are two views on «هو». One of them: it is the pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted, referring to what the pronouns before it referred to. The second: that it is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa); Abū ʿAlī said this. The Shaykh said: "He fled to this only because, had he referred it to Allah, the implied form would become «الله الله», and the speech would be composed of two nouns identical in wording and meaning with no predicative relation between them." I say: the pronoun refers only to the One previously described with those majestic attributes, namely the creation of the heavens and the earth, the making of the darknesses and the light, and the creation of people from clay, to the end of them; so in predicating that there is a benefit without doubt. On the view of the majority, then, «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الله» its khabar (predicate), and «في السماوات» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the very word of majesty (the name Allah), because of the meaning of worship that it contains, as if it were said: "and He is the One worshipped in the heavens." This is the view of al-Zajjāj, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Zamakhsharī.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«في السماوات» is attached to the meaning of the name of Allah, as if it were said: and He is the One worshipped in them — and of this is {وَهُوَ الذي فِي السمآء إله} [al-Zukhruf: 84] — or He is the One known for divinity and alone in divinity in them, or He is the One who is called "Allah", no one else sharing this name with Him." I say: he said "or He is the One known… or He is the One who is called Allah" only because there has preceded for you a disagreement about this noble name: is it derived or not? If it is derived, the attachment of the preposition phrase to it is evident. If it is not derived, then it is either transferred (manqūl) or coined (murtajal), and on both assumptions it does not govern, because proper names do not govern. So he needed to interpret that according to each of these three views: his saying "the One worshipped" goes back to derivation; his saying "the One known" goes back to its being a transferred proper name; and his saying "the One who is called Allah" goes back to its being coined. It is as though he — may Allah have mercy on him — sensed the objection mentioned. The objection is transmitted from al-Fārisī, who said: "If you make the adverbial attached to the name of Allah, it is permissible in my view on the analogy of those who say that «الله» is originally «الإله»; but whoever treats this name as a proper name, it must, in his view, not be attached to it, unless you assume in it some kind of verbal meaning." So it is as though al-Zamakhsharī — and Allah knows best — took this from al-Fārisī's statement and expanded it. However, Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted from Abū ʿAlī that «في» is not attached to the name of Allah, because through the entry of the alif and lām, and the change that entered it, it has become like a proper name; and for this reason the Exalted said: {هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيّاً} [Maryam: 65]. The apparent sense of this transmission is that he prevents attachment to it, even if it is originally derived.

Al-Zajjāj said: "It is attached to the meanings that the name of Allah contains, as when you say: «أميرُ المؤمنين الخليفة في المشرق والمغرب» (the Commander of the Faithful is the caliph in the East and the West)." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In my view this is the best of the views and the one that most secures the eloquence of the wording and the weightiness of the meaning. Its explanation is that He wished to indicate His creation, the traces of His power, His encompassing, His dominion and similar attributes, so He gathered all of these in His saying {وَهُوَ الله}, i.e. the One to whom all of these belong in the heavens and in the earth; as if He said: and He is the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of life and the Encompasser in the heavens and the earth — as you say «زيد السلطان في الشام والعراق» (Zayd is the sultan in Syria and Iraq). If you intended Zayd's person, it would be absurd; but if the intent of your saying is: [Zayd] is the one who commands and forbids, who appoints and dismisses, it is eloquent and correct; you have put "sultanship" in place of these attributes. Likewise in the noble verse, you have put «الله» in place of those attributes."

The Shaykh said: "What al-Zajjāj mentioned and Ibn ʿAṭiyya clarified is correct in terms of meaning, but the craft of grammar supports it [Translator's note: so in the text; the sequel indicates the intended sense is "does not support it"]; because the two of them claimed that «في السماوات» is attached to the name of Allah because of those meanings it contains, and had those meanings been stated explicitly, not all of them would govern it; rather the governing, in terms of wording, would belong to one of them, even if «في السماوات» is attached to all of them in terms of meaning. Rather, it is better that it be attached to the word «الله» because of the meaning of divinity it contains, even though it is a proper name, because a proper name governs an adverbial because of the meaning it contains, as in his saying:
186 - 3- أنا أبو المِنْهالِ بعضَ الأحيانْ ...
(I am Abū al-Minhāl at certain times.)
«بعضَ» is made accusative by the proper name because it has the meaning of "I am the famous one"." I say: his saying "had they been stated explicitly they would not govern" is not conceded; rather they would govern, and their governing would be by way of contention (tanāzuʿ) — besides, had he kept silent about the answer it would be clear. And when the Shaykh mentioned what al-Zamakhsharī said, he said: "So look how he assumed the governing element in it to be one, not all of them," meaning that he sought support from it for his rebuttal of al-Zajjāj and Ibn ʿAṭiyya.

The second aspect: that «في السموات» is attached to an omitted element which is an adjective of Allah the Exalted, omitted because the meaning is understood. Some assumed it as: "and He is Allah, the One worshipped", and some: "and He is Allah, the Disposer". Omission of the adjective is very rare; only a few places have come of it, and those are open to scrutiny, among them {وَكَذَّبَ بِهِ قَوْمُكَ} [al-Anʿām: 66], i.e. the obstinate ones, and {إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ} [Hūd: 46], i.e. those saved. So this should not be construed on it.

The third aspect: al-Naḥḥās said — "and it is the best that has been said about it" — that the speech is complete at His saying {وَهُوَ الله}, and the genitive phrase is attached to the object of «يَعْلَم», which is «سِرَّكم وجَهْرَكم», [i.e.] He knows your secret and your open [speech] in them. This is very weak, because it involves putting the governed element of the maṣdar (verbal noun) before it, and what is wrong with that is known.

The fourth aspect: that the speech is likewise complete at the word of majesty, and the adverbial is attached to «يعلم» itself. This is evident, and on these two aspects «يعلم» is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

The fifth aspect: that the speech is complete at His saying {فِي السموات}, so {فِي السموات} is attached to the name of Allah, as preceded, and «في الأرض» is attached to «يعلم». This is the view of al-Ṭabarī. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak, because Allah the Exalted is worshipped in the heavens and in the earth, and knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, so neither of the two attributes is specified by one of the two adverbials." It is a fine rebuttal.

The sixth aspect: that «في السماوات» is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «سرَّكم», and then the ḥāl was put before the one it describes and before its governing element.

The seventh: that it is attached to «يَكْسِبون». This is corrupt in that it entails putting the governed element of the ṣila (relative clause) before the relative, because «ما» is a nominal or particle relative. Also, how would those addressed earn in the heavens? Had this proponent held that the speech is complete at His saying «في السماوات» and attached «في الأرض» to «يَكْسِبون», the matter would be easier in terms of meaning, though not in terms of the craft.

The eighth: that «الله» is a first khabar and «في السماوات» a second khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the sense that He is Allah and that He is in the heavens and in the earth, and in the sense that He knows what is in them, nothing being hidden from Him, as if His essence were in them." The Shaykh said: "This is weak because what is governed by «في» does not indicate a restricted (specific) being, it only indicates an absolute (general) being." This is easy to answer, as it has preceded many times.

The ninth: that «هو» is a mubtadaʾ, «الله» a badal (substitute) of it, «يَعْلَمُ» its khabar, and «في السماوات» as preceded.

The tenth: that «الله» is likewise a badal, and «في السماوات» is the khabar in the sense al-Zamakhsharī stated.

The eleventh: that «هو» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the word of majesty is a second mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is «في السماوات» in the aforementioned sense, or «يَعْلَمُ» — and the clause is the khabar of the first, explicating it — and this is the twelfth.

As for «يَعْلَمُ», you have learned the details of what preceded: that it may be resumptive, so it has no [grammatical] position, or in the position of nominative as a khabar, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. As for «سِرَّكم وجهرَكم»: they may be in their proper sense as maṣdars, being annexed to the agent. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed them to stand in the place of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "what you keep secret and what you make public", and he adduced as evidence His saying, Exalted is He: {يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ} [al-Baqara: 77]. But there is no evidence [in it], because «ما» may be maṣdariyya (infinitival). And «ما» in «ما تكسبون» may be maṣdariyya — which is more fitting, matching the two maṣdars before it — or may mean "that which".

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ}: Regarding the two pronouns — I mean «هم» and the hāʾ of «عنه» — there are several views. The first: the nominative one refers to the disbelievers and the genitive one refers to the Qur'an, which is also what the accusative pronoun in «يَفْقهوه» referred to, and what is pointed to by their saying «إنْ هذا». The second: «هم» refers to the disbelievers mentioned before, and the pronoun in «عنه» refers to the Messenger; on this view there is an iltifāt (shift of address) from the second person to the third person, for His saying {جَآءُوكَ يُجَادِلُونَكَ} is an address to the Messenger, and it moved out of this address to the third person. It has also been said: the nominative one refers to Abū Ṭālib and his followers.
In His saying {يَنْهَوْنَ} and {وَيَنْأَوْنَ} there is tajnīs al-taṣrīf (paronomasia of inflection), which means that each word differs from the other by one letter: يَنْهَوْن is distinguished by the hāʾ and يَنْأَوْن by the hamza. Like it is His saying, the Exalted: {وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ} [al-Kahf: 104], {بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ. . . . . . وَبِمَا كُنتُمْ تَمْرَحُونَ} [Ghāfir: 75], and his saying, upon him be peace: «الخيلُ معقودٌ في نواصيها الخيرُ» (goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses). Some call it «tajnīs al-taḥrīf» (paronomasia of alteration), which is the difference between two words by one letter, and they cited:
188 - 4- إنْ لم أشُنَّ على أبن حرب غارةً ... لم تَخْلُ يوماً من نِهاب نفوسِ
(If I do not launch a raid on Ibn Ḥarb, a raid never empty, any day, of the plundering of souls.)
Someone else mentioned that tajnīs al-taḥrīf is when the vowelling is the difference between two words, and counted among it «اللُّهى تفتح اللَّهى» (gifts open uvulas); its full treatment has preceded. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «ويَنَوْن», casting the vowel of the hamza onto the nūn and dropping the hamza; this is a regular (qiyāsī) lightening. النَّأيُ means distance; the poet said:
188 - 5- إذا غيَّر النأيُ المُحِبِّين لم يَزَلْ ... رَسِيسُ الهوى مِنْ حُبِّ مَيَّةَ يبرحُ
(When distance changes lovers, the lingering touch of passion from love of Mayya never ceases to torment.)
And another said:
188 - 6- ألا حَبَّذا هندٌ وأرضٌ بها هندُ ... وهندٌ أتى مِنْ دونها النأيُ البعدُ
(How lovely is Hind, and a land in which Hind is — and Hind, between whom and me has come distance, remoteness.)
— conjoining a thing to itself because of the difference in wording. One says: نأى زيد يَنْأى نأياً, and it is made transitive by the hamza, so one says أَنْأيْتُه; it is not made transitive by doubling, and likewise every verb whose middle radical is a hamza. Al-Wāḥidī reported that one says نَأَيْتُه in the sense of نَأَيْتُ عنه; al-Mubarrad cited:
188 - 7- أعاذِلُ إن يُصْبحْ صَداي بقَفْرَةٍ ... بعيداً نآني صاحبي وقريبي
(O blamer, if my remains lie one morning in a desert, far away, my companion and my kinsman will have gone far from me.)
i.e. نأى عني. Al-Layth related «نَأَيْت الشيء», meaning: I removed it far, and cited:
188 - 8- إذا ما التَقَيْنا سالَ من عَبَراتنا ... شآبيب يُنْآى سَيْلُها بالأصابع
(Whenever we meet, showers of our tears flow, whose stream is pushed away with the fingers.)
So he built it for the object (passive), i.e. it is moved aside and put away. In sum, this root denotes distance; from it is أَتَنَأَّى, i.e. I undertake distancing. المَنْأى is a distant place; al-Nābigha said:
188 - 9- فإنَّك كالموتِ الذي هو مُدْرِكي ... وإنْ خِلْتُ أنَّ المُنْتأى عنك واسعُ
(For you are like death, which will overtake me, even if I imagine that the place of refuge far from you is wide.)
تناءَى means to move apart from one another; from it is النُّؤيُ for the little trench around the tent to keep water away from it. It has been read: {وناءَ بجانبه}, which is a metathesis of نأى; what indicates this is that the origin is the maṣdar (verbal noun), which is النَّأْيُ, with the hamza before the weak letter.
His saying: {وَإِن يُهْلِكُونَ}: «إنْ» is negative, like the one in His saying {إِنْ هاذآ} [al-Anʿām: 25]; «أنفسهم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). The object of «يَشْعرون» is omitted, either by restriction (iqtiṣār) or by abbreviation (ikhtiṣār), i.e. "and they do not perceive that they are destroying themselves".

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بَلْ بَدَا}: «بل» here is for moving from one story to another, not for cancellation (ibṭāl). The wording of some suggests that it contains a cancellation of the disbelievers' speech, for he said: "«بل» is a rejection of what they wished for, i.e. the matter is not as they said, because they did not say that out of desire for faith; rather they said it out of fear of the punishment and in hope of mercy." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "I do not know what this statement is." I say: and I do not know the reason for his not knowing! It is a sound statement in itself: when they said «يا ليتنا», it is as if they said "we wished", but this wish is not genuine, because they only said it as a precaution (taqiyya); a person may wish for something with his tongue while his heart is empty of it. Al-Zajjāj said: «بل» here is istidrāk (rectification) and the affirmation of a negation, as in their saying: ما قام زيد بل قام عمرو (Zayd did not stand; rather ʿAmr stood). The Shaykh said: "I do not know what negation preceded so that «بل» would affirm it." I say: what is apparent is that the negation al-Zajjāj meant is the one in His saying {وَلاَ نُكَذِّبَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا} when we make it resumptive (mustaʾnaf), with the implied form "and we do not deny", and the meaning is: rather, they are deniers.
The fāʿil (agent) of «بدا» is His saying {مَّا كَانُواْ}. «ما» may be a nominal relative noun, which is the apparent view, i.e. there appeared to them that which they used to conceal; the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted. It may also be maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e. their concealing appeared to them, meaning its consequence; or the maṣdar is applied to the meaning of the passive participle, which is far-fetched. The apparent view is that the two pronouns — I mean the genitive and the nominative in His saying {بَدَا لَهُمْ مَّا كَانُواْ يُخْفُونَ} — refer to one thing, namely the disbelievers, or the Jews and Christians specifically. It has also been said: the genitive one is for the followers and the nominative one for the chiefs, i.e. rather, there appeared to the followers what the notable, followed men used to conceal.
His saying: {وَلَوْ رُدُّواْ}: the majority read it with a pure ḍamma on the rāʾ. Al-Aʿmash, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ibrāhīm read «رِدُّوا» with a pure kasra. You already know that the doubled triliteral verb (whose second and third radicals are the same) allows, when built for the object (passive), the same three options in its first radical that are mentioned for the first radical of the hollow verb when passive, such as قيل and بيع; that has preceded. The poet said:
189 - 7- وما حِلَّ مِنْ جهلٍ حُبا حُلمائِنا ... ولا قائلُ المعروف فينا يُعَنَّفُ
(The sitting-cloths of our wise men are never loosened out of folly, nor is the one who speaks what is right rebuked among us.)
with kasra on the ḥāʾ.
His saying: {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ}: discussion of this clause has preceded: is it resumptive, or does it go back to His saying {يا ليتنا}?

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وقالوا}: Is this clause conjoined to the answer of «لو», the implied form being "and if they were returned they would revert and would say", or is it resumptive (mustaʾnafa), not falling within the scope of «لو», or is it conjoined to His saying {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ}? Three views. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned the first and the last, for he said: "«وقالوا» is conjoined to «لعادوا», i.e. if they were returned they would disbelieve and would say: there is nothing but our worldly life, as they used to say before witnessing the Resurrection. It may also be conjoined to His saying {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ}, in the sense: and they are a people who lie in everything." The first view is reported from Ibn Zayd, except that Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected it, saying: "Allah's making them stand, in the verse after it, before the resurrection, and the reference to it in His saying {أَلَيْسَ هذا بالحق} [Āl ʿImrān: 30], refutes this interpretation." [Translator's note: the verse reference «آل عمران: 30» is as printed; the words {أَلَيْسَ هذا بالحق} are in al-Anʿām 6:30.] This may be answered by the difference of two states: their acknowledgement of the resurrection in reality is only in the Hereafter, while their denial of it is only in this world, on the supposition of their return to this world; so their acknowledging it in the abode of the Hereafter does not conflict with their denying it in this world.
His saying: {إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ حَيَاتُنَا}: «إنْ» is negative, «هي» is mubtadaʾ (subject) and «حياتُنا» its khabar (predicate). They were not content with merely stating this, but presented it as restricted by negation and affirmation. «هي» is a vague pronoun explained by its khabar, i.e. we do not know what is meant by it except by the mention of its khabar; it is one of the pronouns explained by what comes after them both in wording and in rank. I treated this earlier at His saying {فَسَوَّاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ} [al-Baqara: 29]. That this is among what is explained by what follows in wording and rank is open to question, since someone may say that «هي» refers to something indicated by the context of speech, as if they said: the continuing custom, or our state and what we have known, is nothing but our worldly life. This speaker relied on al-Zamakhsharī's saying: "This is a pronoun whose intended meaning is not known except by mentioning what follows it"; al-Zamakhsharī gave as examples the Arabs' sayings: «هي النفس تتحمَّل ما حَمَلَتْ» (it is the soul: it bears what it is made to bear) and «هي العرب تقول ما شاءت» (they are the Arabs: they say what they will).
There is no proof for him in what al-Zamakhsharī said, because he means that what the pronoun refers to is not known except by the mention of what follows it, and there is nothing in this indicating that the khabar explains the pronoun. The meaning may be: there is no life but our worldly life; so His saying {إِلاَّ حَيَاتُنَا الدنيا} indicates what explains the pronoun, namely life in general. Thus it is true of it that what is meant by it is not known [Translator's note: the printed text has «لا يعمل», evidently for «لا يُعلم»] except by the mention of what follows, from this angle, not from the angle of explanation. What I have said is supported by the saying of Abū al-Baqāʾ: "«هي» is an allusion to life; it may also be the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa)."
I say: as for the first part of his statement, it is correct; as for its last part, namely his saying that «هي» is the pronoun of the story, it is nothing, because the pronoun of the story is only explained by a clause with both of its parts expressed. If you say: the Kufan permits its explanation by a single word, so he may have followed their approach — the answer is that the Kufan only permits it with a single word that operates like a verb, such as «إنه قائم زيد» and «وظنتُه قائِماً زيدٌ», because it has the form of a clause, since the expression contains a predicand (musnad) and a subject of predication (musnad ilayhi). As for something like «هو زيد», no one permits it with «هو» being a pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) or of the story. «الدنيا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الحياة», and it is not an adjective removing an incidental shared reference — meaning that there is some life other than the worldly one which they acknowledge — because they know only this one; so it is an adjective for mere tawkīd (emphasis); so it has been said, and they mean by that that it has no implied contrary meaning (mafhūm); otherwise, actual emphasis is not apparent, unlike {نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 13]. The bāʾ in His saying «بمبعوثين» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasising the negated khabar; its genitive noun may be accusative in position, on «ما» being Ḥijāzī, or nominative, on its being Tamīmī.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {على رَبِّهِمْ}: There are two views on it. The first: it is a case of omission, its implied form being "before the questioning of their Lord", or "the dominion of their Lord", or "the recompense of their Lord". The second: it is a case of figurative usage (majāz), because it is an allusion to detention for rebuke, just as a slave is made to stand before his master so that he may reproach him. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this and preferred the figurative usage to the omission, since he began with the figurative usage and then said: "And it has been said: [they were made to stand] before the recompense of their Lord." People disagree over preferring one of them to the other. The sum of the matter is that there are three positions: the best known is preferring figurative usage over implication (iḍmār); the second is its reverse; and the third is that they are equal.
His saying: {قَالَ أَلَيْسَ}: There are two views on this clause. The first: it is "istifhāmiyya", i.e. the answer to an implied question. [Translator's note: so in the printed text; the sense, as the following quotation shows, is "istiʾnāfiyya" (resumptive).] Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«قال» is a reply to the saying of one who says: what did their Lord say to them when they were made to stand before Him? And it is answered: He said to them: is this not the truth?" The second: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) is «ربُّهم», as if it were said: they were made to stand before Him while He was saying: is this not the truth? As for what is pointed to, it has been said: it is the resurrection which they used to deny; and it has been said: it is the punishment, indicated by {فَذُوقُواْ العذاب}.
His saying: {بِمَا كُنتُمْ}: «ما» may be a nominal relative noun, the implied form being "تكفرونه", originally "تكفرون به"; the pronoun was attached to the verb after the intermediary [preposition] was dropped. It is not permissible for it to be omitted while still in the genitive, even though it is governed by a preposition like the one governing the relative noun, because what they are attached to differs; this has been explained more than once. It is preferable to make «ما» maṣdariyya (infinitival) with the object of disbelief omitted, the implied form being: because you used to disbelieve in the ʿabath [Translator's note: so printed, «بالعبث»; evidently for «بالبعث», the resurrection] or in the punishment, i.e. in meeting it — that is, because of your disbelief in that.

semin-durr:95-95.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَالِقُ الحب}: It is permissible/ for the iḍāfa (genitive construct) to be pure (maḥḍa), on the view that it is an active participle in the sense of the past, because that has already happened; this is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh «فلق» as a past verb. And it is permissible for the iḍāfa to be impure (ghayr maḥḍa), on the view that it is in the sense of the present or the future, and that is by way of narrating a past state as present (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl); then «الحَبِّ» is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative (manṣūb) in position. Al-filq: it is the splitting of a thing; al-Rāghib restricted it to separating part of it from another part. Al-falaq: the low-lying ground between two hillocks. And al-falaq in His words { أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الفلق} [al-Falaq: 1] is what He taught to Moses, peace be upon him, until he split the sea with it. And it was said: the dawn. And it was said: they are the rivers alluded to in His words: {وَجَعَلَ خِلاَلَهَآ أَنْهَاراً} [al-Naml: 61]. And al-filq with kasra means "the split thing" (al-mafrūq), like al-nikth and al-niqḍ, and from it: «سمعته من فِلْق منه» ("I heard it from his very mouth"). And it was said: al-filq is a wonder. And al-falīq and al-fāliq are what lies between two mountains, and what lies between the two humps of a camel. Some explained «فالق» here as meaning "Creator"; it was said: this is not known in the language. But this is not to be heeded, because this is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk; it is not to be said that this was by way of explanation for the sake of approximation, because al-Farrāʾ transmitted in the language that faṭara, khalaqa and falaqa have one meaning.
[And al-nawā is a generic noun whose singular is nawāt, on the pattern of] qamḥ and qamḥa. And al-nawā also means "distance". One says: nawat al-busra and anwat: its stone became hard. The lām (final radical) of «النواة» is yāʾ, because its ʿayn (middle radical) is wāw, and difference [between the radicals] is the more common.
His words «يُخْرج»: two aspects are permissible in it. The first: that it is a resumptive clause, so it has no grammatical position. The second: that it is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar (predicate) of inna. And His words «ومُخْرِج»: two aspects are also permissible in it. One of them: that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فالق — and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else — i.e. Allah is فالق and مخرج; He is informed about by these two predicates. On this view «يخرج» stands as it is [i.e. on one of its two aspects]; and on the view of its being resumptive, it would be parenthetical, by way of explaining the meaning of the clause before it. The second: that it is conjoined to «يخرج». And is the verb to be taken in the sense of a noun so that conjoining the noun to it is valid, or is the noun to be taken in the sense of the verb so that conjoining it to it is valid? Two possibilities built on what preceded about «يخرج»: if we say that it is resumptive, it is a verb not interpreted as a noun, so the noun is returned to the sense of the verb, as if مُخْرِجاً had the force of يُخْرج. And if we say that it is a second khabar of «إنَّ», it is interpreted as a noun occupying the place of a second khabar, and therefore an explicit noun was conjoined to it. An example of conjoining a noun to a verb because the verb is interpreted as a noun is the poet's saying:
2002 - فألفيتُه يوماً يُبير عدوَّه ... ومُجْرٍ عطاءً يَسْتَخِفُّ المعابرا
(I found him one day destroying his enemy, and pouring forth a gift that makes light of the crossings.)
And his saying:
2003 - يا رُبَّ بيضاءَ من العواهجِ ... أمِّ صبيّ قد حَبَا أو دارج
(How many a fair one among the long-necked [women], mother of a boy who has crawled or is walking.)
And his saying:
2004 - بات يُغَشِّيها بعَضْبٍ باترٍ ... يَقْصِدُ في أَسْوُقِها وجائِرُ
(He spent the night covering them with a cutting sword, aiming at their legs, and swerving.)
That is: «مبيراً», or «أمِّ صبي حابٍ», and «قاصِدٍ».

semin-durr:97-97.t:
The words of the Exalted: {جَعَلَ لَكُمُ النجوم}: The apparent sense is that «جعل» means "created", so it is transitive to one object, and «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جَعَلَ», and likewise «لتهتدوا». If it is said: how can two prepositions identical in wording and meaning be attached [to one verb]? The answer is that the second is a badal (substitute) of the first, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) with repetition of the governing word, for «ليهتدوا» is a preposition and its genitive noun, since the lām is the lām of kay (purpose), and the verb after it is accusative by an implied «أن» according to the Basrans — its establishment has already preceded. The implied form is: He made the stars for you for your being guided. Its parallel in the Qur'an is {لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بالرحمن لِبُيُوتِهِمْ} [al-Zukhruf: 33], for «لبيوتهم» is a badal of «لمن يكفر» with repetition of the governing word. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It may possibly be in the sense of «صيَّر» (made into), and the second object is supplied from «لتَهْتدوا», i.e. He made the stars for you a guidance."
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It is weak because omission of one of the two objects of ẓanna and its sisters is rare." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya did not claim omission of the second object such that he [Abū Ḥayyān] could declare it weak; he only said that it is from «لتهتدوا», i.e. the attachment of the preposition-phrase that occurs as the second object is implied, as it is implied in its parallels, the implied form being: He made the stars for you settled, or existing, for your being guided. As for his words "i.e. He made the stars for you a guidance", that is to clarify and explain the meaning.
The stars are well known; they are the plural of najm. Al-najm is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); one says: najama al-kawkab yanjumu najman wa-nujūman, so it is nājim; then it was applied to the star (al-kawkab) figuratively. So al-najm is used at times as a noun for the star and at times as a maṣdar, and al-nujūm is used at times for the stars and at times as a maṣdar; from it: najama al-nabt, i.e. the plant came up, and najama the horn of the sheep and others. And al-najm among plants is that which has no stem, and al-shajar is that which has a stem. And al-tanjīm: dispersing; from it nujūm al-kināna (the arrows scattered from the quiver), by comparison with the dispersion of the stars.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with kasra of the qāf, and the rest with fatḥa. As for «مُسْتَوْدَع», all read it with fatḥa of the dāl, though al-Aʿwar related from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ its kasra. Whoever read the qāf with kasra made «مستقرَّاً» an active participle, meaning persons, and it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "among you is one who settles (مستقر)", whether in the loins, the wombs or the graves; and on this reading «ومستودَع» with fatḥa of the dāl is consistent.
Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «مستقِر» with kasra of the qāf to be a place [noun], and he began with it, saying: "So it would be a place that settles for you" — end of quote — meaning: the implied form is "and for you is a place that settles". This is not apparent at all, since a place is not described as being مستقِر with kasra of the qāf, but rather as مُسْتَقَرّ فيه (settled in). As for مستودَع with its fatḥa, it may be a passive participle, a place [noun], or a maṣdar (verbal noun). For the first the implied form is: among you is one settled in the loins and one deposited in the wombs; or one settled on the earth visibly and one deposited in it hidden. For the second the implied form is: among you is one who settles, and for you is a place in which you are deposited. For the third the implied form is: among you is one who settles, and for you is a depositing.
As for whoever read the qāf with fatḥa, only two aspects are permissible: that it is a place [noun], or a maṣdar, i.e. for you is a place in which you settle, which is the loins, the womb or the earth; or for you is a settling in what has been mentioned. Its being a passive participle is ruled out, because its verb is intransitive, from which no passive participle is formed — unlike مستودع, in which all three aspects were permissible.
The justification of the reading of Abū ʿAmr in al-Aʿwar's transmission from him of «مستودِع» with kasra is that man is treated as if he were the depositor of his provision and his term, so that when they run out it is as if he has returned them; this is a fine figurative usage. What I have said is strengthened by the poet's saying:
2014 - وما المالُ والأهلون إلا وديعةٌ ... ولا بُدَّ يوماً أن تُرَدَّ الودائعُ
(Wealth and family are nothing but a deposit, and one day the deposits must be returned.)
/ And al-inshāʾ: bringing into being and rearing; from it: inshāʾ al-saḥāb (the raising of clouds). The Exalted said: {أَوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ فِي الحلية} [al-Zukhruf: 18], and here rearing is meant. Al-inshāʾ is mostly used for bringing living beings into existence, though it has come for other things; the Exalted said: {وَيُنْشِىءُ السحاب الثقال} [al-Raʿd: 12]. And al-inshāʾ [as a technical term] is the counterpart of al-khabar (the informative statement): it is that which has no external referent [to correspond to]. Is it subsumed under al-ṭalab (request), or the reverse, or is it a category in itself? There is disagreement. And it was said, by way of approximation: [it is] the concurrence of the utterance with its meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was «يعلمون» said with the mention of the stars, and «يفقهون» with the mention of the bringing-into-being of the children of Adam? I say: it is as if the bringing-into-being of humans from a single soul and their turning through different states is subtler and finer in craftsmanship and governance, so mention of fiqh (understanding), which is the use of acumen and precision of reflection, was fitting for it."

semin-durr:72-72.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَأَنْ أَقِيمُواْ}: there are several views on it. The first: it is in the position of an accusative (naṣb) as the object of the saying, conjoined (nasaq) to His words «إنَّ هُدَى الله هو الهدى», i.e. "Say these two things." The second: it is conjoined to «لِنُسْلَم», the implied form being: "and we were commanded such-and-such for submission (islām) and so that we establish the prayer"; and «أن» can be joined to an imperative, as in their saying «كتبت إليه بأن قم» ("I wrote to him that he should stand"), which Sībawayh reported. This is the view of al-Zajjāj. The third: it is conjoined to «ائتنا». Makkī said: "because its meaning is «أن ائتنا»"; but this is not apparent. The fourth: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the implied object of the command, the implied form being: "and we were commanded to believe and to establish the prayer"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this.
The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "There is no harm in this, since a second object must be implied for «أُمِرْنا»; and it is permissible to omit the thing conjoined to when the meaning is understood. You say: «أضربت زيداً؟» ('Did you strike Zayd?'), and he answers: «نعم وعمراً» ('Yes, and ʿAmr'), the implied form being: 'I struck him and ʿAmr.' Al-Farrāʾ even allowed «جاءني الذي وزيد قائمان» ('there came to me the one who—and Zayd—are standing'), the implied form being «الذي هو وزيدٌ قائمان», so «هو» was omitted because the meaning indicates it." But this which he said there is no harm in is not among the principles of the Basrans. As for «نَعَمْ وعَمْراً», there is no evidence in it, because «نَعَمْ» stands in place of the omitted clause. Makkī said something close to this view, except that he did not explicitly state the omission of the thing conjoined to; for he said: "«أن» is in the position of an accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being «وبأَنْ أَقيموا»." His words «وبأن أقيموا» are the meaning of Ibn ʿAṭiyya's view, except that the latter made it clearer by omitting the thing conjoined to.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: to what is His word {وَأَنْ أَقِيمُواْ} conjoined? I answer: to the position of «لِنُسْلِمَ», as though it were said: 'and we were commanded that we submit and that [we] establish [the prayer].'" The Shaykh said: "The apparent sense of this implied form is that «لنسلم» is in the position of the second object of «أُمِرْنا», and «وأَنْ أقيموا» is conjoined to it; so the lām on this view would be redundant (zāʾida). Yet he had stated before this that the lām gives the reason for the command, so his words contradict each other, because what is a reason cannot possibly be an object. What shows that he meant by his saying «أن نسلم» is in the position of the second object is his statement after that: 'And the implied form may be: and we were commanded for that we submit and for that [we] establish, i.e. for submission and for establishing the prayer'; this is the view of al-Zajjāj. If this view were not different from his first view, his two views would be one, and that is absurd."
Al-Zajjāj said: "«أن أقيموا» is conjoined to His words «لِنُسْلِمَ», its implied form being: 'and we were commanded for that we submit and that [we] establish.'" Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The wording resists it, because «نُسْلِمَ» is declinable (muʿrab) and «أقيموا» is indeclinable (mabnī), and conjoining the indeclinable to the declinable is not permissible, because conjunction requires sharing in the governing word (ʿāmil)."
The Shaykh said: "What he mentioned, that the indeclinable is not conjoined to the declinable, is not as he said; rather it is permissible, e.g. «قام زيد وهذا» ('Zayd and this one stood'), and Allah the Exalted said:
{يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ القيامة فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ النار} [Hūd: 98]. The most that can be said on the matter is that the government takes effect on the declinable and does not take effect on the indeclinable. You say «إنْ قام زيد ويقصدْني أُكرمه» ('If Zayd stands and comes to me, I will honour him'): «إن» did not affect «قام» because it is indeclinable, and it affected «يقصِدْني» because it is declinable." Then Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Unless one makes the conjunction apply to «إنْ» [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably «أنْ»] alone, and that is awkward (qaliq). It can only be explained by taking His words «وأن أقيموا» to mean «ولنقم» ('and let us establish'), then it came out in the wording of the imperative because of the forcefulness of expression in that; so the conjunction became permissible by disregarding the rule of the wording and relying on the meaning. Something similar in a way is what Yūnus reported from the Arabs: «ادخلوا الأول فالأول» ('Enter, the first then the first' [in the nominative]), whereas otherwise only «الأولَ فالأولَ» in the accusative is permissible."
The Shaykh said: "This which he added with his words 'unless…' to the end is exactly what al-Zajjāj meant, namely that «أَنْ أقيموا» is conjoined to «أن نُسْلِمَ», and that both of them are a reason for the omitted thing commanded. It was only awkward for Ibn ʿAṭiyya because he wanted «أن أقيموا» to keep its meaning as originally an imperative, and that is not so; because when «أَنْ» enters upon an imperative verb and is the maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya) one, a maṣdar (verbal noun) is formed from it and the imperative, and when a maṣdar is formed from the two, the imperative meaning disappears. The grammarians—Sībawayh and others—allowed the maṣdar-forming «أَنْ» that puts the imperfect in the accusative to be joined to the past and to the imperative. Sībawayh said: 'And you say: «كتبت إليه بأَنْ قم», i.e. with standing.' If the rule is thus, then His words «لنُسْلِمَ» and «أَنْ أقيموا» are equivalent to: 'for submission and for establishing the prayer.' As for Ibn ʿAṭiyya's likening it to the saying «ادخلوا الأولُ فالأولُ» with the nominative, it is not similar, because «ادخلوا», if the pronoun were removed from it, could not govern what follows it, unlike «أَنْ», which is joined to the imperative; so there is no similarity between them." End of quotation.
As for the Shaykh's saying "It was only awkward for Ibn ʿAṭiyya because he wanted «أَنْ أقيموا» to keep its meaning as originally an imperative": the awkwardness for him was not due to that alone, as the Shaykh restricted it, but rather to another matter on the side of the wording, namely that the structural context, according to what al-Zajjāj said, requires it to be «لنسلم» and «وأن نقيم», so that the second verb would come with the [first-person] pronoun; since it did not say that, it was awkward for him. What shows what I have mentioned is Ibn ʿAṭiyya's saying "meaning «ولنقم», then it came out in the wording of the imperative" to the end.
The fifth: it is construed according to the meaning, since the meaning is: "it was said to us: submit, and that [you] establish [the prayer]."

semin-durr:73-73.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُن}: concerning «يوم» there are eight aspects. The first—and it is the view of al-Zajjāj—is that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not an adverb of time (ẓarf), and it is conjoined to the hāʾ in «اتقوه», i.e. "and fear the day," i.e. the punishment of the day on which He says, or its terror, or its alarm. It is thus like His words in another place: {واتقوا يَوْماً لاَّ تَجْزِي} [al-Baqara: 48], according to the well-known parsing of it. The second: it is also a direct object, but conjoined (nasaq) to «السماوات والأرض», i.e. "and He is the One who created the day on which He says." The third: it is the object of an implied «اذْكُرْ» ("remember") [Translator's note: the printed text reads «لا ذكْرُ», evidently a misprint for «لاذْكُرْ»]. The fourth: it is in the accusative by an implied governing word, and that implied governing word is itself the object of an implied verb as well, the implied form being: "and remember the restoration on the day He says 'Be'," i.e. the day Allah says to the bodies: "Be restored." The fifth: it is conjoined to the position of His words «بالحق», for its position is accusative, and «يقول» is in the sense of the past «قال», as though it were said: "And He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth, and on the day He said to them: Be."
The sixth: that «يوم يقول» is a khabar (predicate) placed first, the mubtadaʾ (subject) being «قوله» with «الحق» as its adjective, i.e. "His word is the truth on the day He says 'Be,' and it is." Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, for he said: "«قوله الحق» is a mubtadaʾ and «يوم يقول» is its khabar placed before it, and its accusative is in the sense of [implied] settledness (istiqrār), as in your saying «يوم الجمعة القتال» ('the fighting is on Friday'); and 'the day' is in the sense of 'the time'. The meaning is: He created the heavens and the earth upholding wisdom, and at the time He says to anything 'Be,' and that thing comes to be, His word is truth and wisdom." The seventh: it is in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), governed by the meaning of the clause «قوله الحق», i.e. His word is true on the day He says "Be." The eighth: it is in the accusative by an omitted [word] indicated by «بالحق».
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The accusative of «اليوم» is by an omitted [word] indicated by His words «بالحق», as though it were said: and at the time He brings into being and decrees, He acts with truth." [Translator's note: the printed text reads «وحين يكونّ ويقدّر يقوم بالحق», apparently a corruption of «وحين يُكَوِّن ويُقَدِّر يقوم بالحق».] The Shaykh said: "This is a strained parsing."
His words: {فَيَكُونُ}: here it is complete (tāmma, i.e. "comes to be"), and likewise His word {كن}; so it suffices with a nominative and needs no accusative. Concerning its fāʿil (agent) there are four aspects. The first: it is a pronoun referring to all that Allah the Exalted creates on the Day of Resurrection; thus Abū al-Baqāʾ restricted it to the Day of Resurrection. Makkī said: "It is said: the implied [referent] of the pronoun in «فيكون» is everything He wills," so he left it unrestricted; this is better, and it is as though Abū al-Baqāʾ took that [restriction] from the context. The second: it is a pronoun referring to the Trumpet (al-ṣūr) that is blown into, indicated by His words {يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي الصور}. The third: it is a pronoun referring to the day, i.e. "and that tremendous day comes to be." The fourth: the fāʿil is «قولُه», with «الحق» its adjective, i.e. "and His true word comes into existence"; on this view the sentence is complete at «الحق».
His words: {قَوْلُهُ الحق}: there are four aspects concerning it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ, «الحق» is its naʿt (adjective), and its khabar is His words «يوم يقول». The second: it is the fāʿil of His word «فيكون», «الحق» again being its adjective. These two aspects have been mentioned already.
The third: that «قولُه» is a mubtadaʾ and «الحقُّ» its khabar: He informs about His word that it is nothing but truth. The fourth: it is again a mubtadaʾ, «الحق» its adjective, and «يوم يُنْفخ» its khabar. On this view there are three aspects in His words «وله الملك». The first: that it be a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, parenthetical between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar, so that it then has no grammatical position. The second: that «الملك» be conjoined to «قوله», the al in it being a substitute for the pronoun, and «وله» being in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الملك», governed by the [implied] settledness; the implied form being: "His true word and His dominion—belonging to Him—are on the day [the Trumpet] is blown." So you have informed about the true word and the dominion which belong to Allah that they both occur on the day the Trumpet is blown. The third: that the clause «وله الملك» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl. This aspect is weak for two reasons. One: it would be an emphatic ḥāl (muʾakkida), whereas the norm is that it be a founding (muʾassisa) one. Two: its governing word is notional (maʿnawī), since it is the settledness implied in the adverbial phrase serving as khabar, and only al-Akhfash and those who follow him allow this. His doctrine has been established more than once with its proofs.
His words: {يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ}: there are eight aspects concerning it. The first: it is the khabar of His words «قوله الحق» [Translator's note: the text here reads «قول الحق»], and this has been set out already with its verification. The second: it is a badal (substitute) from «يوم يقول», so its rule is the rule of that. The third: it is an adverb for «تُحْشَرون», i.e. "and He is the One to whom you will be gathered on the day the Trumpet is blown." The fourth: it is in the accusative by «الملك» itself, i.e. "and His is the dominion on that day." If you say: this entails restricting the dominion to the day of the blowing, whereas the dominion is His at all times—the answer is what was answered concerning His words {لِّمَنِ الملك اليوم؟ لله} [Ghāfir: 16] and His words {والأمر يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ} [al-Infiṭār: 19], namely that the benefit of stating this is that He affirmed the dominion and the command on a day when no one can claim any of that; and so is this. The fifth: it is a ḥāl from «الملك», governed by «له» because of the verbal meaning it contains. The sixth: it is in the accusative by His word «يقول». The seventh: it is in the accusative by «عالم الغيب» after it. The eighth: it is in the accusative by His words «قول الحق». So eight aspects have been obtained in each of the two «يوم»s, and praise be to Allah.
The majority read «يُنْفَخُ» as passive with the yāʾ of the third person, the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) being the prepositional phrase after it. Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of ʿAbd al-Wārith [Translator's note: printed «عبد الوراث»], read «ننفخ» with the nūn of majesty, active. As for «الصُّور», the majority read it with the [ʿayn, i.e. the middle radical] unvowelled, and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read it with a fatḥa on it [«الصُّوَر»]. As for the majority reading, they differed about the meaning of «الصُّور» in it. A group said: «الصُّور» is the plural of «صُورة» ("form"), like «الصُّوف» the plural of «صُوفة» and «الثُّوم» the plural of «ثومة»; this is not a morphological plural but a collective noun (ism jins), since it is distinguished from its singular by the feminine tāʾ; and they supported this view with the reading of al-Ḥasan mentioned above.
Another group said: «الصُّور» is the horn. Some of them said it is the dialect of Yemen, and recited:
195 - 5- نحن نَطَحْناهُمْ غَداة الجَمْعَيْنْ ... بالشامخات في غبار النَّقْعَيْنْ
نَطْحاً شديداً لا كنطح الصُّوْرَيْن
(We butted them on the morning of the two hosts, with lofty [horns], in the dust of the two battle-clouds — a hard butting, not like the butting of the two horns.)
They supported that with what has come in the sound hadiths: he (upon him be peace) said: "How can I enjoy ease when the one with the horn has already put it to his mouth?" It is said in its description that it is an elongated horn with holes in it, and that the souls of all people are in it; when Isrāfīl blows into it, the soul of every body comes out of one of those holes. Abū al-Haytham turned sharply against those who claimed that «الصُّور» is the plural of «صُورة», saying: "A group objected and denied that the ṣūr is a horn, just as they denied the Throne, the Balance and the Path, and claimed that «الصور» is the plural of «الصورة» like «الصوف» the plural of «الصوفة», and they related that from Abū ʿUbayda. This is a gross error and a distortion of the speech of Allah the Mighty and Majestic from its places, because Allah said: {وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ} [Ghāfir: 64] and {وَنُفِخَ فِي الصور} [al-Kahf: 99]; so whoever reads it «ونُفِخ في الصُّوَرِ», i.e. with the fatḥa, and reads «فَأَحْسَنَ صُوْرَكم», i.e. with sukūn, has forged a lie against Allah. Abū ʿUbayd [Translator's note: so in the text here, having said Abū ʿUbayda above] was a man of reports and rare words and had no knowledge of grammar." Al-Azharī said: "Abū al-Haytham argued, and argued well, and in my view nothing other than what he held is permissible, and it is the view of Ahl al-Sunna wa-l-Jamāʿa." End of quotation. But that [view] ought not to be ascribed to the extreme that Abū al-Haytham mentioned. Al-Farrāʾ said: "One says «نَفَخ في الصور» and «نَفَخَ الصورَ»," and he recited:
195 - 6- لولا ابنُ جَعْدَةَ لم يُفْتَح قُهَنْدُزُكُمْ ... ولا خراسانُ حتى يُنْفَخَ الصُّورُ
(Were it not for Ibn Jaʿda, your citadel would not have been opened, nor Khurāsān, until the Trumpet is blown.)
There is more discussion on the question than this, which I have left out preferring brevity.
His words: {عَالِمُ الغيب}: concerning its nominative there are four aspects. The first: that it be an adjective of «الذي» in His words {وَهُوَ الذي خَلَقَ}; this is far-fetched because of the long separation by extraneous material. The second: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the Knower." The third: it is the fāʿil of His word {يقول}, i.e. "the day the Knower of the unseen says." The fourth: it is the fāʿil of an omitted verb indicated by the passive verb; because when He said «يُنفخ في الصور», someone asked: "Who is it that blows?" and it was said: «عالم الغيب», i.e. the Knower of the unseen blows into it, i.e. commands the blowing into it—like His words {يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بالغدو والآصال رِجَالٌ} [al-Nūr: 36–37] [Translator's note: printed «3637»], i.e. men glorify Him; and like it also the saying of the other [poet]:
195 - 7- ليُبْكَ يزيدُ ضارعٌ لخصومةٍ ... ومختبطٌ ممَّا تُطيح الطوائح
(Let Yazīd be wept for — [by] one humbled in a dispute, and one seeking favour because of what calamities sweep away.)
i.e. Who weeps for him? and it was said: one humbled, i.e. one humbled weeps for him. And like it: «وكذلك زُيِّن لكثير من المشركين قَتْلُ أولادِهم شركاؤُهم» in the reading of those who made «زُيِّن» passive and put «قَتْلُ» and «شركاؤهم» in the nominative, as though it were said: "Who made it seem fair to them?" and it was said: "Their partners made it seem fair." The nominative, as stated, is the reading of the majority. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and al-Aʿmash read «عالمِ» in the genitive, and there are three aspects in it. The best of them: it is a badal from the hāʾ in «له». The second: it is a badal from «رب العالمين»; this is far-fetched because of the long separation between the substitute and the thing substituted for. The third: it is an adjective of the hāʾ in «له»; this only works on the view of al-Kisāʾī, since he allows describing a pronoun with a third-person [adjective], and that is weak according to the Basrans and the Kufans other than al-Kisāʾī.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَا تَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ}: «مِنْ آية» is the fāʿil (agent), in which «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) because the two conditions are present, so it has no attachment. «من آيات» is a naʿt (adjective) of «آية», so it is in the position of genitive according to the wording, or of nominative according to the position. The meaning of «مِنْ» is partitive (tabʿīḍ).

His saying: {إِلاَّ كَانُواْ}: this clause with kāna is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). There are two views on the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl). One of them: that it is the pronoun in «تأتيهم»; the second: that it is «من آية», because it has been specified by the qualification. «تأتيهم» may be past in meaning because of His saying «كانوا», and «كانوا» may be future in meaning because of His saying «تأتيهم». Know that a past verb does not occur after «إلا» except under one of two conditions: either its occurring after a verb, as in this noble verse, or its being accompanied by «قد», as in «ما زيدٌ إلا قد قام» (Zayd has done nothing but stand up). Here there is an iltifāt (shift of person) from His addressing them with His saying «خلقكم» and what follows to the third person with His saying «وما تأتيهم».

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فَقَدْ كَذَّبُواْ}: the fāʾ here is for sequence (taʿqīb), meaning that turning away from the signs was followed by denial. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«فقد كذَّبوا» is referred back to an omitted statement, as if it were said: if they are turning away from the signs, then they have denied what is the greatest and mightiest of signs." The Shaykh said: "There is no necessity calling for this, given that the speech is well-ordered." His saying «بالحق» is a case of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, since the original is: «فقد كذَّبوا بها», i.e. with the sign. «الأنباء» is the plural of «نبأ», which is news whose impact is great. There is an omission in the speech, i.e. the content of the tidings will come to them. «به» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the khabar (predicate) of «كانوا». «لمَّا» is a particle of necessitation (ḥarf wujūb) or an adverbial of time, and what governs it is «كَذَّبوا».

«ما» may be a nominal relative, and the pronoun in «به» refers to it. It may be maṣdariyya (infinitival) — Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this — i.e. the tidings of their being mockers; on this view the pronoun does not refer to it, because it is a particle, but refers to «الحق». According to al-Akhfash it refers to it, because in his view it is a noun.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا}: «كم» may be interrogative or declarative (khabariyya), and on both assumptions it suspends (tuʿalliq) the verb of seeing from governing, because the declarative one runs the course of the interrogative in that; and for that reason it was given its rules, such as the necessity of standing at the head of the clause and others. The seeing here is cognitive (ʿilmiyya), and its being visual is weak; on both assumptions it is suspended from governing, because the visual one runs its course. If it is cognitive, then «كم» and what is within its scope stand in the place of two objects; if it is visual, in the place of one.

«كم» may express persons, so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governing element is «أَهْلَكْنا», and «مِنْ قَرْنٍ» on this view is its tamyīz (specification). Or it may express the maṣdar (verbal noun), so it is made accusative as the maṣdar would be by «أهْلَكْنا», i.e. [so many] destructions; and «مِنْ قرن» on this view is a naʿt (adjective) of the object of «أَهْلَكْنا», i.e. We destroyed a people or a troop of the generations, because «قرن» is meant as a plural; «مِنْ» is partitive, and the first [«من», in «مِن قَبْلِهِم»] is for the beginning of the extent. Al-Ḥūfī said: the second «من» is a badal (substitute) of the first «مِنْ»; this is unintelligible, and is a clear delusion. «كم» may also express time, so it is accusative as an adverbial. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its implied form is: how many times did We destroy in them"; and on this view Abū al-Baqāʾ made «من قرن» the mafʿūl bihi, with «مِنْ» redundant in it; that is permissible because the speech is non-affirmative and the genitive is indefinite. However, the Shaykh rejected this on the grounds that in that case the singular would not stand in place of the plural: if you said [«كم أزماناً ضربتُ رجلاً، أو كم مرةً ضربتُ رجلاً» (how many times did I strike a man, or how many times did I strike a man), what is signified by «رجل» would not be "men"], because the question would only be about the number of times or occasions in which you struck; and on the grounds that this is not [a place for the redundancy of «مِنْ», since it is not added in an interrogative] unless it is a pure interrogative or has the meaning of negation, and the interrogative here is not pure, nor is negation intended by it. [End. The answer to what he said: we do not concede that.]

His saying: {مَّكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الأرض}: in the position of genitive as a naʿt of «قَرْن», the pronoun referring to it in the plural in view of its meaning; Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Ḥūfī said this. The Shaykh weakened it on the grounds that «مِنْ قرن» is the tamyīz of «كم», so «كم» is what is spoken about as being destroyed, and so it is what is spoken about as being established, not what comes after it, since «من قرن» runs the course of clarification and is not spoken about. The Shaykh allowed this clause to be resumptive (istiʾnāf), answering an implied question; he said: as if it were said: what was their condition? and it was said: We had established them. He made this the apparent view. There is scrutiny in this, for the indefinite noun needs an adjective, so making it an adjective is more fitting.

The difference between His saying {مَّكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الأرض} [and His saying] «ما لم نمكِّن لكم» is that «مَكَّنه في كذا» means: He set him firmly in it; and of this is:
{وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَاهُمْ فِيمَآ إِن مَّكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ} [al-Aḥqāf: 26]. As for «مكَّن له», its meaning is: He made a place for him; and of this is {إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُ فِي الأرض} [al-Kahf: 84], {أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 57]; and similar to it is «أَرَضَ له», i.e. He made land for him. This is the view of al-Zamakhsharī. As for the Shaykh, it appears from his words that he treats them as equal, for he said: "The verb «مَكَّن» here is made transitive to persons by itself and by a preposition, and more often it is made transitive with the lām: {مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ} [Yūsuf: 21], {إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُ} [al-Kahf: 84], {أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 57]. Abū ʿUbayda said: «مكَّنَّاهم» and «مكَّنَّاهم لهم» [Translator's note: so in the text; the intended form is presumably «مكَّنَّا لهم»] are two eloquent dialectal usages, like «نَصَحْتُه» and «نَصَحْتُ له»." [I say: and this is what] Abū ʿAlī and al-Jurjānī [held].

His saying: {مَا لَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّكُمْ}: there are five aspects regarding this «ما». One of them: that it is a relative meaning "that which", and it is then an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, the implied form being: «التمكين الذي لم نمكِّن لكم» (the establishing which We did not establish for you), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «الذي لم نمكِّنه لكم». The second: that it is an indefinite, an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: «تمكيناً ما لم نمكِّنه لكم»; al-Ḥūfī mentioned both. The Shaykh rejected the first on the grounds that «ما» meaning "that which" is not an adjective of a definite noun, even though «الذي» does occur as its adjective; if you said «ضربت الضرب ما ضَرَبَ زيدٌ», meaning "I struck the striking that Zayd struck", it would not be permissible, but if you said «الضرب الذي ضربه زيد» it would be permissible. And he rejected the second on the grounds that the indefinite «ما» that occurs as an adjective may not have its qualified noun omitted: "if you said «قمت ما وضربت ما», meaning «قمت قياماً ما، وضرباً ما» (I stood some standing, and [struck] some striking), it would not be permissible."

The third: that it is a mafʿūl bihi of «مَكَّن» according to the meaning, because the meaning of «مكَّنَّاهم» is: We gave them what We did not give you; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. The Shaykh said: "This is taḍmīn (implicating one verb with the sense of another), and taḍmīn is not applied by analogy." The fourth: that «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), with the time omitted, i.e. «مدةَ ما لم نمكِّن لكم» (for the period during which We did not establish you), the meaning being: the period of the absence of establishment for you. The fifth: that it is an indefinite qualified by the negated clause after it, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. «شيئاً لم نمكِّنْه لكم» (something We did not establish for you); Abū al-Baqāʾ also mentioned both of these. The Shaykh said about the last: "This is closer to correctness." I say: had Abū al-Baqāʾ assumed it with a specific word, it would have been better than his assuming it with the word «شيء»; he would have said: «مكنَّاهم تمكيناً لم نمكنه لكم» (We established them with an establishing with which We did not establish you).

As for the pronoun in «يروا», it was said that it refers to the mockers, and the address in «لكم» also goes back to them, so on this view it is an iltifāt (shift of person), whose benefit is to allude to how little these were established and how their conditions fell short of the condition of those [earlier ones]: despite their being established and their great number, destruction befell them — so how about you, who are less than them in establishment and number? Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The address in «لكم» is to the believers, to all their contemporaries and to all people universally, as if it were said: what We did not establish for you, O people of this age. It is also possible to assume the sense of saying addressed to these disbelievers, as if He said: O Muhammad, say to them: «ألم يروا كم أهلكنا» to the end of the verse. For when you report that you said — or ordered that something be said — you may, in the eloquent speech of the Arabs, relate the uttered words themselves and so come with the wording of address, and you may come with the meaning in words in the third person rather than address."
End. Its example: «قلت لزيد: ما أكرمك، أو ما أكرمه» (I said to Zayd: how generous you are! — or: how generous he is!).

«القَرْن»: a word applied to many meanings. «القرن» is a community of people, so called because of their being joined together (iqtirān) in a period of time; and of this is his saying, upon him be peace: «خيرُ القرون قرني» (the best of generations is my generation). The poet said:
186 - 4- أُخَبِّرُ أخبارَ القُرونِ التي مَضَتْ ... أَدِبُّ كاني كلما قُمْتُ راكِعُ
(I relate the tidings of the generations that have passed; I creep along as if I were bowing whenever I stand.)
And Quss ibn Sāʿida said:
186 - 5- في الذاهبين الأوَّلِي ... نَ من القرون لنا بصائِرْ
(In those of the first generations who have gone there are lessons for us.)
It was said: its root sense is elevation, and from it is the horn (qarn) of the bull and others; so they were named so because of the rising of age. It was also said: because some of them are joined to others and made assembled with them; and from this is «القَرَن», for the rope with which two camels are tied together. It is also applied to a period of time.

Is its application to people and to time by way of homonymy (ishtirāk), or literal and figurative usage? The preponderant view is the second, because figurative usage is better than homonymy. And if we adopt the preponderant view [as to which] is the literal sense, the apparent one is that it is the people, because it is most often applied to them, and predominance usually indicates originality. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "A qarn is that the elders die and the children are born; this appears from His saying, Exalted is He: {وَأَنْشَأْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْناً آخَرِينَ}." So he made it an abstract meaning, and this is not clear. It was also said: a qarn is people gathered together, whether the years are few or many; and they adduced as evidence his saying, upon him be peace: «خيرُ القرونِ قَرْني», and his [the poet's] saying:
186 - 6- في الذاهبين الأوَّلي ... نَ من القرون لنا بصائرْ
(In those of the first generations who have gone there are lessons for us.)
and his saying:
186 - 7- إذا ذَهَبَ القومُ الذي كنتَ فيهمُ ... وخُلِّفْتَ في قَرْن فأنت غريبُ
(When the people among whom you were have gone, and you are left behind in a [new] generation, then you are a stranger.)
So they applied it to people with the restriction of being gathered together. Then people disagreed about the length of the qarn when it is applied to time. The majority hold that it is a hundred years, and they adduced as evidence his saying, upon him be peace: «يعيش قرناً» (he will live a qarn), and he lived a hundred years. It was said: a hundred and twenty; Iyās ibn Muʿāwiya and Zurāra ibn Abī Awfā [written in the text: «زارة»] said this. It was said: eighty; Ṣāliḥ transmitted it from Ibn ʿAbbās. It was said: seventy; al-Farrāʾ said this. It was said: sixty, because of his saying, upon him be peace: «معترك المنايا ما بين الستين إلى السبعين» (the battleground of deaths is between sixty and seventy). It was said: forty; Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn related it, tracing it back to the Prophet ﷺ, and likewise al-Zahrāwī also traces it back to the Prophet ﷺ. It was said: thirty; al-Naqqāsh related it from Abū ʿUbayda: they held that what is between two qarns is thirty years. It was said: twenty, and this is the opinion of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī. It was said: eighteen years. It was said: it is the average span of the lifetimes of the people of that time; and this was considered good on the grounds that the people of ancient times used to live four hundred years, three hundred, a thousand, more and less.

Some people assumed in His saying, Exalted is He: {كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ} [the word] «أهل», i.e. «أهل قرن» (the people of a qarn), because the qarn is time. There is no need for that, except on the belief that it is literal in [time] and figurative for people, and I have stated before that the preponderant view is the opposite.

His saying: {مَّدْرَاراً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «السماء», if by it the clouds are meant, for clouds are also described as pouring in abundant succession; and likewise if by it the water [rain] is meant. What indicates that the water [rain] is meant by it is his saying in the ḥadīth: «في أثر سماء كانت من الليل» (following a rain [samāʾ] that fell in the night); and they say: «ما نزلنا نطأ السماء حتى أتيناكم» (we kept treading on the rain [samāʾ] until we came to you); and of this is:
186 - 8- إذا نَزَل السماءُ بأرضِ قومٍ ... رَعَيْناه وإن كانوا غضابا
(When the rain [samāʾ] falls on a people's land, we graze it, even if they are angry.)
i.e. we grazed what grows from it. If by it this canopy [the sky] is meant, then a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. «مطر السماء» (the rain of the sky), and «مدراراً» is a ḥāl of it. «مدرار» is of the form mifʿāl, which is for intensiveness, like «امرأة مِذْكار ومِئْناث» (a woman who bears many males / many females). They said: its origin is from «دَرِّ اللبن», which is the abundant flow of milk to the milker; and from it is «لا درَّ درُّه» (may his milk not flow) as an imprecation against him for lack of good. In the proverb: «سبقَتْ دِرَّتُه غِرارَه» (its flow preceded its stoppage) [written in the text: «دِرَّتُ»], which is like their saying: «سبقَ سيلُه مَطَرَه» (its flood preceded its rain). «استدرَّت المِعْزى» (the she-goats sought the flow) is an allusion to their seeking the stud; they said: because when they seek it, they conceive, give birth and give milk.

His saying: {تَجْرِي}: if we make «جَعَلَ» transformative (taṣyīriyya), «تجري» is a second object; if we make it of bringing into existence (ījādiyya), it is a ḥāl. «من تحتهم» allows several aspects: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تجري» — and this is the one from which one should not deviate; that it is a ḥāl, either of the agent of «تجري» or of «الأنهار»; and that it is a second object of «جعلنا», and «تجري» on this view is a ḥāl of the pronoun in the preposition phrase, and there is weakness in this because of its preceding the abstract (maʿnawī) governing element. «من تحتهم» may also be a ḥāl of «الأنهار», as preceded, and «تجري» a ḥāl of the pronoun latent in it, and it has the weakness mentioned before.

His saying: {مِن بَعْدِهِمْ}: attached to «أنشأنا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl of «قرن», because it is an adverbial of time"; he means that, had it come after «قرن», one might have imagined it permissible to be an adjective of it, and since it is placed before it, it might suggest that it is a ḥāl of it; but its being an adverbial of time prevents that, since time is not predicated of bodies nor used to qualify them. It has preceded for you that this is valid with an interpretation that I mentioned in al-Baqara at His saying: {والذين مِن قَبْلِكُمْ} [verse 21]. «آخرين» is a naʿt of «قَرْن», because it is a collective noun like «قوم» and «رهط», and therefore its meaning was taken into account. Whoever says it is time assumes a muḍāf, i.e. «أهل قرن آخرين», and I have stated before that this is the weaker view.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَوْ ترى}: Its answer is omitted because the meaning is understood, the implied form being: "you would have seen something tremendous and a dreadful terror". Omission of the answer is frequent in the Revelation and in verse, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً} [al-Raʿd: 31], and the saying of another:
189 - 0- وجَدِّك لو شيءٌ أتانا رسولُه ... سِواك ولكن لم نَجِدْ لك مَدْفَعا
(By your fortune, had anything other than you sent its messenger to us… but we found no way of repelling you.)
And his saying:
189 - 1- فلو أنها نفسٌ تموتُ جميعةً ... ولكنها نفسٌ تساقَطُ أنفُسَا
(Had it been a soul that dies all at once… but it is a soul that falls away soul by soul.)
And his saying:
189 - 2- كَذَبَ الغواذِلُ لو رَأَيْنَ مُنَاخَنَا ... بحَزيزِ رامةَ والمَطِيُّ سَوَامي
(The blaming women lied — had they seen our halting-place at the rough ground of Rāma, with the mounts raising their heads…)
Omitting the answer is more eloquent; they said: because the listener's mind goes in every direction, whereas if the answer were stated explicitly to him he would steel himself for it and not fear it [much. That is why Kuthayyir said:
189 - 3- فقلتُ لها يا عَزُّ كلُّ مصيبةٍ ... إذا وُطِّنَتْ لها النفسُ ذَلَّتِ]
(So I said to her: O ʿAzza, every calamity, once the soul is steeled for it, becomes light.)
«ترى» may be visual, with its object omitted, i.e. "if you could see their state"; or it may be mental (qalbiyya), the meaning being: if you turned your sound thinking to reflecting on their state, you would increase in certainty.
On this «لو» there are two views. The more apparent: it is the «لو» of impossibility (imtināʿiyya), so the imperfect after it turns to the past; hence «إذ» remains on its original sense of indicating past time. Although this has not yet happened, since it will come on the Day of Resurrection, it is presented in the form of the past because the promise is certain to be fulfilled. The second: it is in the sense of the conditional «إنْ», and «إنْ» here would be in the sense of «إذا»; what led this speaker to that is the fact that it has not yet occurred, and its interpretation has preceded.
The majority read {وُقِفُوا}, built for the object (passive), from the triliteral وقف. «على» may be in its basic sense, which is the apparent view, i.e. they were detained upon it; it has been said it may be in the sense of «في», but that is not strong. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «وَقَفوا», built for the agent (active). «وقف» is both transitive and intransitive, and the Arabs distinguished between them by the maṣdar (verbal noun): the maṣdar of the intransitive is on the pattern فُعول and that of the transitive on فَعْل. One does not say أَوْقَفْتُ. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "I have not heard in the speech of the Arabs أوقفت فلاناً, except that if I saw a man standing and said to him «ما أوقفك ههنا» (what has made you stand here?), that would be good in my view." He only said this because making a verb transitive with the hamza is regular (maqīs), as in ضحك زيد and أضحكته أنا; but others heard أوقفته for the transitive «وقف».
