Al-Rāghib said: "From it — meaning from the expression وَقَفْتُ القومَ — وَقَفْتُ الدابة, in the sense of 'I dedicated it as an endowment (sabbaltuhā)', is borrowed." Thus he made «الوقف» literal in preventing from walking, and figurative, by way of metaphor, in endowment, because the endowed thing is as though prevented from movement. «الوَقْف» is also a word shared between what has preceded and an ivory bracelet; from that is: «حمار مُوَقَّفٌ» (a donkey marked) at its pasterns with something like a bracelet of white.
His saying: {ياليتنا}: Discussion of «يا» directly preceding a particle and a verb has preceded.
Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and al-Kisāʾī read «ولا نُكَذِّبُ» and «نكونُ» with both in the nominative; Ḥamza, from ʿĀṣim [Translator's note: so in the printed text; Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim are meant], read both in the accusative; and Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read the first in the nominative and the second in the accusative. The Shaykh reported from Ibn ʿĀmir that he read both verbs in the accusative, then said after a long discussion: "Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: Ibn ʿĀmir read, in the transmission of Hishām ibn ʿAmmār from his companions from Ibn ʿĀmir: {ولا نكذِّبُ} in the nominative and «نكون» in the accusative."
As for the reading with both in the nominative, there are three views on it. The first: the nominative in both is by conjunction to the verb before them, namely «نُرَدُّ», so they wished for three things: return to the abode of this world, not denying the signs of their Lord, and being among the believers. The second: the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial), the imperfect is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the nominative pronoun of «نُرَدُّ»; the implied form: "would that we were returned, not denying and being among the believers"; so the wish for return is restricted by these two states, and the two verbs are thus also included in the wish.
People found these two views problematic: wishing is inshāʾ (non-declarative speech), and inshāʾ admits neither truth nor falsehood — these only apply to statements (khabar) — yet falsehood has entered this, because of His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ}. They answered this in three ways. The first, mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī, who said: "This is a wish that includes the meaning of a promise, so it may admit of being called a lie, just as a man says: 'Would that Allah granted me wealth, so that I might be good to you and reward you for your kindness.' This is one who wishes in the sense of one who promises; if he were granted wealth and did not do good to his friend or reward him, he would have lied, and it would be correct to call him a liar, as if he had said: 'If Allah grants me wealth, I will be good to you.'"
The second: His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ} is not connected with what was wished for; rather it is a pure statement from Allah the Exalted that lying is their habit and their constant practice, so falsehood did not enter the wish. These two answers are clear, and the second of them is clearer.
The third: we do not concede that a wish admits neither truth nor falsehood; rather it admits them. This was attributed to ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, who argued for it with the poet's saying:
189 - 4- مُنَىً إن تكن حقاً يكنْ أحسنَ المنى ... وإلاَّ فقد عِشنا بها زمناً رغْدا
(Hopes — if they are true, they are the finest of hopes; otherwise, we have lived by them a time of ease.)
He said: "If hopes may be described as being true, they may be described as being false and lies." This answer is utterly worthless, for what is described as true is «المنى», and «المُنى» is the plural of مُنْيَة; the مُنْيَة may be described with truth and falsehood figuratively, because it is as though it promises the soul that it will come to pass, so of what comes to pass of it one says "true", and of what does not, "false". So truth and falsehood only entered the مُنْيَة (the hoped-for thing), not the act of wishing.
The third of the previously mentioned views: His saying «ولا نكذِّبُ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), with no connection to what precedes it. These two verbal clauses were only conjoined to the clause containing the particle of wishing and what is in its scope; they are not included in the wish at all. Rather, Allah the Exalted reported of them that they stated about themselves that they would not deny the signs of their Lord and that they would be among the believers. So this clause and what is conjoined to it are in the position of the accusative as the object of saying, as if the implied form were: "so they said: would that we were returned; and they said: we will not deny and we will be among the believers". Sībawayh chose this view and likened it to their saying «دعني ولا أعودُ» (leave me, and I will not do it again), i.e. "and I will not do it again whether you leave me or not", i.e. I will not return in any case. Likewise the meaning of the verse: they stated that they would not deny the signs of their Lord and that they would be among the believers in any case, whether they were returned or not.
Although people have mentioned this view and preferred it, and Sībawayh chose it — as has passed — some found a difficulty in it, namely: lying does not occur in the Hereafter, so how are they described as lying in the Hereafter in their saying «ولا نكذِّب ونكون»? It has been answered in two ways. The first: His saying {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ} is a confirmation of their being blamed for lying, and that this is their habit, as was stated just above. The second: in that state they were resolved that, if they were returned, they would not go back to disbelief, because of the terrors and punishments they had witnessed; so Allah the Exalted reported that their saying in that state, «ولا نكذِّبُ», even though it came from conviction and resolve, would change on the supposition of their being returned and their actually going back; so their saying «ولا نكذب» would become a lie — just as a thief says under the pain of punishment "I will not do it again", believes it and resolves on it, and then, when released and he returns to it, he is a liar.
[Makkī also answered with two answers, the first of which] is close to what has preceded, and the second belongs to others. He said: "That is: liars in this world, in their denying the messengers and their rejecting the resurrection, in the state they were in. Abū ʿAmr and others permitted that the lying took place in the Hereafter, because they claimed that if they were returned they would not deny the signs of Allah; but Allah knew of what will not be how it would be if it were, and that if they were returned they would not believe and would deny the signs of Allah; so Allah declared them liars in their claim."
As for the accusative in both, it is by an implied «أَنْ» after the wāw that means «مع» (with), as in your saying «ليت لي مالاً وأنفقَ منه» (would that I had wealth and could spend from it). The verb is accusative by an implied «أن», and «أنْ» is maṣdariyya (infinitival): from it and the verb after it an interpreted maṣdar is formed. The wāw is a conjunction, so it requires something to be conjoined to; but there is nothing before it in the verse except a verb — so how can a noun be conjoined to a verb? Necessarily, then, we assume an imagined maṣdar to which this maṣdar formed from «أَنْ» and what follows it is conjoined. The implied form: "would that we had a return, and absence of denial of the signs of our Lord, and being among the believers", i.e. would that we had a return together with these two things. So not denying and being among the believers are also wished for; these three things — I mean return, not denying, and being among the believers — are wished for on condition of their being together, not that each one is wished for on its own; because, as I explained to you before, the condition of this wāw for implying «أنْ» after it is that «مع» could fit in its place. So the accusative specifies one of its possible meanings in your saying «لا تأكلِ السمك وتشرب اللبن» (do not eat fish while drinking milk) and the like. The difficulty mentioned before — namely ascribing lying to a wish — applies here, and its answer has preceded; but part of that answer is impossible here, namely that «لا نكذِّبُ» and «نكونُ» are two resumptive clauses brought for mere statement. What remains is: either that the wish has had the meaning of a promise enter it, or that His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ} does not refer back to their wish, or that a wish admits being called a lie — and the invalidity of that has preceded.
Ibn al-Anbārī said: "He declared them liars in the meaning of the wish, because their wish amounts to the meaning: we will not deny if we are returned. So He, Mighty and Majestic, gave precedence to the interpretation of the speech and declared them liars, and the wording of wishing was not used." The meaning of what Ibn al-Anbārī said has preceded in a clearer form than this. The Shaykh said: "It is often found in grammar books that the verb in the accusative after this wāw is as the answer to the wish, as al-Zamakhsharī said: 'It has been read ولا نكذِّبَ ونكونَ in the accusative, by an implied أَنْ, as the answer to the wish; its meaning is: if we are returned we will not deny and will be among the believers.'" He said: "It is not as he mentioned, for the accusative of the verb after the wāw is not by way of an answer, because the wāw does not occur [in] the answer of a condition, so neither from what precedes it nor from what follows it is a condition and answer formed. It is only the wāw of «مع», by which what follows it is conjoined to the imagined maṣdar before it. It is the wāw of conjunction, one of whose three possible senses is specified by the accusative, namely accompaniment; and what distinguishes it from the fāʾ is the supposition of «مع» in its place, just as the fāʾ of the answer, when followed by an accusative verb, is distinguished by the supposition of a condition before it or a ḥāl in its place. The confusion of whoever said it is an answer is that it puts in the accusative in the places where the fāʾ does, so he imagined it to be an answer. Sībawayh said: 'The wāw puts what follows it in the accusative, in the non-affirmative, in the same way that what follows the fāʾ is put in the accusative; but the wāw and the fāʾ differ in meaning. Do you not see:
189 - 5- لا تَنْهَ عن خلق وتأتيَ مثله ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Do not forbid a trait while doing the like of it yourself…)
— if the fāʾ entered here it would spoil the meaning; he only meant: do not combine forbidding and doing. And you say «لا تأكلِ السمكَ وتشربَ اللبن»; if you put the fāʾ in, the meaning would be spoiled.'" The Shaykh said: "What makes clear to you that it is not an answer is that the fāʾ, unlike it, has the peculiarity that when it is dropped the verb after it becomes jussive by what precedes it, because of the sense of condition that what precedes contains — except in negation, where that is not permissible." I say: Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj, the master of the group, preceded al-Zamakhsharī in this wording. Abū Isḥāq said: "It is accusative as an answer with the wāw in a wish, as you say «ليتك تصير إلينا ونكرمَك» (would that you came to us and we honoured you); the meaning: would that your coming and our honouring occurred; and the meaning [here] is: would that our return occurred and that we did not deny."
As for the wāw not being in the sense of the fāʾ, that is correct; the majority of grammarians hold it. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «إلى أني», evidently for «إلا أني», "except that".] However, I saw that Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī explained the accusative in two ways, one of them being that the wāw is in the sense of the fāʾ. Abū Bakr said: "In the accusative of «نكذِّبَ» there are two views. The first: the wāw is substituted for the fāʾ, the implied form being: would that we were returned, so that we would not deny and would be; the wāw here is thus in the position of the fāʾ in His saying {لَوْ أَنَّ لِي كَرَّةً فَأَكُونَ مِنَ المحسنين} [al-Zumar: 58]. This is confirmed by the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn Abī Isḥāq: «يا ليتنا نردُّ فلا نكذبَ», with the fāʾ and in the accusative. The other view: the accusative is by ṣarf (diversion), whose meaning is the ḥāl, i.e. would that we were returned, not denying."
As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir — with the first nominative and the second accusative — it is clear from what has preceded: the first is nominative according to the interpretations already given, and likewise the accusative of the second is explained by what has preceded; he would then have either included not denying in the wish or made it resumptive. However, the accusative verb may belong to the completion of His saying «نُرَدُّ», i.e. they wished for return together with being among the believers; this is clear if we make «ولا نكذِّب» conjoined to «نردُّ» or a ḥāl from it. If we make «ولا نكذِّبُ» resumptive, this is also permissible, but by way of a parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ). It may also belong to the completion of «ولا نكذِّب», i.e. there will be no denial from us together with our being among the believers; His saying «ولا نكذب» would then be as it was, I mean with its possibilities of conjunction to «نُرَدُّ», of being a ḥāl, or of being resumptive. It is not hidden, then, how their being among the believers enters into the wish or stays out of it, according to what I have set out for you.
It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, the reverse of Ibn ʿĀmir's reading, i.e. with «نكذبَ» accusative and «نكون» nominative. Its explanation is according to what has preceded, except that in it making «ونكونُ من المؤمنين» a ḥāl is weak, since it is an affirmative imperfect, except with a far-fetched interpretation, as in his saying:
189 - 6-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نَجَوْتُ وأَرْهَنُهم مالكاً
(…I escaped, leaving Mālik with them as a pledge.)
i.e. "while I pledged Mālik to them", and their saying «قمتُ وأصكُّ عينه» (I stood up, striking his eye). What indicates the omission of this mubtadaʾ is the reading of Ubayy: «ونحن نكونُ من المؤمنين».

semin-durr:96-96.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَالِقُ الإصباح}: like His words «فالق الحب» in what preceded. The majority read the hamza with kasra, and it is the maṣdar (verbal noun); one says: aṣbaḥa yuṣbiḥu iṣbāḥan. Al-Layth and al-Zajjāj said that al-ṣubḥ, al-ṣabāḥ and al-iṣbāḥ are one, and they are the beginning of the day; likewise al-Farrāʾ. And it was said: al-iṣbāḥ is the light of the sun by day and the light of the moon by night; Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related it from Ibn ʿAbbās. And it was said: it is the shining of the dawn; that was transmitted from Mujāhid. The apparent view is that al-iṣbāḥ was originally a maṣdar by which the morning was named, and likewise al-imsāʾ. Imruʾ al-Qays said: 2005 - ألا أيها الليلُ الطويلُ ألا انْجَلِ ... بصبحٍ وما الإِصباح منك بأمثلِ
(O long night, will you not clear away into morning — though the morning is no better than you.)
Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read: «الأصباح» with fatḥa of the hamza, and it is the plural of ṣubḥ, like qufl and aqfāl, and burd and abrād. And his saying is recited:
2006 - أفنى رياحاً وبني رياحِ ... تناسخُ الأمساءِ والأصباح
(The succession of evenings and mornings has annihilated Riyāḥ and the sons of Riyāḥ.)
with fatḥa of the hamza in الأمساء and الأصباح, as plurals of musy and ṣubḥ, and with its kasra, as two maṣdars. And it was read/ «فالقُ الإِصباحَ» with the accusative of الإِصباح, and that is by dropping the tanwīn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, like his saying:
2007 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا ذاكرَ اللهَ إلا قليلا
(… nor one who remembers Allah save a little.)
And {والمقيمي الصلاة} [al-Ḥajj: 35] and {لَذَآئِقُو العذاب} [al-Ṣāffāt: 38] were read with the accusative, treating the nūn like the tanwīn; except that Sībawayh does not permit dropping the tanwīn for the meeting of two quiescents except in poetry, while al-Mubarrad permitted it in ordinary speech. Yaḥyā, al-Nakhaʿī and Abū Ḥaywa read: «فلق» as a past verb; and it has preceded that ʿAbd Allāh read the first one likewise. This is the clearest proof that the reading for them was a followed sunna (an established, transmitted practice): do you not see how ʿAbd Allāh read «فلق الحب» as a past verb and read «فالق الأَصباح» as an active participle, while the three mentioned did the reverse? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of splitting the morning, when it is the darkness that is split away from the morning, as he said:
2008 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَفَرِّيَ ليلٍ عن بياض نهار
(… like the night splitting away from the whiteness of day.)
I say: there are two aspects in it. One of them: that what is meant is 'the splitter of the darkness of the morning'" — meaning that it is by omission of a muḍāf (first term of a construct) — "The second: that what is meant is the splitter of the morning, which is the pillar of dawn, from the whiteness of the day and its brightening. They said: the pillar of dawn split and cracked; and they named the dawn falaq in the sense of 'split' (mafrūq). Al-Ṭāʾī said:
2009 - وأزرقُ الفجر يبدو قبل أبيضه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The blue of dawn appears before its white …)
And «فالق» and «جاعل» were read with the accusative by way of praise." End of quote. Someone else recited:
2010 - فانشقَّ عنها عمودُ الفَجْرِ جافلةً ... عَدْوَ النَّحوص تخافُ القانِصَ اللَّحِما
(The pillar of dawn split open from her as she fled in alarm, running like the barren she-ass fearing the meat-hungry hunter.)
His words: {وَجَاعِلَ الليل}: The Kufans read «جعل» as a past verb, and the rest in the form of the active participle; the written form (rasm) allows both. الليل is accusative for the Kufans by the requirement of their reading, and genitive for the others. The justification of their reading it as a verb is its fit with what follows, for after it come past verbs such as {جَعَلَ لَكُمُ النجوم} [al-Anʿām: 97], {وَهُوَ الذي أَنشَأَكُم} [al-Anʿām: 98], to the end of the verses. And «سكناً» would be either a second object, on the view that al-jaʿl means "making into", or a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the view that it means "creating", and the ḥāl would be a projected one (muqaddara).
As for the reading of the others, جاعل may be in the sense of the past, and that is the apparent sense, supported by the reading of the Kufans. According to the Basrans, the past [active participle] does not govern except with al- — contrary to some of them who forbid the governing of the one made definite by it, and to al-Kisāʾī who [allows] its governing absolutely. When that is established, «سَكَناً» is accusative by an implied verb according to the Basrans, and on the requirement of al-Kisāʾī's school it [the participle] makes it accusative. Abū Saʿīd al-Sīrāfī claimed that the active participle transitive to two objects may govern the second even if it is past; he said: "Because when it is put in construct with the first, its being put in construct with the second becomes impossible, so its making it accusative is required." And some of them said: "Because by the iḍāfa it came to resemble that which is made definite by al-, so it governs absolutely." On this view «سكناً» is also accusative by it. And if we say that it is in the sense of the present or the future, then its being accusative is by it. And «سَكَنٌ» is [on the pattern] faʿal in the sense of a passive participle, like al-qabaḍ in the sense of maqbūḍ.
His words: {والشمس والقمر حُسْبَاناً}: The majority read «الشمس» and «القمر» in the accusative, and it is clear on the reading of the Kufans, i.e. by conjoining these two accusatives to the two accusatives of «جعل», and «حُسْباناً» has the two aspects of «سكناً»: second object or ḥāl. As for the reading of the majority, if we hold it [جاعل] to be past, then a verb must be implied that makes them accusative, i.e. وجعل الشمس. And if we say it is not past, then the school of Sībawayh too is that the accusative is by an implied verb; you say: «هذا ضاربُ زيدٍ الآن أو غداً أو عمراً» with عمرو in the accusative, by an implied verb, not according to the position of the noun made genitive by the active participle. In the opinion of others, the accusative is according to the position of the genitive noun. They recite his saying: /
2011 - هل أنت باعثُ دينارٍ لحاجتنا ... أو عبدَ رَبٍّ أخاعَوْن بن مِخْراقِ
(Will you send Dīnār for our need, or ʿAbd Rabb, the brother of ʿAwn ibn Mikhrāq?)
with «عبد» in the accusative, and it admits both schools. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or they are conjoined to the position of «الليل». If you say: how can «الليل» have a position, when the iḍāfa is real, because the active participle in construct with it is in the sense of the past, and you do not say: زيدٌ ضاربٌ عمراً أمس? I say: it is not in the sense of the past; it only indicates an action continuous across times."
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "As for his statement 'it only indicates an action continuous across times', he means that it would then govern, and the genitive noun after it would then have a position, so «الشمس والقمر» is conjoined to it." He said: "This is not correct: if it is not restricted to a particular time but is only for continuity, then it may not govern, nor does its genitive noun have a position. They have stated this explicitly and recited for it:
2012 - أَلْقَيْتَ كاسبهم في قَعْرِ مُظْلِمَةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(You threw their earner into the depth of a dark [pit] …)
For the earner here is not restricted to a time. And if it is restricted to a time, then either it is past without al-, so it does not govern according to the Basrans; or with al-, or present or future, so it governs and is put in construct, as is established in grammar." Then he said: "Even granting that the one denoting continuity governs, conjoining to the position of its genitive noun is not permissible; indeed the school of Sībawayh regarding the one in the sense of the present and future is that conjoining to the position of its genitive noun is not permissible, but rather the accusative is by an implied verb. If you said: هذا ضارب زيدٍ وعمراً, the accusative of «عمراً» would not be according to the position, on the correct view, which is the school of Sībawayh, because the condition of conjoining to the position is lacking, namely that the position should have a fixed holder (muḥriz) that does not change. This is explained in the science of grammar."
I say: al-Zamakhsharī mentioned at the beginning of al-Fātiḥa, on {مالك يَوْمِ الدين} [al-Fātiḥa: 4], that since no time is intended by it, its iḍāfa became pure, and therefore it occurred as an adjective of definite nouns. It follows necessarily from his statement that it becomes definite by the iḍāfa that it does not govern, because the governing one is intended as separated from the iḍāfa, and whenever it is intended as separated it is indefinite, and whenever it is indefinite it does not occur as an adjective of a definite noun. This [objection] is good, since it refutes him with his own words; the verification of this has preceded in al-Fātiḥa.
Abū Ḥaywa read: {وَالشَّمْسِ والقَمَرِ} in the genitive, conjoined to the wording. And it was read anomalously (shādhdhan) {والشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ} in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); by rights he should have read «حسبانٌ» in the nominative as the khabar (predicate), but he read it in the accusative, so the khabar is then omitted, its implied form being: "made as a reckoning" or "created as a reckoning". If you say: in this reading it is not possible to put «حسبان» in the nominative so that we could oblige the reader to do so, because the sun and the moon are not themselves the reckoning — the answer is that in the accusative reading they are either first objects with «حسْباناً» the second, or the owners of a ḥāl with حسباناً the ḥāl; and the second object is the first [in reference], and the ḥāl must be true of the owner of the ḥāl. So whatever answer you have, we have the same, and the answer is evident from what preceded.
Regarding al-ḥusbān there are two views. One of them: that it is a plural; it was said: the plural of ḥisāb, like rikāb and rukbān, and shihāb and shuhbān; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayd, al-Akhfash, Abū al-Haytham and al-Mubarrad. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is the plural of ḥusbāna", and this is a mistake, because al-ḥusbāna is a piece of fire, and that is certainly not what is meant. And it was said: rather it is a maṣdar, like al-ruḥjān, al-nuqṣān and al-khusrān, while al-ḥisāb is a noun, not a maṣdar; this is the view of Ibn al-Sikkīt. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And al-ḥusbān with ḍamma is the maṣdar of ḥasabtu" — meaning with fatḥa — "just as al-ḥisbān with kasra" — meaning — "is the maṣdar of ḥasibtu with kasra; its parallel is al-kufrān and al-shukrān." And it was said: rather al-ḥusbān and al-ḥisāb are both maṣdars; this is the view of Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab].
Abū ʿUbayd recited from Abū Zayd, regarding al-ḥusbān occurring as a maṣdar, his saying:
2013 - على الله حُسْباني إذا النفسُ أشرفَتْ ... على طمعٍ أو خاف شيئاً ضميرُها
(Upon Allah is my reckoning when the soul looks out upon some desire, or its heart fears something.)
And «حسباناً» is accusative according to what preceded: as object or as ḥāl. Thaʿlab said, from al-Akhfash: it is accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the implied form being: they run by a reckoning, like His words {لِمَنْ خَلَقْتَ طِيناً} / i.e. from clay. And His words «ذلك» are a reference to what preceded of the splitting or the making, or all that preceded of the predicates in His words «فالق الحَبِّ» up to «حُسْبانا».

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فِي قِرْطَاسٍ}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element, as a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب», whether by «كتاب» the maṣdar (verbal noun) is meant or the written thing. It may also be attached to «كتاباً» itself, whether the maṣdar or the written thing is meant by it. An instance of «الكتاب» coming in the sense of «مكتوب» (something written) is his saying:
186 - 9-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . صحيفةً ... أَتَتْكَ من الحَجَّاج يُتْلى كتابُها
(… a sheet that came to you from al-Ḥajjāj, whose writing is being recited.)
There is some reservation in the mind about making «كتاباً» in the noble verse a maṣdar, because writing itself is not described as being sent down except through a far-fetched figurative usage; but they have said it here. «في قرطاس» may also be attached to «نَزَّلْنا».

«القِرْطاس»: the sheet on which one writes, made of parchment or paper; with kasra and ḍamma on the qāf, the kasra being the eloquent form, and it was read with ḍamma as an irregular (shādhdh) reading; Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted it. «القِرْطاس» is an arabicised foreign noun, and it is called «قرطاس» only when it has writing on it; otherwise it is «طِرْس» and «كاغَد». Zuhayr said:
187 - 0- لها أخاديدُ مِنْ آثارِ ساكنها ... كما تردَّدَ في قِرْطاسِه القلمُ
(It has furrows from the traces of its inhabitants, as the pen goes back and forth over its sheet.)

His saying: {فَلَمَسُوهُ}: the accusative pronoun may refer to «القِرْطاس», or to «كتاب» in the sense of something written. «بأيديهم» is attached to «لَمَسَ», and the bāʾ is for seeking aid (istiʿāna), as in «عملت بالقَدُوم» (I worked with the adze). «لقال» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو», coming according to the more eloquent usage of joining its affirmative apodosis with the lām.

His saying: {إِنْ هاذآ}: «إنْ» is negative, «هذا» a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «إلا سحرٌ» its khabar (predicate); so it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). The negated clause is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying. He put the overt noun in place of the pronoun in His saying «لقال الذين كفروا» as testimony against them of disbelief. The counterfactual clause (al-jumla al-imtināʿiyya) is a clause with no grammatical position, because it is resumptive.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {وَقَالُواْ لولا}: the apparent view is that this clause is resumptive, brought to report about them their excessive obstinacy and rigidity in their disbelief. It was said: it may also be conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو», i.e. had We sent down to you a book, they would have said such-and-such, and they would have said: «لولا أُنْزِل عليه مَلَك»; the apodosis being brought according to one of the two permissible forms, I mean omitting the lām from the affirmative. There is remoteness in this, because their saying «لولا أُنْزل» is not consequent upon His saying {وَلَوْ أَنزَلْنَا}. «لولا» here is for urging (taḥḍīḍ). As for the pronoun in «عليه», the apparent view is that it refers to the Prophet ﷺ. It was said: it may refer to the book or the sheet, the meaning being: why was not an angel sent down upon the book, to testify to its truth? — as it is narrated in the story that it was said to him: we will not believe until you ascend and bring a book, with four angels accompanying it testifying. This is evident on the opinion of those who say that the clause from His saying {وقالوا: لولا أُنْزل} is conjoined to the apodosis of «لو», for it is then connected to it in terms of meaning.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {مَّا يَلْبِسُونَ}: there are two views on «ما». One of them: that it is a relative meaning "that which", i.e. and We would have confused for them what they confuse for themselves or for others; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and «ما» is then a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The second: that it is maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e. and We would have confused for them just as they confuse for others and lead them along. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «ولَبَسْنا» with a single lām, which is the first radical of the verb, and did not bring a lām in the apodosis, being content with it in what it is conjoined to. Al-Zuhrī read «ولَلَبَّسْنا» with two lāms and a doubled verb, for multiplicity.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَقَدِ استهزىء}: Ḥamza, ʿĀṣim and Abū ʿAmr read it with kasra on the dāl, according to the basic rule for the meeting of two vowelless letters; the rest [read it] with ḍamma by harmonisation (itbāʿ), the vowelless letter not being taken into account because it is a barrier that is not impregnable. I have established this rule with its proofs in al-Baqara at His saying: {فَمَنِ اضطر} [verse 173]. «برسلٍ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «استهزئ», and «مِنْ قبلك» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسل»; its interpretation is what preceded regarding «من قبل» occurring as a ṣila (relative clause).

His saying: {فَحَاقَ بالذين سَخِرُواْ}: the fāʿil (agent) of «حاق» is «ما كانوا». «ما» may be a nominal relative, the returning pronoun being the hāʾ in «به»; «به» is attached to «يستهزئون», and «يستهزئون» is the khabar (predicate) of «كان». «منهم» is attached to «سخروا», on the view that the pronoun refers to the messengers; the Exalted said: {إِن تَسْخَرُواْ مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسْخَرُ مِنكُمْ} [Hūd: 38]; and it may be made transitive with the bāʾ, as in «سَخِرْت به». «منهم» may also be attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of «سَخِروا», the pronoun in «منهم» referring to those who mocked. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "to the mockers (al-mustahziʾīn)", and al-Ḥūfī said: "to the nations of the messengers."

The Shaykh rebutted al-Ḥūfī on the grounds that it entails referring it to something not mentioned; the answer to this is that it is equivalent to what is mentioned. He rebutted Abū al-Baqāʾ on the grounds that the meaning would become: then there encompassed those who mocked, being of the mockers — and there is no need for this ḥāl, because it is understood from His saying «سخروا». They also allowed «ما» to be maṣdariyya (infinitival); the Shaykh mentioned it and did not address the pronoun in «به». What appears is that it refers to the messenger contained in the plural, as if it were said: then the consequence of their mocking the messenger included in the totality of the messengers encompassed them. As for the opinion of al-Akhfash and Ibn al-Sarrāj, it refers to the maṣdariyya «ما», because in their view it is a noun.

«حاق»: its alif is changed from a yāʾ, as evidenced by «يَحِيق», like «باع يبيع». The maṣdar is «حَيْق», «حُيُوق» and «حَيَقان», like «الغَلَيان» and «النَّزَوان». Some claimed that it is from «الحَوْق», which is what encircles a thing, and some that it is from «الحقّ», one of the two qāfs having been changed into yāʾ, as in «تظنَّنْتُ» [→ «تظنَّيت»]. These two are worthless: as for the first, because of the difference of root, unless they mean the greater derivation (al-ishtiqāq al-akbar); as for the second, because it is a bare claim without proof. The meaning of «حاق» is: encompassed. It was said: the evil consequence of his plotting returned upon him; al-Farrāʾ said this. It was said: it turned around [upon them]. The meaning revolves around encompassing and comprehensiveness, and it is used only of evil. The poet said:
187 - 1- فأوطأ جُرْدُ الخيلِ عُقْرَ ديارهمْ ... وحاقَ بهم من بأسِ ضَبَّةَ حائقُ
(The short-haired horses trampled the heart of their abodes, and an encompassing [blow] of the might of Ḍabba encompassed them.)
Al-Rāghib said: "It was said: its origin is «حَقَّ», and it was changed, as in «زلَّ» and «زال»; and it has been read: «فأزلَّهما» and «فأزالهما» [written in the text: «وأزلَهما»]; and on this pattern are «ذمَّه» and «ذامه»." Al-Azharī said: "Abū Isḥāq made «حاق» mean «أحاط» (encompassed), and it is as though he derived it from «الحَوْق», which is what encircles the glans." He said: "It is possible that «الحَوْق» is a fuʿl form from «حاق يحيق», as if it were originally «حُيْق», the yāʾ being changed into wāw because of the ḍamma before it." Is there a need to assume a muḍāf before «ما كانوا»? Al-Wāḥidī transmitted that from most of the exegetes, i.e. "the punishment of what they used to…" or "the recompense of what they used to…"; then he said: "This is if you make «ما» express the Qurʾān, the sharīʿa, and what the Prophet ﷺ brought. But if you make «ما» express the punishment with which he ﷺ used to threaten them if they did not believe, you dispense with assuming the muḍāf, and the meaning is: then the punishment which they used to mock and deny encompassed them."

«السُّخْرِيَّة»: mocking and derision. One says «سَخِر منه» and «سَخِر به»; but one says only «استهزأ به» [written in the text: «استهزاءً به»], so it is not made transitive with «مِنْ». Al-Rāghib said: "«سَخَرْتُهُ» is when you subject him (sakhkhartahu) to ridicule. One says «رجل سُخَرَة», with fatḥa on the khāʾ, when he mocks others, and «سُخْرة», with it vowelless, when he is mocked; and similarly «ضُحَكة» and «ضُحْكة»; and it is not applied by analogy. His saying: {فاتخذتموهم سِخْرِيّاً} [al-Muʾminūn: 110] may be from «التسخير» (subjugation) or from «السُّخْرية» (mockery)." It has been read «سُخرياً» and «سِخرياً», with ḍamma and kasra on the sīn. Further explanation of it will come in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {ثُمَّ انظروا}: conjoined to «سيروا». In the Qurʾān, conjunction in a place like this has come only with the fāʾ, but here it came with «ثم», so a distinction is needed. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned the distinction, namely: that He made the looking caused by the travelling in His saying {فانظروا} [written in the text: {انظروا}], as if it were said: "Travel for the sake of looking, and do not travel the travelling of the heedless"; whereas here its meaning is the permission to travel in the land for trade and other benefits, and the obligation of looking at the traces of those destroyed; and He drew attention to that with «ثم» because of the distance between the obligatory and the permissible.

The Shaykh said: "What he mentioned first is self-contradictory, because he made the looking caused by the travelling, so the travelling is the cause of the looking; then he said: so it is as though it were said: travel for the sake of looking, thus making the travelling the effect of the looking, with the looking its cause — so they contradict each other. And the claim that the fāʾ is causal is a claim with no proof; its meaning is only sequence (taʿqīb). As for «زنى ماعِزٌ فَرُجم» (Māʿiz committed adultery, so he was stoned), the causality is understood from a contextual indication other than it." He said: "And on the assumption that it is conceded that it conveys causation, why is the travelling here a travelling of permission and in the other [places] a travelling of obligation?" I say: this is a valid objection, except for his saying "the fāʾ does not convey causality", for that is not acceptable, and its proof is in another place than this. Similar to this place, in that al-Zamakhsharī made something a cause and then made it an effect, is what will come, if Allah wills, at the beginning of al-Fatḥ, and its answer will come there.

His saying: {كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ}: «كيف» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «عاقبة» is its noun [the noun of kāna]. Its verb was not made feminine because its femininity is non-real, and because it is in the sense of «المآل» and «المنتهى» (the outcome, the end); for «العاقبة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern of fāʿila, which is preserved in words whose mention has preceded; it is the end of a thing and what it comes to. «العاقبة», when used absolutely, is specific to reward; the Exalted said: {والعاقبة لِلْمُتَّقِينَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 128]. With annexation it is sometimes used of punishment, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {ثُمَّ كَانَ عَاقِبَةَ الذين أَسَاءُواْ السواأى} [al-Rūm: 10], {فَكَانَ عَاقِبَتَهُمَآ أَنَّهُمَا فِي النار} [al-Ḥashr: 17]; so it is valid for it to be a borrowing from its opposite, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 21]. «كيف» suspends (tuʿalliq) the [verb of] looking, and is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition (ʿalā isqāṭ al-khāfiḍ), because its meaning here is reflecting and contemplating.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بَغْتَةً}: There are four views on its accusative. The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the fāʿil (agent) of «جاءَتْهم», i.e. "taking them by surprise", or from its object, i.e. "being taken by surprise". The second: it is a maṣdar not from the verb's own root, because the meaning of «جاءتهم» is "it took them suddenly", so it is like their saying «أتيته رَكْضاً» (I came to him at a gallop). The third: it is accusative by an omitted verb of its own wording, i.e. "it surprises them suddenly". The fourth: by a verb not of its own wording, i.e. "it came to them suddenly".
البَغْت and البَغْتة mean a thing coming upon one swiftly, without one reckoning with it or paying attention to it; so that if a person sensed it beforehand and then it came to him swiftly, it would not be called بَغْتة. That is why the poet said:
189 - 8- إذا بَغَتَتْ أشياءُ قد كان قبلها ... قديماً فلا تَعْتَدَّها بَغَتَاتِ
(When things come suddenly that were long foreshadowed before them, do not count them as surprises.)
The alif-lām in «الساعة» is for predominance (ghalaba), as in النجم and الثريا, because it has become predominantly used for the Day of Resurrection. The Resurrection was called «ساعة» (an hour) because of the swiftness of the reckoning in it for the Creator, the Exalted. His saying «قالوا» is the answer of «إذا».
His saying: {ياحسرتنا}: This is figurative (majāz), because regret cannot come forward [when called]; the meaning is only hyperbole in the intensity of grieving, as if they called out to regret and said: if you have a time, this is the time for your presence. Like it is «يا ويلتا». The aim is to draw attention to the error of the caller, in that he abandoned what, by abandoning it, made him need to call out to these things.
His saying: {على مَا فَرَّطْنَا} is attached to «الحسرة», and «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e. "for our neglect". The pronoun in «فيها» may refer to the Hour, and a muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "in its matter and in belief in it"; or it may refer to the bargain implied in His saying {قَدْ خَسِرَ الذين} — al-Ḥasan said this; or it may refer to the worldly life, even though it has not [been] mentioned, since it is known — al-Zamakhsharī said this. It has also been said: it refers to their dwellings in Paradise when they see them [Translator's note: printed «مازلهم», evidently for «منازلهم»]; this is far-fetched.
التفريط is falling short in a thing while being able to do it. Abū ʿUbayd said: "It is squandering." Ibn Baḥr said: "It is going ahead; from it is الفارط, i.e. the one who goes ahead of the people. So the meaning of فرَّط with doubling is: he left the going ahead to someone else; the doubling in it is for privation (salb), as in جلَّدْتُ البعير (I skinned the camel), and from it is {فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نَافِلَةً} [al-Isrāʾ: 79]."
His saying: {وَهُمْ يَحْمِلُونَ}: the wāw is of the ḥāl, and the one it describes is the wāw in «قالوا», i.e. they said «يا حَسْرَتَنا» while carrying their burdens. This clause was headed by a pronoun as mubtadaʾ (subject) so that it is mentioned twice, which is more eloquent. As for carrying here, it has been said that it is figurative for their suffering the punishment caused by the burdens; and it has been said that it is literal. In the ḥadīth: "His deed is represented to him in an ugly, foul-smelling form, and he carries it." The back was singled out because it can bear loads that other limbs, such as the head and the shoulders, cannot — just as preceded in {فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ} [al-Anʿām: 7], because the hand is stronger in tactile perception than other parts.
الأوزار is the plural of وِزْر, like حِمْل and أَحْمال, عِدْل and أعدال.
الوِزْر originally means weight; from it is وَزِرْتُهُ, i.e. I made him carry something heavy. The king's vizier (وزير) is from this, because he bears the burdens that the king has charged him with of providing for his subjects and his retinue. From it also is أوزار الحرب for its weapons and equipment; the poet said:
189 - 9- وأعدَدْتُ للحرب أوزارَها ... رماحاً طِوالاً وخيلاً ذُكورا
(And I prepared for war its burdens: long spears and stallion horses.) [Translator's note: the printed rhyme word is «ذُكروا»; «ذكورا» is evidently meant.]
It has also been said: the origin of this is الوَزَر, with fatḥa on the wāw and the zāy, which is the refuge in a mountain to which one resorts; the Exalted said: {كَلاَّ لاَ وَزَرَ} [al-Qiyāma: 11]. Then weight was called وِزْر by likening it to a mountain; then الوِزْر was borrowed for sin, likening it to it in the hardship one meets from it. In sum, this root denotes heaviness and protection.
His saying: {أَلاَ سَآءَ مَا يَزِرُونَ}: «ساء» here admits three views. The first: it is the fully conjugable transitive «ساء», whose pattern is then فَعَل with fatḥa on the middle radical; its object is then omitted and its fāʿil is «ما». «ما» admits three views: a nominal relative noun, a particle relative (maṣdariyya), or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, which is far-fetched. On making it nominal or an indefinite qualified noun, you assume a referent pronoun for it; the particle one needs none according to the majority. The implied form: "Lo, that which they bear grieved them", or "a thing that they bear", or "their bearing". Ibn ʿAṭiyya began with this view and said: "As you say: this matter grieved me (ساءني); and the speech is a pure statement, as in his saying:
190 - 0- رَضِيْتَ خِطَّةَ خَسْفٍ غيرَ طائلةٍ ... فساءَ هذا رِضَىً يا قيسَ عيلانا
(You accepted a plan of humiliation, worthless; how bad is this as acceptance, O Qays ʿAylān!)"
The Shaykh said: "It is not necessary that «ما» [Translator's note: so printed; the line contains no «ما», and «ساء» is evidently meant] in the verse be a pure statement; rather it admits the three views." End quote; and that is clear.
The second: it is for exclamation (taʿajjub), so it moves from فَعَل with fatḥa on the middle radical to فَعُل with ḍamma, and is given the rule of the verb of exclamation: non-conjugability and leaving pure statement for inshāʾ (non-declarative speech) [Translator's note: printed «إلا الإنشاء», evidently for «إلى الإنشاء»], if we say exclamation is inshāʾ, which is the correct view. The meaning: how bad — i.e. how ugly — is what they bear, or a thing they bear, or their bearing. The third: it is in the sense of «بئس», for intensifying blame, and so it is given its rules as well; the disagreement about the «ما» occurring after it applies, as mentioned at {بِئْسَمَا اشتروا} [al-Baqara: 90]. The difference between these three views has become clear: in the first it is transitive and conjugable and the speech with it is a pure statement; in the last two it is intransitive, frozen (jāmid) and non-declarative. The difference between the last two views is that the exclamatory one does not require in its fāʿil what is required in the fāʿil of «بئس». The Shaykh said: "The difference between this view — meaning its being in the sense of بئس — and the one before it — meaning its being exclamatory — is that in it [the exclamatory] what is required of the fāʿil of «بئس» is not required, nor is it a clause formed of mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate); it is formed only of a verb and fāʿil." End quote.
Its apparent sense is not clear except by an interpretation, namely that blame must have a specified object of blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm), which is a mubtadaʾ, and the verbal clause before it is its khabar; so from this clause a mubtadaʾ and khabar are formed. But someone may say: this only works on one of the parsings of the specified object; and even if conceded, the specified object of blame has no part in the clause of blame as regards its being verbal; so then no difference appears between them and the exclamatory one, in that each of them is formed of a verb and a fāʿil.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا الحياة الدنيآ إِلاَّ لَعِبٌ}: It may be hyperbole, making life itself play and amusement, as in her saying:
190 - 1-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإنما هي إقبالٌ وإدبار
(…for she is nothing but coming and going.)
This is better. It may also be that there is an omission in the speech, i.e. "and the deeds of life are nothing but…". Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: "And the people of the worldly life are nothing but people of play", so he assumed two omitted things.
اللَّهْو is turning the soul from seriousness to jest. From it is لها يلهو [Translator's note: printed «لو يلهو», evidently for «لها يلهو»]. As for لَهِي عن كذا, its meaning is: he turned himself away; the root is one, the wāw turning into yāʾ because of the kasra before it, as in شَقِي and رضي. Al-Mahdawī said: "The one whose meaning is turning away has yāʾ as its third radical, as shown by their saying لَهْيان, and the third radical of the first is wāw." The Shaykh said: "This is nothing, because the wāw turned into yāʾ in the dual, so its origin is not yāʾ. Do you not see the dual of شَجٍ: شَجِيان, which is from الشَّجْو?" End quote. He means that they say for its active participle لَهٍ, like شجٍ, and the dual is built on the singular; it has turned [into yāʾ] in the singular, so let it turn in the dual. [We have a discussion of this which we deposited in "al-Tafsīr al-Kabīr", praise be to Allah.] By this the invalidity of al-Mahdawī's rejection of al-Rummānī becomes clear. Al-Rummānī said: "Play is an activity that occupies the soul away from what benefits it; and lahw is turning the soul from seriousness to jest; one says لَهَيْتُ عنه, i.e. I turned myself away from it." Al-Mahdawī said: "In this there is weakness and remoteness, because the one that has the meaning of turning away has yāʾ as its third radical, as shown by their saying in the dual «ليهان»." [Translator's note: so printed; above it is given as «لَهْيان».] End quote. The invalidity of this rejection has preceded. Al-Rāghib said: "اللَّهْو is what occupies a person from what concerns and matters to him; one says لَهَوْتُ بكذا, or لهيت عن كذا: I was occupied away from it by amusement." What al-Rāghib mentioned is what led al-Mahdawī to distinguish between the two roots.
His saying: {وَلَلدَّارُ الآخرة}: The majority read it with two lāms: the first is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), the second for definiteness; and they read «الآخرةُ» in the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «الدار», with «خيرٌ» as its khabar (predicate). Ibn ʿĀmir read «ولَدارُ» with one lām, the lām of inception, and «الآخرةِ» in the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). On this reading there are two interpretations. The first is the view of the Basrans: it is a case of omitting the qualified noun and putting the adjective in its place, the implied form being "the abode of the last Hour" or "the abode of the last life", indicated by «وما الحياة الدنيا». Like it are their sayings «حبة الحمقاء», «مسجد الجامع», «صلاة الأولى», and «مكان الغربي», the implied forms being: the seed of the foolish herb (purslane), the mosque of the gathering place, the prayer of the first hour, and the place of the western side. What also makes this good in the verse is that this adjective has come to behave like non-derived nouns in frequently directly following governing words; and likewise everything that comes in which the annexation of the qualified noun to its adjective is imagined. They needed this only to avoid annexing a thing to itself, which is impossible, because annexation is either for definiteness or for specification, and a thing neither makes itself definite nor specifies itself.
The second — the view of the Kufans — is that when the wording of the qualified noun and its adjective differ, annexing it to it is permissible; and they cited the examples I gave earlier. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is annexing a thing to itself, as in your saying بارحة الأولى, يوم الخميس, and حق اليقين; it is only permissible when the two words differ." Ibn ʿĀmir's reading agrees with his muṣḥaf, for it was written in the muṣḥafs of the Syrians with one lām. Some chose it because it agrees with what is unanimously read in Yūsuf: {وَلَدَارُ الآخرة خَيْرٌ} [Yūsuf: 109]; in the muṣḥafs of [other] people it is with two lāms.
«خيرٌ» may be an elative (for preference), with the thing compared against omitted because it is known, i.e. better than the worldly life; or it may be merely descriptive of goodness, as in His saying, the Exalted: {أَصْحَابُ الجنة يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً} [al-Furqān: 24]. {لِّلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ} is attached to an omitted element, because it is a naʿt of «خير». What is fitting — or necessary — is that the lām be for clarification (bayān), i.e. "I mean, for those who…", and likewise everything of its kind, such as {خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ الأولى} [al-Ḍuḥā: 4].
His saying: {أَفَلاَ تَعْقِلُونَ}: Discussion of the like of this hamza entering upon the fāʾ, and its sisters the wāw and ثم, has preceded. Ibn ʿĀmir, Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read {تَعْقِلُون} as an address to those in his presence, upon him be peace, and in his time. The rest read it with the yāʾ of the third person, referring back to the third-person nouns mentioned before. The object of «تَعْقِلون» is omitted because it is known, i.e. "do you not understand that the matter is as mentioned, so that you renounce this world", or "that it is better than this world".

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قَدْ نَعْلَمُ}: «قد» here is a particle of confirmation (taḥqīq). Al-Zamakhsharī and al-Tabrīzī said: "«قد نعلم» is in the sense of «ربما» which comes for the increase and multiplicity of the action, as in his saying:
190 - 2-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . قد يُهْلِكُ المالَ نائِلُهْ
(…his giving often destroys his wealth.)"
The Shaykh said: "This view is not well known among grammarians, though some held it, arguing from his saying:
190 - 3- قد أَتْرُكُ القِرْن مُصْفرَّاً أناملُه ... كأنَّ أثوابه مُجَّتْ بفِرصادِ
(Often I leave my match with yellowed fingertips, as though his clothes had been sprayed with mulberry juice.)
and the saying of the other:
أخي ثقةٍ لا تُتْلِفُ الخمرُ مالَه ... ولكنه قد يُهْلك المالَ نائلُه
(A trustworthy brother: wine does not waste his wealth, but his giving often destroys it.)
What appears is that multiplicity is not understood from «قد», but from the context of speech, since boasting of killing a single match is of no worth. And even supposing that, it is impossible in the verse, because His knowledge, the Exalted, does not admit of multiplication." I say: this may be answered by saying that the multiplicity is in the objects of knowledge, not in the knowledge. Then he said: "And as for his saying 'in the sense of «ربما» which comes for the increase and multiplicity of the action', the well-known view is that «رُبَّ» is for paucity, not for multiplicity, and adding «ما» to it does not take it out of that; rather «ما» prepares it for entering upon the verb, and the preparatory «ما» does not remove a word from its original meaning, just as it does not remove «لعلَّ» from hope, nor «كأنَّ» from likening, nor «ليت» from wishing." Ibn Mālik said: "«قد» is like «ربما» in [expressing] paucity and in turning [the imperfect] to the meaning of the past; it is then for confirmation and emphasis, as in {قَدْ نَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُ لَيَحْزُنُكَ} and {وَقَد تَّعْلَمُونَ أَنِّي رَسُولُ الله} [al-Ṣaff: 5], and his saying:
190 - 4- وقد تُدْرِكُ الإِنسانَ رحمةُ ربِّه ... ولو كان تحت الأرض سبعين واديا
(The mercy of his Lord may reach a man even if he were seventy valleys beneath the earth.)
It may be free of paucity while turning to the meaning of the past, as in His saying {قَدْ نرى تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ} [al-Baqara: 144]."
Makkī said: "«قد» here and in similar places comes to emphasise a thing, affirm it and confirm it; and «نعلم» means «عَلِمْنا»." Discussion of this particle has preceded, and that it wavers between being a particle and a noun. The Shaykh said here: "«قد» is a particle of expectation (tawaqquʿ). When it enters a future verb, the expectation is on the part of the speaker, as in your saying 'the rain may fall in such-and-such a month'; when it is a past verb or a present verb with past meaning, the expectation is on the part of the listener, whereas the speaker asserts what he reports. The imperfect was used here because what is meant is being characterised by knowledge and its continuity, without regard to time, as in their saying: he gives and withholds."
{إِنَّهُ لَيَحْزُنُكَ} stands in place of the two objects, since [«نعلم»] is suspended (muʿallaq) from operating; [«إنّ»] has kasra because the lām enters its khabar (predicate). Discussion of «لَيَحْزُنك» has preceded, and that it is read with fatḥa and ḍamma on the yāʾ, from حَزَنه and أَحْزنه, in Āl ʿImrān. «الذي يقولون» is the fāʿil (agent), and its referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. what they say of attributing to him what does not befit him. The pronoun in «إنه» is the pronoun of the matter and of the account (ḍamīr al-shaʾn wa-l-ḥadīth), and the clause after it is a khabar explaining it. It is not permissible to take this imperfect as equivalent to an active participle raising a fāʿil, as is done in your saying «إنَّ زيداً يقوم أبوه», lest it entail explaining the pronoun of the matter by a single word, and it has preceded that this is forbidden among the Basrans.
His saying: {لاَ يُكَذِّبُونَكَ}: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read {لا يَكْذِبُونك} [Translator's note: so printed; the reading meant is «لا يُكْذِبونك», as the following discussion shows] without doubling, from أَكْذَبَ; the rest read it with doubling, from كذَّب, and this is the reading of ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās. People disagreed about this. It has been said: both mean the same, like أَكْثَر and كثَّر, نَزَّل and أنزل. It has also been said: there is a difference between them. Al-Kisāʾī said: the Arabs say «كذَّبْتُ الرجلَ» with doubling when you attribute lying to him, and «أَكْذَبْتُه» when you attribute falsehood to what he brought without attributing it to him. They also say أَكْذَبْتُ الرجل when you find him to be a liar, like أَحْمَدْتُه when you find him praiseworthy. So the meaning of «لا يُكْذِبونك» without doubling is: they do not attribute lying to you and do not find you to be a liar; this is clear.
As for the doubled reading, it is a pure statement that they do not deny him. If it is said: this is impossible, because denial necessarily occurred from some of them — the answer is that this, even though it is attributed to all of them — I mean the absence of denial — only some of them are meant by it figuratively, as in His saying {كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 105] and {كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 16] [Translator's note: so printed; the verse is al-Shuʿarāʾ 160], even though among them were some who did not deny him; it is a general expression meaning the particular. The second: He negated the denial because of the absence of the harms that follow from it, as if it were said: they do not deny you a denial that matters and harms you, for you are not a liar, so their denial is as no denial; it is negating the cause because its effect is absent. [Translator's note: the printed text has «لانتقاء», evidently for «لانتفاء».] Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is that denying you is a matter that goes back to Allah, because you are His Messenger whose truth is confirmed; so in reality they do not deny you; they only deny Allah by rejecting His signs. So desist from your grief — as a master says to his servant when some people have insulted him: they have not insulted you; they have only insulted me. And in this manner is {إِنَّ الذين يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ الله} [al-Fatḥ: 10]."
His saying: {بِآيَاتِ الله}: Two views are possible for this prepositional phrase. The first: it is attached to «يَجْحَدون»; this is the apparent view, from which one should not depart. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be attached to «الظالمين», saying: "As in His saying, the Exalted: {وَآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ الناقة مُبْصِرَةً فَظَلَمُواْ بِهَا} [al-Isrāʾ: 59]." What he said is not good, because the bāʾ there is causal, i.e. they did wrong because of it, while the bāʾ here means transitivity; and here there is something to which it is clearly attached, so there is no necessity calling for departure from it. In this verse an overt noun is put in the place of a pronoun, since the original would be "but they reject the signs of Allah"; but it draws attention to the fact that wrongdoing is what drove them to rejection.
الجُحود and الجَحْد mean denying what the heart holds to be established, or affirming what the heart holds to be negated. It has been said: الجَحْد is denying what one knows, so it is not synonymous with negation in every respect.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذْ قَالَ}: «إذ» is in the accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "remember," and it is conjoined to «أقيموا»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. And «قال» is in the position of a genitive by the adverb (ẓarf).
His words: {آزَرَ}: the majority read «آزرَ» on the pattern of «آدم», with fatḥa on the zāy and the rāʾ. Its parsing on that reading is according to several aspects. The first: it is a badal (substitute) from «أبيه», or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it, if «آزر» was a nickname (laqab) of his. If it is an adjective meaning "the one who errs," as al-Zajjāj said, or "the crooked one," as al-Farrāʾ said, or "the decrepit old man," as al-Ḍaḥḥāk said, then it is a naʿt (adjective) of «أبيه», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, meaning "while he is in a state of crookedness or error"; this is attributed to al-Zajjāj. And if it is said that «آزر» is the name of an idol his father used to worship, then in that case it is an ʿaṭf bayān to «أبيه» or a badal from it; the explanation of that is that when he clung to its worship he was nicknamed by it and it became a laqab for him, as one of the modern (muḥdath) poets said:
195 - 8- أُدْعى بأسماءَ نَبْزاً في قبائِلها ... كأنَّ أسماءَ أَضْحَتْ بعضَ أسمائي
(I am called by [the name] Asmāʾ as a nickname among her tribes, as if Asmāʾ had become one of my names.)
Thus al-Zamakhsharī attributed it to one of the moderns, and the Shaykh attributed it to one of the grammarians. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Just as Ibn Qays was nicknamed after the Ruqayyas about whom he composed love poetry, so that he was called Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt." Or it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "to his father, the worshipper of Āzar"; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. On this view, «عابد» ("worshipper") is an adjective of «أبيه», and this [word] was given its case. Or it is in the accusative as censure (ʿalā al-dhamm).
«آزر» is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), and there is disagreement about the cause of its being diptote. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The nearest view is that the pattern of «آزر» is fāʿal, like «عابَر», «شالَخ» and «فالَغ»"; on this view it is diptote because of being a proper name and foreign. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its pattern is afʿal, and it is diptote because of foreignness and definiteness, on the view of those who do not derive it from al-azr or al-wizr; and those who derive it from one of the two say it is Arabic and made it diptote because of definiteness and the verbal pattern." This disagreement resembles the disagreement about «آدم», which has already been mentioned, and that al-Zamakhsharī's choice there is that it is fāʿal like «عابَر», and what follows that. If we hold that it is an adjective, as al-Zajjāj said, meaning "the one who errs," or meaning "the crooked one," or meaning "the decrepit," as al-Farrāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said, then its being diptote is problematic, and its occurring as an adjective of a definite noun is also problematic.
The first [problem] may be answered by saying that the difficulty is removed by claiming its pattern is afʿal, so that it is then diptote because of the verbal pattern and adjectival status, like «أحمر» and its class; but on al-Zamakhsharī's view this does not work. The second may be answered by saying that we do not concede that it is an adjective of «أبيه» such that describing definite nouns with indefinite ones would follow; rather it is in the accusative as censure, or it is intended as having al. Al-Zajjāj said both of these. The second is weak, because omitting al while intending its meaning either produces diptote status [as] in «سحر» used for a specific day, and that is called ʿadl (deflection), or produces indeclinability, and that is called taḍammun (implication), as in «أمس»; and on «سحر» and «أمس» there is a long discussion for which this is not the place. Nor can it be said that «آزَر» became diptote as «سحر» did, i.e. because of deflection from al, because ʿadl causes diptote status in it together with definiteness, since it is for a specific time; unlike this, for it is an adjective, as you have supposed [Translator's note: the text reads «قرضتم», evidently for «فرضتم»].
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid, among others, read it with ḍamma on the rāʾ [«آزرُ»], as a munādā (the one addressed) whose vocative particle has been omitted, as in His words {يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ} [Yūsuf: 29] and as in his saying:
195 - 9- ليُبْك يزيدُ ضارعٌ لخصومةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Let Yazīd be wept for — one humbled in a dispute…)
in one of the two aspects, i.e. "O Yazīd." It is supported by what is in the codex of Ubayy: «يا آزر», with its particle present. This only works on the claim that it is a proper name; on the claim that it is an adjective it is weak, because omitting the vocative particle is rare with adjectives, as in their sayings «افتدِ مخنوقُ» ("Ransom yourself, O strangled one") and «صاحِ شَمِّرْ» ("O companion, roll up your sleeves").
Ibn ʿAbbās, in one transmission, read «أَأَزْراً تتخذ» with two hamzas with fatḥa, an unvowelled zāy and a rāʾ in the accusative with tanwīn, and «تتخذ» without the interrogative hamza. When al-Zamakhsharī reported this reading he did not drop the interrogative hamza from «أتتخذ». As for the first reading, Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, explaining its meaning: "Is it as a support, strength and backing against Allah that you take…? It is from His words {اشدد بِهِ أَزْرِي} [Ṭā Hā: 31]." End of quotation. On this view, «أزراً» may be in the accusative in three ways. The first: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and «أصناماً آلهة» is in the accusative by «تتخذ», as will be explained; the meaning is: "Do you take idols as gods for the sake of strength and backing?" The second: that it be in the accusative as a ḥāl, because it is originally an adjective of «أصناماً»; when it was placed before it and before its governing word, it became accusative as a ḥāl. The third: that it be in the accusative as a second object placed before its governing word, the original being: "Do you take idols as gods, as a support," i.e. strength and backing.
As for the second reading, al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the name of an idol, and its meaning is 'Do you worship Azr?' by way of denunciation; then He said 'you take idols as gods' to confirm and establish that, and it falls under the rule of the denunciation, because it is like an explanation of it." On this view «أزْراً» is in the accusative by an omitted verb indicated by the meaning. But his saying "and it falls under the rule of the denunciation" strengthens [the view] that «أَتَتَّخِذُ» was not read with the interrogative hamza, because if it had an interrogative hamza with it, it would carry the denunciation independently, and he would not have needed to say: "it falls under the rule of the denunciation because it is like an explanation of it."
Ibn ʿAbbās also, and Abū Ismāʿīl al-Shāmī, read «أَإزراً» with an interrogative hamza followed by a hamza with kasra, and the rāʾ in the accusative with tanwīn. Ibn ʿAṭiyya made [the second hamza] a replacement of a wāw, deriving it from al-wizr ("burden"), like «إسادة» and «إشاح» for «وسادة» and «وشاح». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "There are two aspects in it; one of them: the second hamza is the first radical of the word and is not a replacement of anything, and its meaning is heaviness." Al-Zamakhsharī made it the name of an idol, and the discussion of it is like the discussion of «أزراً» with fatḥa on the hamza, which has been given.
Al-Aʿmash read «إزْراً تَتَّخِذُ» without an interrogative hamza, but with kasra on the hamza, an unvowelled zāy and the rāʾ in the accusative with tanwīn; its accusative is clear from what has been said. «تتخذ» may be the one that takes two objects, in the sense of "making into" (taṣyīr), or the one that takes one object because it means "to make"; it is reported in the exegesis that his father used to carve and fashion them. The interrogative clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of the saying, and likewise His words {إني أَرَاكَ}. «أراك» may be the cognitive one (ʿilmiyya), which is the apparent one, so it takes two objects; or it may be the visual one, which is not strong, in which case «في ضلال» is a ḥāl. On both assumptions it is attached to an omitted [word], except that in the first it is one of the two parts of the sentence, and in the second it is an extra element (faḍla).
«مبين» is the active participle of «أبان» used intransitively, meaning "became manifest." It may also be from the transitive [«أبان»], with the object omitted, i.e. "making manifest your disbelief in your Creator." On this view, Ibn ʿAṭiyya's saying "and it is not the transitive verb transferred from «بان يبين»" is not conceded. He made error a container (ẓarf) encompassing them, as an intensification of their being characterised by it; so it is more eloquent than saying "I see you to be in error."

semin-durr:75-75.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَكَذَلِكَ}: there are three aspects concerning this kāf. The most apparent: it is for comparison, and it is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Zamakhsharī gave its implied form as: "And like that acquainting and making-to-see, We acquaint Abraham and make him see the dominion (malakūt)." Al-Mahdawī gave it as: "And just as We guided you, O Muhammad, We showed Abraham." The Shaykh said: "This is far from what the wording indicates." I say: it was only far because the omitted [element] is not from what was uttered; had he given it as "And just as We showed you, O Muhammad, guidance," it would have been close, because both the wording and the meaning together indicate it. Abū al-Baqāʾ gave it two implied forms. In the first he said: "It is in the accusative by implying «أريناه», its implied form being: and just as he saw his father and his people in manifest error, We showed him that," i.e. what he saw as right, through Our acquainting him with it. In the second he said: "It may be in the accusative by «نُري» which follows it, as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: We show him the dominion of the heavens and the earth, a showing like the seeing of his father's error." End of quotation. I say: his saying "by implying «أريناه»" is not needed at all, and because it entails that His words «نُري إبراهيم ملكوت» are not connected with what precedes them.
The second: it is for giving a reason, in the sense of the lām, i.e. "and because of that denunciation that came from him against them, and the call to Allah at a time when others than Allah were called upon as gods, We show him the dominion." The third: that the kāf is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and the matter is thus," i.e. what he saw of their error. Abū al-Baqāʾ and others reported the last two aspects.
«ونُري»: this is an imperfect, and what is meant by it is the narration of a past state. «نري» may be the one taking two objects, because it is originally visual, and the hamza of transfer gave it a second object [Translator's note: printed «معفولاً», for «مفعولاً»]. Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it transferred from «رأى» meaning "to know (ʿarafa)," and so did al-Zamakhsharī, for he said in what I reported from him earlier: "And like that acquainting, We acquaint." The Shaykh said after reporting Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words: "That «رأى» should mean 'to know (ʿarafa)' and then take two objects by means of the hamza needs to be transmitted from the Arabs. What the grammarians have transmitted is that «رأى», when visual, takes one object, and when it means «علم» which puts two objects in the accusative, it takes two objects." I say: it is strange that he singled out Ibn ʿAṭiyya for the objection, and not Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī]. This clause containing the comparison or the reason is parenthetical between His words «وإذ قال إبراهيم», disapproving of his father's and his people's worship of idols, and the argument against them for the oneness of Allah the Exalted. It may also not be parenthetical, if we say that His words «فلمَّا» are conjoined to what precedes; this will come.
«المَلَكوت» is a maṣdar on the pattern faʿalūt meaning "dominion (al-mulk)"; it was built on this pattern, and the addition is for intensification. This was mentioned before at the discussion of «الطاغوت». The majority read «مَلَكوت» with fatḥa on the lām, and Abū al-Sammāl read it with sukūn on it [«مَلْكوت»], which is a dialectal form.

semin-durr:76-76.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَلَمَّا جَنَّ}: this clause may be conjoined (nasaq) to His words {وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ}, as a conjoining of the proof to what it proves, so that {وَكَذَلِكَ نري إِبْرَاهِيمَ} is parenthetical, as stated before. It may also be conjoined to the clause {وَكَذَلِكَ نري إِبْرَاهِيمَ}. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The fāʾ in His word «فلمَّا» links the clause after it with what is before it, and it makes it preponderant that what is meant by the malakūt (dominion) is the detail mentioned in this verse." The first is better, and al-Zamakhsharī inclined to it.
«جَنَّ» means "covered." The derivation of this root has been given at the mention of {الجنة} [al-Baqara: 35]. Here there is a particularity of usage for the verb when attributed to the night. One says «جَنَّ عليه الليل» and «أجنّ عليه» meaning "[the night] grew dark upon him," so it is used intransitively; and «جنَّه» and «أجنّه», so it is used transitively. So this is one of the cases where faʿala and afʿala agree in being intransitive and transitive, except that the better usage is «جنَّ عليه الليل» and «أجنَّه الليل», so the triliteral is intransitive and afʿala transitive. Of the triliteral coming as transitive is his saying:
1961 - ... وماءٍ وَرَدَتْ قُبَيْلَ الكَرَى
وقد جَنَّه السَّدَفُ الأدهَمُ ...
(…and many a water I came to shortly before sleep, when the pitch-black darkness had covered it.)
Its maṣdar is «جَنٌّ», «جَنان» and «جُنون». Al-Rāghib distinguished between «جَنَّه» and «أَجَنَّه», saying: "«جنَّه» is when he covered it, and «أجنَّه» is when he provided it with something that covers it, like your saying «قَبَرْتُه» ('I buried him') and «أقبرته» ('I gave him a grave'), and «سَقَيْتُه» and «أَسْقَيْتُه»." Something of this has been given to you at the mention of «حزن» and «أحزن». «جنَّ» in the noble verse may be transitive with its object omitted, its implied form being: "it covered things and visible objects from him."
His words: «رأى كوكباً»: this is the apodosis (jawāb) of «لمَّا». The readers have a great disagreement about it and about the two verbs after it, regarding imāla (inclining the vowel toward i/e) or its absence. So let me mention that in summary, with its reasons, and I say: As for «رأى» with its alif retained, the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, and Ibn Dhakwān from Ibn ʿĀmir applied full imāla to its rāʾ and hamza. Abū ʿAmr in full [i.e. both his transmitters] applied imāla to the hamza only, without the rāʾ; and al-Sūsī from Abū ʿAmr, with a disagreement from him, also applied imāla to the rāʾ, so al-Sūsī in one of his two aspects agrees with the group mentioned first. Warsh applied in-between (bayna bayna) imāla to the rāʾ and the hamza of this word wherever it occurs. All of this is when no pronoun is attached to it, as in the above. When a pronoun is attached to it, as in {فَرَآهُ فِي سَوَآءِ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 55], {فَلَمَّا رَآهَا} [al-Naml: 10] and {وَإِذَا رَآكَ الذين} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 36], Ibn Dhakwān has two aspects from him, and the rest follow their principles stated above.
As for «رأى» when its alif is omitted, it is of two kinds. A kind in which it never returns, neither in continuous reading nor in pause, such as {رَأَتْهُمْ مِّن مَّكَانٍ} [al-Furqān: 12] and {رَأَوُاْ العذاب} [Yūnus: 54]; there is no imāla in any of it, and likewise where its alif has turned into a yāʾ, as in {رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ} [al-Insān: 20]. And a kind whose alif is omitted because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters in continuous reading, and returns in pause, such as {رَأَى القمر} [al-Anʿām: 77], {رَأَى الشمس} [al-Anʿām: 78], {وَرَأَى المجرمون النار} [al-Kahf: 53] and {وَإِذَا رَأى الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [al-Naḥl: 85]. In this there is also disagreement among the people of imāla, sometimes considering the [actual] pronunciation and sometimes the underlying form. Ḥamza and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim applied imāla to the rāʾ alone without disagreement, and al-Sūsī alone with a disagreement from him.
As for the hamza, Abū Bakr and al-Sūsī applied imāla to it together with the rāʾ, with a disagreement from both of them. All this is when you read continuously; when you pause, the alif returns because what required its omission is absent, and the rule of this verb is then the rule of [the verb] to which no unvowelled letter is joined, so the details given before return in it, as when you pause on «رأى» in such as {رَأَى القمر} [al-Anʿām: 77]. As for the imāla of the rāʾ of «رأى», it is in order to make it follow the imāla of the hamza—this is how they express it; in reality the imāla is only for the alif, because it is converted from a yāʾ, and imāla, as you know, is to incline the alif toward yāʾ and the fatḥa before it toward kasra; hence it is correct to say: the rāʾ was given imāla because of the imāla of the hamza.
As for Ibn Dhakwān's distinction according to whether the pronoun is attached or not, its reasoning is that when the verb is attached to the pronoun, its alif becomes distant from the end, so it is not given imāla. The reasoning of those who apply imāla to the hamza in «رأى القمرَ» is regard for the alif even though it is omitted, since its omission is incidental. Then some of them confined themselves to imāla of the hamza, because considering it as present is weak; and some did not confine themselves, giving it the rule of something truly present, so they made the rāʾ follow the hamza in that.
«الكَوْكَبُ» is the star (al-najm), and one also says «كَوْكبة». Al-Rāghib said: "It, i.e. the star, is not called «كوكب» except when it appears." There are three aspects concerning its derivation. The first: it is from the root «وكب», so the kāf is extra. This view was held by al-Shaykh Raḍiyy al-Dīn al-Ṣaghānī; he (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "«كوكب» ought, according to the skilled grammarians, to be mentioned under the root «وكب», for according to them it came with an extra kāf; but al-Jawharī entered it under the combination k-w-k-b, and perhaps he followed al-Layth in that, for he mentioned it among the quadriliterals, holding that the wāw is a radical." This is an explicit statement from al-Ṣaghānī that the kāf is extra; but an extra kāf is not permissible according to the grammarians, and the letters of augmentation are confined to those ten. As for their saying «هِنْدِيٌّ» and «هِنْدِكيّ» with one meaning, namely "related to India," and the poet's saying:
1962 - ومُقْرَبةٍ دُهْمٍ وكُمْتٍ كأنَّها ... طَماطِمُ من فوق الوفازِ هَنادِكُ
(And many a horse kept close [to the tents], black and bay, as though they were barbarous-tongued Indians on top of the high grounds.)
its apparent sense is that the kāf is extra; but the grammarians explained it as being of the type of «سَبْط» and «سِبَطْر», i.e. of what comes with two forms, one longer than the other, without [the shorter] being the root of it. Just as it is not said, by agreement, that the rāʾ is extra, so too this kāf. That is why the Shaykh said: "I wonder who the skilled grammarians are who hold that it is extra, especially at the beginning of the word!" The second: the word is entirely radical, quadriliteral, of the kind in which the first radical is repeated, so its pattern is faʿfal like «فَوْفَل», which is a rare pattern. The third: al-Rāghib's presentation suggests that it is from the root «كبَّ» and «كَبْكب», for he said: "Al-kabkaba is the tumbling of a thing into a pit; one says «كَبَّ» and «كَبْكَبَ», like «كفَّ» and «كَفْكَفَ», and «صَرَّ الريحُ» and «صرصر»; and al-kawākib are the visible stars." The apparent sense of this presentation is that the wāw is extra and the kāf replaces one of the two bāʾs [Translator's note: the text reads «الياءين» ("the two yāʾs"), apparently for «الباءين»]; and this is very strange.
His words: «قال هذا ربِّي»: concerning «قال» there are three aspects. The most apparent of them: it is resumptive (istiʾnāf); he stated that saying, or asked about it, according to the disagreement. The second: it is an adjective of «كوكباً», so it is in the position of an accusative. But how can it be an adjective of «كوكباً» when neither the grammar nor the meaning supports it? As for the grammar, because of the absence of a pronoun referring back from the clause serving as adjective to what it qualifies.
