It cannot be said that the link is achieved by the demonstrative, because that is specific to the subject–predicate construction; that is why omitting the referent pronoun is frequent from the adjective clause and rare from the khabar, and the permissibility of something in this does not entail its permissibility in that; and claiming an omitted pronoun, i.e. "he said about it: this is my Lord," is far-fetched. As for the meaning, it leads to the implied form "he saw a star characterised by this saying," and that is certainly not intended. The third: it is the apodosis of «فلما جَنَّ»; on this view His words «رأى كوكباً» are in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "when the night covered him, seeing a star."
«هذا ربي» is reported speech governed by the saying. It is said that it is a pure statement, with an interpretation that the exegetes mention; and it is said rather that it is with the interrogative hamza omitted, i.e. «أهذا ربي» ("Is this my Lord?"). They recited:
1963 - لعَمْرَك ما أدري وإن كنتُ داريا ... بسبعٍ رَمَيْنَ الجمرَ أم بثمان
(By your life, I do not know—though I am one who knows—whether they threw the pebbles with seven or with eight.)
and his saying:
1964 - أفرحُ أن أُرْزَأ الكرامَ وأَنْ ... أُوْرَثَ ذَوْداً شصائِصاً نَبْلا
(Shall I rejoice that I am bereaved of the noble ones, and that I inherit a small herd of dry, scrawny camels?)
and his saying:
1975 - ... طَرِبْتُ وما شوقاً إلى البيض أطربُ
ولا لَعِباً مني وذو الشيب يلعبُ ...
(I was moved with emotion—yet it is not out of longing for the fair women that I am moved, nor in play on my part; and does the grey-haired one play?)
[Translator's note: the verse is numbered 1975 in the text, out of sequence between 1964 and 1966; presumably 1965.] and the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيّ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 22] [Translator's note: the text gives al-Shuʿarāʾ: 13; the verse is 26:22]. They said: its implied form is «أبسبع», «أأفرح», «أذو» and «أتلك». Ibn al-Anbārī said: "This is only permissible where there is a distinguishing sign between the statement and the question," meaning if there is a verbal indication, such as the presence of «أم» in the first verse, unlike what follows it.
«الأُفول» is disappearance and going away. One says «أَفَلَ يأفُل أُفولاً». Dhū al-Rumma said:
1966 - ... مصابيحُ ليسَتْ باللواتي تقودُها
نجومٌ ولا بالآفلاتِ شُموسُها ...
(…lamps [i.e. noble men] that are not led by stars, nor are their suns ones that set.)
«الإِفَال» are young sheep, and «الأَفيل» is the puny weaned young camel.

semin-durr:77-77.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {بَازِغاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «القمر». «البزوغ» is rising. One says «بَزَغَ» with fatḥa on the zāy, «يبزُغ» with ḍamma on it, «بُزوغاً». It is used intransitively and transitively: one says «بَزَغ البَيْطار الدابَّة», i.e. the farrier made the animal's blood flow, «فَبَزَغ هو», i.e. it flowed. This is the original sense; then every rising was called «بُزوغ», and from it: «بَزَغَ ناب الصبي والبعير» ("the boy's / the camel's tooth came out"), by comparison with that. «القمر» (the moon) is well known; it was so named because of its whiteness and the spread of its light. «الأقمر» is the donkey that has the colour of a moonlit night, and «القَمْراء» is the moonlight. It is also said that it was called «قمر» because it overcomes (yaqmuru) the light of the stars and wins it. «الليالي القُمْر» are the nights when the moon is round, and they are the white nights, because the moonlight continues in them until morning. It is said that it is not called «قمر» until after it fills out on the third night, and before that it is «هلال» (crescent)—according to a disagreement among the lexicographers which I set out earlier in [the commentary on] al-Baqara at His words {عَنِ الأهلة} [al-Baqara: 189]. When it reaches the third night after the tenth it is called «بدر» (full moon), up to the fifteenth. One says «قَمِرْتُ فلاناً كذا», i.e. "I tricked so-and-so out of such-and-such"; it is as though it were taken from «قَمِرَتْ القِرْبَةُ», [the waterskin] was spoiled by the moonlight.

semin-durr:78-78.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {هذا رَبِّي}: the demonstrative was only made masculine while what is pointed to [the sun] is feminine for one of several reasons: either treating it as "the star," or treating it as "the light" and "the radiance," or by interpreting it as "the riser," "the figure" or "the thing"; or because, when something masculine was predicated of it, it was given its rule. You say «هند ذاك الإِنسان» and «تِيْكَ الإِنسان» ("Hind is that person"). He said:
1967 - تبيت نُعْمَى على الهِجْران غائبةً ... سُقْياً ورُعْياً لذاك الغائبِ الزاري
(Nuʿmā passes the night absent in estrangement — may rain and care be granted to that absent, disdainful one.)
So he pointed to «نُعمى», which is feminine, with the masculine demonstrative, because he described her with the description of males; or because [the sun] has two usages, masculine and feminine, even though feminine is more common; and the noble verse combined the two, making it feminine in His word «بازغة» and masculine in His word «هذا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He made the mubtadaʾ (subject) like the khabar (predicate) because they both refer to one thing, as in their sayings «ما جاءت حاجتك» and «مَنْ كانت أمك», and {لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ} [al-Anʿām: 23]. And choosing this way was necessary to protect the Lord from any suspicion of femininity; do you not see that they said in describing Allah «عَلاَّم» and did not say «عَلاَّمة», even though it is more intensive, guarding against the feminine marker?" I say: this is close to what preceded in my saying that a feminine [noun], when something masculine is predicated of it, is treated as masculine, as in «هند ذاك الإِنسان». It is also said: because it means "this luminous body" or "this visible thing."
The Shaykh said: "It may be said that most of the languages of the non-Arabs do not distinguish between masculine and feminine in pronouns or demonstratives, and they have no feminine marker; rather masculine and feminine are the same. Therefore, when He narrated the words of Abraham, He pointed to what is feminine for us with what is used to point to the masculine; indeed, even if the feminine had a vulva, it would have no marker indicating it in their speech. And when Allah the Exalted spoke about them in His own words «بازغة» and «أَفَلتْ», it came according to the requirements of Arabic, since that is not narration." End of quotation. This would only be evident if He had narrated their words exactly in their language; but something expressed in the language of the Arabs being given its rule in the language of the non-Arabs is open to consideration.
His words: «مِمَّا يُشْرِكون»: «ما» is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), i.e. "free of your associating"; or it is relative (mawṣūla), i.e. "of those whom you associate with Allah in His worship," with the referent pronoun omitted. It may also be the qualified [indefinite] «ما» (mawṣūfa), the referent pronoun again being omitted, except that omission of the referent pronoun of an adjective clause is rarer than omission of the referent pronoun of a ṣila (relative clause). So the clause after it has no grammatical position on the first two views, and its position is genitive on the third.

semin-durr:79-79.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ}: they implied a muḍāf before it, i.e. "I have turned my face to His worship and to His good pleasure," as though by that they rejected the misconception of whoever imagines direction [for Allah]. «حنيفاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «وَجَّهْتُ». The explanation of these words has been given before. «ما» may be the Ḥijāzī [which governs like «ليس»] or the Tamīmī [which does not govern].

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لِّمَن مَّا فِي السموات}: «لمَنْ» is a fronted khabar (predicate), whose fronting is obligatory because it contains something that has the right to stand at the head of the speech, for «مَنْ» is interrogative; the mubtadaʾ (subject) is «ما», meaning "that which"; the meaning is: to whom belongs that which is in the heavens? As for His saying: {قُل للَّهِ}: it was said that He commanded him to answer, even though the intent is that others answer, only so that he would be the first to hasten to acknowledge that. It was also said: when he asked them, it is as though they said: to whom does it belong? So Allah said: say: to Allah; al-Jurjānī mentioned this. On this view His saying «قل لله» is an answer to the implied question coming from the side of the disbelievers. This is far-fetched, because they did not doubt that it belongs to Allah; this is only a question of silencing and rebuke, and had they answered, they could not have answered except with that. His saying «لله» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. it, or that, belongs to Allah.

His saying: {كَتَبَ على نَفْسِهِ}: i.e. He decreed and made obligatory — an obligation of grace, not that it is something owed by Him, Exalted is He. It was said: its meaning is the oath; and on this view His saying {لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ} is its apodosis (jawāb), because of the meaning of oath it contains, and on this view there is no pause at His saying «الرحمة». Al-Zajjāj said: "The clause from His saying {لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ} is in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) of «الرحمة»", because he interpreted His saying {لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ} as: He has given you respite and extended your life and provision despite your disbelief — so it is an explanation of the mercy. Al-Farrāʾ mentioned these two aspects, I mean that the clause is complete at His saying «الرحمة», or that «ليجمعنكم» is a badal of it; he said: "If you wish, you make «الرحمة» the end of the speech and then begin anew after it with «ليجمعنكم»; and if you wish, you put it in the position of accusative, as He said: {كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ على نَفْسِهِ الرحمة أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 54]." I say: his adducing this verse as evidence is very good.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected this on the grounds that it entails the entry of the nūn of emphasis in an affirmative statement; he said: "It only enters the imperative, the prohibition and the apodosis of an oath." The Shaykh rejected Ibn ʿAṭiyya's restriction of the occurrence [written in the text: «وردَ»] of the nūn of emphasis to what he mentioned, and he is correct. He rejected «ليجمعنَّكم» being a badal of «الرحمة» on another ground, namely that «ليجمعنَّكم» is the apodosis of an oath, and the clause of the apodosis by itself has no grammatical position; the grammatical position is assigned only to the two clauses of the oath and the apodosis together. I say: Makkī mixed the two views and made them one view; he said: «ليجمعنَّكم» is in the position of accusative as a badal of «الرحمة», and the lām is the lām of the oath, so it is the apodosis of «كتب», because it means "He made that obligatory upon Himself", so it contains the meaning of an oath. An answer may appear to what the Shaykh raised against those other than Makkī: namely, that they made «ليجمعنَّكم» a badal of «الرحمة», meaning it together with its omitted counterpart [the oath], and they dispensed with mentioning the oath by it because it is mentioned in the wording; so it is as though they said: the oath clause is in the position of accusative as a badal of «الرحمة». And just as they say "the oath clause" and dispense with it from mentioning the apodosis clause, so too they dispense with the apodosis from mentioning the oath, especially since it is not mentioned.

As for Makkī, this does not appear to be an answer for him, because he stated explicitly that it is the apodosis of «كَتَبَ»; insofar as he made it the apodosis of «كتب» it has no position, and insofar as he made it a badal its position is accusative, so the two are mutually incompatible. What is fitting in this verse is that the pause is at His saying «الرحمة», and His saying «ليجمعنَّكم» is the apodosis of an omitted oath, i.e. "by Allah, He will surely gather you"; and the oath clause has no connection with what precedes it in terms of grammatical analysis, even if it is connected to it in terms of meaning.

«إلى» is in its proper sense, i.e. He will surely gather you, ending up at the Day of Resurrection. It was said: it has the meaning of the lām, as in His saying: {إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ الناس لِيَوْمٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 9]. It was said: it means «في», i.e. He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection. It was said: it is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. He will surely gather you the Day of Resurrection; and the reading of those who read {تهوى إليهم} with fatḥa on the wāw may testify for it, [but] that there is necessity here for that [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense seems to require "that there is no necessity here for that"].

His saying: {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ}: its like preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «يوم», and the pronoun in «فيه» refers to the day. It was said: it refers to the gathering indicated by the verb, because it is a rebuttal of those who deny the resurrection.

His saying: {الذين خسروا}: there are six aspects on it. One of them: that it is accusative by implying «أذمُّ» (I censure); al-Zamakhsharī assumed it as «أريد» (I mean), and this is not evident. The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ of which the predication is made by His saying {فَهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}, the fāʾ being added in its khabar because of the conditional meaning it contains; al-Zajjāj said this, as if it were said: whoever loses himself does not believe. The third: that it is genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «المكذبين». The fourth: that it is a badal of them; these two aspects are far-fetched. The fifth: that it is accusative as a badal of the pronoun of the person addressed. You have learned what is wrong with this more than once, namely: may a whole-for-whole badal be substituted for a pronoun of the present [first or second person] without encompassing and comprehensiveness, or not? Al-Akhfash's school permits it; we have mentioned the majority's proof, his proofs and how they were answered, so there is no need to repeat them. Al-Mubarrad rejected his school on the grounds that substitution from the pronoun of address is not permissible, just as «مررت بك زيدٍ» (I passed by you, Zayd) is not permissible. This is strange, because he adduced as evidence the very point in dispute, namely «مررت بك زيدٍ». Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected his rebuttal, saying: "What is in the verse differs from the example, because the benefit of the badal results from the second [term]; if you say «مررت بك زيدٍ», there is no benefit in the second. His saying {لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ}, however, is suitable for addressing all people, so substituting «الذين» for the pronoun tells us that they are the ones specially intended by the address, and they were singled out by way of threat; and this comes as a substitution of the part for the whole."

The Shaykh said: "This rebuttal is not good, because if we make «ليجمعنَّكم» suitable for addressing all people, «الذين» would be a part-for-whole badal, and it would then need a pronoun, its implied form being: «خسروا أنفسهم منهم» (those of them who lost themselves). And his saying "so substituting «الذين» for the pronoun tells us that they are the ones specially intended by the address, and they were singled out by way of threat" requires it to be a whole-for-whole badal; so the beginning of his statement contradicts its end, because in terms of suitability it is a part-for-whole badal, and in terms of the address being specific to them it is a whole-for-whole badal; so they contradict each other." I say: how far it is from contradiction! For the substitution of the part for the whole is among the specifiers (mukhaṣṣiṣāt), like specification by adjective, by the limit (ghāya) and by condition; the scholars have stated this explicitly. Once this is established, the thing substituted for is, with respect to the wording, general on the surface, while in meaning only what the speaker intended is meant by it. So if there came, for example, «اقتلوا المشركين بني فلان» (kill the polytheists, the tribe of so-and-so), «المشركين» is suitable for every polytheist with respect to the wording, but what is meant by it is the tribe of so-and-so; the generality is in the wording and the specificity in the meaning. Likewise Abū Muḥammad's saying "suitable for addressing people" means that it includes them in wording; and his saying "so substituting [for] the pronoun tells us…" to the end — this is the specifier. So no contradiction arises at all, and this is established in the science of the principles of jurisprudence (uṣūl al-fiqh).

The sixth: that it is nominative by way of censure; al-Zamakhsharī said this. His wording on it and on the first aspect is: "accusative by way of censure, or nominative, i.e. I mean those who lost themselves, or you [are those who] lost themselves." End. I say: he assumed the mubtadaʾ as «أنتم» only so that it would be linked with His saying «ليجمعنَّكم»; and His saying «خسروا أنفسهم» is in consideration of the relative noun. Had he said «أنتم الذين خسروا أنفسهم» in consideration of the address, it would be permissible; you say «أنت الذي قعد» (you are the one who sat), and, if you wish, «قَعَدْت» (… who sat [lit. you sat]).

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَهُ مَا سَكَنَ}: a clause made of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). There are two views on it. The more evident of them: that it is a resumptive (istiʾnāf) statement reporting that. The second: that it is in the position of accusative, coordinated with His saying «لله», i.e. with the clause related [as speech] by «قل», i.e. say: it belongs to Allah, and say: to Him belongs whatever dwells. «ما» is a relative meaning "that which", and nothing else is permissible. As for «سَكَنْ», it was said: its meaning is: is established and settled; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. It was also said: it is from «سَكَن» as the opposite of «تَحَرَّك» (moved). On the first [view] there is no omission in the noble verse. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is made transitive with «في», as in His saying: {وَسَكَنتُمْ فِي مساكن الذين ظلموا أَنفُسَهُمْ} [Ibrāhīm: 45]." Ibn ʿAṭiyya preferred this interpretation. On the second, they disagreed: some of them said that there must be something omitted because the meaning is understood, and assumed that omitted element as a conjoined term, saying: its implied form is «وله ما سكن وما تحرك» (to Him belongs whatever is still and whatever moves), as in His saying in another place: {تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81], i.e. "and the cold"; the omission of the conjoined term is widespread in their speech; and he recited:
187 - 2- كأنَّ الحصى مِنْ خلفِها وأمامِها ... إذا نَجَلَتْهُ رِجْلُها خَذْفُ أَعْسَرا
(As if the pebbles behind her and in front of her, when her foot kicks them away, were the flinging of a left-handed man.)
187 - 3- فما كان بين الخيرِ لو جاء سالماً ... أبو حُجُرٍ إلا ليلٍ قلائلُ
(There would have been, between the good [and me], had Abū Ḥujur come safely, only a few nights.)
He means: her foot and her hand; and: between the good and me. Others said: there is no omission, because everything that moves may become still. It was also said: because what moves is fewer and what is still is more, so it was preferred for mention.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {إِنْ عَصَيْتُ}: a condition whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because what precedes indicates it; and for that reason the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) was brought in the past. There are two aspects regarding this conditional clause. One of them: that it is parenthetical between the verb, namely «أخاف», and its object, namely «عذاب». The second: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The Shaykh said: "As if it were said: I fear, while disobeying my Lord"; there is scrutiny in this, since the meaning rejects it. «أخاف» and what is within its scope is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», and «إنَّ» and what is within its scope is in the position of accusative by «قل».

semin-durr:99-99.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَأَخْرَجْنَا}: In it is iltifāt (a shift of person) from the third person to the first person with the nūn of majesty. The bāʾ in «به» is causal. His words {نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ}: it was said: what is meant is everything called "plants" in the language. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The provision of everything, i.e. what is fit to be nourishment for everything, so it is restricted to what is used as nourishment." Al-Ṭabarī said: "It is everything that grows, of animals, plants and minerals, because all of that is nourished by water." A point of i'rab technique follows from this: if we adopt a view other than al-Farrāʾ's, the iḍāfa (genitive construct) reverts in meaning to the iḍāfa of something like an adjective to the thing it qualifies, since the meaning then becomes: "So We brought forth by it every growing thing", for al-nabāt is in the sense of al-munbat (that which is made to grow), and is not a maṣdar (verbal noun) as it is in {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]. And if we adopt al-Farrāʾ's view, the iḍāfa is an iḍāfa between two distinct things, since the meaning becomes: the nourishment of everything, or its provision. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] transmitted from al-Farrāʾ only this view, but al-Farrāʾ has the two aforementioned views on this verse, for he said: "The provision of everything", and he said: "Thus it came in the exegesis, and it is the [proper] sense of the speech; and it may be permissible in Arabic to put al-nabāt in construct with «كل شيء» while by «كل شيء» you also mean the plants, so it would be like His words {حَقُّ اليقين} [al-Wāqiʿa: 95], where al-yaqīn is al-ḥaqq."
His words: {فَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهُ}: There are two aspects regarding the hāʾ. One of them: that it refers back to al-nabāt; this is the apparent one, and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else; «مِنْ» is then in its basic sense of the beginning of extent, or it is partitive — but that is not strong. The second: that it refers back to the water, and «مِنْ» is causal. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned the two aspects, saying: "«وأخرجنا منه», i.e. because of it. And it is permissible for the hāʾ in «منه» to refer back to al-nabāt, and that is more likely. On the first [view] «فأخرجنا» is a badal (substitute) of the first «أخرجنا»." That is, in meaning the informing by this second clause suffices; otherwise a technical badal is not apparent, and the apparent view is that «فأخرجنا» is conjoined to the first «فأخرجنا». The Shaykh said: "Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be a badal of فأخرجنا." I say: he only made it a badal on the basis of the pronoun in «منه» referring back to the water, so it is not correct to report from him that he made it a badal unconditionally, since being a badal is not conceivable when the hāʾ in «منه» is made to refer back to al-nabāt.
And al-khaḍir means al-akhḍar (green), like ʿawir and aʿwar. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: "One says: ikhḍarra yakhḍarru, so it is khaḍir and akhḍar, like iʿwarra, so it is ʿawir and aʿwar." And al-khuḍra is one of the colours; it lies between white and black, but it is closer to black, and for this reason "black" has been applied to "green" and vice versa; from it is «سَواد العراق» ("the blackness of Iraq") because of the greenness of its land with trees.
And the Exalted said: {مُدْهَآمَّتَانِ} [al-Raḥmān: 64], i.e. intensely dark because of their abundant watering. Al-mukhāḍara: selling green produce and fruits before they ripen. Al-khaḍīra: a palm tree whose unripe dates fall while still green. And his words, peace be upon him: «إياكم وخضراءَ الدِّمَن» ("Beware of the green growth of the dung-heaps") — he himself, peace be upon him, explained it with his words: «المرأة الحسناء في المنبت السوء» ("the beautiful woman of bad stock"); al-diman: the places where refuse and filth are thrown, in which there may grow what the onlooker finds pleasing.
His words: {نُّخْرِجُ مِنْهُ}, i.e. from al-khaḍir. The majority read «نُخْرج», ascribed to the pronoun of the One who glorifies Himself. Ibn Muḥayṣin and al-Aʿmash read «يخرج» with the yāʾ of the third person, in the passive, with «حَبٌّ» standing in place of its agent (nāʾib fāʿil). On both readings the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «خَضِراً», and this is the apparent view; they also allowed it to be resumptive. And «متراكب», nominative and accusative [in the two readings], is an adjective of «حَبّ» under the two considerations.
His words: {وَمِنَ النخل مِن طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ}: Several aspects are permissible in this clause. The first, and it is the best: that «من النخل» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «من طَلْعِها» a badal of part from whole with repetition of the governing word, so it is like His words: {لَّقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ الله أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُو الله} [al-Mumtaḥana: 6] [Translator's note: the source gives "al-Mumtaḥana: 6"; the wording quoted matches al-Aḥzāb: 21, while al-Mumtaḥana: 6 reads «لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِيهِمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُو اللَّهَ»], and «قِنْوان» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); this is a nominal clause conjoined to the verbal clause before it. The second: that «قِنْوان» is a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition-phrase before it, namely «من النخل», with «من طلعها» as badal as preceded; that is on the opinion of al-Akhfash. The third: that the case belongs to the topic of tanāzuʿ (two governors competing for one word), meaning that each of the two preposition-phrases seeks قنوان as its fāʿil, on al-Akhfash's opinion: if you make the second govern — the preferred view of the Basrans — you imply a pronoun in the first, and if you make the first govern — the preferred view of the Kufans — you imply a pronoun in the second. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The other aspect is that «قِنْوان» is nominative as the fāʿil of «من طلعها», so in «من النخل» there is [a pronoun explained by قنوان]; and if you make «قنوان» nominative by His words «ومن النخل», on the view of whoever makes the first of the two verbs govern, it is permissible, and in «من طلعها» there is a nominative pronoun." I say: by his words "as the fāʿil of «من طلعها»" he pointed to making the second govern.
The fourth: that «قنوان» is a mubtadaʾ and «من طلعها» the khabar, and in «من النخل» there is [something implied], its implied form being: "and there grew from the palms something", or "fruit", so «من طلعها» is a badal from it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it is a statement that is not sound, because after he made «مِنْ طلعها» the khabar, how can it be made a badal? If it is said: he makes it a badal from it because «من النخل» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ — the answer is that he had already put forward that aspect and set it against this one, so this one must be other than it; for he said before that: "There are two aspects in its being nominative. One of them: it is a mubtadaʾ, and there are two aspects regarding its khabar; one of them is «من النخل», with «من طَلْعِها» a badal with repetition of the preposition."
The Shaykh said: "This is an i'rab in which there is confusion."
The fifth: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted because «أخرجنا» indicates it, its implied form being: "and brought forth from the spathes of the palm are clusters." This is the text of al-Zamakhsharī, and it is, as the Shaykh said, unnecessary, because the clause is self-sufficient in informing without it.
The sixth: that «من النخل» is attached to an implied verb, and {مِن طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ} is a nominal clause in the position of the object of «نخرج». Ibn ʿAṭiyya held this, for he said: "«ومن النخل», its implied form being «ونُخْرِجُ من النخل», and «من طلعها قنوان» is a mubtadaʾ with its khabar fronted, and the clause is in the position of the object of «نخرج»." The Shaykh said: "This is a mistake, because with a verb transitive to one object a clause does not occur in the position of its object, unless the verb is one that can be suspended (yuʿallaq) and there is in the clause a barrier preventing it from governing any of its single components, as explained in grammar; and «نُخْرج» is not one of those that are suspended, and there is nothing in the clause that prevents governing its components, since if the verb were given power over any of the components of the clause the construction would be «ونخرج من النخل مِنْ طَلْعِها قنواناً», with the accusative as direct object."
And the Shaykh said: "Whoever reads «يُخْرَج منه حب متراكب», it is permissible for His words {وَمِنَ النخل مِن طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ} to be conjoined to it, like: «يُضرب في الدار زيد وفي السوق عمرو»" — meaning that «قنوان» is conjoined to «حب» and «من النخل» to «منه». Then he said: "And it is permissible for it to be a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and that is the more likely." Al-qinwān is the plural of «قِنْو», as al-ṣinwān is the plural of ṣinw. Al-qinw: al-ʿidhq, with kasra of the ʿayn, which is the cluster of the palm tree; it is also called al-kibāsa. Imruʾ al-Qays said: 2015 - وفَرْعٍ يُغَشِّي المَتْنَ أسودَ فاحِمٍ ... أثيثٍ كقِنْو النخلة المُتَعَثْكِل
(And long hair covering the back, coal-black, thick like the branching cluster of the palm.)
And he also said:
2016 - سوامِقُ جَبَّارٍ أَثِيثٍ فروعُه ... وعالَيْنَ قِنْواناً من البُسْر أحمرا
(Lofty ones of a tall [palm], dense in its branches, raising up clusters of red unripe dates.)
And al-qinwān is a broken plural. Abū ʿAlī said: "The kasra in قِنْوان is not the one that was in قِنْو, because that one was deleted in the broken plural and another kasra replaced it, just as the kasra of «هِجان» as a plural is reckoned to be changed from its kasra as a singular; so the kasra of هِجان as a plural is like the kasra of ظِراف." Al-Wāḥidī said: "This is something clarified by the ḍamma at the end of «منصور» on the view of whoever says «يا حارُ»" — meaning that the ḍamma is not the one that was in it/ on the view of whoever says «يا حارِ», meaning with kasra. There are [several] dialectal forms of it: the dialect of the Ḥijāz is «قِنْوان» with kasra of the qāf, and it is the reading of the majority. Al-Aʿmash, al-Ḥubāb from Abū ʿAmr, and al-Aʿraj read it with ḍamma; al-Sulamī related it from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib; it is the dialect of Qays. Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted the reverse of this, making the ḍamma the dialect of the Ḥijāz, for he said: "It was related from al-Aʿraj [that he read] ḍamma of the qāf, as the plural of «قُنو» with ḍamma of the qāf." Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is the dialect of Qays and the people of the Ḥijāz, and the kasra is better known among the Arabs."
The third dialectal form: qanwān with fatḥa of the qāf; it is the reading of Abū ʿAmr in the transmission of Hārūn from him. Ibn Jinnī explained it as a collective noun (ism jamʿ) of qinw, not a plural, since among the plural patterns there is none on the measure faʿlān with fatḥa of the fāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī compared it with rakb, and Abū al-Baqāʾ with al-bāqir; Abū al-Baqāʾ's comparison is better, because there is no disagreement about al-bāqir being a collective noun, whereas regarding rakb there is a well-known disagreement on the part of Abū al-Ḥasan [al-Akhfash]. Something else also indicates this: kasra and ḍamma of the qāf have been heard in the singular, and the plural came on both of them, whereas fatḥa did not occur in the singular.
The fourth dialectal form: qunyān with ḍamma of the qāf with yāʾ instead of wāw. The fifth: qinyān with kasra of the qāf, also with the bāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source, «مع الباء»; evidently a misprint for «الياء» (yāʾ)]; these two are the dialects of Tamīm and Rabīʿa. As for the singular, they do not say it with yāʾ at all but with wāw, whether they read the qāf with kasra or ḍamma: they say only qinw and qunw, and do not say qiny or quny; so the plural differs from its singular in root material, which is strange.
There is disagreement about what «القِنْو» denotes. It was said: it is the palm-pith (al-jummār); this is almost a mistake — how could it be described as being near, i.e. close to picking, when the jummār is only in the heart of the palm? The well-known view is that it is the cluster (al-ʿidhq), as preceded. Abū ʿUbayd said: "When you put qinw in the dual you say qinwāni with kasra of the nūn; then its plural came on the wording of the dual, like ṣinw and ṣinwān, with the case-inflection on the nūn in the plural; and these two have no parallel in the speech of the Arabs." He [the poet] said:
2017 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ومالَ بقِنْوانٍ مِنَ البُسْرِ أحمرا
(… and it bent down with clusters of red unripe dates.)
I say: when one pauses on «قنوان» as a nominative dual and on «قنوان» as a plural, verbal ambiguity occurs: do you not see that if you said «عندي قنوان» in pause, it would admit what I mentioned of dual and plural? When you connect, the difference arises, for you put the case-inflection on the nūn in its plural state, like ghirbān and ṣirdān, with kasra of the nūn in the dual.
The difference also arises in other ways, among them: the change of the alif into yāʾ in the accusative and genitive in the dual, as in رأيت قِنْوَيْك وصِنْويك and مررت بقنويك وصنويك. Among them: the deletion of the nūn of the dual in construct, and the retention of the nūn in the plural, as in جاء قنواك وصنواك and قنوانك وصنوانك. Among them: in the relative adjective (nisba), for you delete the two markers of the dual and say قِنْوَيّ and صِنْوَي, but you do not delete the alif or the nūn when you mean the plural; rather you say قِنْوانيّ and صِنْواني. These two words, as broken plurals, resemble sound plurals, in that each of them has two added markers attached to its end in the plural state without the structure of the singular changing with them; and the difference is what I have set out for you. Moreover, the plurality of قنوان and صنوان we understood only from the pattern fiʿlān, not from the two additions — unlike al-zaydīn (the Zayds), where we understood the plurality from them. This section I have mentioned is among the fine points of the sciences of i'rab, morphology and lexicon.
Al-Rāghib said, after mentioning that it is the cluster: "And al-qanāt (the spear-shaft) resembles al-qinw in that both are branches. As for the qanāt in which water flows, it was called that because it resembles the spear-shaft in line and extension. And it was said: its origin is from qanaytu al-shayʾ, when you store it, because it stores water. And it was said: it is from qānāhu, i.e. mixed with it. He said — meaning Imruʾ al-Qays —/:
2018 - كبِكْرِ مُقاناةِ البياضِ بصُفْرةٍ ... غَذَاها نُمَيْرُ الماءِ غيرَ مُحَلَّلِ
(Like the first pearl [or ostrich egg] whose whiteness is mixed with yellow, nourished by pure, wholesome water not muddied by visitors.)
As for «القنا», which is the curvature of the nose, it is compared in shape to the spear-shaft; one says: a man aqnā and a woman qanwāʾ, like aḥmar and ḥamrāʾ." And al-ṭalʿ: the first thing that comes out of the palm in its sheaths. Abū ʿUbayd said: "Al-ṭalʿ: the spathe (al-kufurrā) before it splits open to reveal the inflorescence (al-ighrīḍ), and al-ighrīḍ is [also] called ṭalʿ. One says: aṭlaʿat al-nakhla when it puts forth its ṭalʿ, tuṭliʿu iṭlāʿan; and ṭalaʿa al-ṭalʿu yaṭluʿu ṭulūʿan — so they distinguished between the two ascriptions." And someone recited to me, regarding the stages of what the palm bears, the poet's saying:
2019 - إن شِئْتَ أن تَضْبِطَ يا خَليلُ ... أسماءَ ما تُثْمِرُه النخيلُ
فاسمَعْه مَوْصوفاً على ما أذكرُ ... طَلْعٌ وبعده خَلال يظهر
وبَلَحٌ ثم يليه بُسْرُ ... ورُطَب تجنيه ثم تَمْرُ
فهذه أنواعُها يا صاحِ ... مضبوطةً عن صاحب الصِّحاح
(If you wish, O friend, to fix the names of what the palms bear, hear it described as I mention: ṭalʿ, and after it khalāl appears, then balaḥ, then busr follows it, and ruṭab which you pick, then tamr. These are its kinds, O companion, fixed on the authority of the author of al-Ṣiḥāḥ.)
His words: «وجنَّات»: The majority read the tāʾ of «جنات» with kasra, because it is accusative, conjoined to نبات, i.e. "So We brought forth by the water the plants and gardens". It is the conjoining of the specific to the general, to honour these two kinds above others, like the words of the Exalted: {وملائكته وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ} [al-Baqara: 98]. On this view His words {وَمِنَ النخل مِن طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ} are a parenthetical clause; this clause was brought as parenthetical and put in the form of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) only to magnify the favour in it, because it is among the greatest staples of the Arabs, since it combines delicacy and staple food. It is also permissible for «جنات» to be accusative conjoined to «خضراً». Al-Zamakhsharī allowed — and made it the best — that it is accusative by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), like His words «والمقيمي الصلاة»; he said: "because of the excellence of these two kinds." His words make it understood that the well-known reading according to him is with «جنات» in the nominative, and the reading with its accusative is anomalous (shādhdha), for the first thing he mentioned was the justification of the nominative, as will come; then he said: "And «وجنات» was read in the accusative," and mentioned the two aforementioned aspects.
Al-Aʿmash, Muḥammad ibn Abī Laylā, and Abū Bakr in one transmission from him from ʿĀṣim read «وجنات» in the nominative, and there are three aspects in it. The first: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar omitted. The expressions of the grammarians differed in its implied form: some of them implied it fronted, and some implied it postponed. Al-Zamakhsharī implied it fronted, i.e. "and there are gardens"; Abū al-Baqāʾ implied it as "and from the vine are gardens", and this is a good implied form because it corresponds to His words «ومن النخل», i.e. from the palms such-and-such and from the vine such-and-such; al-Naḥḥās implied it as "and they have gardens", and Ibn ʿAṭiyya as "and you have gardens". Its parallel is the reading {وَحُورٌ عِينٌ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 22] after His words: {يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُّخَلَّدُونَ بِأَكوابٍ}, i.e. and they have wide-eyed houris; Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ agreed on the permissibility of the like of this.
And [some] implied it postponed, saying: i.e. and gardens of grapes We brought forth. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "And His earlier words «فأخرجنا» indicate its implied form, as you say: أكرمت عبد الله وأخوه, i.e. وأخوه أكرمته." I say: Ibn al-Anbārī preceded him to this implied form, for he said: "«الجناتُ» is made nominative by something implied after it, whose interpretation is: and gardens of grapes We brought them forth; so it runs like the Arabs' saying «أكرمت عبدَ الله وأخوه», meaning: وأخوه أكرمته. Al-Farazdaq said:
2020 - غداةَ أحلَّتْ لابنِ أَصْرَمَ طَعْنَةٌ ... حصينٍ عَبيطاتِ السَّدائِفِ والخمرُ
(On the morning when a spear-thrust made lawful for Ibn Aṣram — Ḥuṣayn — the fresh slices of hump-fat, and wine.)
So he put «الخمر» in the nominative though it is an object, in the sense: and wine, the spear-thrust made it lawful." The second aspect: that it is nominative conjoined to «قنوان», giving preponderance to proximity (jiwār), as the poet said:
2021 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وزجَّجْنَ الحواجبَ والعيونا
(… and they plucked thin the eyebrows and the eyes.)
He conjoined «العيون» to «الحواجب», giving preponderance to proximity, though eyes are not plucked — just as gardens of grapes are not from the spathes. This too is the explicit doctrine of Ibn al-Anbārī, so he has two doctrines regarding the verse. In sum, the [argument from] proximity is weak, and it has preceded that it is among the special properties of the naʿt (adjective).
The third: that it is conjoined to «قنوان». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the sense: surrounded [by] or brought forth from the palms are clusters, and gardens of grapes, i.e. of the plants of grapes." The Shaykh said: "This conjoining is on the basis that no restriction 'from the palms' is regarded in it, as if He said: and from the palms are low-hanging clusters, and gardens of grapes existing; as you say: «من بني تميم رجل عاقل ورجل من قريش منطلقان»." I say: al-Ṭabarī also mentioned this aspect, I mean its being conjoined to «قنوان», and Ibn ʿAṭiyya declared it weak, as though what was apparent to Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] of the meaning referred to was not apparent to him. Abū al-Baqāʾ forbade its being conjoined to «قنوان», saying: "Because grapes do not come out of the palm." Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim rejected this reading. Abū Ḥātim said: "This reading is impossible, because gardens of grapes are not from the palms." I say: the answer to Abū al-Baqāʾ is in what al-Zamakhsharī said, and the answer to Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim is in the justification of the nominative that preceded. And «من أعناب» is an adjective of جنات, so it is in the position of the nominative or accusative according to the two readings, and is attached to something omitted.
His words: {والزيتون والرمان}: No one read them except in the accusative. Their accusative is either by conjunction to جنات or to نبات; this is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words, for he said: "And «وجنات» was read in the accusative, conjoined to «نباتَ كل شيء», i.e. and We brought forth by it gardens of grapes, / and likewise His words: والزيتونَ والرُّمَّان."
Abū al-Baqāʾ stated this explicitly, saying: "And جنات in the accusative conjoined to نبات, and likewise: الزيتونَ والرمانَ." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Conjoined to «حَبَّاً»; and it was said: to «نبات»." It has preceded for you that in the third conjoined item and beyond there are two possibilities. One of them: conjoining it to what immediately precedes it. The second: conjoining it to the first, as in مررت بزيدٍ وعمروٍ وخالد: Khālid may be conjoined to Zayd or to ʿAmr. And it has preceded that the benefit of the disagreement appears in something like «مررت بك وبزيد وبعمرو»: if you make it conjoined to the first, the bāʾ is required; otherwise it is [merely] permissible.
Al-zaytūn: its measure is fayʿūl, so the yāʾ is augmented [Translator's note: the source says «فالتاءُ مزيدةٌ» ("so the tāʾ is augmented"); on the measure fayʿūl the augment is the yāʾ, so this appears to be a misprint for «فالياء»], and the nūn is radical, because that one drops in derivation and this one remains: they said ʾarḍ zatina, i.e. having many olive trees. So it is a parallel of qayṣūm; and also because [the pattern] faʿlūl is non-existent or rare. One should not imagine that its tāʾ is radical and its nūn augmented on the evidence of al-zayt (oil), for they are two different roots, even though oil is pressed from it. One says: zāta ṭaʿāmahu, i.e. put oil in it; and zāta raʾsahu, i.e. anointed it with it; and izdāta, i.e. anointed himself — the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form was changed to dāl after the zāy, as in izdajara and izdāna. And al-rummān: its measure is fuʿʿāl, its nūn radical, so it is a parallel of ʿunnāb and ḥummāḍ, because of their saying ʾarḍ ramina, i.e. having many of it.
His words: {مُشْتَبِهاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from «الرمان», because of its proximity, with the ḥāl of the first omitted, its implied form being: and the pomegranate, resembling — the meaning of resemblance being in colour and non-resemblance in taste. And it was said: it is a ḥāl from the first, with the ḥāl of the second omitted; this is like what preceded for you about the omitted khabar, as in {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62]. Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, for he said: "And the olive, resembling and not resembling, and the pomegranate likewise, like his saying:
2022 - رماني بأمرٍ كنت منه ووالدي ... بريئاً. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(He accused me of a matter of which I and my father were innocent …)"
The Shaykh said: "On his view the implied form of the verse is: I was innocent of it, and my father likewise, i.e. innocent. But what he mentioned is not necessarily the case in the verse, because بريئاً is on the measure faʿīl like ṣadīq and rafīq, so it may correctly be predicated of the singular, the dual and the plural; thus «بريئاً» may be the khabar of «كان», with the pronoun and the overt noun conjoined to it sharing in it, since it may be a khabar of both, while it may not be a ḥāl of both, since if it were, the construction would be «مشتبهين وغير مشتبهين»." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "A ḥāl of الرمان and of the whole." If he meant in meaning, it is correct, and it is by omission as preceded; if he meant technically, it is nothing, because agreement would then be required.
The majority read «مشتبهاً», and it was read anomalously «متشابهاً وغير متشابه», like the second; they have one meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Like your saying: ishtabaha al-shayʾāni and tashābahā, like istawayā and tasāwayā; the iftiʿāl and tafāʿul forms often share [meaning]." End of quote. Moreover, He combined them in this verse in His words «مشتبهاً وغير متشابه».
His words: {إلى ثَمَرِهِ}: attached to «انظروا», which is in the sense of seeing; it was made transitive with إلى only because of the reflection it implies.
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «ثُمُرِه» with two ḍammas, and the rest with two fatḥas; and it was read anomalously with ḍamma of the first and sukūn of the second.
As for the reading of the two brothers, it admits four aspects. The first: that it is a singular noun, like ṭunub and ʿunuq. The second: that it is a plural of a plural: thumur is the plural of thimār, and thimār the plural of thamara; that is like ukum, the plural of ikām, and ikām the plural of akama; so it is a parallel of kuthbān and kuthub. The third: that it is the plural of thamar, as they said asad and usud. The fourth: that it is the plural of thamara. Al-Fārisī said: "It is best that it be the plural of thamara, like khashaba and khushub, and akama and ukum; its parallel among weak-lettered words: lāba and lūb, nāqa and nūq, sāḥa and sūḥ."
As for the reading of the majority, al-thamar is a generic noun whose singular is thamara, like shajar and shajara, baqar and baqara, jazar and jazara. As for the reading with sukūn, it is a lightening of the reading of the two brothers; and it was said: rather it is the plural of thamara, like budn, plural of badana. Someone transmitted that thamura is said, on the measure of samura; by analogy its [collective] would then be thamur, like samur, by deleting the tāʾ when its plural is intended, and the analogical broken plural would be athmār, like ʿaḍud and aʿḍād. Abū ʿAmr read the one in Sūrat al-Kahf with ḍamma and sukūn of the mīm, so this reading here is eloquent; Abū ʿAmr's analogy would have been to read both the same way, were it not that reading is based on transmission. Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Qunbul read «خُشْب», and the rest with ḍamma, so this reading is a parallel of that one. This disagreement — I mean in «ثَمَرِه» — and the same justification apply in Sūrat Yā-Sīn. As for the one in Sūrat al-Kahf, there are three readings in it: ʿĀṣim reads it with two fatḥas as he reads it in this sūra and in Yā-Sīn, so he kept to one practice; the two brothers read it with two ḍammas in the three sūras,/ so they kept to one practice; as for Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir, they read what is in al-Anʿām and Yā-Sīn with two fatḥas and what is in al-Kahf with two ḍammas; and as for Abū ʿAmr, he read what is in al-Anʿām and Yā-Sīn with two fatḥas and what is in al-Kahf with a ḍamma and sukūn. They mentioned, in justifying the two ḍammas in al-Kahf, what cannot apply in the two [other] sūras: they said regarding al-Kahf: al-thumur with ḍamma is wealth, and with fatḥa what is eaten.
His words: {إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ}: an adverb (ẓarf) for His words «انظروا». It may be purely adverbial, or conditional with its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) omitted, or fronted according to whoever holds that view, i.e. when it bears fruit, look at it.
His words: {وَيَنْعِهِ}: The majority read «ينعه» with fatḥa of the yāʾ and sukūn of the nūn. Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with ḍamma of the yāʾ, and it is the reading of Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Yamānī read: «يانعة» [Translator's note: so in the source; the variant is usually cited as «ويانِعِه»], and al-Zamakhsharī attributed it to Ibn Muḥayṣin, so he may have two readings. Al-yanʿ with fatḥa and ḍamma is a maṣdar (verbal noun): yanaʿat al-thamara, i.e. ripened; the fatḥa is the dialect of the Ḥijāz and the ḍamma the dialect of some of Najd; one also says yunuʿ and yunūʿ, with a wāw after two ḍammas. And it was said: al-yanʿ with fatḥa is the plural of yāniʿ, like tājir and tajr, ṣāḥib and ṣaḥb. One says yanaʿat al-thamara and aynaʿat, as triliteral and quadriliteral, with the same meaning. Al-Ḥajjāj said: «أرى رؤوساً قد أينعت وحان قطافها» ("I see heads that have ripened and whose time for plucking has come").
And yāniʿ is an active participle. And it was said: aynaʿat al-thamara and yanaʿat mean "it turned red"; al-Farrāʾ said this; from it is the ḥadīth on mutual imprecation (al-mulāʿana): «إنْ وَلَدَتْهُ أحمرَ مثلَ اليَنَعَة» ("If she bears him red like the yanaʿa"), which is a red bead; it was said: it is carnelian or a kind of it. One says: yanaʿat tayniʿu, with fatḥa of the ʿayn in the past and kasra in the imperfect; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayd, and he recited:
2023 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... حولها الزيتونُ قد يَنَعَا
(… around it the olives have ripened.)
Al-Layth said the reverse of this, i.e. with kasra in the past and fatḥa in the imperfect. The closing of this verse with His words «لقوم يؤمنون» is fitting because what preceded indicates His oneness and His bringing into being the various made things, which must have a Disposer, even though they grow from a single earth and are watered with a single water; and these proofs benefit only the believers who reflect, not others.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَغَيْرَ الله}: the first object of «أتَّخِذُ», and «وليَّاً» is the second object. He put the first object before its verb only for a meaning, namely the denial that anyone other than Allah should be taken as a protector — not the denial of taking a protector. Similar to it is your saying to someone who insults Zayd while he deserves honour: «أزيداً أهنت» (is it Zayd you insulted?!): you deny that someone like him should be insulted. This has preceded with clarification at His saying: {أَأَنتَ قُلتَ لِلنَّاسِ} [al-Māʾida: 116]. Similar to it are: {أَغَيْرَ الله أَبْغِي رَبّاً} [al-Anʿām: 164] [written in the text: 114], {أَفَغَيْرَ الله تأمروني أَعْبُدُ} [al-Zumar: 64], {ءَآللَّهُ أَذِنَ لَكُمْ} [Yūnus: 59], {ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ} [al-Anʿām: 143] [written in the text: 13]; and this is frequent. «أتخذ» may also be transitive to one object, so «غيرَ» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «وليَّاً», because it is originally an adjective of it. It may not be an exception at all — so Abū al-Baqāʾ forbade it, without explaining why. What appears is that the obstacle is its preceding the thing excepted from «في لامعنى» [Translator's note: so in the text; probably «في المعنى» "in meaning", or a corruption of «في اللفظ» "in the wording"], namely «وليَّاً». As for the meaning, it does not reject the exception, because the interrogative is not meant literally; rather denial is meant by it, so it is as though it were said: I do not take a protector other than Allah — and had it been said thus, it would be correct. So it appears that the obstacle in his view is only the precedence over the thing excepted from; but that is permissible, even if rare, and of it is:
187 - 4- وما ليَ آل أحمدَ شيعةٌ ... وما لي إلا مَشْعبَ الحقِّ مَشْعَبُ
(I have no party but the family of Aḥmad, and I have no path but the path of truth.) [Translator's note: the first hemistich is printed without «إلا»; the well-known form is «وما ليَ إلا آلَ أحمدَ شيعةٌ», which is the form the gloss follows.]

The majority read «فاطرِ» in the genitive, and there are two analyses of it. One of them — held by al-Zamakhsharī, al-Ḥūfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya — is that it is an adjective of the word of majesty made genitive by «غير»; and the separation between the adjective and the qualified noun by this verbal clause and its object does no harm, because it is not foreign, since it governs the governing element of the qualified noun. The second — towards which Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined — is that it is a badal (substitute) of the name of Allah; it is as though he fled from separating the adjective from its qualified noun. If it is said: this applies to him with the badal too, for he has also separated the follower from what it follows — it is said: separation between the badal and what it substitutes for is easier, because the badal is in the intention of repeating the governing element, so it is closer to separation. His analysis has been preferred on another ground: «فاطر» is an active participle, and the meaning is not past so that its annexation would be non-genuine (ghayr maḥḍa), entailing the qualification of a definite noun by an indefinite, since it would be in the intention of separation from annexation. But one does not say: Allah is the Originator of the heavens and the earth in the past, so neither present nor future is meant [Translator's note: so in the text; the sequel indicates that the argument is that the past is not meant]; because the speech of Allah the Exalted is eternal, preceding the creation of the heavens, so what is meant by it is definitely the future. What indicates the permissibility of its being in the intention of tanwīn is what I will soon mention from Abū al-Baqāʾ.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it in the nominative, and its analysis is easy: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). Ibn ʿAṭiyya analysed it as a mubtadaʾ, so it needs a khabar to be assumed, whose indication is obscure — unlike assuming the mubtadaʾ, for that is the pronoun of the first [noun], i.e. «هو فاطر» (He is the Originator). It was read, irregularly (shādhdh), in the accusative, and Abū al-Baqāʾ analysed it in two ways. One of them: that it is a badal of «وليَّاً». He said: "The meaning on this view is: shall I make the Originator of the heavens and the earth other than Allah?" — so he assumed; and there is scrutiny in this, for he made the first object, namely «غير الله», a second object, and made the badal of the second object a first object, so the implied form is the reverse of the original construction.

The second: that it is an adjective of «وليَّاً». He said: "It may be an adjective of «وليَّاً», the tanwīn being intended." I say: by his saying "the tanwīn being intended" he means that the active participle governs by implication, so it is in the intention of separation, and for that reason it occurred as an adjective of an indefinite, as in His saying: {هذا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا} [al-Aḥqāf: 24].

This aspect is hardly valid, since the meaning would become: shall I take other than Allah as a protector, originator of the heavens…, and so on, thereby describing that protector as the Originator of the heavens. Al-Zuhrī read «فَطَر» as a past verb, and it is a clause in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the word of majesty, just as «فاطر» was its adjective in the majority's reading. On Abū al-Baqāʾ's opinion it may be an adjective of «ولياً». It may not be an adjective of the word of majesty, because the clause is indefinite.

«الفَطْر»: splitting in general; al-Rāghib restricted it to splitting [lengthwise] [Translator's note: so in the text; the restriction is not stated], and al-Wāḥidī restricted it to splitting a thing at its beginning. «الفَطْر» is also originating and making without precedent; and from it is «فاطر السماوات», i.e. He brought them into existence without a model to be imitated. From Ibn ʿAbbās: "I did not know what «فَطَر» and «فاطِر» meant until two Bedouins came to me disputing over a well, and one of them said: «أنا فَطَرْتُها», i.e. I made it and began it." One says: «فَطَرْتُ كذا فَطْراً، وفَطَر هو فُطوراً، وانفطر انفطاراً» [the text has «فَطَرْتُ كذا فَطْر هو فُطوراً»]; «فَطَرْتُ الشاة»: I milked it with two fingers; «فَطَرْت العجين»: I baked it at once. His saying, Exalted is He: {فِطْرَتَ الله التي فَطَرَ الناس عَلَيْهَا} [al-Rūm: 30] is an allusion from Him to what He originated (faṭara), i.e. invented and implanted in people, of knowledge of Him. So the fiṭra of Allah is what has been implanted of the perceptive faculty for knowing Him, and it is what is alluded to by His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ الله} [al-Zukhruf: 87]; and on it [is based]: «كلُّ مولودٍ يُولَدُ على الفطرة…» (every child is born upon the fiṭra…), the ḥadīth. This is the best I have heard in explaining "the fiṭra of Allah" in the Book and the Sunna.

His saying: {وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ وَلاَ يُطْعَمُ}: the well-known reading has the first in the active and the second in the passive, the pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted; the meaning is: and He provides and is not provided for; and it agrees with His saying, Exalted is He: {مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنْهُم مِّن رِّزْقٍ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطْعِمُونِ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 57]. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid ibn Jabr, al-Aʿmash, Abū Ḥaywa, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ in one transmission from him read «ولا يَطْعَمُ», with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ʿayn, meaning: and He does not eat; the pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Yamān al-ʿUmānī read «ولا يُطْعِم», with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn, like the first; so the two pronouns — I mean «هو» and the one latent in «يطعم» — refer to Allah the Exalted, and the pronoun in «ولا يُطْعِم» to the protector. Yaʿqūb, in the transmission of Ibn al-Maʾmūn, read:
«وهو يُطْعَمُ ولا يُطْعِم», with the first in the passive and the second in the active, the reverse of the well-known reading; and the three pronouns — I mean «هو» and the two latent in the two verbs — refer to the protector only, i.e. that protector is fed by others and does not feed anyone, because of his incapacity.

Al-Ashhab read: {وهو يُطْعِمُ ولا يُطْعِم}, with both in the active. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned two analyses of it, the second of them his own, for he said — after relating the reading —: "It was explained as meaning: and He feeds and does not ask to be fed. Al-Azharī related «أطعمت» in the sense of «استطعمت» (I asked for food), and similar to it is «أَفَدْت». It is possible that the meaning is: He feeds at one time and does not feed at another, according to what is beneficial, as when you say: He gives and withholds, straitens and expands, enriches and impoverishes." I say: [thus the Shaykh mentioned this reading; and the reading of al-Ashhab is] exactly like the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-ʿUmānī, with no difference between them; so he should have mentioned this reading for all of them; otherwise this gives the impression that they are two different readings, and it is not so.

It was read, irregularly: {يَطْعَم}, with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ʿayn, «ولا يُطْعِم», with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn, i.e. and he eats and does not feed others. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this reading and said: "The pronoun refers to the protector who is other than Allah." So these are six readings. In some of them — namely where the two verbs differ — there is, from the craft of badīʿ (rhetorical embellishment), tajnīs al-tashkīl (paronomasia by vowelling): that the vowelling is what distinguishes the two words. Usāma ibn Munqidh called it tajnīs al-taḥrīf (paronomasia by alteration), which is a hideous name, so naming it tajnīs al-tashkīl is more appropriate.

His saying: {مَنْ أَسْلَمَ}: «مَنْ» may be an indefinite qualified [by the following clause] standing in place of a collective noun, i.e. the first group that submitted; or it may be a relative, i.e. the first of the group which submitted. The pronoun in «أسلم» is singular either in consideration of the wording of the implied «فريق», or in consideration of the wording of «مَنْ». The discussion of «أول» and how it is annexed to a singular, with the interpretation mentioned in al-Baqara, has preceded.

His saying: {وَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ}: there are two interpretations of it. One of them is on the implication of the saying, i.e. and it was said to me: do not be. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Had it been conjoined to what precedes it in wording, He would have said: «وأنْ لا أكون»." Abū al-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, for he said: "«ولا تكونَنَّ»: and it was said to me: do not be; its meaning is: I was commanded to submit and forbidden from polytheism." The second: that it is conjoined to what is governed by «قل», construed according to the meaning; the meaning is: say: it was said to me: be the first to submit, and do not be among the polytheists. [So both] are construed upon the saying; but the first came without the wording of saying while having its meaning, so the second was construed according to the meaning. [It was said]: it is conjoined to «قل»: he was commanded to say such-and-such and forbidden from such-and-such.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِّن قَبْلِكَ}: It is attached to «كَذَّبَتْ». Abū al-Baqāʾ disallowed its being a naʿt (adjective) of «رسل» because it is [an expression of] time, and corporeal beings are not described by time. The discussion of this has preceded more than once; I treated it thoroughly in al-Baqara and mentioned it recently here at His saying {وَأَنْشَأْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْناً} [al-Anʿām: 6].
His saying: {وَأُوذُواْ}: Four views are possible on it. The most apparent: it is conjoined to His saying «كُذِّبَتْ», i.e. the messengers were denied and were harmed, and they bore all of that patiently. The second: it is conjoined to «صَبَروا», i.e. they were patient and they were harmed. The third — which is far-fetched — is that it is conjoined to «كُذِّبوا», so it falls within the ṣila of the maṣdar particle, the implied form being: they bore patiently their being denied and their being harmed. The fourth: it is resumptive. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is possible that the pause [Translator's note: printed «القف», evidently for «الوقف»] is complete at His saying «كُذِّبوا», and then He began anew, saying «أُوْذوا»."
The majority read {وأُوْذُوا} with a wāw after the hamza, from the quadriliteral آذى يؤذي. Ibn ʿĀmir read, in an irregular (shādhdh) transmission, «وأُذوا» without a wāw after the hamza; it is from the triliteral أَذَيْتُ الرجل, not from the quadriliteral «آذيت».
His saying: {حتى أَتَاهُمْ نَصْرُنَا}: The apparent view is that this limit is attached to His saying «فصبروا», i.e. the limit of their patience was Allah's helping them. If we make «وأوذوا» conjoined to it, it is the limit of both, which is very clear. If we make it resumptive, it is the limit of it alone; and if we make it conjoined to «كُذِّبَتْ», the limit is for the three. «النصر» is annexed to its fāʿil (agent), and its object is omitted, i.e. "our helping them". There is an iltifāt (shift) in it from the third-person pronoun to the first person, since before it is «بآيات الله» [Translator's note: printed «قلبه», evidently for «قبله»]; had it come accordingly, it would have been said «نَصْرُه». The benefit of the shift is ascribing the help to the first-person pronoun, which conveys majesty.
His saying: {وَلَقدْ جَآءَكَ مِن نَّبَإِ المرسلين}: There are two views on the fāʿil of «جاء». The first: it is latent (muḍmar), and they disagreed over what this pronoun refers to. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The correct view in my opinion is that one assumes: clarity and explanation." Al-Rummānī said: "Its implied form is: and there has come to you news." The Shaykh said: "What appears to me is that it refers to what the meaning of the preceding clause indicates, i.e. and there has come to you this report of the followers of the messengers denying the messengers, and the patience and the harm, until they were helped." On these views, «من نبأ المرسلين» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from that pronoun, and its governor is «جاء», since it governs the one it describes. The second: «من نبأ» is the fāʿil; al-Fārisī mentioned this. This only works for him on al-Akhfash's view, because he does not stipulate any condition for its being redundant; and this — as you see — is affirmative speech, and the noun governed by «مِنْ» is definite. It has also been considered weak in terms of meaning, in that not every report of the messengers came to him, because of His saying:
{مِنْهُم مَّن قَصَصْنَا عَلَيْكَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن لَّمْ نَقْصُصْ عَلَيْكَ} [Ghāfir: 78]; and the redundancy of «مِنْ» would lead to [the meaning] that all the reports came to him, because it is an annexed generic noun, whereas the matter is otherwise.
Al-Zamakhsharī did not address the fāʿil, except that he said: "And there has come to you, of the news of the messengers, some of their reports and stories" [Translator's note: printed «أبنائهم», evidently for «أنبائهم»]. This is an explanation of the meaning, not of the iʿrāb, since «مِنْ» cannot be a fāʿil. Nor may «من نبأ» be an adjective of an omitted fāʿil, i.e. "and there has come to you a report from the news of the messengers", because the fāʿil is never omitted, except in specific places that have been mentioned — so they said. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible according to all that «مِنْ» be an adjective of something omitted, because the fāʿil is not omitted; and a preposition, if not redundant, cannot be a fāʿil, because a preposition makes [a verb] transitive, and every verb governs the fāʿil without transitivity." By his saying "it cannot be a fāʿil" he means: the noun governed by that preposition cannot be; otherwise the preposition itself can never be a fāʿil at all.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن كَانَ كَبُرَ}: This is a condition whose answer is the fāʾ entering upon the second condition; the answer of the second is omitted, its implied form being: "then if you are able to seek, do so". Then the second condition and its answer were made the answer to the first condition. The like of this has preceded at His saying {فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم. . . . . فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلاَ خَوْفٌ} [al-Baqara: 38], and the precise treatment of it has preceded, except that the answer of the second is expressed there. As for «كان», there are two views on its noun (ism). The first: it is «إعراضهم», and «كَبُرَ» is a verbal clause in the position of the accusative as a khabar (predicate) placed before the noun. This is a disputed question: is it permissible to place the khabar of «كان» before its noun when it is a verb raising a latent (mustatir) pronoun, or not? As for when it is the khabar of a mubtadaʾ (subject), it is not permissible at all, lest it be confused with the chapter of the fāʿil (agent); but here confusion is excluded. The ground for prohibiting it is holding to the original rule. And «كَبُر», if it is said to be the khabar of «كان» — does it need «قد» to be implied or not? The apparent view is that it does not, because the past verb has frequently occurred as its khabar without «قد», in verse and prose. Some restrict this to «كان» and forbid it in its other sisters except with «قد», overt or implied. Among instances of this in the khabar of its sisters is the saying of al-Nābigha:
190 - 5- أمسَتْ خَلاءً وأمسى أهلُها احَتَمَلُوا ... أَخْنى عليها الذي أخنى على لُبَدِ
(It has become desolate, and its people have departed; that which destroyed Lubad has destroyed it.)
The second: its noun is the pronoun of the affair and the matter (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), and the verbal clause explains it, in the position of the accusative as the khabar; so «إعراضُهم» is nominative by «كَبُر», whereas on the first view it is by «كان». There is no pronoun in «كَبُر» on the second view, and there is one on the first. Like this in admitting these two views is His saying, the Exalted: {وَدَمَّرْنَا مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 137] and {وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنَا} [al-Jinn: 4]: «فرعون» may be the noun [of kāna] or the fāʿil, and likewise «سفيهُنا». Like it also is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
190 - 6- وإنْ تَكُ قد ساءَتْكِ مني خَليقةٌ ... فَسُلِّي ثيابي مِنْ ثيابك تَنْسُلِ
(If some trait of mine has displeased you, then pull my garments from yours and they will come apart.)
«خليقة» admits both. The explicit «قد» here supports the view of those who stipulate it. Is tanāzuʿ (contention of two governors for one noun) permissible in a construction like this? For each of «كان» and the verbs after it in these examples seeks the nominative in terms of meaning, and the conditions of governance are present. Long ago I asked the Shaykh about this, and he answered that it is forbidden, arguing that a condition of governance [in tanāzuʿ] is that neither of the two contending governors depend on the other or be part of the completion of its meaning, whereas «كان» depends on its khabar, which is part of the completion of its meaning. What he mentioned of prohibition and its justification is clear, except that the grammarians have not mentioned it among the conditions of governance.
His saying {وَإِن كَانَ كَبُرَ} is interpreted as future, namely its becoming clear and evident; so it is like His saying {إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ} [Yūsuf: 26], i.e. if it becomes clear and evident; otherwise these actions have already occurred and passed, so how could they be a condition? It has preceded that al-Mubarrad keeps «كان» specifically on its past meaning with conditional particles, and that is nothing. As for «فإن استطعتَ», it is future in meaning, since it had not happened, unlike the fact that their turning away weighed on him and the tearing of the shirt. «أن تبتغي» is the object of «الاستطاعة», and «نَفَقاً» is the object of «الابتغاء».
النَّفَق is a tunnel passing through the earth. Its origin is in the burrow of the jerboa; from it are النافقاء and القاصِعاء. That is because the jerboa digs a tunnel [in] the ground and makes two exits for it — and it has been said three: النَّافِقاء, القاصعاء and الدَّابِقاء — and then thins by its digging whatever is near the surface of the ground; when something befalls it, it pushes that thin crust and goes out. The full treatment of this root has preceded for you at the mention of {يُنْفِقُونَ} [al-Baqara: 3] and {المنافقين} [al-Nisāʾ: 61].
His saying {فِي الأرض}: its apparent sense is that it is attached to the verb before it. It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «نَفَقاً», and thus attached to an omitted element; it is then an adjective for mere tawkīd (emphasis), since a tunnel is only in the earth. Abū al-Baqāʾ, besides these two views, permitted it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of «تَبْتغي», i.e. "while you are on earth", and said: "Likewise «في السماء»", meaning the three views are permissible. This third view ought not to be permitted, since it lacks benefit.
السُّلَّم: it has been said to be a means of ascent; and it has been said to be steps; and it has been said to be a means (sabab) — the Arabs say: «اتَّخِذْني سُلَّماً لحاجتك», i.e. a means. Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr said:
190 - 7- ولا لكما مَنْجَىً من الأرض فابغِيا ... بها نَفَقاً أو في السماوات سُلَّماً
(And you two have no escape on earth; so seek a tunnel in it, or a ladder into the heavens.)
It is derived from السَّلامة (safety); they said: because by it one safely reaches the place of ascent. السُّلَّم is masculine; al-Farrāʾ reported its being feminine. Some said: that is not by original coinage, but because it means المِرْقاة (ladder), just as some made الصوت feminine in his saying:
190 - 8- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... سائِلْ بني أَسَدٍ ما هذه الصَّوْتُ
(…ask the Banū Asad what this voice is.)
since it was in the sense of «الصرخة» (the scream).

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والموتى يَبْعَثُهُمُ الله}: There are three views on it. The most apparent: it is a clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), brought to state His power: whoever is able to raise the dead is able to bring the hearts of the disbelievers to life with faith, so do not grieve over whoever disbelieves. The second: «الموتى» is accusative by an implied verb explained by the overt one after it; this view was preferred over the nominative by inception because the clause of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb) is conjoined to a verbal clause before it, so it is [Translator's note: printed «فو», evidently for «فهو»] analogous to {والظالمين أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذَاباً أَلِيماً} [al-Insān: 31] after His saying {يُدْخِل}. The third: it is nominative, conjoined to the relative noun before it, and what is meant by the dead is the disbelievers, i.e. only the believers who hear respond from the first moment, and the disbelievers whom Allah the Exalted answers [Translator's note: so printed, «يجيبهم»; perhaps «يُحييهم», "revives", is meant] with faith and grants them success in it. On this view the clause {يَبْعَثُهُمُ الله} is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). However, this view is made unlikely by His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ}, unless it is a tarshīḥ (reinforcement) of the figurative usage. Its parallels have preceded.
It has been read {يَرْجِعون}, from the intransitive رَجَع.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying, the Exalted: {مِّن رَّبِّهِ}: There are two views on it. The first: it is attached to «نُزِّل». The second: it is attached to an omitted element, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «آية», i.e. a sign coming from his Lord. Discussion of «لولا» has preceded, and that it is for urging (taḥḍīḍ).

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ}: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) because the two conditions are present, and it [with its noun] is the mubtadaʾ (subject); «إلا أممٌ» is its khabar (predicate), together with what is conjoined to it. His saying «في الأرض» is a naʿt (adjective) of «دابة», so you may make it genitive in position with regard to the wording, or nominative in position with regard to the place [in the sentence].
His saying: {وَلاَ طَائِرٍ}: The majority read it in the genitive, conjoined to the wording of «دابة». Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it in the nominative, conjoined to its position. Ibn ʿAbbās read «ولا طيرٍ» without an alif; discussion of it has preceded: is it a plural or a collective noun? His saying {يطير}, in the majority reading, may be in the genitive position with regard to its [the noun's] wording, or in the nominative position with regard to its place; on the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAbla it is in the nominative position only. In His saying «ولا طائر» there is mention of the specific after the general, because «الدابة» includes everything that moves, birds and others; so it is like His saying {وملائكته. . . . . وَجِبْرِيلَ} [al-Baqara: 98]. This is open to question, since the contrast here negates that «الدابة» includes the bird.
His saying: {بِجَنَاحَيْهِ}: There are two views on it. The first: the bāʾ is attached to «يطير», and the bāʾ is for instrumentality (istiʿāna). The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial), an emphatic ḥāl; it removes a figurative sense that might be imagined, because flying is used metaphorically for speed; the poet said:
190 - 9- قومٌ إذا الشرُّ أبدَى ناجِذَيْه لهم ... طاروا إليه زَرافاتٍ ووِحْدانا
(A people who, when evil bares its molars at them, fly to it in groups and singly.)
And «الطير» is applied to one's deeds; the Exalted said: {وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَآئِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ} [al-Isrāʾ: 13].
His saying: {إِلاَّ أُمَمٌ} is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. It is plural even though only two things preceded it, because what is meant by them is the genus. «أمثالكم» is a naʿt of «أُمَم», meaning they are like them in provisions, terms of life, death, life, gathering, and retribution for the wronged among them from the wrongdoer. It has also been said: in knowing Allah and worshipping Him.
His saying: {مِن شَيْءٍ}: There are three views on it. The first: «مِنْ» is redundant in the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the implied form being "we have not neglected anything", with «فرَّطنا» implying the meaning of "we left out" and "we overlooked"; the meaning: we have not overlooked or left out anything. They then differed over what is meant by «الكتاب». It has been said: the Preserved Tablet; on this the generality is evident, because Allah the Exalted has recorded in it what has been and what will be. It has also been said: the Qur'an; on this, does the generality remain? Some said yes, and that all things are recorded in the Qur'an, either explicitly or by allusion; others said that the particular is meant, and the meaning is: of anything that the morally responsible need. The second: «مِنْ» is partitive, i.e. we have not left out or overlooked in the Book any part of a thing that the morally responsible person needs. The third: «من شيء» is in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), with «من» redundant in it too. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted nothing else, for he said: "«مِنْ» is redundant, and «شيء» here occurs in the place of the maṣdar, i.e. any neglect.
On this interpretation no proof remains in the verse for whoever thinks that the Book contains the explicit mention of everything. Its parallel is {لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئاً} [Āl ʿImrān: 120]. It cannot be a mafʿūl bihi, because «فرَّطْنا» is not transitive by itself but only by a preposition, and it has been made transitive to «الكتاب» by «في», so it is not made transitive by another preposition. Nor is it correct for the meaning to be 'we have not left anything in the Book', because the meaning is otherwise; so the interpretation is clearly as we have mentioned." End quote. His saying "contains the explicit mention of everything" — no one has held this, because it would be obstinacy against what is self-evident. Al-Aʿraj and ʿAlqama read «فَرَطْنا» without doubling; it has been said that the two have the same meaning. From al-Naqqāsh: «فَرَطْنا» means "we delayed", as they say: «فَرَط الله عنك المرض», i.e. He removed it.

semin-durr:80-80.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أتحاجواني}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Dhakwān and Hishām (with a disagreement from him) read it with a single light nūn, and the rest with a doubled (heavy) nūn. The doubling is the original, because the first nūn is the nūn of the nominative in the "five verb forms" (al-amthila al-khamsa) and the second is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and their coming together was felt to be heavy. There are three usages in it: separating them and leaving both as they are, assimilation (idghām), and omission. All these usages have been read in the words of Allah the Exalted {أَفَغَيْرَ الله تأمروني أَعْبُدُ} [al-Zumar: 64]; here it was read only with omission or assimilation. Likewise in Sūrat al-Ḥijr {فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ} [al-Ḥijr: 54]: Ibn Kathīr's reading is with assimilation and Nāfiʿ's with omission, and the rest give the nūn fatḥa, because for them it is the nūn of the nominative. In Sūrat al-Naḥl, {تُشَاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ} [al-Naḥl: 27] is read by the majority with fatḥa on the nūn, because it is the nūn of the nominative, and Nāfiʿ reads it with a light nūn with kasra, by omission. So Nāfiʿ omitted one of the two nūns in all these places I have mentioned to you, for he also reads [the verse] in al-Zumar with one of them omitted. As for the words of Allah the Exalted {أتعدانني} [al-Aḥqāf: 17], Hishām read it with assimilation and the rest with the two pronounced separately, without omission.
The grammarians differed as to which of the two is omitted. The doctrine of Sībawayh and those who follow him is that the omitted one is the first; the doctrine of al-Akhfash and those who follow him is that the omitted one is the second.
