Sībawayh argued for that from the fact that omission of the nūn of the nominative is attested without meeting an identical letter, in the nominative; and there was recited:
1968 - فإنْ يكُ قومٌ سَرَّهمْ ما صنعتُمُ ... سَتَحْتَلبوها لاقِحاً غير باهِلِ
(If there are people whom what you did has pleased, you will milk it [i.e. the war] pregnant, not one left unmilked [i.e. you will reap its bitter yield].)
i.e. «فستحتلبونها». It cannot be said that the nūn was omitted for the jussive in the apodosis of the condition, because the fāʾ here must enter, since the apodosis clause is not fit to be a protasis. Once it is established that the fāʾ is required, and that it was omitted only by poetic necessity, it is established that the nūn of the nominative ought to have been retained, but it was omitted by necessity. They also recited his saying:
1969 - أبيتُ أَسْرِي وتَبِيتي تَدْلُكي ... وجهكِ بالعنبرِ والمِسْك الذكي
(I pass the night travelling, while you pass the night rubbing your face with ambergris and fragrant musk.)
i.e. «تبيتين» and «تَدْلُكين». And in the hadith: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another"; the «لا» on «تدخلوا» and «تؤمنوا» is negative, not prohibitive, since the meaning would be spoilt by that. Once its omission is established without meeting an identical letter, in the nominative, then its omission when meeting an identical letter, because of heaviness, is all the more fitting. Also, the nūn stands in for the ḍamma, and omission of the ḍamma is attested in eloquent speech, as in Abū ʿAmr's reading {يَنصُرْكُمُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 160], {يُشْعِرُكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 109] and {يَأْمُرُكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 67] and its class with the end of the verb unvowelled, and his saying:
1970 - فاليومَ أشربْ غيرَ مُسْتَحقِبٍ ... إثماً من اللهِ ولا واغِلِ
(So today I drink, not burdening myself with a sin before Allah, nor intruding [on others' drinking].)
And if omission of the original is established, then let omission of the derivative be established too, lest it follow that a derivative is preferred over its original. Also, claiming omission of the nūn of the nominative does not necessitate another omission, while omission of the nūn of protection may necessitate that. The explanation is that when a jussive or subjunctive particle enters one of these forms, if the omitted [nūn] were the nūn of protection, this [remaining] nūn ought to be dropped, since it is the nūn of the nominative, and that drops for the subjunctive and jussive particle; unlike claiming omission of the nūn of the nominative, which does not necessitate that, since [the particle] has no effect on the one for protection.
Someone may say: the permissibility of omitting the original does not entail omitting the derivative, because in the original there is a strength that permits its omission, unlike the derivative. And on the other point he may say: this is countered by the nullification of the governing word; for if the omitted [nūn] were the nūn of the nominative because of the nūn of protection, and the jussive or subjunctive particle entered, it would find nothing to omit, because the nūn had been omitted for another incidental reason. They also argued for Sībawayh that the nūn of protection has kasra, so keeping it as it is entails no change, unlike if we claimed its omission, for then we would have to change the nūn of the nominative from fatḥa to kasra, and minimising operations is preferable. They also argued that it has been omitted together with its like even where it was not a nūn of protection, as in his saying:
1971 - كل له نِيَّةٌ في بُغْضِ صاحبِهِ ... بنعمةِ الله نَقْلِيْكُمْ وتَقْلُونا
(Each has an intent of hating his fellow; by Allah's grace we loathe you and you loathe us.)
i.e. «وتَقْلُوننا»; the omitted one is the nūn of the nominative, not the nūn of «نا», because it is part of a pronoun. This was countered by [saying] that the nūn of the nominative also has strength because it indicates the case inflection, so omitting it is also not permissible. Sībawayh made the omitted one in the poet's saying:
1972 - تراه كالثَّغامِ يُعَلُّ مِسْكاً ... يَسُوءُ الفالِياتِ إذا فَلَيْني
(You see it [his hair] like white thaghām, drenched again and again with musk; it grieves the women delousing [it] when they delouse me.)
the nūn of the agent, not the nūn of protection. Al-Akhfash argued that the heaviness arose only through the second; and because it is dispensable, since it was only brought to protect the verb from kasra, and that is secured because the kasra falls on the nūn of the nominative; and because it indicates no meaning, unlike the nūn of the nominative. Also, it is omitted in e.g. «ليتني», so one says «ليتي», as in his saying:
1973 - كمُنْيَةِ جابر إذ قال ليتي ... أُصادِفُه وأُتْلِفُ بعضَ مالي
(Like the wish of Jābir when he said: would that I met him, even if I lost some of my wealth.)
Know that omitting the nūn in this kind of case is permissible and eloquent, and no attention is paid to the view of those who forbade it except in poetic necessity or in a little of speech. For this reason Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib was faulted when he said: "The omission is far-fetched in Arabic, ugly and disliked; it is permissible only in poetry for the metre, and the Quran does not admit it, since no necessity calls for it." Some of them even dared to say: "This reading—I mean lightening the nūn—is a solecism (laḥn)." Both of these views are rejected, because [this reading] is mass-transmitted (mutawātir); I have already given the proof of its correctness linguistically. Also, trustworthy authorities transmitted that it is an established usage of the Arabs, namely of Ghaṭafān, so there is no sense in denying it.
«في الله» is attached to «أتحاجُّوني», not to «حاجَّه». The question belongs to the topic of tanāzuʿ (two governing words competing for one governed word); he gave government to the second, because, when [the object] is pronominalised in the first, it is omitted; had he given government to the first, it would have been pronominalised in the second without omission. Like it is {يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ قُلِ الله يُفْتِيكُمْ فِي الكلالة} [al-Nisāʾ: 176]. So said the Shaykh; but this is open to consideration, since the meaning is not that «وَحَاجَّهُ» governs His words «في الله», as what is apparent is that the clause of the saying is cut off from what precedes it. His words «في الله» mean: concerning His affair and His oneness.
His words: «وَقَدْ هَدَاني»: in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Concerning the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) there are two aspects. The more apparent: it is the [first-person] tāʾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the pronoun meant is the yāʾ] in «أتحاجونني», i.e. "Do you dispute with me concerning Him while I am guided by Him?"
The second: it is a ḥāl from «الله», i.e. "Do you contend with me concerning Him while He is my guide? Your argument is of no avail, since it is refuted."
His words: {وَلاَ أَخَافُ مَا تُشْرِكُونَ بِهِ}: this clause may be resumptive: he (upon him be peace) states that he does not fear what you associate with his Lord, trusting in Him; they had frightened him with harm that would befall him because of reviling their gods. It may also be in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, in two respects. One: that it be a second [ḥāl] conjoined to the first, so that the two ḥāls are from the yāʾ in «أتحاجونِّي». The second: it is a ḥāl from the yāʾ in «هداني», so it is a ḥāl clause from part of a ḥāl clause, close to the "overlapping ḥāl" (mutadākhila). But on this aspect a mubtadaʾ must be implied before the imperfect verb, because, as stated before, the imperfect verb with «لا» has the rule of the affirmative in that the wāw does not directly precede it.
In «ما» the three aspects are possible. That it be maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya): on this view the hāʾ in «به» does not refer back to «ما», according to the majority, but to Allah the Exalted, the implied form being: "And I do not fear your associating with Allah," with the object omitted, i.e. what you associate—others than Allah—with Him. That it be in the sense of «الذي». And that it be a qualified indefinite. On these two aspects the hāʾ in «به» refers to «ما», and the meaning is: "And I do not fear that with which you associate Allah"; so the object is omitted here too, as in the first aspect. Abū al-Baqāʾ implied a muḍāf before the pronoun, saying: "The hāʾ may refer to «ما», i.e. and I do not fear that because of which you associate"; there is no need for that.
His words: «إلا أَنْ يشاء»: there are two views concerning this exception. The more apparent: it is connected (muttaṣil). The second: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). Those who hold it connected differed about the thing excepted from. Al-Zamakhsharī made it a time, saying: "Except at the time of my Lord's willing something to be feared; so the [word for] time was omitted. That is: I do not fear your objects of worship at any time at all, because they have no power of benefit or harm, unless my Lord wills." Abū al-Baqāʾ made it a state, saying: its implied form is "except in the state of my Lord's willing," i.e. I do not fear them in any state except in this state. Among those who held it disconnected are Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Ḥawfī, and Abū al-Baqāʾ in one of his two aspects. Al-Ḥawfī said: "Its implied form is: but Allah's willing me harm, I fear." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "An exception not from the first [category]; since the thrust of the speech is that he does not fear harm, he excepted his Lord's will in wanting harm for him."
His words: «شيئاً»: two aspects are possible in it. The more apparent: it is in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "unless my Lord wills something of willing." The second: it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يشاء». The first was more apparent for two reasons. One: emphasised speech is stronger and more firmly fixed in the mind than unemphasised.
The second: it has been stated before that the object of «المشيئة» and «الإرادة» is not mentioned unless there is something unusual about it, as in his saying:
1974 - ولو شِئْتُ أَنْ أبكي دماً لبَكَيْتُه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And had I wished to weep blood, I would have wept it…)
His words: «عِلْماً»: there are two aspects. The more apparent: it is in the accusative as a tamyīz (specification), converted from the fāʿil (agent), its implied form being: "My Lord's knowledge encompasses everything," like His words {واشتعل الرأس شَيْباً} [Maryam: 4]. The second: it is in the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because the meaning of «وَسِعَ» is «عَلِم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Because what encompasses a thing has comprehended it, and the knower of a thing comprehends it in his knowledge." This figurative usage he claims is far-fetched. «كل شيء» is the object of «وسع» on both assumptions. «أفلا تتذكرون» is a clause of affirmation and rebuke, and it has no grammatical position because it is resumptive.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَكَيْفَ أَخَافُ مَآ أَشْرَكْتُمْ}: the discussion of «كيف» was given at the beginning of al-Baqara, and this is its counterpart. In «ما» the three aspects are possible, I mean its being a nominal relative (mawṣūla ismiyya), a qualified indefinite, or maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); the referent pronoun on the first two is omitted, i.e. "what you have associated with Allah," or "your associating others with Allah."
His words: «ولا تخافون»: this clause may be conjoined (nasaq) to «أخاف», so that it falls within the scope of the wonder and denunciation; or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "And how should I fear what you associate, while you yourselves do not fear the consequence of your associating?" A mubtadaʾ (subject) must be implied before the imperfect negated with «لا», for the reason stated more than once, i.e. "How should I fear what you associate, or how should your associating be feared, while you feel secure from the plan of Allah with whom you have associated others?" This clause, even though it contains no link referring back to the one described by the ḥāl, is not harmed by that, because the wāw is itself a link. Look at the beauty of this well-balanced arrangement: He made the object of the fear on his part the idols, and the object of the fear on their part their associating others with Allah, avoiding putting the Creator the Exalted on a par with their idols, [as would have happened] had the construction been laid out thus, saying "and you do not fear Allah" as a counterpart to his saying "and how should I fear your objects of worship." He used «ما» in His words «ما أشركتم» and in His words {مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطَاناً} because they are not rational beings, since they are inanimate stones, and since they used to carve them and worship them.
His words: «ما لم يُنَزِّلْ»: the object of «أَشْرَكْتُم»; it is a nominal relative or an indefinite, and it cannot be maṣdar-forming because the meaning would be spoilt. «به» and «عليكم» are attached to «يُنَزِّل». Another aspect is possible in «عليكم»: that it be a ḥāl from «سلطاناً», because if it came after it, it could be an adjective. The majority read «سُلْطاناً» with an unvowelled lām wherever it occurs, and it has been read with ḍamma on it [«سُلُطاناً»]. It is said that this is an independent dialectal form, so that the pattern fuʿul with ḍamma on the first and second radicals is established by it; or it is the making of one vowel follow another.
His words: «فأيُّ الفريقين أحقُّ»: he did not say "which of us is more entitled, we or you?" in order to bind his opponent by what he himself claims against him, and because a speaker does not praise himself. This is unlike the saying of the other:
1975 - فلئِنْ لقيتُكَ خالِيَيْنِ لتعلمَنْ ... أيّي وأيُّك فارسُ الأحزابِ
(If I meet you with the two of us alone, you will surely know which of me and you is the knight of the confederates.)
So to Allah belongs the eloquence of the Quran and its refinement! His words «إن كنتم»: its apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then tell me"; and the object of the knowing is omitted. It may also be that no object is intended for it, i.e. "if you are among those who have knowledge."

semin-durr:82-82.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {الذين آمَنُواْ}: is it from the words of Abraham, from the words of his people, or from the words of Allah the Exalted? Scholars have three views, and the parsing depends on them. If we say it is from the words of Abraham, as an answer to the question in his words «فأيُّ الفريقين», and likewise if we say it is from the words of his people, and that they answered with what is an argument against them, then the relative noun is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are those who believed." If we make it from the words of Allah the Exalted, and that He commanded His Prophet to answer the foregoing question with it, it is the same too. If we make it a mere statement from the Creator the Exalted, the relative noun is a mubtadaʾ, and there are several aspects concerning its khabar. The first: it is the clause after it; «أولئك» is a second mubtadaʾ, «الأمن» a third mubtadaʾ, and «لهم» its khabar; the clause is the khabar of «أولئك», and «أولئك» with its khabar is the khabar of the first.
The second: that «أولئك» be a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), «لهم» the khabar of the relative noun, and «الأمنُ» the fāʿil (agent) of it, because it is supported [by what precedes]. The third: the same, except that «لهم» is a khabar placed first and «الأمن» a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of the relative noun. The fourth: that «أولئك» be a second mubtadaʾ, «لهم» its khabar and «الأمن» its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of the relative noun. The fifth—and Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās and al-Ḥawfī held it—that «لهم الأمن» is the khabar of the relative noun, and «أولئك» is a separating element (fāṣila); this is strange, because separation (faṣl) is the function of pronouns, not of demonstratives. As for our view that «الذين» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, then «أولئك» is only a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being the clause after it or the prepositional phrase alone, with «الأمنُ» as its fāʿil. On this view the first clause is in the accusative by an implied saying, i.e. "Say: they are those who believed," if it is from the words of al-Khalīl [Abraham], or "they said: they are those who…," if it is from the words of his people. His words «ولم يَلْبسوا»: two aspects are possible in it. One: it is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), so it then has no grammatical position. The second: the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause after it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they believed without mixing their faith with wrongdoing." It is like His words {أنى يَكُونُ لِي غُلاَمٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ} [Maryam: 20]. No attention is paid to the view of Ibn ʿUṣfūr, who made the occurrence of a negated clause as a ḥāl rare, nor to the view of Ibn Kharūf, who made the wāw obligatory on such a clause even if it contains a pronoun referring to the one described by the ḥāl.
The majority read «يَلْبِسُوا» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, meaning "they mix it," and ʿIkrima read it with ḍamma on it [«يُلْبِسُوا»], from «الإلباس». «وهم مهتدون» may be resumptive or a ḥāl.

semin-durr:111-111.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {قُبُلاً}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «قِبَلاً» here and in al-Kahf with kasra on the qāf and fatḥa on the bāʾ; the Kufans, here and in al-Kahf, with ḍamma on both; Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr with ḍamma on both here, and with kasra on the qāf and fatḥa on the bāʾ in al-Kahf. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Abū Ḥaywa and Abū Rajāʾ read it with ḍamma and sukūn. Ubayy and al-Aʿmash read «قبيلاً», with a yāʾ (two dots beneath) after a bāʾ (one dot) with kasra. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «قَبْلا», with fatḥa on the qāf and sukūn on the bāʾ.

As for the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, it admits two views. The first: that it means "face to face", i.e. by direct sight and witnessing; on this view it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). This was said by Abū ʿUbayda, al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj, and al-Wāḥidī also transmitted it from all the lexicographers. One says: «لَقِيته قِبَلاً», i.e. "openly, before my eyes". Ibn al-Anbārī said: "Abū Dharr said: I said to the Prophet ﷺ: Was Ādam a prophet? He said: Yes, he was a prophet; Allah spoke to him قِبَلاً (face to face)." Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda and Ibn Zayd explained it thus, and al-Zamakhsharī reported nothing else; so it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl, as stated earlier. The second: that it means "the direction of his face"; this was said by al-Mubarrad and a group of lexicographers such as Abū Zayd. It is then accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), as in their saying: «لي قِبَلُ فلان دَيْنٌ» ("so-and-so owes me a debt") and «ما قِبَلك حق» ("you owe nothing"). One says: «لَقِيْتُ فلاناً قِبَلاً ومُقابلةً وقُبُلاً وقُبَلاً وقَبْلِيَّاً وقبيلاً», all with a single meaning. Abū Zayd mentioned this and followed it with a long and useful discussion — may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him and reward him well.

As for the reading of the others here, it admits several views. The first: that «قُبُلاً» is the plural of قبيل in the sense of "guarantor" (kafīl), like رَغيف / رُغُف, قضيب / قُضُب and نَصِيب / نُصُب, and it is accusative as a ḥāl. Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj said: "The plural of قبيل meaning guarantor, i.e. as guarantors of the truthfulness of Muḥammad, upon him be peace." One says: «قَبَلْتُ الرجل أَقبَلُه قَبالة», with fatḥa on the bāʾ in the past tense and on the qāf in the maṣdar, i.e. "I stood surety for him". القبيل, الكفيل, الزعيم, الأَذِين, الضمين and الحَمِيل all have one meaning. Suretyship (kafāla) was called قَبالة only because it is the most binding form of undertaking (taqabbul), and with regard to the meaning of suretyship a written covenant is called قَبالة. Al-Farrāʾ said in Sūrat al-Anʿām: "«قُبُلاً» is the plural of «قبيل», which is the guarantor." He said: "I chose here that القُبُل be in the sense of suretyship only because of their saying {أَوْ تَأْتِيَ بالله والملائكة قَبِيلاً} [al-Isrāʾ: 92]: they would guarantee that."

The second: that it is the plural of قبيل in the sense of "group by group" or "kind by kind"; the meaning is: and We had gathered before them everything, troop by troop and kind by kind, of all created things.

The third: that «قُبْلاً» [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the reading under discussion is «قُبُلاً».] has the meaning of قِبَلاً, as in the first reading in one of its two views, namely facing, i.e. face to face and by direct sight. From this is «آتيك قُبُلاً لا دُبُراً» ("I will come to you from the front, not from behind"), i.e. I will come to you from the direction of your face. Allah the Exalted said: {إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ} [Yūsuf: 26], and it was read «لقُبُل عِدَّتِهِنَّ», i.e. at its commencement. Al-Farrāʾ said: "قُبُلاً may also mean: from the direction of their faces."

As for the one in al-Kahf, the meanings of facing, direct sight, and group kind by kind are all valid in it, because what is meant by the punishment there is the genus; further explanation of it will come.

«قُبُلاً» is accusative as a ḥāl, as has passed, from «كلَّ», even though it is indefinite, because of its generality and its being in a construct. It was stated earlier that, on one of its views, it is accusative as an adverb according to al-Mubarrad. As for the reading of al-Ḥasan, it is a lightened form of the one with ḍamma; Ubayy read it in the original form, which is the singular. As for the reading of Ṭalḥa, it is an adverb cut off from the construct, its meaning being: or he brings Allah and the angels before it. But it ought then to have been indeclinable (mabnī), since the construct is intended.

His saying: {مَّا كَانُواْ} is the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو». It was stated earlier that when it is negated, the lām is ruled out. Al-Ḥūfī said: "The implied form is لَمَا كانوا; the lām was omitted while being intended." This is not good, because the lām rarely enters an apodosis negated with «ما» — indeed some do not permit it at all — and with an apodosis negated with «لم» it is absolutely impossible. This lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), which puts into the genitive the interpreted maṣdar formed from «أَنْ» and the verb it makes accusative. The verification of all this has preceded, by the help of Allah the Exalted.

His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ الله}: it may be a connected exception (muttaṣil), i.e. they would not believe in any circumstance except in the circumstance of Allah's willing it, or at any time except at the time of His willing it.

And it was said: it is an exception from a general cause, i.e. they would not believe for any reason whatsoever except through the will of Allah the Exalted. The second: that it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ); al-Ḥūfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted this, and the Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] considered it far-fetched.

semin-durr:112-112.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَكَذَلِكَ}: the kāf is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Zamakhsharī/ gave its implied form as: "Just as We have left you and your enemies to each other, so We did with those before you." Al-Wāḥidī said: "«وكذلك» is conjoined to His saying {كَذَلِكَ زَيَّنَّا} [al-Anʿām: 108], i.e.: just as We did that, so We have made for every prophet an enemy." Then he said: "And it was said: its meaning is: We have made for you an enemy just as We made for the prophets before you; so His saying «وكذلك» is conjoined to the meaning of the preceding speech, and what precedes indicates its meaning, namely that He made enemies for him." And «جَعَل» takes two objects, in the sense of «صَيَّر» (to make into). Al-Zamakhsharī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Ḥūfī parsed it here in the same way as they parsed His saying, Exalted is He: {وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ الجن} [al-Anʿām: 100]. So the first object is «شياطين الإِنس» and the second is «عَدُوَّا», and «لكلِّ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «عدوَّاً», because it was originally its adjective, or it is attached to the verb «جَعَل» before it. It is also possible that the first object is «عدوَّاً» and «لكلِّ» is the second, placed first, with «شياطين» a badal (substitute) for the first object.

The construct in {شَيَاطِينَ الإنس} may be of the type of annexing an adjective to the noun it qualifies, the original being: the devilish men and jinn, like «جَرْد قطيفة» ("a worn-out velvet cloth"). I have preferred this on the grounds that the intended purpose is consolation and taking example from the prophets who came before, since among their nations there were those who showed them enmity, as in the nation of Muḥammad ﷺ. It may also be of the construct that carries the meaning of lām, and not of the type of annexing an adjective to the noun it qualifies; the meaning then is: the devils that belong to mankind and the devils that belong to the jinn, for Iblīs divided his troops into two divisions: a division set over mankind and another over the jinn — so it came in the exegesis. «عَدُوَّاً» occurs, on one of the two parsings, as a second object for «شياطين» in the singular form because the singular suffices for that; its supporting evidence has preceded, and from it is:

2033 - إذا أنا لم أَنْفَعْ صديقي بودِّه ... فإنَّ عدوِّي لن يَضُرَّهُمُ بُغْضي
(If I do not benefit my friend with my affection, then my hatred will not harm my enemies.)

He referred the pronoun in «يَضُرَّهُم» back to «عدّو», which shows that it is plural in sense.

His saying {يُوحِي}: it may be resumptive, informing about them with that; or a ḥāl from «شياطين»; or an adjective for «عدو». It was stated earlier that it stands in place of أعداء, and for that reason the pronoun referring to it is plural in His saying «بعضهم».

His saying {غُرُوراً}: it was said that it is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. in order to deceive others. And it was said: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. deceiving. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object), because the governing word has its meaning, as though it were said: they deceive with a deceiving by the inspiration. Al-zukhruf is adornment; «كلامٌ مُزَخْرَف» is embellished speech. Its origin is gold, and since gold is admired by everyone, anything considered beautiful and adorned was called zukhruf. Abū ʿUbayda said: "Everything you have embellished and adorned while it is false is zukhruf." This does not necessarily follow, since it may be applied to adornment that is genuine; «بيت مزخرف» is a house adorned with carvings. From this is the ḥadīth:

"The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not enter the Kaʿba until he ordered the zukhruf, and it was removed" — meaning that they used to adorn the Kaʿba with carvings and images gilded with gold, and we were ordered to remove them.

His saying: {وَمَا يَفْتَرُونَ}: «ما» is a nominal relative, or an indefinite qualified by an adjective, and on both of these views the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. «وما يفترُونه»; or it is maṣdariyya. On every view its position is accusative, and there are two views about it. The first: that it is conjoined to the object in «فَذَرْهُمْ», i.e. leave them and leave their fabrication. The second: that it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); this is the weaker view, because whenever conjunction is possible without weakness in the construction or the meaning, it is preferable to the mafʿūl maʿahu.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مَّن يُصْرَفْ}: «مَنْ» is conditional, and its position may be nominative or accusative, as will be explained after mentioning the two readings. So we say: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «يَصْرِف», with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, naming the agent; the rest [read it] with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive).

As for the first reading, «مَنْ» in it may be nominative or accusative. The nominative is in one way, namely as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), or the apodosis (jawāb), or both, according to the disagreement. There are then two possibilities for the object of «يَصْرِف». One of them: that it is mentioned, namely «يومئذ», and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. [whoever] Allah turns away from him the terror of that Day — or the punishment of that Day — He has had mercy on him; so the pronoun in «يَصْرِف» refers to Allah the Exalted, as indicated by the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb «مَنْ يَصْرِف اللَّهُ», stating it explicitly; and the two pronouns in «عنه» and «رَحِمَه» refer to «مَنْ». The second: that it is omitted because what was mentioned before indicates it, i.e. whoever Allah turns the punishment away from; and «يومئذ» is accusative as an adverbial. Makkī said: "It is not good to assume a hāʾ [pronoun], because the hāʾ is omitted only from relative clauses (ṣilāt)." I say: he means that the object is not assumed to be a pronoun referring to «عذاب يوم», because the conditional clause in his view is an adjective of «عذاب», and the returning pronoun from it is omitted; but omission occurs only from the ṣila, not from the adjective. This is also the meaning of al-Wāḥidī's statement. However, by Makkī's saying "it is omitted only from relative clauses" he means in the best usage; otherwise it is omitted from adjectives, predicates and ḥāls, but less than from the ṣila.

The accusative is in two ways. One of them: that it is a fronted object of «يَصْرِف», and the pronoun in «عنه» on this view must refer to the punishment mentioned before; the implied form is: whatever person Allah turns away from the punishment. The second: that it is accusative by ishtighāl (pre-occupation), with an implied verb that does not appear, explained by this overt one in its meaning, not its wording; the implied form is: «مَنْ نُكْرِمْ أو مَنْ نُنَجِّ يَصْرِفِ الله» (whomever We honour or whomever We save, Allah turns away…), and the pronoun in «عنه» refers to the conditional [«مَن»]. As for the object of «يَصْرِفْ» on this view, it allows the two aspects mentioned before, I mean that it is mentioned, namely «يومئذ», with a muḍāf omitted, or omitted for brevity.

As for the second reading, «مَنْ» allows two aspects. One of them: that it is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being what comes after it, as preceded; the omitted agent is Allah the Exalted, as indicated by the reading of Ubayy mentioned before. There are four aspects regarding what stands in its place [as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. One of them: that it is the pronoun of the punishment, the pronoun in «عنه» referring to «مَنْ» only. The adverbial then has three aspects. One of them: that it is accusative by «يُصْرَف». The second: that it is accusative by «العذاب», i.e. the one whose pronoun stands in place of the agent; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. This entails the maṣdar (verbal noun) governing while being a pronoun; but it may be said that this is overlooked in adverbials.
The third: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun." I say: he means the pronoun which stands in place of the agent; and it is permissible for the ḥāl to be an adverbial of time because it is [predicated] of an abstract meaning, not of a body.

The second of the four aspects: that what stands in place of the agent is the pronoun of «مَنْ», the pronoun in «عنه» referring to the punishment; the adverbial is accusative either by «يُصْرف» or as a ḥāl of the hāʾ of «عنه». The third of the aspects of what governs «يومئذ» is impossible here, and this is clear. The implied form is: whatever person is turned away from the punishment. The third: that what stands in place of the agent is «يومئذ», either with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. whoever has the alarm of that Day or the terror of that Day turned away from him, or by the adverbial standing [in place of the agent] without a muḍāf, as in your saying «سير يوم الجمعة» (Friday was travelled). «يومئذ» is only built (mabnī) on fatḥa because of its annexation to something not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkin); had it been read in the nominative, it would be permissible in speech. It has been read: {ومِنْ خزي يومئذ} with fatḥa and with genitive, by two considerations, and they are two different considerations. If it is said: not assuming the omission of a muḍāf entails making an incomplete adverbial stand in place of the agent, whereas they have stated explicitly that an adverbial cut off from annexation is not used as a predicate and does not stand in place of an agent — if you said «ضُرب قبلُ» it would not be permissible — and the adverbial here has the status of one cut off from annexation, so it may not stand in place of the agent except with a muḍāf omitted; the answer is that this is equivalent to an annexed adverbial, since the tanwīn is a substitute for it. This holds on the opinion of the majority; as for al-Akhfash, no, because in his view the tanwīn is the tanwīn of full declension (ṣarf), and the kasra is a kasra of inflection. I have clarified that sufficiently in another place.

The fourth: that what stands in its place is «عنه», the pronoun in «عنه» referring to «مَنْ», and «يومئذ» is accusative as an adverbial, governed by «يُصْرَفْ». The last two aspects are not permissible, I mean its being accusative as a ḥāl — because the pronoun is for a body, and time does not occur as a ḥāl of them [bodies], just as it does not occur as a predicate — and I mean its being governed by «العذاب», since it is not standing in place of the agent.

The second of the two aspects of «مَنْ»: that it is in the position of accusative by an implied verb which the overt one after it explains. This is when we make «عنه» in the position of accusative, by making what stands in place of the agent either the pronoun of the punishment or «يومئذ»; the implied form is: whomever Allah honours or whomever He saves, the punishment, or the terror of that Day, is turned away from him. Its parallel is «زيدٌ مُرَّ به مرورٌ حسن» (Zayd — a fine passing was made by him): you made the maṣdar stand [in place of the agent], so «به» [written in the text: «عنه»] remained accusative in position, and the implied form is: «جاوزت زيداً مُرَّ به مرورٌ حسن». But if «عنه» is made to stand in place of the agent, its [«مَن»'s] nominative as a mubtadaʾ is required.

Know that whenever you say "accusative by ishtighāl", it is assumed only after «مَنْ», because it has the right to the head of the speech; and for that reason I did not express it except placed after. For this reason some forbade ishtighāl with what has the right to the head of the speech, such as the interrogative and the condition. The tanwīn in «يومئذ» is a substitute for an omitted clause contained in the preceding speech, the implied form being: the day when the recompense takes place. I said so only because no explicitly stated clause preceded in the speech for the tanwīn to be a substitute for. Al-Akhfash's disagreement has preceded.

This conditional clause allows two aspects: being resumptive, and being an adjective of «عذاب يوم». Wherever we put in it a pronoun referring to «عذاب يوم», either from «يُصْرف» or from «عنه», it may be an adjective — and this is the apparent view — or resumptive; and wherever we do not put in it a pronoun referring to it — and you have learned how that is — it must be resumptive, and may not be an adjective because it is devoid of the pronoun.

People have spoken about preferring one of these two readings over the other, as is their custom. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: "The reading «يَصْرِفْ»" — meaning the active — "is better, because it matches His saying «رحمه»"; he means that each of them is active, and He did not say «فقط رُحِمَ» [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably «فقد رُحِمَ» "he has been shown mercy"]. Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd chose it. Some preferred the passive reading because of their consensus on reading His saying: {ليس مصروفاً عنهم}, meaning in that it came in the form of a passive participle attributed to the pronoun of the punishment mentioned first. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr preferred it on the grounds that it involves less implication (iḍmār). And Makkī — may Allah have mercy on him — «تلعثهم» [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably «تلعثم», "stumbled"] in his statement preferring the reading of the two brothers, and brought corrupt examples in his book al-Hidāya; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. I have stated at the beginning of the book, from scholars — Thaʿlab and others — that this, I mean preferring one of the mutawātir readings over another such that the other is weakened, is not permissible. The clause from His saying {يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ} [i.e. «فقد رحمه»] is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the condition, and the fāʾ is obligatory.

His saying: {وَذَلِكَ الفوز}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. This clause was brought to confirm the content of the clause before it. The reference by «ذلك» is to the maṣdar understood from His saying «يُصْرف», i.e. that turning away. «المبين» may be transitive, the object being omitted, i.e. the one making other things clear; or intransitive, meaning "being clear". It has preceded that «أبان» is intransitive meaning "appeared" and transitive meaning "made apparent".

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {بِضُرٍّ}: the bāʾ here is for transitivity (taʿdiya), and likewise in «بخير». The meaning is: and if Allah makes harm touch you, i.e. makes you touch it; and when you touch harm, it has touched you. However, transitivity with the bāʾ in a [already] transitive verb is very rare; and of it is their saying «صَكَكْتُ أحد الحجرين بالآخر» (I struck one of the two stones with the other). The Shaykh said: "And of it is His saying" — [the phrase "and of it is His saying" is repeated in the text] — {وَلَوْلاَ دَفْعُ الله الناس بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ} [al-Baqara: 251]. Al-Wāḥidī said: "If it is said: touching is an attribute of bodies, so how did He say «وإن يمسَسْك الله»? The answer is that the bāʾ is for transitivity, and the bāʾ and the alif [of the afʿala form] alternate in making transitive. The meaning is: if Allah makes harm touch you (amassaka), i.e. makes it touch you; so the act belongs to the harm, even if on the surface it is attributed to the name of Allah the Exalted — as in your saying «ذهب زيد بعمرو» (Zayd took ʿAmr away), where the going is an act of ʿAmr, except that Zayd is the one who caused it and brought it about. Likewise here, the touching belongs to the harm, and Allah the Exalted made it touch."

His saying: {فَلاَ كَاشِفَ لَهُ}: «له» is the khabar (predicate) of «لا» [of generic negation]. There is something omitted there, its implied form being «فلا كاشفَ له عنك» (there is none to remove it from you). This omitted element is not attached to «كاشف», since that would require it to have tanwīn and be inflected; rather it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. «أعني عنه» (I mean, from you).

«إلا هو» has two aspects. One of them: that it is a badal (substitute) of the position of «لا كاشف», for its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The second: that it is a badal of the pronoun latent in the khabar. It may not be made nominative by the active participle, namely «كاشف», because it would then become extended (muṭawwal), and whenever it is extended it is inflected in the accusative. Likewise it may not be a badal of the pronoun latent in «كاشف», for the reason mentioned, since the badal takes the place of what it substitutes for.

If it is said: the counterpart of good (khayr) is evil (sharr), so why did He turn away from the word «الشر»? The answer is that He wished to give mercy predominance over its opposite, so on the side of evil He brought something more specific than it, namely harm, and on the [other] side the general term, which is good, giving this side predominance. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Harm stood here in place of evil — even though evil is more general than it — and was set against good. This, from eloquence, is a departure from [the norm of artifice and formulation; for the way of artifice and the formulations of speech] is that a thing be joined with what is specific to it by some kind of specificity, agreement or resemblance. Of that is: {إِنَّ لَكَ أَلاَّ تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلاَ تعرى وَأَنَّكَ لاَ تَظْمَأُ فِيهَا وَلاَ تضحى} [Ṭā Hā: 118-119], where He brought hunger with nakedness, whereas its way is to be with thirst; and of it is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
187 - 5- كأنّيَ لم أركبْ جواداً لِلَّذةٍ ... ولم أَتَبَطَّنْ كاعِباً ذاتَ خَلْخال
ولم أَسْبَأ الزِّقَّ الرَّويَّ ولم أقْلْ ... لخيلي كُرِّي كَرَّةً بعد إجْفالِ
(As if I had never ridden a steed for pleasure, nor lain with a full-breasted maiden wearing anklets; nor bought the brimming wineskin, nor said to my horsemen: charge again after the rout.)"
Ibn ʿAṭiyya did not clarify that. Its clarification, in the verse of Ṭā Hā, is that hunger and nakedness share something specific, namely emptiness: hunger is emptiness and vacancy on the inside, and nakedness is emptiness and vacancy on the outside; and thirst and exposure to the sun share burning: thirst is a burning on the inside — and for that reason you say: «بَرَّد الماء حرارة كبدي وأوام عطشي» (the water cooled the heat of my liver and the burning of my thirst) — and exposure to the sun is a burning of the outside.

As for the two verses, what unites riding for pleasure, namely hunting, and lying with the full-breasted maiden is that they share the pleasure of mounting, overpowering, capturing and winning such a mount. Do you not see that they call a woman's private part «رَكَباً», with fatḥa on the rāʾ and the kāf, which is faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl (what is ridden), as in his saying:
187 - 6- إنَّ لها لَرَكَباً إرْزَبَّا ... كأنه جبهةُ ذَرَّى حَبَّا
(She has a plump mound, like the brow of one who winnows grain.)
As for the second verse, what unites buying wine and returning [to fight] after defeat is that they share giving freely: buying wine is the giving of wealth, and returning after defeat is the giving of one's life. He, Blessed and Exalted is He, put the touching of harm before the touching of good to match the connection of the touching of harm with the intimidation before it, indicated by His saying «إني أخاف». The apodosis of the first condition came with restriction (ḥaṣr), alluding to His being alone in removing harm, none other; and the second came with His saying {فَهُوَ على كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدُيرٌ}, alluding to His dazzling power, in which touching with good and other things are included. Besides, had it been said that the apodosis of the second is omitted, it would be a valid aspect, i.e. and if He touches you [with good], there is none to repel His bounty — because its like is stated explicitly in another place.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {فَوْقَ}: there are several aspects on it. The most evident of them: that it is accusative by the active participle before it, and "aboveness" here expresses superiority and dominance. The second: that it is nominative as a second khabar (predicate): He is predicated with two things, one of them that He is the Subduer, and the second that He is above His servants by dominance and subjugation. The third: that it is a badal (substitute) of the khabar. The fourth: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «القاهر», as if it were said: and He is the Subduer, being exalted or dominant; al-Mahdawī and Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. The fifth: that it is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being: and He is the Subduer of His servants; and similar to it is: {فاضربوا فَوْقَ الأعناق} [al-Anfāl: 12]. This is rejected, because nouns are not redundant.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والذين كَذَّبُواْ}: It is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows is the khabar (predicate). «صمٌّ» may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, with that clause being the khabar of the first, the implied form being: "and those who denied — some of them are deaf and some of them are dumb". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«صمٌّ وبُكْمٌ» is the khabar, like «حلو حامض» (sweet-sour), and the wāw does not prevent that." I say: what he said is not permissible for two reasons. The first: that is only so when the two predicates are in the meaning of a single predicate — because those two mean «مُزّ» (sourish), and [likewise] «أَعْسَرُ يَسَرٌ» means «أضبط» (ambidextrous) — whereas each of these two predicates conveys a meaning independently. The second: the wāw is not permissible in such a case except according to Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, and it is a weak view.
His saying: {فِي الظلمات}: There are several views on it. The first: it is a second khabar of His saying {والذين كَذَّبُواْ}, and it would be an expression for blindness, making it the parallel of the other verse {صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ} [al-Baqara: 18]; blindness is expressed by what necessarily accompanies it, and what is meant is blindness of insight. The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun concealed in the khabar, its implied form being: "astray, while settled in darkness". The third: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «بُكْم», and so likewise attached to an omitted element, i.e. dumb, being in darkness. The fourth: it is an adverbial in its literal sense, an adverbial for «صُمُّ» or for «بُكْم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "or for what stands in their place as a verb", i.e. because the two adjectives are as strong as explicitly stating the verb.
His saying: {مَن يَشَإِ الله يُضْلِلْهُ}: There are two views on «مَنْ». The first: it is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is what follows it, as has been known more than once; the object of «يشأ» is omitted, i.e. whomever Allah wills to lead astray. The second: it is accusative by an implied verb, explained in meaning by what follows it; that verb is assumed to come after the conditional noun, lest it be removed from the head position. Attention has been drawn to that before, and that there is disagreement about it. The implied form: "whomever Allah makes wretched, He wills his being led astray; and whomever He makes happy, He wills his guidance". If you say: may «مَنْ» be a preposed object of «يشأ»? — the answer is that this is not permissible, because the meaning would be corrupted. If you say: I assume an omitted muḍāf which is the object, and «مَنْ» was put in its place, the implied form being "the leading astray of whomever He wills, and the guidance of whomever He wills", and the answer of the condition indicates this muḍāf — the answer is that al-Akhfash reported from the Arabs that with a conditional noun other than an adverbial, and with what is annexed to a conditional noun [Translator's note: printed «سام الشرط», evidently for «اسم الشرط»], there must be in the apodosis a pronoun referring to it or to what it is annexed to. So the pronoun in «يُضْلِلْه» and «يِجْعَلُه» either refers to the omitted muḍāf — as in His saying {أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ} [al-Nūr: 40], where the hāʾ in «يغشاه» refers to the muḍāf, i.e. like one in darkness whom it covers — or it refers to the conditional noun. The first is impossible, since the implied form would become "the leading astray of whomever Allah wills, He leads it astray", i.e. He leads the leading astray astray, which is corrupt.
The second is also impossible, because the answer would lack a pronoun referring to what is annexed to the conditional noun. If it is said: the meaning could be "whomever Allah wills with leading astray", with «مَنْ» a preposed object, because «شاء» means «أراد», and «أراد» is made transitive with the bāʾ; the poet said:
191 - 0- أرادَتْ عَراراً بالهَوانِ ومَنْ يُرِدْ ... عَراراً لعَمْري بالهَوان فقد ظَلَمْ
(She intended ʿArār with humiliation — and whoever, by my life, intends ʿArār with humiliation has done wrong.)
— it is answered: it does not follow from «شاء» meaning «أراد» that it takes the same complement. Thus we find a single word whose transitivity differs according to what it is attached to: you say دخلت الدار and دخلت في الأمر, but you do not say دخلتُ الأمرَ. If that is so with a single word, what then of two words? And making «شاء» transitive with the bāʾ is not preserved from the Arabs, even though it has the meaning of «أراد».

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بَلْ إِيَّاهُ تَدْعُونَ}: «بل» is a particle of iḍrāb (turning away) and transition, not of cancellation, for what you have learned more than once, that it is so in the speech of Allah. «إياه» is a preposed object, for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) according to al-Zamakhsharī — that is why he said: "Rather, you single Him out with supplication" — and for concern [with it] according to others; if there is restriction and specification, it is from another indication. «إياه» is a detached accusative pronoun, discussed exhaustively in al-Fātiḥa. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said here: "«إيَّا» is a pronominal noun treated like overt nouns in that it is always annexed." The Shaykh said: "This is contrary to the doctrine of Sībawayh, for Sībawayh's doctrine is that what follows «إيَّا» is a particle that shows the states of the pronoun, and it is not annexed to what follows it, lest it entail the definiteness of annexation, which presupposes its being indefinite; and pronouns do not admit indefiniteness, so they do not admit annexation."
His saying: {مَا تَدْعُونَ}: Four views are possible on «ما». The most apparent: it is a relative noun in the sense of «الذي», i.e. "so He removes that which you call [Him] for", and the referent pronoun is omitted because the conditions are fulfilled, i.e. «تَدْعونه». The second: it is adverbial (ẓarfiyya); Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. On this view, the object of «يكشفُ» is omitted, its implied form being: "so He removes the punishment for the duration of your calling", i.e. as long as you are calling on Him.
The Shaykh said: "There is no need for this, besides which it involves connecting it to an imperfect, which is very rare. You say «لا أُكَلِّمك ما طلَعت الشمس» (I will not speak to you as long as the sun has risen), and «ما تطلع الشمس» is weak." I say: in his saying "an imperfect", he should have said "an affirmative [imperfect]", because when it is negated with «لم» its connection to it is frequent, as in his saying:
192 - 1- ولَنْ يَلْبَثَ الجُهَّالُ أن يَتَهَضَّموا ... أخا الحلم ما لم يَسْتَعِنْ بجَهول
(The ignorant will not delay in oppressing the forbearing man, so long as he does not seek help from an ignorant one.)
And of its connection to an affirmative imperfect is his saying:
192 - 2- أُطَوِّفُ ما أُطَوِّفُ ثم آوي ... إلى أمَّا ويَرْويني النقيعُ
(I roam as long as I roam, then I return to a mother, and fresh milk quenches my thirst.)
and the saying of the other:
192 - 3- أُطَوِّفُ ما أُطّوِّفُ ثم أوي ... إلى بيتٍ قعيدَتُهُ لَكاعِ
(I roam as long as I roam, then I return to a house whose mistress is a base woman.)
So «أُطَوِّفُ» is the ṣila of the adverbial «ما».
The third: it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. The referent pronoun is again omitted, i.e. "so He removes something that you call Him for", i.e. you call for its removal; omission from an adjectival clause is less frequent than from a ṣila (relative clause). The fourth: it is maṣdariyya (infinitival). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It may correctly be infinitival, with an omission in the speech." Al-Zajjāj said: "It is like {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82]." I say: the implied form is "so He removes the cause of your calling and what occasions it". The Shaykh said: "This is a claim of an unspecified omitted element, and it is contrary to the apparent." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not infinitival, unless you make it a maṣdar in the sense of the passive participle", meaning its implied form becomes: "so He removes what you call about", i.e. that for which you call, which is the harm and the like.
His saying: {إِلَيْهِ}: There are two views on what it is attached to. The first: it is attached to «تَدْعون», and the pronoun then refers to the relative «ما», i.e. that which you call for its removal; and «دعا», with regard to the object of the calling, is made transitive by «إلى» or the lām. The Exalted said: {وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلاً مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى الله} [Fuṣṣilat: 33] and {وَإِذَا دعوا إِلَى الله} [al-Nūr: 48]; and the poet said:
192 - 4- وإن أُدْعَ للجُلَّى أكنْ مِنْ حُماتها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And if I am called to a great matter, I am among its defenders…)
And he said:
192 - 5- وإنْ دَعَوْتِ إلى جُلَّى ومَكْرُمَةٍ ... يوماً سَراةَ كرامِ الناس فادْعِينا
(And if one day you call the chiefs of noble people to a great matter and a noble deed, then call us.)
And he said:
192 - 6- دعوتُ لِما نابني مِسْوَراً ... فَلَب‍ِّيْ فَلَبَّيْ يَدَيْ مِسْوَرِ
(I called Miswar for what had befallen me, and he answered — so here I am at the service of Miswar's hands, again and again.)
The second: it is attached to «يَكْشِفُ»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. He lifts it to Himself." End quote. On this view the pronoun refers to Allah the Exalted. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned the two views of attachment without addressing the pronoun, and you have now learned it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The pronoun in «إليه» may refer to Allah, with the implied form: so He removes that about which you call to Him." The Shaykh said: "This is not good, because «دعا» takes a direct object without a preposition: {ادعوني أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ} [Ghāfir: 60], {إِذَا دَعَانِ} [al-Baqara: 186], and among the speech of the Arabs: «دعوتُ الله سميعاً»." I say: and like it is {قُلِ ادعوا الله أَوِ ادعوا الرحمن أَيّاً مَّا تَدْعُواْ} [al-Isrāʾ: 110] and {ادعوا رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعاً} [al-Aʿrāf: 55]. He said: "And one does not say in this sense «دعوت إلى الله» meaning «دعوت الله»; but his words may be corrected by way of taḍmīn (implying one verb's meaning in another): «تدعون» was made to imply the meaning of 'you take refuge with Allah concerning it'. But taḍmīn is not regular (qiyās); one does not resort to it except out of necessity, and there is no necessity calling for it here."
I say: taḍmīn is not restricted to necessity; it occurs in the Qur'an more often than can be counted. A good number of instances of it have preceded for you, and the like will come to you, Allah willing. Moreover, it may be said that Abū Muḥammad's [Ibn ʿAṭiyya's] allowing the pronoun to refer to Allah the Exalted is to be understood as «إليه» being attached to «يكشف», as was reported above from Abū al-Baqāʾ, and that its meaning is "He lifts it"; so the objection mentioned would not follow — were it not that his implied form "تدعون فيه إليه" disturbs this, since his assuming «فيه» apparently means that he holds it to be attached to «تَدْعُون».
His saying: {إِنْ شَآءَ}: Its answer is omitted because the meaning is understood and what precedes it indicates it, i.e. if He wills to remove, He removes. The claim that the answer of the condition is placed before it here is clear, since it is joined with the fāʾ, so it is better than [in] the saying «أنت ظالم إن فعلت» (you are a wrongdoer if you do it). But what prevents it from being the answer here is that [the fāʾ] is causal and sequential, i.e. it conveyed the removal following upon the calling and that the calling is a cause of it — besides which we have a disagreement about the fāʾ of the apodosis: does it convey [Translator's note: printed «تفي», evidently for «تفيد»] causality or not?
His saying: {وَتَنسَوْنَ مَا تُشْرِكُونَ}: The apparent view on «ما» is that it is a nominal relative noun, meaning whatever is worshipped besides Allah in general, rational beings and others; but non-rational beings were given precedence over them, as in His saying {وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَا فِي السموات} [al-Naḥl: 49]. The referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. what you associate with Allah in worship. Al-Fārisī said: "The original is: and you forget calling on what you associate; the muḍāf was omitted." It may also be maṣdariyya, and then, according to the majority, it needs no referent pronoun. Then, does this maṣdar remain in its literal sense, i.e. you forget the associating itself, because of the bewilderment and confusion that overtakes you? Or does it stand in the place of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Translator's note: printed «المعفول», evidently for «المفعول»], i.e. and you forget that which is associated, namely the idols and others? On this the meaning is like the first. Then the context admits [forgetting] being in its basic sense of heedlessness, or in the sense of abandoning, even though they remember them, i.e. the idols and others.

semin-durr:100-100.t:
The words of the Exalted: {شُرَكَآءَ الجن}: The majority read «الجن» in the accusative, and there are five aspects in it. The first, and it is the apparent one: that «الجن» is the first object, and the second is «شركاء», fronted, and «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) شركاء. The jaʿl here is in the sense of "making into" (taṣyīr). The benefit of the fronting, as al-Zamakhsharī said, is "to present as enormous that anyone — whether angel, jinn or human — should be taken as a partner to Allah; and for that reason the name of Allah was put before the partners." End of quote. The meaning of their making the jinn partners to Allah is that they believe that they create harmful things, snakes and beasts of prey, as has come in the exegesis. And it was said: there is a group of angels called jinn which some of the Arabs used to worship.
The second: that «شركاء» is the first object and «لله» is attached to something omitted, as the second object, and «الجنّ» is a badal (substitute) of «شركاء». Al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Ḥawfī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib permitted that; except that Makkī, when he mentioned this aspect, made the lām of «لله» attached to جَعَلَ, for he said: "الجنَّ is the first object of جَعَلَ and «شركاءَ» a fronted second object, and the lām in «لله» is attached to شركاء; and if you wish you can make «شركاء» the first object and الجن a badal of شركاء, and «لله» in the position of the second object, with the lām attached to جعل." I say: after he made «لله» the second object, how can it be conceived that he makes the lām attached to the jaʿl? This is not permissible, because once it has become the second object its attachment to something omitted is required, as you have learned more than once. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What they permitted — meaning al-Zamakhsharī and those mentioned with him — is not permissible, because the badal should be able to take the place of the one it substitutes so that the speech is well-formed; if you said: وجعلوا لله الجنَّ it would not be correct. The condition of the badal is that it be on the intention of repeating the governing word, on the better known of two views, or that it be governed by the governor of the substituted noun, on one view; and this is not correct here at all, for the reason we mentioned." I say: al-Farrāʾ and Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] preceded them to this view attributed to al-Zamakhsharī and those mentioned with him, for they both permitted them to be two objects with the second fronted before the first, and permitted «الجن» to be a badal of «الشركاء» and an explanation of the partners — this is the exact text of their expression — and it is a sound meaning, I mean the badal being explicative, so there is no sense in rejecting this view. Moreover, he himself replied to al-Zamakhsharī at the words of the Exalted {إِلاَّ مَآ أَمَرْتَنِي بِهِ أَنِ اعبدوا} [al-Māʾida: 117] that it is not required of every badal that it be able to take the place of the substituted noun; he said: "Do you not see the grammarians' permitting «زيد مررت به أبي عبد الله», while if you said «زيد مررت بأبي عبد الله» it would not be permissible except on the opinion of al-Akhfash?" This preceded in al-Māʾida. So he himself established/ that it is not required for the badal to take the place of the substituted noun; how then does he refute with it here?
The third: that «شركاء» is the first object and «الجن» the second object; al-Ḥawfī said it. This is not correct, for you know that the first [object] in this chapter is originally a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the second originally a khabar (predicate), and it is established that when a definite and an indefinite come together you make the definite the mubtadaʾ and the indefinite the khabar, not the reverse, except in poetic necessity; attention was drawn earlier to what has occurred of it.
The fourth: that «شركاء الجن» are the two objects as explained before, and «لله» is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «شركاء», because if it came after it, it could be an adjective of it; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. This is not correct, because the meaning would become: they made them partners in the state of their being Allah's, i.e. owned; and this is a permanent ḥāl that is never separated, and it cannot be said that it is non-transitory because it is emphatic, since there is no emphasis in it here. Moreover, it involves preparing the governor for a governed word and then cutting it off from it, for «شركاء» seeks this preposition-phrase to govern it, and the meaning is directed toward that.
The fifth: that «الجنَّ» is accusative by an implied verb, in answer to an implied question, as if someone asked after the words of the Exalted {وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ}: whom did they make partners to Allah? And it was said: the jinn, i.e. they made the jinn. The Shaykh transmitted it from his teacher Abū Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr, and considered it better than what preceded; he said: "This is supported by the reading of Abū Ḥaywa and Yazīd ibn Quṭayb «الجنُّ» in the nominative, on the implied form 'they are the jinn', in answer to whoever said: [whom] did they make partners to Allah? And it was said: they are the jinn. That is by way of presenting as enormous what they did and belittling those whom they made partners to Allah the Exalted." Makkī said: "Al-Kisāʾī permitted the nominative of «الجن» in the sense 'they are the jinn'"; so he did not relate it from him as a reading, and it seems he was not aware that others read it so.
Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamza, and Yazīd ibn Quṭayb and Abū Ḥaywa in another transmission from them, read «شركاءَ الجنِّ» with «الجن» in the genitive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And it was read in the genitive, by an iḍāfa (genitive construct) of explanation (tabyīn); the meaning is: they associated them in their worship, because they obeyed them as they obeyed Allah." The Shaykh said: "The meaning of this reading is not clear, since the implied form is: and they made the partners of the jinn to Allah." I say: its meaning is clear from al-Zamakhsharī's explanation in his words "the meaning is: they associated them in their worship …" to the end, and for that reason he called it an iḍāfa of explanation, i.e. it explains the partners, as if it were said: the partners who obey the jinn.
His words: {وَخَلَقَهُمْ}: The majority read «خَلَقَهم» with fatḥa of the lām as a past verb. In this clause there are two possibilities. One of them: that it is circumstantial, with «قد» implied according to some and not implied according to others.
The second: that it is resumptive with no grammatical position. Regarding the pronoun in «خلقهم» there are two aspects. One of them: that it refers back to those who make [partners], i.e. they made partners for Him although He created them and brought them into being, alone in that, with no one sharing with Him in their creation; so how can they associate with Him others who had no effect in their creation? The second: that it refers back to the jinn, i.e. while the case is that He created the partners; so how can they make what He created a partner to Him?
Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read: «وَخَلْقهم» with sukūn of the lām. The Shaykh said: "And so it is in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh." I say: his statement "and so it is in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh" is open to question, in that the conventional vowel-marking — I mean what indicates the three vowels and what indicates sukūn, like the jazm sign — the codices of the early generations were free of it, and the pointing present in our hands today is a later development; it is said that the first to introduce it was Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar. So how can that be attributed to the codex of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd? [Translator's note: the source reads «كالجزء منه», rendered here following the evident sense «كالجزم» (like the jazm sign).] There are two interpretations of this reading. One of them: that «خَلْقهم» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of their fabrication. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. their fabricating of falsehood; meaning: they ascribed to Allah their fabrication, since they attributed their foul deeds to Allah in their saying «والله أمَرَنا بها» ('and Allah commanded us to do them')." End of quote. So «لله» is the second object, fronted before the first. The second interpretation: that «خَلْقهم» is a maṣdar in the sense of what they make (makhlūqahum), so it is conjoined to «الجن», and its second object is omitted, its implied form being: and they made what they make — which is the idols they carve, as in the words of the Exalted: {قَالَ أَتَعْبُدُونَ مَا تَنْحِتُونَ} — partners to Allah the Exalted.
The words of the Exalted: «وخَرَقوا»: The majority read «خَرَقوا» with the rāʾ unstressed, and Nāfiʿ with it doubled. Ibn ʿAbbās read it with the undotted ḥāʾ and the fāʾ, with the rāʾ unstressed [i.e. «وحَرَفوا»], and Ibn ʿUmar likewise except that he doubled the rāʾ. The unstressed form in the reading of the majority means fabrication. Al-Farrāʾ said: "One says khalaqa al-ifka, kharaqahu, ikhtalaqahu, iftarāhu, iftaʿalahu and kharaṣahu, meaning he lied in it." The doubling is for multiplicity, because those who said that were a great multitude. And it was said: they are two dialectal forms, the unstressed one being the original. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may/ be from kharaqa al-thawba, when he tore the garment, i.e. they split off (ishtaqqū) for Him sons and daughters." As for the reading with the undotted ḥāʾ, its meaning is falsifying, i.e. they falsely fabricated children for Him, because the falsifier distorts and changes the truth into falsehood.
His words {بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ}: there are two aspects in it. One of them: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. they fabricated for Him a fabrication without knowledge; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it, and it is weak in meaning. The second, and it is the better: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of «خرقوا», i.e. they fabricated the lie accompanied by ignorance, which is the absence of knowledge.

semin-durr:101-101.t:
The words of the Exalted: {بَدِيعُ}: The majority read it with the ʿayn in the nominative, and there are three aspects in it. The most apparent: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هو بديعُ», so the pause is on His words «والأرض», and it is a self-standing clause. The second: that it is the fāʿil (agent) of His words «تعالى», i.e. "exalted is the Originator of the heavens", and this verbal clause is conjoined to the implied verb before it, which makes سبحان accusative, for «سبحان», as preceded, is among the maṣdars whose accusative-governing verb must be implied. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is what follows, namely His words {أنى يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ}. Al-Manṣūr read «بديعِ» in the genitive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Referring back (raddan) to His words وجعلوا لله, or to سبحانه." So he said, without explaining on which of the aspects of i'rab it is; likewise the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] reported it from him and passed over it. By "referring back" he means its being a follower either of «لله» or of the genitive pronoun in «سبحانه»; its following it is by being a badal (substitute) of «لله» or of the hāʾ in «سبحانه». It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «لله», on the view that the iḍāfa of «بديع» is pure, as you will learn. As for its following the hāʾ, it must be a badal, and it cannot be an adjective even if we hold it to be definite by the iḍāfa, because of another obstacle: a pronoun is not qualified by an adjective — except the third-person pronoun on the opinion of al-Kisāʾī, on whose opinion that may be permissible.
Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Shāmī read «بديعَ» in the accusative; its accusative is by way of praise, and it supports the genitive reading. The aforementioned nominative reading may originally have been following [the preceding] in the genitive as a badal, and then the follower was cut off into the nominative. Badīʿ may be in the sense of mubdiʿ (originator) — its meaning has preceded — or it may be a ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle) put in construct with its nominative, as in your saying: فلان بديع الشعر, i.e. his poetry is original. On these two views its iḍāfa is verbal (lafẓiyya), because in the first it belongs to the topic of putting the active participle in construct with its accusative, and in the second to the topic of putting the ṣifa mushabbaha in construct with its nominative. And it may be in the sense of "having no peer or likeness in them", as if it were said: the Matchless One in the heavens and the earth; on this view the iḍāfa is a pure iḍāfa.
His words: {أنى يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ}: أنَّى is in the sense of "how" or "from where". There are two aspects in it. One of them: that it is the khabar of incomplete kāna, «له» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «ولد» is its noun. It may also be accusative by resemblance to the ḥāl or the adverb, like His words «كيف تكفرون بالله»; and the governor in it, Abū al-Baqāʾ said, is «يكون» — this is on the opinion of whoever permits «كان» to govern ḥāls, adverbs and the like — with «له» the khabar of يكون and «ولد» its noun. It is also permissible for «يكون» to be complete (tāmma), and this is better, i.e. how could a child come to exist for Him when the causes of having a child are absent?
His words: «ولم تكنْ له صاحبةٌ»: this wāw is circumstantial, and the clause after it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the content of the preceding clause, i.e. how could He have a child, while He has no consort? It is known that a child comes only from between a male and a female, and He is exalted above that.
The majority read «تكن» with the tāʾ (feminine prefix). Al-Nakhaʿī read it with the yāʾ (masculine prefix), and there are four aspects in it. The first: that the verb is ascribed to «صاحبة» as well, as in the well-known reading, and the masculine was permissible only because of the separation, like his saying:
2024 - لقد وَلَدَ الأخيطِلَ أمُّ سوءٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(An evil mother gave birth to the little Akhṭal …)
And his saying:
2025 - إنَّ امرَأً غَرَّه في الدنيا واحدةٌ ... بعدي وبعدك في الدنيا لمغرور
(A man whom a single woman has deceived in this world, after me and after you, is indeed deluded.)
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Making kāna and its sisters masculine with a feminine noun is easier than that in other verbs." The Shaykh said: "I do not know this from the grammarians; they did not distinguish between kāna and others." I say: this is a correct statement, and it is supported by the fact that al-Fārisī, although he holds that some of them, like laysa, are particles, does not permit dropping the tāʾ from it: if you said «ليس هند قائمة», it would not be permissible. The second: that in «يكون» there is a pronoun referring back to Allah the Exalted, «له» is a fronted khabar, «صاحبة» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of «يكون». The third: that «له» alone is the khabar, and «صاحبةٌ» is its fāʿil, because it is supported (iʿtimād)/; this is preferable to what precedes it, because the preposition-phrase is closer to a single word, and the default in predicates is the single word. The fourth: that in «يكون» there is the pronoun of the matter and the case (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), «له» is a fronted khabar, «صاحبةٌ» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of «يكون», explaining the pronoun of the case. In this [aspect] it is not permissible for «له» alone to be the khabar with «صاحبةٌ» its fāʿil, as was permissible in the aspect before it. The difference is that the pronoun of the case is explained only by an explicit clause, and it has preceded that this kind belongs to the category of single words. And «تكن» may be the incomplete or the complete [kāna], according to what preceded in what is before it.
His words: {وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ}: this is an informative, resumptive clause; it may also be a ḥāl, and it is a permanent ḥāl.

semin-durr:102-102.t: The words of the Exalted: {ذلكم}: i.e. that One, described by those preceding attributes, is Allah; so the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الله» its khabar (predicate), and likewise «ربكم», and likewise the clause {لا إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}, and likewise «خالق». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a mubtadaʾ, and what follows are successive predicates." I say: this is according to whoever permits multiple predicates unconditionally. It is also permissible for «الله» alone to be the khabar and what follows it badals (substitutes); so said Abū al-Baqāʾ. This is open to question, in that some of them are derived, and the badal is rare with derived words; though it may be said that these, even if derived, have become like non-derived (jāmid) words with respect to Allah the Exalted, by being exclusive to Him. It is also permissible for «الله» to be the badal, with what follows likewise predicates. Whoever forbids multiple predicates implies a mubtadaʾ before each khabar, or makes them all equivalent to a single noun, as if it were said: that described One is He who combines these attributes.

semin-durr:104-104.t:
The words of the Exalted: {قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ بَصَآئِرُ}: The verb was made masculine only for two reasons: one of them, the separation by the object; the second, that the feminine gender is figurative. Al-baṣāʾir is the plural of al-baṣīra, which is the indication that necessitates souls' perceiving a thing; from it the blood that points to the slain person was called baṣīra [Translator's note: the source has «بصرة»; the word for such blood is usually given as «بَصِيرة»]. Al-baṣīra is specific to the heart, as al-baṣar (sight) is to the eye; this is the view of some. Al-Rāghib said: "The perceiving power of the heart is called baṣīra and baṣar; the Exalted said: {مَا زَاغَ البصر وَمَا طغى} [al-Najm: 17]." The verification of this has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara.
And {مِن رَّبِّكُمْ} may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it, or attached to something omitted as an adjective of what precedes it, i.e. baṣāʾir existing from your Lord; and «مِنْ» in both aspects is for the beginning of extent, figuratively.
His words: {فَمَنْ أَبْصَرَ}: [مَنْ] may be conditional or relative; the fāʾ is [introducing] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) on the first, and added in the khabar (predicate) on the second, because of the relative's resemblance to the conditional noun. Before the lām of the genitive there must be something omitted by which the speech becomes sound, the implied form being: "then the seeing is for himself, and whoever is blind, then the blindness is against it." The seeing and the blindness are two mubtadaʾs (subjects), the preposition-phrase after them is the khabar, and the fāʾ enters upon this clause which occurs as an apodosis or a khabar; its mubtadaʾ was omitted only because it is known. Al-Zajjāj implied something close to this, saying: "Then for himself is the benefit of that, and whoever is blind, then against it is the harm of that." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "So whoever sees the truth and believes, then for himself he has seen and himself he has benefited; and whoever is blind, then against it, i.e. against himself he has been blind, and himself he has harmed." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What we implied of the maṣdar (verbal noun) — namely 'the seeing' and 'the blindness' — is preferable, for two reasons. One of them: that the omitted element is a single word, not a clause, and the preposition-phrase is a pillar (ʿumda), not a complement (faḍla), whereas in his implied form the omitted element is a clause and the preposition-phrase a complement. The second, and it is stronger: that if the implied form were a verb, the fāʾ would not enter, whether «مَنْ» is conditional or a relative resembling the condition, because when the past verb is neither a supplication nor non-inflecting (jāmid) and occurs as the apodosis of a condition or the khabar of a mubtadaʾ resembling the condition, the fāʾ does not enter the apodosis or the khabar; if you said «مَنْ جاءني فأكرمتُه», it would not be permissible — unlike our implied form, in which the fāʾ is required and may not be omitted except in poetry." I say: this implied form that al-Zamakhsharī implied was preceded by someone: al-Kalbī preceded him to it, for he said: "So whoever sees, believes, and has faith in Muḥammad ﷺ, then for himself he has acted; and whoever is blind and does not believe, then against himself he has brought the punishment." And his statement "the fāʾ does not enter in what was mentioned" may be disputed: if, in what is fit to be an explicit apodosis and in which/ the effect of the jussive particle appears, like the imperfect, the entry of the fāʾ is permissible — as in {وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ الله مِنْهُ} [al-Māʾida: 95] — then the past verb is all the more fit and worthy of its entry.

semin-durr:159-159.t:
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read: {فَارَقُوا} — from mufāraqa (parting) — and there are two views on it. The first: that the form fāʿala has the meaning of faʿʿala, as in ضاعَفْتُ الحساب and ضعَّفْتُه ("I doubled the account"). It was also said: it is from mufāraqa, which is abandoning and leaving alone; and whoever divides his religion, believing in part and disbelieving in part, has parted from the upright religion. The rest read فرَّقوا with doubling (tashdīd). Al-Aʿmash, Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibrāhīm read فَرَقوا with the rāʾ undoubled. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It has the meaning of the doubled form, and it may mean: they separated it from the true religion." The meaning of الشيع has already been given.
His words {لَسْتَ مِنْهُمْ} are in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of إنَّ, and «منهم» is the khabar of «ليس», since the meaning is complete with it, as in the words of al-Nābigha:
2131 - إذا حاولْتَ في أسد فُجورا ... فإني لستُ منك ولست مني
(If you seek wickedness against Asad, then I am not of you and you are not of me.)
Its counterpart in the affirmative is: {فَمَن تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي} [Ibrāhīm: 36]. On this view «في شيء» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the notion of being-settled to which «منهم» is attached, i.e.: you are not settled among them in anything, i.e. in anything of their dividing. It is also possible that «في شيء» is the khabar and «منهم» a ḥāl (circumstantial) placed before it; that is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.: you are not in anything that is of their dividing; when the adjective was placed first, it was made accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:160-160.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا}: The number is given the masculine form [without tāʾ] although the counted noun is masculine for several reasons. Among them: that the iḍāfa (genitive construct) has an effect, as has been stated more than once, so the masculine acquired femininity from the feminine and was given the ruling of the feminine, namely dropping the tāʾ from its number. For that reason its verb is made feminine when it is annexed to a feminine, as in: {تَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ السيارة} [Yūsuf: 10], and [his saying]:
