2132 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما شَرِقت صدرُ القَنَاةِ. . . . .
(…as the top of the spear choked [with blood]…)
[and his saying]:
2133 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تسفَّهت أعاليَها مرُّ الرياح. . .
(…the passing of the winds swayed their tops…)
and other examples whose verification has been given before. Among them: that this masculine denotes a feminine, so the intended meaning was taken into account rather than the wording; on this is the poet's saying:
2134 - وإنَّ كلاباً هذه عشرُ أَبْطُنٍ ... وأنت بريء من قبائلها العشرِ
(Kilāb, this one, is ten clans, and you are quit of its ten tribes.)
He did not attach the tāʾ to the number of أبطن although it is masculine, because it denotes a feminine, namely the tribes, as though it were said: Kilāb, this one, is ten tribes. Similar is the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
2135 - وكان مِجَنِّي دونَ مَنْ كنت أتَّقي ... ثلاثُ شُخوصٍ كاعبانِ ومُعْصِرُ
(My shield against the one I was wary of was three figures: two full-bosomed maidens and a girl come of age.)
He did not attach the tāʾ to the number of «شخوص», which is masculine, since it denotes the women. This is better than the previous one because the feminine is stated explicitly in his saying كاعبان ومعصر. This is just as, when a feminine word is meant with a masculine sense, they look to what is intended rather than the wording and attach the tāʾ to the number of the feminine; from that is the poet's saying:
2136 - ثلاثةُ أنفسٍ وثلاثُ ذُوْدٍ ... لقد جار الزمانُ على عِيالي
(Three souls and three camels — time has wronged my household.)
He attached the tāʾ to the number of «أنفس», which is feminine, because males are meant by it. Similar is: {اثنتي عَشْرَةَ أَسْبَاطاً} [al-Aʿrāf: 160] on one of the two views, which will come, if Allah wills, in its place.
Among them: that he took into account the omitted described noun (mawṣūf), the implied form being: "he will have ten good deeds (ḥasanāt) like it"; then the described noun was omitted and its adjective put in its place, leaving the number as it was. Similar is «مررت بثلاثة نسابات» ("I passed by three genealogists"): the tāʾ was attached to the number of the feminine out of regard for the omitted described noun, since the original is: بثلاثة رجال نسابات ("three men, genealogists"). Abū ʿAlī said: "Two matters have come together here, each of which requires the feminine; when they combined, the feminine became strong. One of them: that الأمثال are in meaning 'ḥasanāt', so the feminine was allowed, as in his saying:
2137 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ثلاثُ شخوصٍ كاعبان ومعصر
(…three figures: two full-bosomed maidens and a girl come of age.)
by شخوص he meant women. The other: that what is annexed to a feminine may be made feminine even if it is masculine, as in the saying of the one who said: 'قُطِعَتْ بعض أصابعه' ('some of his fingers were cut off'), {يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ السيارة} [Yūsuf: 10]."
Yaʿqūb, al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Aʿmash and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read with tanwīn: «أمثالُها» in the nominative as an adjective of عشر, i.e.: he will have ten good deeds like that good deed. This reading is free of the interpretations mentioned for the well-known reading.
[Translator's note: In the reading attributed here, the tanwīn falls on «عشرٌ» (عشرٌ أمثالُها); the source text says only "with tanwīn".]

semin-durr:161-161.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {دِيناً}: Its accusative has several explanations. The first: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the sense, i.e.: He guided me with the guidance of an upright religion; or on the implied verb «عَرَّفني ديناً» ("He made known to me a religion"), or "adhere to a religion". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is the second object of هداني." This is a mistake, because the second object here is the noun made genitive by إلى, which sufficed. Makkī said: it is accusative as a badal (substitute) from the position of «إلى صراط». It was also said: [it is accusative] by an implied هداني, because the first «هداني» indicates it; this is like the previous one in meaning.
[Translator's note: The closing quotation mark after Abū al-Baqāʾ's words is misplaced in the source; the rendering above follows the evident sense.]
The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read: «قِيَماً» with kasra on the qāf and an undoubled fatḥa on the yāʾ, and the rest with fatḥa on it [the qāf] and a doubled kasra on the yāʾ. The explanation of one of the two readings has been given in al-Nisāʾ and al-Māʾida. «مِلَّة» is a badal from «ديناً», or accusative by an implied أعني ("I mean"). «حنيفاً» was discussed in al-Baqara.
Nāfiʿ read ومَحْيايْ with sukūn on the yāʾ of the first person, and it involves bringing two quiescent letters together.
Al-Fārisī said: it is like their saying «التقت حَلْقتا البطان» ("the two rings of the girth met") and «ولفلان ثلثا المال» ("so-and-so has two-thirds of the property"), meaning the two alifs. Some people have criticised this reading on account of what I mentioned, the joining of two quiescents, and expressed surprise that this reader moves the yāʾ of «مماتي» and makes the yāʾ of «مَحْياي» quiescent. Some have reported that Nāfiʿ retracted that. Abū Shāma said: "So it ought not to be permissible to report the sukūn of the yāʾ of «محياي» from him." Nāfiʿ read, in one transmission, «محيايِ» with kasra on the yāʾ, which resembles Ḥamza's reading in {بِمُصْرِخِيَّ} [Ibrāhīm: 22], which will come, if Allah the Exalted wills. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿĪsā al-Jaḥdarī read: ومَحْيَيَّ, changing the alif to yāʾ and assimilating it into the yāʾ of the first person; this is the dialect of Hudhayl, and I have cited for it the verse of Abū Dhuʾayb:
2138 - سبقوا هَوَيَّ وأعنقوا لهواهُمُ ... فَتُخُرِّمُوا ولكلِّ جَنْبٍ مَصْرَعُ
(They went before my desire and hastened to their own desire, and were carried off; and for every side there is a place of falling.)
in Sūrat al-Baqara. From here to the end of the sūra its i'rab is clear because of the repeated parallels. He emphasised his saying «لغفور» with the lām to indicate the breadth of His mercy, and did not emphasise the swiftness of punishment in that way here, though He did emphasise it in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, because there the context is one of frightening and threatening, and after mentioning the story of those who transgressed on the Sabbath and others, so emphasising punishment suited it there. And He brought two attributes, forgiveness and mercy, while on the side of punishment He brought only one attribute, indicating His forbearance and the breadth of His forgiveness and mercy.
[Translator's note: «ʿĪsā al-Jaḥdarī» is as written in the source; ʿĪsā (ibn ʿUmar) and al-Jaḥdarī are usually two different readers.]

semin-durr:113-113.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {ولتصغى}: there are three views about this lām. The first: that it is the lām of kay (purpose), and the verb after it is accusative by an implied أَنْ. As to what it is attached to (mutaʿalliq), there are two possibilities. The first possibility: that it is attached to «يُوحي», being conjoined to «غروراً», «غروراً» being a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the implied form is: some of them inspire others for the sake of deception and for the sake of inclining. But since the first object of purpose fulfilled the conditions for the accusative, it was put in the accusative, and since this one does not fulfil the conditions, the verb reached it through the particle of cause. Of the conditions it lacks is that the agent is not the same in both, for the agent of the inspiring is «بعضهم» while the agent of the inclining is the hearts; it also lacks the condition of being an explicit maṣdar (verbal noun). The second possibility: that it is attached to something omitted, placed after it. Al-Zajjāj gave its implied form as: "and so that [the hearts] incline to it, they did that." Al-Zamakhsharī gave a similar implied form, saying: "«ولتصغى»: its correlate is omitted, its implied form being: and so that that may come about, We made for every prophet an enemy" — [Translator's note: the source here repeats the clause «الزمخشري فقال: ولتصغى جوابُه محذوف تقديره: وليكونَ ذلك جَعَلْنا», evidently a copying duplication] — "on the basis that the lām is the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra)."

The second view: / that the lām is the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra), which they also express as the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba). This is the opinion of al-Zamakhsharī, as was also reported from him above.

The third view: that it is the lām of the oath. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Except that it was given kasra since the verb was not emphasised with the nūn." What he said is not known; rather, what is known in this opinion is that this is the lām of kay, and it is the response of an omitted oath, its implied form being: «والله لَتَصْغَى», so «لِتَصْغَى» was put in the place of «لَتَصْغَيَنَّ», and the response of the oath became of the category of a single word, as when you say: «واللهِ لَيقومُ زيدٌ», i.e. "I swear by Allah to the standing of Zayd". This is the doctrine of al-Akhfash, and he cited:

2034 - إذا قلتُ قَدْني قال بالله حَلْفَةً ... لِتُغْنِيَ عني ذا إنائك أجمعا
(When I say, "Enough for me," he says, swearing an oath by Allah: "You shall drain this vessel of yours for me entirely.")

His saying «لتُغْني» is the response of the oath. So it has become clear that the one holding this opinion says it is the lām of kay; the most that can be said is that it occurred in the position of the response of the oath, not that it is itself a response, and it was given kasra when the nūn of emphasis was omitted from it. What shows the unsoundness of that is that the nūn has been omitted while the lām of the response remains with its fatḥa; the poet said:

2035 - لَئِنْ تَكُ قد ضاقَتْ عليكم بيوتُكُمْ ... لَيَعْلَمُ ربِّي أنَّ بيتيَ واسعُ
(If your houses have become too narrow for you, my Lord knows that my house is spacious.)

His saying «لَيَعْلَمُ» is the response of the oath prepared for by the lām in «لِئنْ» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «لَئِنْ»], and yet it has fatḥa despite the omission of the nūn of emphasis. The verification of this question with al-Akhfash has a place other than this.

The pronoun in His saying «ما فعلوه» and in «إليه» refers either to the inspiration, or to the embellishment (zukhruf), or to the speech, or to the deception, or to the enmity, since it has the sense of mutual hostility. «ولتصغى» means "and so that they incline". This root denotes inclining, and from it is His saying, Exalted is He: {فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا} [al-Taḥrīm: 4] [Translator's note: the source gives the verse number as 5; it is verse 4]. In the ḥadīth: «فأصغى لها الإِناء» ("so he tilted the vessel for it"). A man's ṣāghiya are his relatives who incline towards him, and «عين صَغْوى» is a slanting eye. Al-Aʿshā said:

2036 - ترى عينها صَغْواءَ في جَنْبِ مُؤْقِها ... تُراقب في كَفِّي القطيعَ المحرَّما
(You see her eye slanting at the corner of its socket, watching the plaited whip in my palm.)

Al-ṣaghā is a slant in the jaw and the eye; «صَغَت الشمس والنجوم» means the sun and the stars inclined towards setting. One says صَغَوْتُ, صَغِيْتُ and صَغَيْتُ, so the third radical is wāw or yāʾ, and with the yāʾ the ghayn of the past tense takes kasra or fatḥa. The Shaykh said: "The maṣdar of the first is صَغْوٌ, of the second صُغِيٌّ, and of the third صَغَاً, and their imperfect is يَصْغَى with fatḥa on the middle radical." I say: al-Aṣmaʿī reported, as the maṣdar of صَغَا يَصْغُو, the form صَغَاً; so «صَغَاً» is not exclusively the maṣdar of «صَغِي» with kasra. Al-Farrāʾ added «صُغِيَّاً» and «صُغُوَّاً», with doubled yāʾ and doubled wāw. As for his saying "and their imperfect" — i.e. the imperfect of the three verbs — "is يَصْغَى with fatḥa on the middle radical", Abū ʿUbayd reported from al-Kisāʾī «صَغَوْتُ أصغو», and likewise Ibn al-Sikkīt reported «صَغَوْتُ أَصْغُو»; so they differentiated between their imperfects, and «صَغَوْت أَصْغُو» is the widespread regular pattern, for the regular imperfect of faʿala whose third radical is a weak wāw is yafʿulu with ḍamma on the middle radical. The Shaykh also said: "They" — meaning the three verbs — "are intransitive", i.e. they do not take an object; and «أصغى» is likewise intransitive, but it also occurs as transitive, the hamza then being for transfer (causative). He cited for the intransitive «أَصْغَى» the poet's saying:

2037 - ترى السَّفيهَ به عن كل مُحْكِمَةٍ ... زَيْغٌ وفيه إلى التشبيه إصغاء
(You see the fool deviating from every clear verse, and in him is an inclining towards anthropomorphism.)

I say: and like it is the saying of another:

2038 - تُصْغِي إذا شدَّها بالرَّحْلِ جانحةً ... حتى إذا ما استوى في غَرْزِها تَثِبُ
(She leans sideways when he binds the saddle on her, until, once he is settled in her stirrup, she springs up.)

You say: «أصغى فلانٌ بأذنه إلى فلان» ("so-and-so inclined his ear to so-and-so"). He cited for the transitive «أصغى» the saying of another:

2039 - أَصاخَ مِنْ نَبْأَةٍ أَصْغى لها أُذُنَاً ... صِماخُها بدخيس الذوق مستور
(He listened intently at a faint sound, inclining to it an ear whose canal is hidden by its dense inner part.)

I say: and in the ḥadīth: «فأصغى لها الإِناء». What he claimed — that صغَى, صَغِيَ or صَغَا are intransitive — is not agreed upon; rather al-Rāghib reported that one says «صَغَيْتُ الإِناء» and «أصغيتُه» ("I tilted the vessel"). «صَغِيت» with kasra on the ghayn may be from the roots with yāʾ, or it may be from the roots with wāw, the wāw having been changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it, like «قَوِي», which is from القوة. The reading of al-Nakhaʿī and al-Jarrāḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh is «ولِتُصْغَى», from the four-letter «أصغى», which is intransitive here.

Al-Ḥasan read: «وَلْتَصْغى ولْيَرْضَوْه/ ولْيقترفوا» with sukūn on the lām in all three. Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī said: "The reading of al-Ḥasan is only «ولِتَصْغِي», with kasra on the ghayn." I say: so it would be like the reading of al-Nakhaʿī. And it was said: al-Ḥasan read «ولِتصغى» with kasra on the lām like the majority, and «ولْيرضوه ولْيقترفوا» with sukūn on the lām. They explained the sukūn of the lām in one of two ways. Either it is the lām of kay, given sukūn only by treating it together with what follows like كَبِد and نَمِر [Translator's note: i.e. words in which the kasra may be dropped as كَبْد and نَمْر]. Ibn Jinnī said: "It is strong in analogy, irregular in attested usage." The second: that it is the lām of the command. Even if this works in «ليرضوه» and «ليقترفوا», it does not work in «ولتصْغَى», since the weak letter would be dropped in the jussive. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not the lām of command, because the verb is not made jussive." I say: the weak letter has been retained in the jussive in the mutawātir readings, among them: «أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَداً نَرْتَعي وَيَلْعَبْ», {إِنَّهُ مَن يَتَّقِ وَيِصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ الله} [Yūsuf: 90], {سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلاَ تنسى} [al-Aʿlā: 6], {لاَّ تَخَفْ دَرَكاً وَلاَ تخشى} [Ṭāhā: 77]. In all of these there are interpretations which you will come upon, Allah the Exalted willing; so let this irregular reading be like these places. To say that the lām of «لتصغى» is the lām of kay given sukūn because of the succession of vowels, while the two lāms after it are lāms of command, is far-fetched and mere whim. Al-Naḥḥās said: "And it is read «ولْيقترفوا»" — meaning with sukūn — and he said: "It carries the sense of threat." I say: he means it is a command of threat, like His saying: {اعملوا مَا شِئْتُمْ} [Fuṣṣilat: 40]. He did not report the sukūn in «لتصْغَى» nor in «ليرضوه».

«ما» in «ما هم مُقْتَرِفون» is a nominal relative, or an indefinite qualified by an adjective — [Translator's note: the source repeats «أو نكرة موصوفة»] — or maṣdariyya; the referent pronoun on both of the first two views is omitted, i.e. «ما هم مقترفوه». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "He kept the nūn since the hāʾ was omitted." He means that for a pronoun attached to a dual active participle, or to one in the sound plural, the nūn of the dual and plural is dropped, as in «هذان ضارباه» and «هؤلاء ضاربوه»; when the pronoun is omitted, the cause disappears and the nūn returns. This — I mean dropping the nūn when the pronoun is attached — is the more frequent usage, but it has also been retained; the poet said:

2040 - ولم يَرْتَفِقْ والناسُ مُحْتَضِرُونه ... جميعاً وأيدي المعتفين رواهقهْ
(He did not recline at ease while the people were all crowding round him and the hands of the seekers of favour were pressing upon him.)

And he said:

2041 - هم الفاعلونَ الخيرَ والآمرونهُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . .
(They are the doers of good and the commanders of it…)

Al-iqtirāf is acquisition (iktisāb); «اقترف فلان لأهله» means he earned for his family. It is mostly said of evil and sin, but it is also applied to good; Allah the Exalted said: {وَمَن يَقْتَرِفْ حَسَنَةً نَّزِدْ لَهُ فِيهَا حُسْناً} [al-Shūrā: 23]. Ibn al-Anbārī said: "قَرَف and اقْتَرَف mean to acquire." And he cited:

2042 - وإني لآتٍ ما أَتَيْتُ وإنني ... لِمَا اقترفَتْ نفسي عَليَّ لَراهِبُ
(I indeed do what I have done, and I am indeed fearful of what my soul has earned against me.)

The origin of al-qirf and al-iqtirāf is peeling the bark of a tree, and the skin from the top of the wound — [Translator's note: the source reads «الحَرَج»; «الجُرْح» (the wound) is evidently intended] — and what is taken from it is called qirf. Then iqtirāf was borrowed for acquiring, whether good or bad, being more often used for the bad. «قارف فلان أمراً» means he engaged in something for which he is blamed. And it was said: confession (al-iʿtirāf) removes the wrongdoing (al-iqtirāf). «رجل مُقْرِف» is a man of mixed (ignoble) lineage; the poet said:

2043 - كم بجودٍ مُقْرِفٍ نال العُلى ... وشريفٍ بُخْلُه قد وضَعَهْ
(How many a man of low birth has attained the heights through generosity, and how many a nobleman has his miserliness brought low!)

«قَرَفْتُه بكذا» means I accused him of it or blamed him with it.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). You have learned from what has passed that «أيّ» is part of what it is annexed to; so when it is interrogative, the apparent sense requires that it be named by the name of what it is annexed to. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This necessitates that Allah the Exalted be called «شيئاً» (a thing)." On this view, the word of majesty is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. that thing is Allah the Exalted. The word of majesty may also be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being: Allah is greater in testimony. «شهيد», on these two views, is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. He is a witness between me and you. The clause from His saying {قُلِ الله}, on the two aspects mentioned, is an answer to «أيّ» in terms of both wording and meaning. The word of majesty may also be a mubtadaʾ and «شهيد» its khabar; on this view the clause is an answer to «أيّ» in terms of meaning, i.e. it indicates the answer and is not the answer itself.

His saying: {شَهَادةً}: accusative as a tamyīz (specification); and this is the only thing the grammarians recognise. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is valid as an object, by construing «أكبر» as resembling the ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the active participle)." This is utterly worthless, since the grammarians have stated explicitly that the meaning of its resemblance to the active participle lies in its being made feminine, dual and plural, whereas afʿal min (the elative with «مِن») is not made feminine, dual or plural, so it does not resemble the active participle — to the point that the Shaykh attributed this blunder to the copyist rather than to Abū Muḥammad.

His saying: {بِيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «شهيد». The original was «قل الله شهيد بيننا» (say: Allah is witness between us), and «بين» was repeated for emphasis. It is parallel to his saying:
187 - 7- فأيِّي ما وأيُّك كان شراً ... فَسِيقَ إلى المَقامةِ لا يراها
(Whichever of me and of you was the worse, may he be driven to the assembly without seeing it [i.e. blind].)
and his saying:
187 - 8- يا ربَّ موسَى أظلمي وأَظْلَمُهْ ... فاصْبُبْ عليه ملِكاً لا يَرْحَمُهْ
(O Lord of Moses, whichever of me and him is the more unjust, pour upon him a king who has no mercy on him.)
and his saying:
187 - 9- فلئِنْ لَقِيْتُك خالِيَيْنِ لَتَعْلَمَنْ ... أيِّي وأيُّك فارسُ الأحزابِ
(If I meet you with the two of us alone, you will surely know which of me and of you is the horseman of the confederates.)
What unites them is that, since he annexed to the yāʾ alone, he needed to repeat that annexed noun. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «بيني» to be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «شهيد», so it would be in the position of nominative; but the apparent view is otherwise.

His saying: {وَأُوحِيَ}: the majority [read it] in the passive, the agent being omitted because it is known, namely Allah the Exalted; and «القرآن» is nominative by it. Abū Nahīk, al-Jaḥdarī, ʿIkrima and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «وأَوْحَى» in the active, with «القرآن» accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «لأنذركم» is attached to «أُوحِي». It was said: there is a conjoined term there that was omitted because the speech indicates it, i.e. to warn you with it and give you glad tidings with it, as in His saying: {تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81]; a good number of such instances has preceded. It was also said: there is no need for it, because the context is one of instilling fear.

His saying: {وَمَن بَلَغَ}: there are three views on it. One of them: that it is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the accusative [pronoun] in «لأُنْذِرَكم», «مَنْ» being a relative whose returning pronoun from its ṣila (relative clause) is omitted, i.e. and to warn whoever the Qurʾān reaches.

The second: that in «بَلَغ» there is a nominative pronoun referring to «مَنْ», the object being omitted; it too is accusative in position, coordinated with the object of «لأنذركم»; the implied form is: and to warn whoever has reached puberty; so the returning pronoun here is latent in the verb. The third: that «مَنْ» is nominative in position, coordinated with the nominative pronoun in «لأنذرَكم»; that is permissible because the separation by the object and the preposition phrase made emphasising it unnecessary; the implied form is: that I may warn you with it, and that whoever the Qurʾān reaches may warn you.

His saying: {أَئِنَّكُمْ}: the majority read it with two hamzas, the first of them for the interrogative, which is an interrogative of reproach and rebuke. The discussion of the readings of the like of this has preceded. The Shaykh said: "And with easing (tashīl) of the second, and with inserting an alif between the first hamza and the eased hamza; al-Aṣmaʿī transmitted this last from Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ." End. This statement suggests that it is a strange reading, and it is not so; rather what is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr is the prolongation between the two hamzas, and there is no disagreement from Qālūn about that. It was read with a single hamza, which may be interrogative, the [interrogative hamza] having been omitted because the meaning is understood and the well-known reading indicates it; and it may be a pure statement.

Then this interrogative clause may be accusative in position because it is within the scope of the saying — and this is the apparent view — as if he was commanded to say: what thing is greatest in testimony, and to say: do you indeed testify…? It may also not be within its scope, and it then has no position. «أخرى» is an adjective of «آلهة», because the plural of what is not rational is treated like the feminine singular, as in His saying: {مَآرِبُ أخرى} [Ṭā Hā: 18] and {الأسمآء الحسنى} [al-Aʿrāf: 180].

His saying: {إِنَّمَا هُوَ إله وَاحِدٌ}: two aspects are allowed for this «ما». The more evident of them: that it restrains (kāffa) «إنَّ» from governing; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ, «إله» the khabar, and «واحد» its adjective. The second: that it is a relative meaning "that which", «هو» a mubtadaʾ and «إله» [written in the text: «وإليه»] its khabar; this clause is a ṣila with its returning pronoun, the relative is in the position of accusative as the noun of «إن», and «واحد» is its khabar; the implied form is: «إن الذي هو إله واحد» (that which is God is one). Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is weak. What indicates the correctness of the first aspect is that it is the only possible one in His saying, Exalted is He: {إِنَّمَا الله إله وَاحِدٌ} [al-Nisāʾ: 171], since «ما» cannot be a relative there, because the clause is devoid of a pronoun referring to the relative. Abū al-Baqāʾ said, regarding this aspect: "It is more fitting than the one before it", and I do not know what the reason for that is.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الذين آتَيْنَاهُمُ الكتاب}: the relative is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يَعْرِفونه» its khabar (predicate). The accusative pronoun may refer to the Messenger, or to the Qurʾān because it preceded in His saying: {وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هذا القرآن}, or to the divine oneness (tawḥīd) as indicated by His saying: {إِنَّمَا هُوَ إله وَاحِدٌ}, or to their [own] Book, or to all of that; and the pronoun is singular in consideration of the meaning, as if it were said: they know what We have mentioned and narrated. The iʿrāb of this clause has preceded in al-Baqara.

His saying: {الذين خسروا}: there are four aspects regarding its position. The most evident of them: that it is a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being the clause from His saying: {فَهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}; the fāʾ entered because of what you have learned about the relative's resemblance to the condition. The second: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «الذين آتيناهم الكتاب»; al-Zajjāj said this. The third: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. they are those who have lost. The fourth: that it is accusative by way of censure; these two aspects are branches of the naʿt, because they are cut off from it. On the last three views, {فَهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ} is a case of conjoining a nominal clause to its like. It may also be conjoined to «خسروا», but there is scrutiny in this, in that it leads to their not believing being the consequence of their loss, whereas the apparent sense is that the loss is the consequence of not believing. On the first aspect, «الذين خسروا» is more general than the rejecters among the polytheists [Translator's note: the text reads «من أهل الجاحدين», apparently corrupt]; on the others it is specific to the People of the Book, the implied form being: those of them — i.e. of the People of the Book — who have lost themselves.

A difficulty was raised against its being a naʿt: that they are cited as witnesses against the disbelievers of Quraysh and other Arabs — that is, how can they be cited as witnesses and be censured in one verse? It was said: this was brought for censure, not for citing as witnesses. It was also said: rather it was brought for citing as witnesses, even though in part of the speech there is censure of them, because that is in two respects [written in the text: «بوجيهن»] and two considerations. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "That is valid because what they were cited as witnesses in differs from what they were censured for, and the censure and the citing as witnesses are not from one aspect."

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ}: there are five aspects on it. One of them: that it is accusative by an implied verb after it, remaining an adverbial, i.e. and on the day We gather them, such-and-such will happen; it was omitted to be more effective in instilling fear. The second: that it is conjoined to an omitted adverbial, that adverbial being governed by His saying: {لاَ يُفْلِحُ الظالمون}; the implied form being: the wrongdoers will not succeed today in this world nor on the day We gather them; Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said this. The third: that it is accusative by His saying: {انظر كَيْفَ كَذَبُواْ}; there is remoteness in this because of its distance [written in the text: «لعبده»] from its governing element through the many intervening elements. The fourth: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied «اذكر» (mention). The fifth: that it is also a mafʿūl bihi, its governing element being "beware of" or "fear the day We gather them", as in His saying: {واخشوا يَوْماً} [Luqmān: 33]; but this is like the one before it, so it is not counted as a fifth.

The majority read «نَحْشرهم» with the nūn of majesty, and likewise «ثم نقول». Ḥumayd and Yaʿqūb read both with the yāʾ of the third person, referring to Allah the Exalted. The majority [read] ḍamma on the shīn of «نَحْشُرهم», and Abū Hurayra kasra; they are two dialectal forms in the imperfect. The accusative pronoun in «نحشرهم» refers to those who fabricate lies. It was said: to all people, these being included among them, while the rebuke is specific to them. It was said: it refers to the polytheists and their idols, as indicated by His saying: {احشروا الذين ظَلَمُواْ وَأَزْوَاجَهُمْ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعْبُدُونَ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 22]. «جميعاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «نحشُرهم». It may also be a tawkīd (emphasis), according to those grammarians who affirm it [as such], like «أجمعين». Conjunction was made here with «ثُمَّ» because of the interval occurring between the gathering and the saying. The two objects of «تَزْعُمون» are omitted because they are known, i.e. you claim them to be partners, or you claim that they are your intercessors.

His saying: {ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ}: if we make the pronoun in «نحشرهم» refer to those who fabricate lies, this is a case of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, since the original is «ثم نقول لهم»; it was made overt only to draw attention to the ugliness of polytheism.

semin-durr:83-83.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنَآ آتَيْنَاهَآ}: «تلك» points to the proofs given before, from His words {وَكَذَلِكَ نري إِبْرَاهِيمَ} [al-Anʿām: 75] to His words {وَمَآ أَنَاْ مِنَ المشركين} [al-Anʿām: 79]. Two aspects are possible in «حُجَّتنا». One: that it be the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject); in «آتيناها» there are then two aspects. One: it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the meaning of pointing; this is indicated by the explicit occurrence of the ḥāl in a parallel case, as in the words of Allah the Exalted {فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةً} [al-Naml: 52]. The second: it is in the position of a nominative as a second khabar; it is informed about with two predicates, one a single word and the other a clause. The second of the first two aspects: that «حُجَّتنا» be a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to «تلك», the khabar being the verbal clause.
Al-Ḥawfī said: "The clause «آتَيْناها» is in the position of an adjective (naʿt) of «حُجَّتنا», intending separation, since the implied form is «حجة لنا» ('an argument of Ours')"—meaning separation from the iḍāfa (genitive construct), so that the indefiniteness that permits a clause to be an adjective of «حُجَّتنا» is obtained. This ought not to be said. He also said: "«إبراهيم» is the second object of «آتيناها», and the first object is «ها»." I have already told you, early in al-Baqara at His words {آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الكتاب} [al-Baqara: 53], that this is the doctrine of al-Suhaylī, and that the doctrine of the majority is to make the first [object] the one that is rational and the second the other, regardless of placing before or after.
His words: «على قومه»: there are two aspects. One: it is attached to «آتينا»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Ḥawfī said this, i.e. "We made it prevail for Abraham over his people." The second: it is attached to an omitted [word], being a ḥāl, i.e. "We gave it to Abraham as an argument against his people," or "as a proof against his people"; so Abū al-Baqāʾ gave its implied form. This implied form entails that it is an emphatic ḥāl (muʾakkida), since the implied form is: "and that is Our argument, We gave it to him as an argument."
The Shaykh implied it with an omitted muḍāf, saying: "i.e. We gave it to Abraham rising above the arguments of his people and overpowering them"; and this is good. Abū al-Baqāʾ forbade that it be attached to «حجتنا», saying: "Because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and «آتيناها» is a khabar or a ḥāl, and neither of them may separate the relative [i.e. the maṣdar] from its ṣila." The Shaykh also forbade that, but because «الحجة» is not a maṣdar; he said: "It is only the speech composed to argue for something." Then he said: "And even if we made it a maṣdar, that would also not be permissible, because neither the khabar nor such a ḥāl may separate the maṣdar from what it requires." But his prohibition and Abū al-Baqāʾ's prohibition of that are open to consideration, because the ḥāl, even if it is a clause, is not extraneous such that separating by it would be forbidden, since it is among the things the maṣdar requires. I have given a parallel to this before, more fully than here.
His words: «نرفع»: there are two aspects. The apparent one: it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The second—Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it and began with it—is that it is in the position of a ḥāl from «آتيناها», meaning from the fāʿil (agent) of «آتيناها», i.e. "while We are raising"; it cannot be a ḥāl from the object, since there is no pronoun in it referring to it.
«نرفع» is read with the nūn of majesty and with the yāʾ of the third person [«يرفع»], and likewise «يشاء» [«نشاء»]. The people of Kufa read «درجات» with tanwīn, and likewise the one in Yūsuf, and the rest with the genitive construct in both. In the reading of the Kufans, the accusative of «درجات» may be explained in five ways. The first: it is in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and «مَنْ» is the object of «نرفع», i.e. "We raise whom We will in ranks and stations." The second: it is in the accusative as a second object placed before the first; this requires making «نرفع» include the meaning of a verb that takes two objects, e.g. «يُعْطي» ("gives"), i.e. "We give, by raising, whom We will degrees," i.e. ranks; and the degrees are what is raised, as in His words {رَفِيعُ الدرجات} [Ghāfir: 15], and in the hadith: "O Allah, raise his degree in ʿIlliyyīn"; when the degree is raised, its owner is raised. The third: it is in the accusative by omission of the preposition, i.e. "to stations and to degrees." The fourth: it is in the accusative as a tamyīz (specification), transferred from objecthood, so it comes back to the reading of the majority, since the original is {نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَّن نَّشَآءُ} in the genitive construct, then it was converted, as in His words {وَفَجَّرْنَا الأرض عُيُوناً} [al-Qamar: 12], i.e. the springs of the earth. The fifth: it is in the accusative as a ḥāl, by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of degrees." This reading is supported by the words of Allah the Exalted {وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ} [al-Anʿām: 165], {وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ لِّيَتَّخِذَ} [al-Zukhruf: 32] and {وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٍ وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى} [al-Baqara: 253].
As for the reading of the majority, «درجات» is the object of «نرفع». The address in «إنَّ ربك» is to the Messenger Muhammad (upon him be peace); and it is said: to Abraham al-Khalīl, in which case there is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to the second, drawing attention thereby to His honouring him.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَوَهَبْنَا}: there are two aspects concerning it. The correct one: it is conjoined to the nominal clause «وتلك حُجَّتنا»; conjoining a nominal clause to a verbal one and the reverse is permissible. The second—Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed it—is that it be conjoined (nasaq) to «آتيناها». The Shaykh rejected it on the grounds that «آتيناها» has a grammatical position, either khabar (predicate) or ḥāl (circumstantial), while this one has no position, since if it were conjoined to the khabar or the ḥāl a link would be required in it. «كلاً» is in the accusative by «هَدَيْنا» after it, the implied form being: "and each one of these mentioned."
His words: «ومن ذريَّته»: the hāʾ in «ذريته» has two aspects. One: it refers to Noah, because he is the nearest mentioned, and because Abraham and the prophets after him are all traced to him. The second: it refers to Abraham, because he is the one being spoken about and the story is set out to mention him and his account. But this view was rejected because Lot is not of his offspring; he is only his brother's or sister's son. Makkī and others mentioned that.
It has been answered. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "These prophets are all attributed to the offspring of Abraham, even if among them is one who is not joined to him by birth through a mother or a father, because Lot is the son of Abraham's brother, and the Arabs make the paternal uncle a father." Abū Sulaymān al-Dimashqī said: "'And We granted him Lot' in support and help." On this view «لوطاً» is in the accusative by «وهبنا» without being restricted to being of his offspring. His word «داود» and what is conjoined to it are in the accusative either by the verb of granting or by the verb of guiding. In «مِنْ ذريته» two aspects are possible. One: it is attached to that omitted verb, and «مِنْ» marks the starting point. The second: it is a ḥāl, i.e. "while these prophets are traced to him." «وكذلك نجزي»: [the kāf is in the position of an accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We reward them with a reward like that reward"; it may also be in the position of a nominative, i.e. "the matter is thus"]. This was given before at His words {وَكَذَلِكَ نري إِبْرَاهِيمَ} [al-Anʿām: 75].

semin-durr:86-86.t:
His words: «واليَسَع»: the majority read «الْيَسَعَ» with a single lām and fatḥa on the yāʾ after it, and the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «اللَّيْسَع» with a doubled lām and an unvowelled yāʾ after it. The majority reading has two interpretations. One: it is transferred from an imperfect verb, the original being «يَوْسَع» like «يَوْعِد»; the wāw fell between a yāʾ and an implied kasra—because the fatḥa was only brought for the sake of the guttural letter—so it was omitted as it is omitted in «يَضَع», «يَدَع», «يَهَب» and its class. Then it was used as a name, stripped of a pronoun, and al was added to it in the way it is added in his saying:
1976 - رأيت الوليدَ بنَ اليزيد مبارَكاً ... شديداً بأعباءِ الخلافةِ كاهِلُهْ
(I saw al-Walīd son of al-Yazīd blessed, his shoulders strong for the burdens of the caliphate.)
and as in his saying:
1977 - باعَدَ أمَّ العمروِ من أسيرِها ... حُرَّاسُ أبوابٍ على قصورِها
(Guards of gates at her palaces have kept Umm al-ʿAmr far from her captive [i.e. her lover].)
It is also said that al in it is for definiteness, as though its indefiniteness were assumed. The second: it is a foreign name without derivation, because al-Yasaʿ is said to be Joshua (Yūshaʿ) son of Nūn, the young man of Moses; so al in it is either extra or definite, as stated before. Is al obligatory in it, on the assumption that it is extra? Al-Fārisī said: it is obligatory, anomalously, as it is obligatory in «الآن». Ibn Mālik said: "Where the article accompanied its transfer [as a name], as in al-Naṣr and al-Nuʿmān, or its improvisation [as a name], as in al-Yasaʿ and al-Samawʾal, mostly al is retained in it, and it may be omitted."
As for the reading of the two brothers, its original is «لَيْسَع», like «ضَيْغَم» and «صَيْرَف», and it is a foreign name; the entry of al into it is on the two aspects mentioned. Abū ʿUbayd chose the light reading, saying: "We have heard the name of this prophet in all the hadiths as al-Yasaʿ, and none of them named him al-Laysaʿ." There is no argument in this, because he related the word in one of its two forms; the narrators preferred this form for its lightness, not because the other is unsound. Al-Farrāʾ said about the doubled reading: "It is more like the names of the non-Arabs." It has been stated before that there are three forms in the nūn of «يونس», and likewise in the sīn of «يوسف».
His words: «وكلاَّ فَضَّلْنا» are like His words «كلاًّ هَدَيْنَا».

semin-durr:87-87.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمِنْ آبَائِهِمْ}: there are two aspects. One: it is attached to that implied verb, i.e. "and We guided some of their fathers," or "We favoured some of their fathers," and «مِنْ» is partitive. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "And We guided groups from their fathers, their offspring and their brothers." So «مِنْ» is partitive and the object is omitted. The second: it is conjoined to «كلاًّ», i.e. "and We favoured some of their fathers." Abū al-Baqāʾ gave this aspect the implied form: "and We favoured each of their fathers, [or] and We guided each of their fathers."
His words: «واجتَبَيْناهم» may be conjoined to «فَضَّلنا», or may be resumptive; and He repeated the word of guidance for emphasis, and because guidance is the root of every good [Translator's note: the text reads «خبر», evidently for «خير»].

semin-durr:88-88.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {ذلك هُدَى الله}: what is pointed to is the maṣdar (verbal noun) understood from the verb before it: either the choosing (ijtibāʾ) or the guiding, i.e. "that choosing is guidance," or "that guidance to the straight path is the guidance of Allah." «هدى الله» may be a khabar (predicate), or it may be a badal (substitute) from «ذلك», with the khabar being «يهدي به». On the first view «يهدي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the demonstrative; it may also be a second khabar. «مِنْ عبادِه» is an explication (tabyīn) or a ḥāl, either from «مَنْ» or from its omitted referent pronoun.

semin-durr:89-89.t: The hāʾ in «بها» refers to the three things, namely the Book, the judgement and the prophethood; this is the view of al-Zamakhsharī. It is also said: it refers to the prophethood only, because it is the nearest mentioned. The bāʾ in «بها» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «ليس», and was placed before its governing word for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil). The bāʾ in «بكافرين» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis.

semin-durr:90-90.t:
«أولئك» is an object placed before {هَدَى الله}. Making it a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the referent pronoun omitted, i.e. "Allah guided them," is weak, as in His words {أَفَحُكْمَ الجاهلية يَبْغُونَ} [al-Māʾida: 50] with «حكم» in the nominative.
His words: «اقتدِهْ»: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it with this hāʾ omitted in continuous reading, and the rest retained it in continuous reading and in pause—except that Ibn ʿĀmir gives it kasra, and Ibn Dhakwān transmitted two aspects from him: one, the kasra without joining a lengthening (madda) to it; the second, joining a lengthening to it—and the rest give it sukūn. As for the pause, the readers agreed on retaining it unvowelled. They also differed over {مَالِيَهْ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 28] and {سُلْطَانِيَهْ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 29] in al-Ḥāqqa, and over {مَاهِيَهْ} [al-Qāriʿa: 10] in al-Qāriʿa, regarding omission and retention; and they agreed on retaining it in {كِتَابيَهْ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 19] and {حِسَابِيَهْ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 20].
As for the reading of the two brothers, the hāʾ for them is the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt), which is why they omitted it in continuous reading, since its place is the pause, and retained it in pause following the script of the codex. As for those who retained it unvowelled, there are two possibilities for them. One: it is the hāʾ of pause, but it was retained in continuous reading, treating continuous reading like pause, as in His words {لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ وانظر} [al-Baqara: 259] on one of the views, as stated before.
The second: it is the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun), given sukūn in continuous reading, again treating continuous reading like pause, as in {نُؤْتِهِ} [Āl ʿImrān: 145], {فَأَلْقَهِ} [al-Naml: 28], {أَرْجِهْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 111], {نُوَلِّهِ} [al-Nisāʾ: 115] and {وَنُصْلِهِ} [al-Nisāʾ: 115].
There is disagreement about the maṣdar to which this hāʾ refers. It is said: the guidance, i.e. "follow the guidance," meaning "follow with the following of the guidance"; and «الهدى» may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "so follow their guidance for the sake of guidance." And it is said: the following, i.e. "follow [with] the following." Of the pronominalisation of the maṣdar is his saying:
1978 - هذا سُراقةُ للقرآنِ يدرسُه ... والمرءُ عند الرُّشا إن يَلْقَها ذيبُ
(This is Surāqa, studying the Quran — yet a man, at bribes, if he meets them, is a wolf.)
i.e. "he studies [with] the studying." The hāʾ cannot be the pronoun of the Quran, because the verb has already been made to reach it, and the lām was only added to strengthen it since its governed word was placed first. That is why the grammarians made the accusative of «زيداً» in «زيداً ضربته» due to an implied verb, contrary to al-Farrāʾ. Ibn al-Anbārī said: "It is the pronoun of the emphatic maṣdar that stands in for the verb, and the original is «اقتد اقتد»; then the maṣdar was made a substitute for the second verb, then pronominalised, and so attached to the first."
As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, the apparent explanation is that it is a pronoun, given the kasra sometimes without a joined [lengthening], which the readers call ikhtilās (snatching the vowel), and sometimes with the joining [lengthening], which is called ishbāʿ (full lengthening), as «أَرْجِهِ» and the like were read. Once this is established, Ibn Mujāhid's statement about Ibn ʿĀmir—"he gives the hāʾ a trace (ishmām) [of kasra] without reaching a yāʾ, and this is an error, because this hāʾ is a hāʾ of pause that is never inflected in any state, i.e. it is not vowelled, and it only enters to make clear the vowel of what precedes it"—is not good, because of what I have established for you, that it is the pronoun of the maṣdar. Al-Fārisī rejected Ibn Mujāhid's statement with what has been said. The second aspect: it is a hāʾ of pause treated like the hāʾ of the pronoun, just as the hāʾ of the pronoun was treated like it in being unvowelled; this is not good. The saying of al-Mutanabbī is related:
1979 - واحرَّ قلباه ممَّن قلبُه شَبِمُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O the burning of my heart, because of one whose heart is cold…)
with ḍamma and kasra on the hāʾ, on the basis that it is a hāʾ of pause likened to the hāʾ of the pronoun and so vowelled. It is better to make the kasra due to the meeting of two unvowelled letters, not to its resemblance to the pronoun, because the hāʾ of the pronoun is not given kasra after an alif—so how much less what resembles it?
«الاقتداء» originally means seeking agreement [with someone]; al-Layth said this. One says «قُدْوَة» [and «قِدْوٌ»; its origin is from «القِدْو»], which is the root form from which the inflections of «الاقتداء» branch out. «بهداهم» is attached to «اقتد». Al-Zamakhsharī, according to his principle, made its placement first convey restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ). The hāʾ in «عليه» refers to the Quran or to the conveying [of the message]; they were pronominalised even though no mention of them has occurred, because the context indicates them. «إنْ» is negative and has no governing effect according to the well-known view; and even if it governed, its government would be cancelled by «إلاَّ». «للعالمين» is attached to «ذكرى», and the lām makes [the maṣdar] reach its object (muʿaddiya), i.e. "the Quran is nothing but a reminding of the worlds." It may also be attached to an omitted [word] as an adjective of «ذكرى».

semin-durr:1-1.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَجَعَلَ الظلمات}: «جعل» here takes a single object, because it means «خلق» (created); this is how the grammarians express it, its outward sense being that the two are synonymous. However, al-Zamakhsharī distinguished between them, saying: "The difference between الخَلْق and الجَعْل is that in الخَلْق there is the meaning of determining (taqdīr), and [in] الجعل the meaning of transforming (taṣyīr), such as producing a thing from a thing, or making a thing into a thing, or moving it from a place to a place; of this is {وَجَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا} [al-Aʿrāf: 189] and {وَجَعَلَ الظلمات والنور}, because darkness is from the dense bodies and light is from fire." End of quote. [Translator's note: the source prints «من كان إلى مكان»; «كان» is evidently a misprint for «مكان»; translated accordingly.] Al-Ṭabarī said: "«جَعَل» here is the one that is used freely at the edge of speech, as you say: جعلت أفعل كذا (I began doing such); so it is as though [it were]: and He made their darkening and their lighting." This does not resemble the speech of the people of the language. Because for Abū al-Qāsim it does not mean «خلق», he explained it here as meaning "brought into being and produced". Likewise al-Rāghib made it mean "brought into existence".

Then the Shaykh objected to him here when he digressed and mentioned that it may mean صَيَّر (to make into), giving as an example His words: {وَجَعَلُواْ الملائكة الذين هُمْ عِبَادُ الرحمن إِنَاثاً} [al-Zukhruf: 19]. He said: "What he mentioned, that «جَعَل» means صَيَّر in His words {وَجَعَلُواْ الملائكة}, is not valid, because they do not make them into females; some grammarians only mentioned that here it means سمَّى (named)." I say: what is meant by transforming is not transforming by act, but transforming by word; al-Zamakhsharī stated this explicitly, and further explanation of it will come — if Allah wills — in its place. The difference between assigning the heavens and the earth to "creating" and darkness and light to "making" has become clear from what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned. He made light singular and darkness plural only because light is of one kind, namely fire, while darknesses are many, for there is no body without a shadow, and its shadow is darkness. What also made this good is that the ṣila (relative clause) before it has a plural followed by a singular, so you conjoined this to it in the same way. The wisdom in making the heavens plural and the earth singular has preceded in al-Baqara. «الظلمات» was put first in mention because that accords with existence, since darkness is before light according to the majority.

His words: {ثْمَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ}: this «ثم» is not for temporal sequence; it is only for the distance between the two ranks, and what is meant is to deem it far-fetched that they should equate another with Him despite the proofs He has made clear. This is conjoined either to His words «الحمد لله» or to His words «خلق السماوات». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what then is the meaning of «ثم»? I say: deeming it far-fetched that they should doubt about Him after it has been established that He is the One who gives them life, causes them to die and resurrects them." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«ثم» indicates the ugliness of the act of those who disbelieve; for His creation of the heavens and the earth and others has been established, His signs have shone forth, and His bounty in that has become clear; then, with all this, they equate others with Him."

The Shaykh said: "What these two said, that it is for rebuke and deeming far-fetched, is not correct, because it was not coined for that; the deeming far-fetched and the rebuke are derived from the context, not from «ثم». I know of none of the grammarians who mentioned that. Rather, «ثم» here is for an interval in time, and it conjoins a nominal clause to a nominal clause" — meaning to «الحمد لله». Then he objected to al-Zamakhsharī's permitting it to be conjoined to «خَلَق», on the grounds that «خَلَق» is a ṣila, so what is conjoined to it is given its ruling, yet there is no link in it returning to the relative. Then he said: "Unless it is on the view of those who hold linking by an overt noun, as in their saying: «أبو سعيدٍ الذي رَوَيْتُ عن الخدري» (Abū Saʿīd, the one from whom I related — from al-Khudrī), which is very rare; the Book of Allah should not be interpreted according to it." I say: al-Zamakhsharī only means conjunction by «ثم» for the distance between the two ranks; he does not mean distance in time, as he himself stated explicitly. So how does what he [the Shaykh] mentioned, the lack of a link, bind him? And how can it be imagined to be for an interval in time, as the Shaykh mentioned?

His words: {بِرَبِّهِمْ}: it may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كفروا», in which case «يَعْدِلون» means "they turn away from Him", from العُدول, and it then has no object. It may also be attached to «يعدِلون», fronted for the verse-endings; in that case there are two possibilities for the bāʾ. The first: that it means «عن», and «يَعْدِلون» is also from العُدول, i.e. they turn away from their Lord to another. The second: that it is for transitivity, and «يَعْدِلون» is from العَدْل, which is making two things equal, i.e. "then those who disbelieve make others among created beings equal to their Lord"; so the object is omitted.

semin-durr:105-105.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وكذلك}: The kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Zajjāj implied it as: "And We vary the signs the like of how We varied them in what has been recited to you"; and others implied it as: We vary the signs in other than this sūra with a variation like the variation in this sūra.
His words: «ولِيقولوا»: The majority read the lām with kasra; it is the lām of kay (purpose), and the verb after it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ», so it is in the sense of a maṣdar made genitive by it, as has been learned more than once. Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya called it the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra), like the words of the Exalted: {فالتقطه آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً وَحَزَناً} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8], and like his saying:
2026 - لِدُوا للموتِ وابنُوا للخَراب ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Give birth for death and build for ruin …)
That is: since their affair came to that, He expressed it with this expression, and purpose is not meant in these examples. The meticulous scholars refuse to make it [the lām] for consequence and outcome, and interpret what has come of that as figurative. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted both aspects in it — I mean its being the lām of consequence or of real purpose — for he said: "The lām is the lām of consequence, i.e. their affair comes to this. And it was said: He intended by the variation that they should say 'you have studied', as a punishment for them" — meaning that this is an explicit purpose. Someone clarified this, saying: "The meaning is: He varies these proofs state after state, so that some of them say 'you have studied [with others]' and thus increase in disbelief, and as an alert to others of them so that they increase in faith; like {يُضِلُّ بِهِ كَثِيراً وَيَهْدِي بِهِ كَثِيراً} [al-Baqara: 2]" [Translator's note: the source gives "al-Baqara: 2"; the verse is al-Baqara: 26]. Abū ʿAlī made it the lām of outcome in some readings and the lām of purpose in others, saying: "The lām in ليقولوا in the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and those who agree with him means 'lest they say', i.e. the signs were varied and made firm lest they say 'these are the tales of the ancients, old, worn out and repeated in the ears'; and the lām in the other readings is the lām of outcome." I say: the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir is دَرَسَتْ, on the measure of akalat and saraqat, a past verb ascribed to the pronoun of the signs; the verification of the readings of this word, both the mutawātir and the anomalous, will come. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What he permitted, of implying «لا» after the lām after which «أَنْ» is implied, is the doctrine of some Kufans, just as they implied it after the overt «أَنْ» in {أَن تَضِلُّواْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 176]; the Basrans do not permit implying «لا» except in the oath, as was explained there."
Then this lām must have something it is attached to. Al-Zamakhsharī and others implied it postponed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And «وليقولوا»: its answer is omitted, its implied form being: and so that they say 'you have studied', We vary them. If you say: what difference is there between the two lāms in لِيَقُولوا and ولنبيِّنه? I say: the difference between them is that the first is figurative and the second real; that is, the signs were varied for the sake of explaining, and were not varied so that they should say 'you have studied'; but since this saying came about through the variation of the signs, just as [the explaining] came about, it was likened to it and brought in its manner, and 'so that they say' was said as 'so that We explain it' was said." I say: he has explicitly stated here that the lām of «ليقولوا» is a figurative purpose.
Some permitted this lām to be conjoined to an omitted purpose. Ibn al-Anbārī said: "The wāw entered «وليقولوا» as conjoining to something implied, the implied form being: and thus We vary the signs to bind them with the proof, and so that they say." I say: on this view the lām is attached to the verb of varying in terms of meaning, and for that reason whoever implied it implied it postponed with «نُصَرِّف». The Shaykh said: "What the grammarians and exegetes mentioned, that the lām is the lām of kay or the lām of outcome, is not necessarily so; rather the apparent view is that it is the lām of command, with the verb jussive by it. This is supported by the reading of whoever read the lām with sukūn, and the meaning on it is well-founded, as if it were said: and thus We vary the signs, and let them say what they say — that you studied them and learned them, or that they [the signs] are worn out, i.e. old and outdated — for no heed is paid to them nor attention to their saying. It is a command whose meaning is threat and menace and indifference to their saying, i.e. We vary them, and let them claim about them whatever they wish, for there is no concern for their claim."
This is open to question, in that the meaning is as people have said and understood it; moreover after it comes/ «ولنبيِّنَه», which is explicit for the lām of kay. As for the sukūn of the lām in the anomalous reading, it is no proof, since it may be the lām of kay given sukūn by treating the word like katif and kabid. The Shaykh also objected to al-Zamakhsharī where he said: "«وليقولوا»: its answer is omitted", saying: "His calling what His words «وليقولوا» are attached to an 'answer' is a strange terminology; one does not say of «جئتَ» in your saying «جئت لتقوم» that it is an answer." I say: this expression recurs in al-Zamakhsharī, and that will come at His words {ولتصغى} [al-Anʿām: 113] as well, and the Shaykh said there: "This is a strange terminology." What appears is that he calls this kind an "answer" only because it occurs as an answer to a questioner: you say, where is that to which this preposition-phrase is attached? and it is given in answer; so it was called an answer in this respect, and it was put in construct with the preposition-phrase in his words «وليقولوا جوابه» because the iḍāfa [occurs] with the slightest connection. Otherwise, the speech of an imām that recurs is not to be interpreted as erroneous.
As for the readings in «دَرَسَتْ», there are three among the mutawātir: Ibn ʿĀmir read «دَرَسَتْ» on the measure of ḍarabat; Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr «دارَسْتَ» on the measure of qābalta (you [masc.] compared); and the rest «درسْتَ» on the measure of ḍarabta (you struck). As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, its meaning is: they are worn out, old, and repeated in the ears — they point to their being among the stories of the ancients, as they said "tales of the ancients".
As for the reading of Ibn Kathīr [and] Abū ʿAmr, its meaning is: you have studied, O Muḥammad, with others among the people of past reports and bygone generations until you memorised them and said them, as He related from them, saying: {إِنَّمَا يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ لِّسَانُ الذي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ} [al-Naḥl: 103]; and in the exegesis: they used to say, he studies with Salmān and ʿAddās. As for the reading of the rest, its meaning is: you have memorised and mastered by study the reports of the ancients, as He related from them: {وقالوا أَسَاطِيرُ الأولين اكتتبها فَهِيَ تملى عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلاً}
[al-Furqān: 5], i.e. it is repeated to him by study so that he memorises it. This word was read in ten other anomalous readings, so thirteen readings came together in it. Ibn ʿAbbās (with disagreement from him), Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and Qatāda read «دُرِسَتْ», a past verb in the passive, ascribed to the pronoun of the signs. Ibn Jinnī and al-Zamakhsharī explained it with two meanings, one of which contains a difficulty. Abū al-Fatḥ said: "It may mean 'were effaced' or 'were worn out'." Abū al-Qāsim said: "In the sense of 'were read' or 'were effaced'." The Shaykh said: "As for the meaning 'were read' and 'were worn out' [Translator's note: so in the source, «قُرِئَتْ وبَلِيَتْ»], it is clear, because darasa in the sense of repeating the reading is transitive. As for «دَرَس» in the sense of wearing out and being effaced, I do not know it as transitive, and we have found it only intransitive among those Arabs whose poetry we have come across." I say: this does not need inductive survey, for its meaning does [not] admit of its being transitive, since its event does not pass beyond its agent; so it is like qāma and qaʿada: just as we do not need an inductive survey to know the intransitivity of qāma and qaʿada but know it by the meaning, so too this.
And «دَرَّسْتَ» was read, a past verb with doubling, active, addressed to the second person. It may be for multiplicity, i.e. you studied many books, like dhabbaḥtu al-ghanam and qaṭṭaʿtu al-athwāb; or for transitivisation (taʿdiya), with both objects omitted, i.e. you taught others the books — but this is not apparent, since the exegesis is contrary to it. And «دُرِّسْتَ» was read, like the previous one except that it is passive, i.e. others taught you the books; so the doubling is for transitivisation only. And «دُوْرِسْتَ» was read, ascribed to the tāʾ of the addressee, from dārasa like qātala, except that it was made passive, so its augmented alif was changed into wāw; the meaning is: others studied with you.
And «دارسَتْ» was read with a quiescent feminine tāʾ attached to the end of the verb. Regarding its agent there are two possibilities. One of them: that it is the pronoun of the group, implied though not previously mentioned, because the context indicates it, i.e. the group studied with you — they point to Abū Fukayha and Salmān; this preceded in the reading of Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr. The second: the pronoun of the females [i.e. the signs], by way of hyperbole, i.e. the signs themselves studied with you, though their people are meant.
And «دَرُسَتْ» was read with fatḥa of the dāl and ḍamma of the rāʾ, ascribed to the pronoun of the signs; it is an intensification of دَرَسَتْ in the sense of being worn out, old and effaced, i.e. their effacement and wearing out became intense. Ubayy/ read «دَرَسَ», its agent being the pronoun of the Prophet ﷺ or the pronoun of the Book, in the sense that the Prophet read it, recited it and it was repeated to him; or in the sense that the Book wore out and was effaced. And so it is in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh: درس.
Al-Ḥasan read in one transmission «دَرَسْنَ», a past verb ascribed to the nūn of the females, which is the pronoun of the signs; and so it is in some of the codices of Ibn Masʿūd. And «دَرَّسْنَ» was read, [like] the one before it except with doubling, in the sense that their effacement and wearing out became intense, as preceded. And «دارسات» was read, plural of dārisa, in the sense of "old ones", or in the sense of "possessing effacement", like ʿīsha rāḍiya and māʾ dāfiq; its nominative is as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. they are dārisāt, and the clause is in the position of the accusative by the verb of saying before it.
His words {وَلِنُبَيِّنَهُ}: it has preceded that this is conjoined to what precedes it, so its ruling is its ruling. Regarding the accusative pronoun there are four possibilities. The first: that it refers back to the signs; that was permissible though they are feminine, because they are in the sense of the Qur'an. The second: that it refers back to the Book, because the context indicates it; this is strengthened by its being the agent of دَرَسَ in the reading of whoever read it so. The third: that it refers back to the maṣdar understood from نُصَرِّف, i.e. We explain the variation. The fourth: that it refers back to the maṣdar understood from «لنبينه», i.e. We explain the explaining, like ضَرَبْتُه زيداً, i.e. I struck the striking [on] Zayd. «لقوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it, and «يَعْلَمُون» is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of the indefinite noun before it.

semin-durr:106-106.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مَآ أُوحِيَ}: [مَا] may be nominal, with the resumptive pronoun being what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil), and «إليك» a complement (faḍla). They also permitted it to be maṣdariyya, in which case what stands in place of the agent is the preposition and its genitive noun, i.e. the revelation coming from your Lord. «مِنْ» is for the beginning of extent figuratively, so «مِنْ ربك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أُوْحِي. And it was said: rather it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما» itself. And it was said: rather it is a ḥāl of the latent pronoun in «أوحي», and it has the same meaning as the previous one.
His words: {لا إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}: a parenthetical clause between these two imperative clauses; this is the best. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be a ḥāl of «ربك», an emphatic ḥāl, its implied form being: from your Lord, alone.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله}: The object of the willing is omitted, i.e. had Allah willed their faith; it has preceded that it is not mentioned except when it is unusual. His words: «جَعَلْناك» are in the sense of «صيَّر» (made into), so the kāf is the first object and «حفيظاً» the second, and «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) it, fronted for emphasis or for the verse-endings. The object of «حفيظ» is omitted, i.e. a keeper of their deeds over them. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This supports the view of Sībawayh on the governing of faʿīl", meaning that it is an intensive form, and people disagree about its governing and the governing of faʿil: Sībawayh affirmed it and others denied it. But how does it support it, when there is nothing in the wording that testifies to it?
His words: {وَمَآ أَنتَ}: [مَا] may be the Ḥijāzī [mā], so «أنت» is its noun and «بوكيل» its khabar (predicate), in the position of the accusative; or it may be the Tamīmī [mā], so «أنت» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «بوكيل» its khabar, in the position of the nominative; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) on both assumptions. «عليهم» is attached to وكيل, fronted for the reason given for what precedes it. This clause has the meaning of the clause before it, because the meaning of "you are not a guardian over them" is the meaning of "We have not made you a keeper over them", i.e. a watcher.

semin-durr:108-108.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مِن دُونِ الله}: may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يَدْعُون», or attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial), either of the relative noun or of its omitted resumptive pronoun, i.e. they call upon them while they are settled [as objects of worship] besides Allah.
His words: {فَيَسُبُّواْ}: The apparent view is that it is accusative as the answer to the prohibition, by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ, i.e. do not revile their gods, for what you dislike — the reviling of Allah — may follow from it. It may also be jussive, conjoined to the prohibited verb before it, as in their saying «لا تَمْدُدْها فتشقَّها» ("Do not stretch it, lest you tear it"). The occurrence of «الذين», though it is specific to rational beings, for idols which do not reason was permissible by treating them as rational beings, just as «مَنْ» was used for them in His words: {كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ} [al-Naḥl: 17]. It may also be by way of predominance (taghlīb), because among those worshipped besides Allah are rational beings, like the Messiah, ʿUzayr, the angels and others, so the rational was made to predominate. It is also permissible that by «الذين يدعون» the polytheists are meant, i.e. do not revile the disbelievers who call upon other than Allah besides Him; this is a clear aspect.
His words {عَدْواً}: The majority read it with fatḥa of the ʿayn, sukūn of the dāl and the wāw unstressed. Its accusative is from three aspects. The first: that it is accusative as a maṣdar (absolute object), because it is a kind of its governor, since reviling is of the genus of aggression (ʿadw). The second: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of aggression. The apparent sense of al-Zajjāj's words is that he mixed the two views and made them one view, for he said: "And عَدْواً is accusative as a maṣdar, because the meaning is: so they transgress/ a transgression"; he said: "And it may be with the lām intended, the meaning being: so they revile Allah out of injustice." The third: that it is accusative as occurring in the place of an emphatic ḥāl, because reviling is never other than aggression. Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Yaʿqūb, Qatāda, Sallām and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd read «عُدُوَّاً» with ḍamma of the ʿayn and the dāl and doubling of the wāw; it too is a maṣdar of «عدا», and its accusative is on the three aspects that preceded. Ibn Kathīr in one transmission read — and it is the reading of the people of Mecca according to what al-Naḥḥās transmitted — «عَدُوَّا» with fatḥa of the ʿayn, ḍamma of the dāl and doubling of the wāw, in the sense of "enemies"; its accusative is as an emphatic ḥāl, and «عدوّ» may occur as the khabar (predicate) of a plural; the Exalted said: {هُمُ العدو} [al-Munāfiqūn: 4], and the Exalted said: {إِنَّ الكافرين كَانُواْ لَكُمْ عَدُوّاً مُّبِيناً} [al-Nisāʾ: 101]. One says: ʿadā yaʿdū ʿadwan, ʿuduwwan, ʿudwānan and ʿadāʾan. And «بغير عِلْم» is a ḥāl, i.e. they revile Him without knowing, i.e. accompanied by ignorance, because had they esteemed Him with the esteem due to Him, they would not have ventured upon it. His words «كذلك» are an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. We have made their deeds fair-seeming to these with a making-fair like Our making-fair to every community their deed. And it was said: its implied form is: like the making-fair of idol-worship to the polytheists, We have made fair-seeming to every community their deed; this is close to the first.

semin-durr:114-114.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَفَغَيْرَ الله}: the accusative of «غير» may be explained in two ways. The first: that it is the object of «أبتغي», placed before it, and it directly follows the hamza for the reason given earlier on His saying {أَغَيْرَ الله أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيّاً} [al-Anʿām: 14]. «حكماً» is then either a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a tamyīz (specification) of «غير»; al-Ḥūfī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned this, comparing their saying: «إن لنا غيرها إبلاً» ("we have camels other than these"). The second: that «غير» is accusative as a ḥāl from «حَكَماً», because originally it could be its adjective, and «حَكَماً» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). So there result two views on the accusative of «غير».

As for the accusative of «حكماً», there are three views: its being a ḥāl, an object, or a tamyīz. Al-ḥakam is more emphatic than al-ḥākim. It was said: because the ḥakam is one from whom judgement issues repeatedly, unlike the ḥākim, for the term applies to others too [Translator's note: the source reads «فإنه يُصَدِّق غيره», literally "it confirms another"; the sense appears to be "it is applicable to others"]. And it was said: because the ḥakam judges only with justice, whereas the ḥākim may be unjust. His saying «وهو الذي أنزل»: this clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «أبتغي», and «مفصلاً» is a ḥāl from «الكتاب».

His saying: {والذين آتَيْنَاهُمُ} is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يعلمون» is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive. «من ربك» is for the beginning of the extent, figuratively, and «بالحق» is a ḥāl [Translator's note: the source has «خال», a misprint for «حال»] from the pronoun latent in «مُنَزَّل», i.e. accompanied by the truth; so the bāʾ is for accompaniment. Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, read «مُنَزَّل» with a doubled zāy, and the rest with it single. It was stated earlier that أنزل and نزَّل are two dialectal forms, or that there is a difference between them.

semin-durr:115-115.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {صِدْقاً وَعَدْلاً}: there are three views on their accusative. The first: that they are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. the words were completed being truthful in the promise and just in the threat. The second: that they are accusative as tamyīz (specification). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is not correct"; among those who said it is a tamyīz are al-Ṭabarī and Abū al-Baqāʾ. The third: that they are accusative as mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. it was completed for the sake of the truthfulness and justice occurring from them; this is open to question. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this view.

The Kufans read «كلمة» in the singular here, and in Yūnus in His saying {كَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى الذين فسقوا} [Yūnus: 33] and {إِنَّ الذين حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ} [Yūnus: 96] — two places — and in Ghāfir: {وَكَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ} [verse 6]. Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr agreed with them on what is in Yūnus and Ghāfir but not in this sūra; the rest read the plural in the three places. The Shaykh said: "The Kufans read «كلمة» in the singular here, in Yūnus in the two places and in al-Muʾmin, and Nāfiʿ read all of that «كلمات» in the plural; Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr followed him here." I say: how did he forget Ibn ʿĀmir? It cannot be said that the copyist dropped him and the original was "Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir", because he said «تابعه» ("followed him"); had it been so, he would have said «تابعهما» ("followed the two of them"). The rationale of the singular is that the genus is intended, analogous to رسالته and رسالاته. The plural reading is evident, because His words, Exalted is He, are varied [Translator's note: the source reads «متبوعة» ("followed"); «متنوعة» ("varied") seems intended] with respect to command, prohibition, promise and threat; and there is consensus on the plural in His saying {لاَ مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَاتِهِ} and {وَلاَ مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَاتِ الله} [al-Anʿām: 34].

His saying {لاَ مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَاتِهِ}: it may have no grammatical position because it is resumptive, or it may be a circumstantial clause from the agent of «تَمَّتْ». If you say: where then is the link between the possessor of the ḥāl and the ḥāl? The answer is that the link is achieved by the overt noun; the original is «لا مبدِّل لها», and it was only brought out as an overt noun to magnify them and because of their annexation to the noble Divine Name. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may not be a ḥāl from «ربك», lest the ḥāl be separated from its possessor by something extraneous, namely «صدقاً وعدلاً» — unless «صدقاً وعدلاً» is made a ḥāl from «ربك», not from «الكلمات»." I say: if «صدقاً وعدلاً» is made a ḥāl from «ربك», no separation follows from that, because they would be two ḥāls of one possessor; but his rule forbids multiple ḥāls for a single possessor, and also forbids the ḥāl coming from the muḍāf ilayhi, even if the muḍāf is part of the second; yet he did not forbid it here on any of these grounds. The script of «كلمات» in the places where I indicated the readers' disagreement can accommodate their disagreement, for in the noble muṣḥaf it is written without an alif after the mīm.

semin-durr:116-116.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: {إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ} and {إِنْ هُمْ إِلاَّ يَخْرُصُونَ}: «إنْ» is negative, in the sense of «ما», in both places. Al-kharṣ is estimation by guessing, and it is used to express lying and fabrication. Its origin is from conjecture, which is saying what one has not ascertained and verified; al-Azharī said this. From it is «خَرَص النخل» (estimating the yield of palms): one says «خَرَصها الخارص خَرْصاً فهي خِرْص»; the form with fatḥa is the maṣdar (verbal noun), and the form with kasra has the meaning of the passive participle, like النَّقض and النِّقض, and الذَّبح and الذِّبْح.

semin-durr:117-117.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مَن يَضِلُّ}: there are two opinions about this «أعلم». The first: that it is not for preference (tafḍīl) but has the meaning of an active participle, in its force, as though it were said: "Your Lord, He knows". Al-Wāḥidī said: "That is not permissible, because it does not correspond to {وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بالمهتدين}." The second: that it is in its proper sense of preference. Then those holding this differed over the position of «مَنْ».

[The first:] Some of the Basrans said: it is genitive by an implied preposition which was omitted while its effect remained, because of the strong indication of it in His saying {وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بالمهتدين}. This is nothing, because the preposition is not omitted with its effect remaining except in places that were pointed out earlier; whatever occurs contrary to them is poetic licence, like his saying:

2044 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أشارت كليبٍ بالأكف الأصابعُ
(…the fingers pointed with the palms to Kulayb.)

[And his saying]:

2045 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... حتى تبذَّخ فارتقى الأعلامِ
(…until he grew haughty and climbed to the summits.)

The second: that it is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, like his saying:

2046 - تمرُّون الديار ولم تعوجوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(You pass the abodes and do not turn aside…)

Abū al-Fatḥ said this. It is rejected on two grounds: first, that this is not regular; second, that afʿal of preference does not make a noun accusative by itself, because of its weakness. The third — the opinion of the Kufans — that it is made accusative by the afʿal itself, for in their view it operates as the verb does. The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied verb indicated by the afʿal; al-Fārisī said this, and on this basis he explained the poet's saying:

2047 - أكَرَّ وأَحْمَى للحقيقةِ منهمُ ... وأَضْرَبَ منا بالسيوف القوانِسا
(More given to charging, and more protective of what must be defended, than they, and more striking with swords at the helmet-crests than we.)

So القوانِس is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. «يَضْرِبُ القوانس», because afʿal is weak, as established. The fifth: that its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), «يضلُّ» being its khabar (predicate), and the clause is suspended (muʿallaqa) by the afʿal of preference, so it is in the position of accusative by it, as though it were said: "He knows best which of the people goes astray", like His saying: {لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أحصى} [al-Kahf: 12]. This is the opinion of al-Kisāʾī, al-Zajjāj, al-Mubarrad and Makkī. However, the Shaykh rejected this on the grounds that suspension (taʿlīq) is a consequence of the established ability to govern a direct object, / and afʿal does not govern it, so it cannot be suspended. The preponderant of these opinions is its being accusative by an implied verb, which is the opinion of al-Fārisī, and the rules of the Basrans agree with it. It is not permissible for «مَنْ» to be in the position of genitive by the annexation of afʿal to it, lest a grave impermissible consequence follow: namely that afʿal of preference is annexed only to its own genus, so if you said «زيد أعلمُ الضالين» it would follow that Zayd is one of those astray, i.e. characterised by straying; so this view is impossible in this noble verse. This is for those who read «يَضِلُّ» with fatḥa on the imperfect prefix.

As for those who read it with ḍamma — «يُضِلّ» — namely al-Ḥasan and Aḥmad ibn Abī Surayj, Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«مَنْ» may be in the position of genitive by the annexation of «أفعل» to it."
