He said: "Either in the sense: He knows best those who lead astray (al-muḍillīn), i.e. who finds the straying — and that is the one whom I 'aḍlaltu', i.e. found him astray, like «أَحْمَدْتُه», i.e. I found him praiseworthy — or in the sense that he leads astray from guidance." I say: there is no need to commit something like this in such delicate places. He had expressed it before that in phrasings which I found too grave to utter, so I turned from them to examples of my own wording.

What this reading is to be construed upon is the preferred view stated earlier, namely the accusative by an implied verb. The agent of «يُضِلّ» on this reading is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, in the sense that He finds him astray or creates straying in him — He is not questioned about what He does. It may also be the pronoun of «مَنْ», i.e. He knows best who leads people astray, the object being omitted. As for the well-known reading, the agent is the pronoun of «مَنْ» only. «مَنْ» may be a relative — which is the apparent view — or an indefinite qualified by an adjective; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this.

semin-durr:118-118.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: {فَكُلُواْ}: there are two views about this fāʾ. The first: that it is the response of an implied condition. Al-Zamakhsharī said, after some discussion: "So it was said to the Muslims: if you are truly established in faith, then eat." The second: that it conjoins to something omitted. Al-Wāḥidī said: "The fāʾ entered to conjoin to what the beginning of the speech indicates, as though it were said: be upon guidance, so eat." The apparent view is that it conjoins to the content of the preceding clauses, as though it were said: follow what Allah has commanded you, of eating what is properly slaughtered rather than carrion, so eat.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُكُم}: It is permissible to transfer the vowel of the interrogative hamza to the lām of «قُلْ» and drop the hamza for lightening; this is the reading of Warsh, and it is a regular lightening (tashīl). This «أرأيتكم» is in the sense of «أَخْبِرْني» (tell me), and it has rules peculiar to it, about which people's statements have been confused and their disagreement widespread; so it is necessary to address that. I say:
«أرأيْتَ», if it is the visual one, or the cognitive one remaining in its [original] meaning, or the one meaning striking the lung — as in their saying «رَأَيْتُ الطائر», i.e. I struck its lung — then lightening its hamza, which is its middle radical, is not permissible in it [Translator's note: printed «فها», evidently for «فيها»]; rather it is pronounced fully and nothing else, or lightened "between-between" (bayna bayna) without substitution or dropping. Nor may a kāf be attached to it as a particle of address; rather, if a kāf is attached to it, it is a pronoun, the first object, and it agrees with what is meant by it in masculine and feminine, singular, dual and plural. When the tāʾ of address is attached to it, it must agree with what is meant by it in what was mentioned, and it is a pronoun, the fāʿil (agent), as in أرأيتم, أرأيتما, أرأيتنَّ; and suspension (taʿlīq) and cancellation (ilghāʾ) apply to it.
If it is the cognitive one made to include the meaning of «أخبرني», it has other rules peculiar to it. Among them: its hamza may be lightened by substituting an alif for it; this is transmitted from Nāfiʿ by way of Warsh. The grammarians consider substituting an alif for this hamza weak; rather, the well-known [way] among them is lightening it between-between, which is the well-known transmission from Nāfiʿ. However, Quṭrub and other lexicographers reported pure substitution. Some said: "This is an error wrongly attributed to him", i.e. to Nāfiʿ. The reason is that it leads to the meeting of two quiescent letters, for the yāʾ after it is quiescent. Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām reported from Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ and others of the people of Medina that they drop the hamza and claim that the alif is a replacement for it. I say: this wording suggests that this alif is not a substitute for the hamza but was brought as compensation for the dropped hamza.
Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: "Substitution of an alif for the hamza has been transmitted from Warsh, because the transmission from him is that he lengthens the second, and lengthening is not possible except with substitution. What made substitution acceptable in a hamza followed by a quiescent letter is that the first is a letter of lengthening and softness, for the [lengthening] that arises with the quiescence stands in place of a vowel by which one reaches the pronunciation of the quiescent letter." Something of this has preceded for you at His saying «أأنذرتهم».
Among them: the hamza which is the middle radical of the word may be dropped; al-Kisāʾī read so, and it is widespread in verse and prose. From verse is his saying:
191 - 1- أرَيْتَ ما جاءت به أُمْلُودا ... مُرَجَّلاً ويلبسُ البُرودا
أقائِلُنَّ أحضِروا الشهودا ...
(Tell me, if she brought him forth smooth-bodied, with combed hair and wearing striped cloaks — would they [then] say: bring the witnesses?)
Another said:
191 - 2- أرَيْتُكَ إذ هُنَّا عليك ألم تَخَفْ ... رقيباً وحولي مِنْ عَدُوِّك حُضَّرُ
(Tell me, when we were of little worth to you, did you not fear a watcher, while around me were your enemies present?)
And al-Kisāʾī cited from Abū al-Aswad:
191 - 3- أَرَيْتَ امرَأً كنت لم أَبْلُهُ ... أتاني فقال اتَّخِذْني خليلا
(Tell me of a man whom I had not tested, who came to me and said: take me as a close friend.)
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that this dialect is that of most of the Arabs. He said: "In «أَرَأيْتَ» there are two usages and two meanings. The first: a man asks: أرأيت زيداً, i.e. did you know [him]? — this one has the hamza. The second: you say أرأيت in the sense of 'tell me'; here the hamza is left out if you wish, and that is most of the speech of the Arabs; one inclines to leaving out the hamza to distinguish between the two meanings." End quote.
On how this hamza is dropped there are three views. The first — which is the apparent one — is that combining two hamzas in a verb attached to a pronoun was felt to be heavy, so he lightened it by dropping one of the two hamzas; the second was more fitting, because the heaviness arose through it, because its dropping is established in the imperfect of this verb, as in أرى, يرى, نرى and ترى, and because dropping the first would impair understanding, since it is for the question. The second: he substituted an alif for the hamza, as Nāfiʿ did in the transmission of Warsh; then two quiescent letters met, so he dropped the first of them, which is the alif. The third: he substituted a yāʾ for it, then made it quiescent, then dropped it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it is far-fetched. Then he said: "What made this closer in it is its dropping in the future of this verb", meaning in يرى and its pattern. Some preferred al-Kisāʾī's position on the grounds that the hamza has been boldly dropped, and cited:
191 - 4- إنْ لم أُقاتِلْ فالبِسَوني بُرْقُعا ...
(If I do not fight, then dress me in a veil.)
And he cited from Abū al-Aswad:
191 - 5- يابا المُغِيرةِ رُبَّ أمرٍ مُعْضِلٍ ... فرَّجْتُه بالمَكْرِ مني والدَّها
(O Abū al-Mughīra, many a perplexing matter have I relieved by my cunning and shrewdness.)
And their saying «وَيْلُمِّه», and his saying:
191 - 6- وَيْلُمِّها خُلَّةً قد سِيْطَ مِنْ دَمِها ... فَجْعٌ وَوَلْعٌ وأخلافٌ وتَبْديلُ
(Woe to her mother — what a friend she is! Into her blood are mixed bereavement, lying, broken promises and change.)
He also cited:
191 - 7- ومَنْ رَاْ مثلَ مَعْدانَ بِن سعدٍ ... إذا ما النِّسْعُ طال على المَطِيَّةْ
(And who has seen the like of Maʿdān ibn Saʿd, when the saddle-strap grows long on the mount?)
i.e. «ومن رأى».
Among them: neither suspension nor cancellation applies to it, because it is in the sense of «أخبرني», and «أخبرني» is not suspended according to the majority. Sībawayh said: "You say: أَرَأَيْتَك زيداً أبو مَنْ هو? [Translator's note: printed «أو مَنْ هو», evidently for «أبو مَنْ هو», "whose father is he?"] Only the accusative of «زيد» is good in it. Do you not see that if you said «أرأيت أبو من أنت?» it would not be good, because it has the meaning of 'tell me about Zayd', and the question has come to be in the position of the second object." Others among the grammarians disagreed with Sībawayh and said: «أرأيت» is often suspended, and there is much of that in the Qur'an. They cited this verse that we are on, His saying {أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وتولى أَلَمْ يَعْلَم} [al-ʿAlaq: 13–14], and his saying:
191 - 8- أرَيْتَ ما جاءَتْ به أملودا ...
This does not count against Sībawayh, and its interpretation will come shortly.
Among them: the tāʾ attached to it must be kept singular and masculine, and attaching to it the markers of the derived forms [dual, plural, feminine] is dispensed with by attaching them to the kāf — unlike the one not made to include the meaning of «أخبرني», in which it agrees, as preceded, with what is meant by it.
Among them: a kāf is attached to it which is a particle of address, agreeing with what is meant by it in singular and masculine and their opposites. Is this tāʾ the fāʿil and the kāf a particle of address showing the states of the tāʾ, as it shows them when it is a pronoun? Or is the tāʾ a particle of address and the kāf the fāʿil, the accusative pronoun being borrowed in place of the nominative pronoun? Or is the tāʾ also the fāʿil and the kāf a pronoun in the position of the first object [Translator's note: printed «مضوع», evidently for «موضع»]? Three well-known positions: the first is the view of the Basrans, the second the view of al-Farrāʾ, and the third the view of al-Kisāʾī.
Let us confine ourselves to some of the proofs of each party.
Abū ʿAlī said: "Their saying «أَرَأَيْتَكَ زيداً ما فعل», with the tāʾ having fatḥa in all cases: the kāf must either be for address alone, stripped of the meaning of nounhood, or it indicates a noun along with indicating address. If it were a noun, the noun after it would have to be identical to it, because the second object of these verbs is the first in meaning; but it is not the same; so it is settled that it is stripped of nounhood. And when it is established that it is for address, stripped of nounhood, it is established that the tāʾ cannot be for mere address. Do you not see that it is not fitting [Translator's note: printed «ينبغي», the sense requires «لا ينبغي»] for two markers of address to attach to a word, just as two markers of the feminine or two markers of interrogation do not attach to it? Since that is not permissible, the tāʾ was made singular in all cases, since the verb must have a fāʿil, and it was put in all cases in one form, dispensing [with agreement] by what attaches to the kāf. Had the markers of the derived forms attached to the tāʾ, two markers of address would have come together — what would attach to the tāʾ and what would attach to the kāf; since that leads to something without parallel, it was rejected, and [the construction] was made to run as the rest of their speech runs."
Al-Zajjāj said, after [Translator's note: printed «عبد», evidently for «بعد»] reporting al-Farrāʾ's position: "This view was not accepted by the early grammarians, and it is a mistake, because in your saying «أرأيتك زيداً ما شأنه», if the seeing passed over to the kāf and to Zayd, the meaning would become: did your self see Zayd, what is his affair? — and this is absurd." Then he mentioned the Basrans' position. Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib said, after reporting al-Farrāʾ's position: "This is absurd, because the tāʾ is the kāf in «أرأيتكم», so the plural marker would have had to appear on the tāʾ; and it would have had to be the fāʿil of a single verb while both are for one thing; and the meaning of your saying «أرأيتَك زيداً ما صنع» would have to be: did you see yourself, Zayd, what he did? — because the kāf is the one addressed. This is absurd in meaning and contradictory in iʿrāb and meaning, because you ask about himself at the beginning of the question, then turn the question to someone else at its end; you address him first, then bring in another absent person; or because it would become three objects of «رأيت». None of this is permissible. If you said «أرأيتك عالماً بزيد» (do you consider yourself knowledgeable about Zayd?), it would be correct speech, with «رأى» passing over to two objects."
Abū al-Baqāʾ said, after reporting the Basrans' position: "The proof of this is that if it — i.e. the kāf — were a noun, it would be either genitive — which is false, since there is no governor of the genitive here — or nominative, which is also false for two reasons: first, the kāf is not among the nominative pronouns; second, it has nothing to make it nominative, since it is not the fāʿil, because the tāʾ is the fāʿil, and a single verb does not have two agents — or accusative, and that is false for three reasons. The first: this verb passes over to two objects, as in your saying «أرأيت زيداً ما فعلَ»; if the kāf were made an object, it would be a third.
The second: if it were an object, it would be the fāʿil in meaning, but the meaning is not so, since the purpose is not 'did you see yourself' but 'did you see someone other than yourself'. That is why you said «أرأيت زيداً», and Zayd is other than the one addressed, nor is it a badal (substitute) for him. The third: if it were accusative as an object, the markers of dual, plural and feminine would have appeared on the tāʾ, and you would say: أرأيتماكما, أرأيتموكم, أرأيتكنَّ." Then he mentioned al-Farrāʾ's position and said: "In what we have mentioned is the refutation of his position."
Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī defended al-Farrāʾ's position, saying: "If the kāf were for emphasis, dual and plural would have been expressed by the tāʾ, as they are expressed by it when there is no kāf. Since the tāʾ was given fatḥa in addressing a plural and the plural marker fell on something else, that is proof that the kāf is not for emphasis. Do you not see that if the kāf were dropped it would not be proper to say to a group «أرأيت»? By this it is clear that the verb turns to the kāf and that it is necessary, required and needed." What Abū Bakr said is refuted by the kāf attached to the demonstrative noun, for the plural marker falls on it, yet it is a particle.
Al-Farrāʾ said: "The position of the kāf is accusative and its interpretation is nominative, because the verb shifts from the tāʾ to it; it is like the kāf in «دونك» when it is used for incitement, as you say «دونكَ زيداً» (here, take Zayd!): you find the kāf genitive in wording and nominative in meaning, because it is the one commanded. Likewise this kāf: its position is accusative and its interpretation nominative." I say: this specious argument is invalid from what has preceded; and the disagreement over «دونك», «إليك» and their kind is well known, and attention has been drawn to it more than once.
Al-Farrāʾ also said something good which I saw fit to mention, for it is clear and useful. He said: "The Arabs have two usages and two meanings in «أرأيْتَ». One of them is seeing with the eye: when you mean this, you pass the seeing by the pronoun over to the one addressed [Translator's note: printed «المخطاب», evidently for «المخاطب»], and it is inflected as other verbs are. You say to a man «أرأيتك على غير هذه الحال» (have you seen yourself in other than this state?), meaning: have you seen yourself? Then you make it dual and plural, saying أرأيتماكما, أرأيتموكم, أرأيتكنَّ. The other meaning: you say «أرأيتك» meaning 'tell me', as in your saying: أرأيتك إنْ فَعَلْتَ كذا ماذا تفعل — i.e. tell me. When you mean this meaning you leave the tāʾ singular in every case, saying أرأيتكما, أرأيتكم, أرأيتكنَّ. The Arabs only left the tāʾ singular because they did not mean the action to fall from the one addressed upon himself, so they were content, for the marker of the addressee, with mentioning it in the place [of the kāf], and left the tāʾ masculine and singular, since the action was not falling [on the addressee]."
He said: "Seeing is among the deficient verbs which the addressee makes pass over to himself with a pronoun, like ظننتُني and أريتُني [Translator's note: so printed: «ظنتُني وأريتُني»]; they do not say that with complete verbs: they do not say to a man قتلتَك meaning 'you killed yourself', nor أحسنتَ إليك, as they say: متى تظنُّك خارجاً? (when do you think yourself going out?). That is because they wanted to distinguish between a verb that may be cancelled and a verb whose cancellation is not permissible. Do you not see that you say «أنا أظنُّ خارجٌ», cancelling «أظن»? And Allah the Exalted said: {أَن رَّآهُ استغنى} [al-ʿAlaq: 7], and did not say 'that he saw himself'. In poetic necessity complete verbs have been treated like deficient ones. Jirān al-ʿAwd said:
191 - 9- لقد كان لي عن ضَرَّتَيْنِ عَدِمْتُني ... وعَمَّا أُلاقي منهما مُتَزَحْزِحُ
(I had — may I lose myself! — a way of escape from two co-wives and from what I suffer from them.)
The Arabs say عَدِمْتني, وَجَدْتُني and فَقَدْتُني, but it is not the regular way of speech." End quote.
Know that people disagreed about the interrogative clause occurring after the accusative noun with «أرأيتك», as in أرأيتك زيداً ما صنع? The majority hold that «زيداً» is the first object and the clause after it is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the second object. It has preceded that suspension is not permissible in this one, even though it is permissible in others of its sisters, as in علمت زيداً أبو مَنْ هو? Ibn Kaysān said: "The interrogative clause in أرأيتك زيداً ما صنع is a badal (substitute) from أرأيتك." Al-Akhfash said: "After «أرأيت» meaning 'tell me' there must be the noun about which information is sought, and the clause after it must be interrogative, because «أخبرني» agrees with the meaning of interrogation." He also claimed that it may leave its basic use and be in the sense of «أما» or «تنبَّه» (take note), and then it has neither two objects nor one object; and he counted among that {أَرَأَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَآ إِلَى الصخرة فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ الحوت} [al-Kahf: 63]. This ought not to be permissible, because it takes the word out of its coined meaning without any reason calling for it.
When this is settled, let us return to the noble verse, and we say — and success is from Allah: people differed over this verse in three views. The first: the first object and the interrogative clause standing in place of the second are both omitted because the meaning is understood; the implied form: "Tell me — your worship of idols, does it benefit you?", or "your taking other than Allah as a god, does it remove your harm?", and the like. So «عبادتَكم» or «اتِّخاذَكم» is the first object, the interrogative clause stands in place of the second, the tāʾ is the fāʿil, and the kāf is a particle of address.
The second: the condition and its answer — its explanation will come — stand in place of the two objects [Translator's note: printed «المعفولين», evidently for «المفعولين»], because they have achieved the intended meaning, so this verb needs no object. This is nothing, because a condition and its answer are not known to stand in place of the two objects of «ظن»; and the verb's not needing an object takes it out of its coined meaning. If by "they stand in its place" he means that they indicate it, then that is what is claimed [by the first view].
The third: the first object is omitted, and the question belongs to the chapter of tanāzuʿ (contention of two governors) between «أرأيتكم» and «أتاكم», and the noun contended for is the word «العذاب». This is the choice of the Shaykh, and let us bring his words so that it becomes clear, for it is a good statement. He said: "We say: what we choose is that it remains on its rule of passing over to two objects; the first is accusative, and the second we have found by induction to be only an interrogative clause or an oath clause [Translator's note: printed «جلمة», evidently for «جملة»].
When this is settled, we say: the first object in this verse is omitted, and the question belongs to the chapter of tanāzuʿ: «أرأيتكم» and the condition contended for «عذاب الله», and the second, namely «أتاكم», was given governance, so «عذاب» became nominative by it. Had the first been given governance, the construction would have been «عذاب» in the accusative. The parallel of this is «اضرب إنْ جاءك زيد», on giving governance to «جاءك»; had it been made accusative, it would have been permissible, and it would be giving governance to the first. As for the second object, it is the interrogative clause «أغيرَ الله تَدْعُون», and the link between this clause and the omitted first object is omitted, its implied form being: أغيرَ الله تَدْعُون لكَشْفِه [Translator's note: printed «تَدْعُنن», evidently for «تَدْعُون»]. The meaning: Say: tell me about the punishment of Allah, if it comes to you — or the Hour, if it comes to you — do you call on other than Allah to remove it, or to remove its calamities?" End quote [Translator's note: printed «انتها» for «انتهى»]. The parsing he mentioned needs some clarification. Its implied form is: «قل أرأيتَكموه» or «أرأيتَكم إياه» إن أتاكم عذاب الله; so that pronoun is the pronoun of the punishment: since the second governed its overt noun, the cancelled one was given its pronoun; and when a pronoun is implied in the first, it is omitted as long as it is not nominative or originally a khabar (predicate); this pronoun is neither nominative nor originally a khabar, so for that reason it was omitted, and it is not kept except out of necessity.
As for the answer of the condition, there are five views on it. The first: it is omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī assumed it as: "If the punishment of Allah comes to you, whom will you call?" The Shaykh said: "Its correction is to say «فَمَنْ تدعون» with the fāʾ, because when the answer of a condition is an interrogative clause it must have the fāʾ." The second: it is «أرأيتكم»; al-Ḥūfī said this. It is invalid for two reasons. First: the answer of the condition does not come before it according to the majority of the Basrans; only the Kufans, Abū Zayd and al-Mubarrad permitted it. Second: a clause headed by the hamza never occurs as the answer of a condition; of interrogation, only what is with «هل» or with an interrogative noun occurs [as an answer]. A clause headed by the hamza only does not occur as an answer because either you bring the fāʾ with it or you do not. It is not permissible not to bring it, because everything that is not fit to be a condition must be joined with the fāʾ when it occurs as an answer. Nor is it permissible to bring it, because you would bring it either before the hamza, as in «إن قمت فأزيد منطلق», or after it, as in «أفزيد منطلق», and both are impossible: the first, because the fāʾ would take precedence over the hamza; the second, because it leads to lacking the fāʾ in the answer in a place where it must be brought. This is unlike «هل», for you bring the fāʾ before it, saying «إن قمت فهل زيد قائم», because it does not have the complete precedence that the hamza deserves; that is why [the hamza] precedes some conjunctions, as has been explained more than once.
The third: it is «أغير الله»; this is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's wording, for he said: "The condition may be connected to His saying {أَغَيْرَ الله تَدْعُونَ}, as if it were said: do you call on other than Allah if the punishment of Allah comes to you?" The Shaykh said: "The condition may not be connected to His saying «أغير الله», because if it were connected to it, it would be its answer; but it does not occur as an answer, because when the answer of a condition is an interrogation by a particle it occurs only with «هل»" — and he mentioned what I gave above to its end, and attributed it, through al-Akhfash, to the Arabs. Then he said: "It is also not permissible from another angle, because we have established that «أرأيتك» passes over to two objects, one of which is omitted in this verse and that it is a case of tanāzuʿ, and the interrogative clause has fallen in the place of the other; if you made it the answer of the condition, «أرأيتَكم» would remain passing over to one object only, and that is not permissible." I say: this does not bind al-Zamakhsharī, for he does not accept the parsing [the Shaykh] referred to.
As for his saying "it entails its passing over to one object": we say we do not concede this; rather it passes over to two omitted objects, the second of which is an interrogative clause, as others assumed it: أرأيتكم عبادتَكم هل تنفعكم. Then he said: "Also, the Arabs' consistently using a past verb in the condition coming after «أرأيت» is proof that the answer of the condition is omitted, because the answer of a condition is only omitted when its verb is past. The Exalted said: {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ الله} [al-Anʿām: 47] [Translator's note: so printed; the wording is that of al-Anʿām 40], {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخَذَ الله} [al-Anʿām: 46], {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِن جَعَلَ الله} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 71], {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِن جَعَلَ الله} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 72], {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُهُ} [Yūnus: 50], {أَفَرَأَيْتَ إِن مَّتَّعْنَاهُمْ سِنِينَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 205], {أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وتولى} [al-ʿAlaq: 13], among other verses. And the poet said:
192 - 0- أَرَيْتَ إنْ جاءت به أمْلودا ...
(Tell me, if she brought him forth smooth-bodied…)
Also, the coming of the interrogative clause headed by the interrogative hamza is proof that it is not the answer of the condition, since it is not correct for it to occur as the answer of a condition." End quote.
When al-Zamakhsharī permitted that the condition be connected to His saying {أغير الله}, he raised a question and answered it. He said: "If you say: if you connect the condition to it, what do you do with His saying «فيكشِفُ ما تَدْعُون إليه» together with His saying {أَوْ أَتَتْكُمْ الساعة}, when the calamities of the Hour are not removed from the polytheists? I say: He has made the removal conditional on the will, namely His saying «إنْ شاء», as an indication that if He did it there would be a wise reason for it, except that He does not do it for another wise reason that outweighs it." The Shaykh said: "This is built on the condition being connected to «أغير الله», and we have argued that this is not permissible." I say: the Shaykh omitted to point out [Translator's note: printed «التبنيه», evidently for «التنبيه»] what is more important than that, namely his saying "except that He does not do it for another wise reason that outweighs it". This is a corrupt principle among the principles of the Muʿtazila, who claim that His acts, the Exalted, follow benefits and wise purposes, with some of which doing is preponderant, with some of which leaving is preponderant, and with some of which doing or leaving is obligatory. Exalted is Allah above that! Rather, His acts are not explained by any purpose; He is not asked about what He does. The proper place of this question is other than this place, but I have drawn your attention to it [Translator's note: printed «علهيا» for «عليها»] in summary.
The fourth: the answer of the condition is omitted, its implied form being: "if the punishment of Allah comes to you or the Hour comes to you, you will call", indicated by His saying {أَغَيْرَ الله تَدْعُونَ}. The fifth: it is also omitted, but assumed from the kind of what precedes in meaning, its implied form being: "if the punishment of Allah comes to you or the Hour comes to you, then tell me about it: do you call on other than Allah to remove it?" — as you say «أخبرني عن زيدٍ إن جاءك ما تصنعُ به» (tell me about Zayd, if he comes to you, what will you do with him?), i.e. if he comes to you, then tell me about him; the answer was omitted because «أخبرني» indicates it. Its parallel: «أنت ظالمُ إن فعلت», i.e. then you are a wrongdoer; «فأنت ظالمٌ» was omitted because what precedes indicates it. This is what the Shaykh chose. He said: "It runs according to the rules of Arabic", and claimed that he had not seen it from anyone else.
His saying: {أَغَيْرَ الله تَدْعُونَ}: «غيرَ» is a preposed object of «تَدْعون». Its preposing is either for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), as al-Zamakhsharī said: "He rebuked them by His saying 'do you call on other than Allah?', meaning: do you single out your gods with calling, as is your habit when harm afflicts you, or do you call on Allah instead of them?" — or it is for disapproving of their calling on the idols, because what is disapproved is only calling on the idols, not the calling itself. Do you not see that when you say «أزيداً تضربُ» (is it Zayd you are hitting?), you only disapprove of Zayd being the object of the hitting, not of the hitting itself? This is from a rule of rhetoric to which I drew attention earlier at His saying, the Exalted: {أَأَنتَ قُلتَ لِلنَّاسِ اتخذوني} [al-Māʾida: 116].
His saying: {إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ}: Its answer is omitted because the speech indicates it, and likewise the complement of «صادقين». The implied form: "if you are truthful in your claim that something other than Allah is a god, then do you call on it to remove the punishment that befalls you?"

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ}: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «يكن» with the lower yāʾ and «فتنتهم» in the accusative; Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim [read] «تكن» with the upper tāʾ and «فتنتُهم» in the nominative; and the rest [read] also with the upper tāʾ and «فتنتهم» in the accusative. As for the reading of the two brothers, it is the most eloquent of these readings, because it runs according to the rules without interpretation — you will see this in the other two readings — and its iʿrāb is evident. That is, «فتنتهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate) [of kāna], and «أَنْ قالوا», interpreted as a noun, is its delayed noun; the implied form being: then their trial was nothing but their saying. It is the most eloquent only because when two nouns come together, one of them more definite, it is best to make it the noun spoken about and the other the khabar, the statement made about it; and «أَنْ قالوا» resembles a pronoun, and the pronoun is the most definite of definites. In this reading the more definite was made the noun of «كان» and the less definite its khabar; and the verb was not made feminine because it is attributed to a masculine. As for the reading of Ibn Kathīr and those who followed him, «فتنتُهم» is its noun, and for that reason the verb was made feminine, being attributed to a feminine; and «إلا أَنْ قالوا» is its khabar. In it you have made the less definite the noun and the more definite the khabar, so it is not as strong as the first.

As for the reading of the rest, «فتنتَهم» is a fronted khabar and «إلا أن قالوا» a delayed noun. This reading — even though it makes the more definite the noun — is like the first reading, except that it has the sign of the feminine attached to the verb while the agent [the noun of kāna] is masculine; but this is by interpretation. It was said: because His saying {إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ} is equivalent to «مقالتهم» (their statement, feminine). It was also said: because it is the trial in meaning, and when something is predicated with a feminine, it acquires femininity and is treated accordingly. Abū ʿAlī counted among this {فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا} [al-Anʿām: 160]: since «الأمثال» are the good deeds (al-ḥasanāt) in meaning, it was treated as feminine, and the tāʾ was dropped from its numeral. Similar to the verse is his saying:
188 - 0- ألم يكُ غَدْراً ما فَعَلْتُم بسَمْعَلٍ ... وقد خاب مَنْ كانَتْ سريرتَه الغَدْرُ
(Was not what you did to Samʿal treachery? And he has failed whose inner nature was treachery.)
«كانت» is attributed to «الغدر», which is masculine; but since it was predicated with a feminine, its verb was made feminine. Similar to it is the saying of Labīd:
188 - 1- فمضى وقدَّمها وكانت عادةً ... إذا هي عَرَّدَتْ إقدامُها
(So he went on and put her in front, and pressing her forward whenever she shied away was a habit [of his].) [Translator's note: the second hemistich appears to lack a word; the verse is usually cited as «… وكانت عادةً … منه إذا هي عَرَّدَتْ إقدامُها».]
Abū ʿAlī said: "He made «الإقدام» feminine since it was the habit (al-ʿāda) in meaning." He said: "And it has come in speech: «ما جاءت حاجتَك» (what has your need become?), where he made the pronoun of «ما» feminine since it was the need in meaning, and for that reason he made «حاجتك» accusative." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He made «أن قالوا» feminine only because the khabar occurs as a feminine, as in their saying: «من كانت أمَّك» (who was your mother?)."

The Shaykh said: "Al-Zamakhsharī's statement is patched together from the statement of Abū ʿAlī. As for «من كانت أمَّك», he construed the noun of «كان» according to the meaning of «مَنْ», for it has a singular masculine wording and it has a meaning according to what you intend of singular, dual, plural, masculine and feminine; and the construal according to the meaning is not in consideration of the khabar. Do you not see that it comes where there is no khabar, as in His saying:
{وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ} [Yūnus: 42] [and his saying]:
188 - 2-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نكن مثلَ مَنْ يا ذئب يَصْطحبان
(… we will be, O wolf, like two who keep company with each other.)"
I say: I wish I knew for what reason he singled out al-Zamakhsharī with this objection, when it applies to Abū ʿAlī too? For someone may say: the feminine in «جاءت» is for construal according to the meaning of «ما», for it too has a wording and a meaning, like «مَنْ». Besides, it may be said: the feminine has two causes, and the two of them mentioned one of them.

Abū ʿUbayd preferred the reading of the two brothers on the basis of the reading of Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd [written in the text: «وبان مسعود»]: «وما كان فتنتُهم إلا أن قالوا», where the verb was not given the sign of the feminine. Others preferred it on the basis of their consensus on the accusative of «حُجَّتَهم» in His saying, Exalted is He: {مَّا كَانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ} [al-Jāthiya: 25]. It was read, irregularly (shādhdh): «ثم لم يكنْ فتنتُهم إلا أن قالوا», with «يكنْ» masculine and «فتنتهم» nominative. The reason for its irregularity is the dropping of the sign of the feminine while the agent is feminine in wording, even if not real, and making the less definite the noun and the more definite the khabar; so it is the reverse of the first reading on both counts. «أن قالوا» is among what must be placed last because it is restricted [by «إلا»], whether it is made the noun or the khabar.

His saying: {رَبِّنَا}: the two brothers read «ربَّنا» in the accusative, and the rest in the genitive. Its accusative is either as a vocative, or by way of praise — Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this — or by implying «أعني» (I mean) — Abū al-Baqāʾ said this; the implied form [for the vocative] being: O our Lord. On every assumption the clause is parenthetical between the oath and its apodosis, which is His saying {مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ}. Its genitive is on three aspects: naʿt (adjective), badal (substitute) and ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). ʿIkrima and Sallām ibn Miskīn read «واللَّهُ ربُّنا», both nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is by fronting and delaying, as if they said: by Allah, we were not polytheists, and Allah is our Lord." I say: he means that there is an implied oath there.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {كَيْفَ كَذَبُواْ}: «كيف» is accusative in the same way as it is accusative in His saying: {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بالله} [al-Baqara: 28], and its explanation has preceded. «كيف» and what follows it are in the position of accusative by «انظر», because it suspends it from governing. As for «كَذَبوا», even though its meaning is future, because it is on the Day of Resurrection, it was presented in the form of the past because of its certainty. His saying «وضَلَّ» may be coordinated with «كَذَبوا», so it falls within the scope of the looking; or it may be a resumptive statement, so it is not included within the scope of what is looked at. In His saying «ما كانوا», «ما» may be maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e. and their fabrication has strayed from them — this is the view of Ibn ʿAṭiyya; or it may be a nominal relative, i.e. and those whom they used to fabricate have strayed from them. On the first, no returning pronoun referring to «ما» is needed according to the majority; on the second, a pronoun is necessary according to all.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُ}: He took the wording of «مَنْ» into account and so used the singular; had He taken the meaning into account, He would have used the plural, as in His saying in another place: {وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُونَ} [Yūnus: 42]. His saying {وَجَعَلْنَا على قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ}, to the end, was construed according to its meaning.

His saying: {وَجَعَلْنَا}: «جَعَلَ» here may be transformative (taṣyīr), so it takes two objects, the first of them «أكنَّةً» and the second the preposition phrase before it, so that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element, i.e. We made the coverings settled upon their hearts. It may mean "created", so it takes one object, and the preposition phrase before it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), attached to an omitted element, because had it come after, it would have been an adjective of «أَكِنَّة». It may also mean "cast", so «على» is attached to it, as in your saying «ألقيت على زيدٍ كذا» (I cast such-and-such upon Zayd), and His saying: {وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّي} [Ṭā Hā: 39].

This clause allows two aspects. The more evident of them: that it is resumptive, brought to report what it contains of the sealing of their hearts and hearing. It may also be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, the implied form being: whoever listens while a covering has been placed on his heart and deafness in his ear. On the first, a verbal clause has been conjoined to a nominal one; on the second, the wāw is circumstantial, and «قد» is implied after it, according to those who assume it before a past verb occurring as a ḥāl.

«الأَكِنَّة»: plural of «كِنان», which is the encompassing container. [The poet] said:
188 - 3- إذا ما انْتَضْوها في الوغَى مِنْ أكنَّةٍ ... حَسِبْتَ بروقَ الغيث تأتي غيومُها
(When they draw them [the swords] in battle from their sheaths, you would think the lightning of the rain clouds was coming forth from its clouds.)
Some of them said: "«الكِنُّ», with kasra, is that in which a thing is kept, and with fatḥa it is the maṣdar (verbal noun). One says «كنَنْتُه كَنّاً», i.e. I put it in a «كِنّ» (shelter); it is pluralised as «أَكْنان»; the Exalted said: {مِّنَ الجبال أَكْنَاناً} [al-Naḥl: 81]. «الكِنان» is the concealing cover." The verb from this root is used as triliteral and quadriliteral; one says «كَنَنْتُ الشيء» and «أكنَنْتُه», «كِنّاً» and «إكناناً» [written in the text: «أكناناً»]. However, al-Rāghib distinguished between faʿala and afʿala, saying: "«كَنَنْتُ» is specific to what conceals, of a house, a garment or other bodies; the Exalted said: {كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَّكْنُونٌ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 49]; and «أكنَنْتُ» to what is concealed in the soul; the Exalted said: {أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ في أَنْفُسِكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 235]." I say: what he said is also testified to by His saying: {إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ فِي كِتَابٍ مَّكْنُونٍ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 77-78] and His saying, Exalted is He: {مَا تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 69]. «كِنان» is pluralised as «أكِنَّة» for both the plural of paucity and of multitude because it is doubled. That is because faʿāl and fiʿāl, with fatḥa and kasra on the fāʾ, are pluralised for paucity on afʿila, as in «أَحْمِرَة» and «أَقْذِلة», and for multitude on fuʿul, as in «حُمُر» and «قُذُل»; unless it is doubled, like «بَتَات» and «كِنان», or has a weak final radical, like «خِباء» and «قَباء», in which case its plural on afʿila is adhered to, and on fuʿul is not permissible except in a little of speech, as in their saying «عُنُن» and «حُجُج» as plurals of «عِنان» and «حِجاج».

His saying: {أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ}: in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). There are two interpretations of it that have preceded. One of them: «كراهةَ أن يفقهوه» (out of aversion to their understanding it), which is the opinion of the Basrans. The second: the omission of «لا», i.e. «أن لا يفقهوه» (so that they do not understand it), which is the opinion of the Kufans.

His saying: {وَقْراً}: conjoined to «أَكِنَّة», so it is accusative as it is, i.e. and We placed in their ears deafness. «في آذانهم» is like His saying «على قلوبهم». It has preceded that «جَعَل» allows three meanings, so this preposition phrase is built upon them: either a fronted second object, or attached to it [the verb] itself, or a ḥāl.

The majority [read] fatḥa on the wāw of «وَقْراً», and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read it with kasra. The difference between «الوَقْر» and «الوِقْر» is that the one with fatḥa is heaviness in the ear; from it one says «وَقَرَتْ أذنه» [written in the text: «وَقَرِتْ»], with fatḥa and kasra on the qāf, and the imperfect is «تَقِر» and «تَوْقَر» according to the two verbs, like «تَعِد» and «تَوْجَل». Abū Zayd related «أذنٌ مَوْقورة» (a deafened ear), which runs according to analogy, and in it is evidence that the triliteral «وَقَر» may be transitive; and «أذن مُوْقَرَة» was heard, the verb on this basis being the quadriliteral «أَوْقَرْتُ», like «أكرم». «الوِقْر», with kasra, is the load of a donkey, a mule and the like, as «الوَسْق» is for a camel; the Exalted said: {فالحاملات وِقْراً} [al-Dhāriyāt: 2]. On this basis the reading of the majority is clear, i.e. and We placed in their ears heaviness, i.e. deafness. As for the reading of Ṭalḥa, it is as though he made their ears loaded with deafness, as a beast is loaded with a burden. In sum, the root indicates heaviness and gravity; and from it is «الوَقار» for deliberateness and calm. In His saying, Exalted is He: {وفي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْراً} there is separation between the conjunction and what it conjoins by the preposition phrase, while the conjunction consists of a single letter; this is a disputed question whose verification has preceded at His saying: {أَن تُؤدُّواْ الأمانات إلى أَهْلِهَا} [al-Nisāʾ: 58]. The apparent view is that this verse and its parallels, like His saying: {آتِنَا فِي الدنيا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الآخرة حَسَنَةً} [al-Baqara: 201], are not among the cases where the conjunction is separated from what it conjoins. I have verified all of that in the place referred to.

His saying: {حتى إِذَا جَآءُوكَ}: the discussion of «حتى» entering upon «إذا» has preceded at the beginning of al-Nisāʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ said here: "«إذا» is in the position of accusative by its apodosis (jawāb), which is «يقول»; «حتى» has no governing effect here, it only conveys the meaning of limit (ghāya), just as it does not govern clauses." Al-Ḥūfī said: "«حتى» is [for] limit, «يُجادلونك» is a ḥāl, and «يقول» [written in the text: «تقولُ»] is the apodosis of «إذا», and it is what governs «إذا»." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the «حتى» after which clauses occur, and the clause is His saying: {حتى إِذَا جَآءُوكَ يُجَادِلُونَكَ يَقُولُ}; «يجادلونك» is in the position of ḥāl. It may also be the preposition [«حتى»], with «إذا جاؤوك» in the position of genitive, meaning: until the time of their coming; «يجادلونك» is a ḥāl, and His saying {يَقُولُ الذين كفروا} is an explanation of it. The meaning is that their denial of the signs reached the point that they dispute with you and contest with you; and He explained their disputing as their saying: this is nothing but the legends of the ancients."

The Shaykh said: "Al-Ḥūfī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and others were guided to the correct view in that"; then he mentioned the wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Ḥūfī. He also said: "«حتى», when «إذا» occurs after it, may be in the sense of the fāʾ, or in the sense of «إلى أن» (until); so the implied form is: «فإذا جاؤوك يجادلونك يقول» (and when they come to you disputing with you, [those who disbelieve] say), or the implied form is: and We placed coverings upon their hearts, and so on, until they said: this is nothing but the legends of the ancients." It has preceded that «يُجادِلونك» is a ḥāl of the agent of «جاؤوك», and «يقول» is either the apodosis of «إذا» or explanatory of the coming, as its establishment has preceded.

«أساطير»: there are several views on it. One of them: that it is a plural of an assumed singular; and there is disagreement about that assumed singular: it was said «أُسْطورة», it was said «أَسْطارة», it was said «أُسْطور», it was said «أَسْطار», and it was said «إسْطير»; some of them said: rather these singulars were actually uttered. The second: that it is a plural of a plural: «أساطير» is the plural of «أَسْطار», and «أَسْطار» is the plural of «سطَر» with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ; as for «سَطْر» with it vowelless, its plural of paucity is «أَسْطُر» and of multitude «سُطور», like «فَلْس», «أَفْلُس» and «فُلوس». The third: that it is a plural of the plural of a plural: «أساطير» is the plural of «أَسْطار», «أَسْطار» the plural of «أَسْطُر», and «أَسْطُر» the plural of «سَطْر»; this is transmitted from al-Zajjāj. This is worthless, for «أَسْطار» is not the plural of «أَسْطُر»; rather both are patterns of the plural of paucity. The fourth: that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It was said: it is a collective noun having no singular from its own wording." This is worthless, because the grammarians have stated explicitly that if it is on a pattern specific to plurals, they do not call it a collective noun but say it is a plural, like «عباديد» and «شماطيط». The apparent sense of al-Rāghib's statement is that «أساطير» is the plural of «سَطَر» with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ, for he said: "The plural of «سَطَر»" — meaning with fatḥa — "is «أسطار» and «أساطير»." Al-Mubarrad said: "It is the plural of «أُسْطورة», like «أُرْجوحة» and «أراجيح», and «أُحْدُوثة» and «أحاديث»." The meaning of «الأساطير» is false tales and nonsense of what has no reality.

semin-durr:119-119.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَا لَكُمْ} is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). His saying «أن لا تأكلوا» admits two opinions. The first: that it is on the omission of a preposition, i.e. what thing has settled [for you] in refraining from eating of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned. This is the opinion of Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj. When «في» was omitted, the two well-known opinions [Translator's note: i.e. whether the remaining أن-clause is in the position of accusative or genitive] apply. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned no view other than this. The second: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being: "and what is with you, abstaining from eating?" This is supported by the frequent occurrence of an explicit ḥāl in constructions like this, such as {فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التذكرة مُعْرِضِينَ} [al-Muddaththir: 49]. However, this is rejected on two grounds. The first: «أنْ» makes the verb purely future, so how can what follows it be a ḥāl? The second: it, together with what follows it, is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), which most resembles pronouns [in definiteness], as was set out earlier, whereas the ḥāl can only be indefinite. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Unless the omission of a muḍāf is assumed; then it is permissible, i.e. «وما لكم ذوي أن لا تأكلوا» ('and what is with you, being people who do not eat')" — and this is strained. The object of «تأكلوا» is omitted and its adjective remains, the implied form being: "anything of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned". It is also possible that no object is intended, but rather the intended meaning is: "and what is with you that eating should not occur from you", in which case «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. that you should not begin eating from that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned. It was claimed that «لا» is redundant (zāʾida); this is unsound, since there is no reason for its redundancy.

His saying: {وَقَدْ فَصَّلَ لَكُمْ مَّا حَرَّمَ}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read both verbs as passive; Nāfiʿ, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, read both as active; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read the first as active and the second as passive; the reverse of this did not occur. ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī read like the reading of the two brothers [Translator's note: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], except that he lightened the ṣād of «فصل». What stands in place of the agent is the relative noun, and its referent pronoun is from His saying «حَرَّم عليكم». The agent in the reading of those who made it active is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا اضطررتم} admits two views. The first: that it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ); Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Ḥūfī said this. The second: that it is a connected exception (muttaṣil). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ما» is in the position of accusative as an exception from the same genus by way of the meaning, because He rebuked them for abstaining from eating what had been named over, and that implies permissibility absolutely." I say: the first is clearer, and the connected sense is awkward in meaning. Then he said: "And His saying «وقد فصَّل لكم ما حَرَّم عليكم» means: in the state of free choice, and that is / lawful in the state of necessity."

His saying {لَّيُضِلُّونَ}: the Kufans read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, and likewise the one in Yūnus [verse 88]: {رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّواْ}; the rest with fatḥa. There will come parallels to this in Ibrāhīm and elsewhere. Both readings are clear, for one says «ضَلَّ» of going astray oneself and «أضلَّ» of leading another astray. So the object is omitted on the reading of the Kufans, and it is more emphatic in censure, since it includes the ugliness of their deed in that they went astray themselves and led others astray, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَأَضَلُّواْ كَثِيراً وَضَلُّواْ عَن سَوَآءِ السبيل} [al-Māʾida: 77]. The reading with fatḥa does not require an omission, and some preferred it for this reason; also, they agreed on the fatḥa in Ṣād at His saying {إِنَّ الذين يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ الله} [verse 26].

His saying: {بِأَهْوَائِهِم} is attached to «يضلون», and the bāʾ is causal, i.e. because of their following their desires and appetites. His saying «بغير علم» is attached to something omitted, because it is a ḥāl, i.e. they lead astray accompanied by ignorance, i.e. being without knowledge.

semin-durr:121-121.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ}: there are several views about this clause. The first: that it is resumptive. They said: it may not be conjoined to what precedes it, because the former is a request (ṭalabiyya) and this is a statement (khabariyya); this wāw is called the wāw of resumption. The second: that it is conjoined to what precedes it, no account being taken of their differing; this is the doctrine of Sībawayh. The verification of this has preceded, and I have adduced sound evidence for it from poetry and elsewhere. The third: that it is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), i.e. do not eat it while it is ungodliness (fisq). Imām al-Rāzī boasted of this view against the Ḥanafīs, in that he turned their proof against them with it. That is because they forbid eating what was slaughtered without the tasmiya (pronouncing Allah's name), while the Shāfiʿīs do not forbid it, and the Ḥanafīs argued against them from the apparent sense of this verse. So al-Rāzī said: "This clause is circumstantial; it may not be conjoined, because they differ as request and statement, so it must be circumstantial. If it is circumstantial, the meaning is: do not eat it in the state of its being fisq. Then this fisq is unspecified (mujmal), and Allah the Exalted explained it in another place, saying: {أَوْ فِسْقاً أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ الله بِهِ} [al-Anʿām: 145], meaning that if a name other than the name of Allah is mentioned over the slaughtered animal, it may not be eaten, because it is fisq" — and we hold this; but it does not follow from it that if neither the name of Allah nor the name of another is mentioned, it is unlawful, because that is not covered by the explanation we have mentioned. There is room for dispute about this from several angles, among them: we do not concede that a statement may not be conjoined to a request and vice versa, as I reported earlier from Sībawayh. If that is conceded, the wāw is for resumption, as stated, and what follows it is resumptive. And if that too is conceded, we do not concede that «فسقاً» in the other verse explains the fisq in this verse, for this is not of the category of the unspecified (mujmal) and its explanation (mubayyan), because that has conditions not present here.

What he said is drawn from the words of al-Zamakhsharī, who said: "If you say: a group of the mujtahids held that it is permissible to eat that over which the name of Allah was not mentioned, through forgetfulness or deliberately — I say: these interpreted it as carrion and as that over which a name other than Allah's was mentioned, as in His saying: {أَوْ فِسْقاً أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ الله بِهِ} [al-Anʿām: 145]." This is the origin of what Ibn al-Khaṭīb [Translator's note: i.e. al-Rāzī] mentioned and boasted of.

The pronoun in «إنَّه» may refer to the eating indicated by «لا تأكلوا», or to the relative noun — and there are then two interpretations: that you make the relative noun itself the fisq, by way of hyperbole, or that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "and its eating is indeed fisq" — or to the mentioning understood from His saying «ذُكر». The Shaykh said: "The pronoun in «إنه» refers to the eating; al-Zamakhsharī said this and limited himself to it." I say: he did not limit himself to it; rather he mentioned that it may refer to the relative noun, and mentioned the two interpretations given above, saying: "The pronoun refers to the maṣdar of the verb on which the particle of prohibition enters, in the sense: and eating of it is indeed fisq; or to the relative noun, on the basis that eating it is fisq, or he made that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned to be [in] itself fisq."

His saying: {لِيُجَادِلُوكُمْ} is attached to «يُوحُون», i.e. they inspire for the purpose of disputing with you. The original of «يُوحون» is يُوحِيُون, and it underwent weak-letter change. «وإن أَطَعْتموهم»: it was said that [there is] the lām preparing for the oath [Translator's note: i.e. an implied lām al-tawṭiʾa]; that is why the implied oath is answered by His saying «إنكم لمشركون», and the apodosis of the condition was omitted because the response of the oath fills its place; the omission is permissible because the verb of the condition is past. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "He omitted the fāʾ from the apodosis of the condition, and that is good when the condition is in the form of the past, and here it is so, namely His saying «وإن أَطَعْتموهم»." I say: it seems he claimed that the apodosis of the condition is the clause «إنكم لمشركون», the original being «فإنكم» with the fāʾ because it is a nominal clause, and then the fāʾ was omitted because the verb of the condition is in the past form. This is nothing, for the oath is implied before the condition. What shows this is the omission of the preparatory lām before the conditional «إن» where the verb of the condition is not past, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ} [al-Aʿrāf: 23]; here he cannot say that the fāʾ is omitted, because the verb of the condition is imperfect. It seems — and Allah knows best — that Abū al-Baqāʾ took this from al-Ḥūfī, for I saw it in him just as Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it; and the Shaykh rejected it in a way similar to what has preceded.

semin-durr:122-122.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَوَ مَن كَانَ}: «أو مَنْ كان»: it was stated earlier that this hamza may be placed before the conjunction — which is the opinion of the majority — or that it is in its own place, with an implied verb between it and the wāw. «مَنْ» is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «كمَنْ» is its khabar (predicate); it is a relative noun. «يمشي» is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «نوراً». «مَثَلُه» is a mubtadaʾ and «في الظلمات» is its khabar, / and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «مَنْ»; and «مَنْ» is genitive by the kāf, and the kāf with its genitive noun is, as stated, in the position of nominative as khabar of the first «مَن». «ليس بخارج» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun, i.e. like the one who has settled in darkness, in the state of remaining in it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ليس بخارجٍ» is in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun in «منها»; it may not be a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «مَثَلُه», because of the separation between it and the ḥāl by the khabar." Makkī made the clause a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in «الظلمات». Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «أَفَمَنْ كان», with fāʾ instead of the wāw.

His saying: {كَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ} is an adjective of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Some gave its implied form as: "it was made attractive to the disbelievers with an adorning just as We gave life to the believers"; others gave it as: "it was made attractive to the disbelievers with an adorning, because of the disbelievers' being in darkness, remaining in it". The omitted agent of «زُيِّن», for which [the deputy] stands, is Allah the Exalted; it may also be Satan. Each of the two agents has been stated explicitly with the word «زَيَّن»: Allah the Exalted said: {زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ} [al-Naml: 4], and Allah the Exalted said: {وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشيطان أَعْمَالَهُمْ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 38]. {مَا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ} is what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil). «ما» may be a nominal relative, or a particle (maṣdariyya), or an indefinite qualified by an adjective; the referent pronoun on the first and third opinions is omitted, but not on the second according to the majority, as has been known more than once. Al-Zajjāj said: "The position of the kāf is nominative, and the meaning is: like that which We have narrated to you, their deeds were made attractive to the disbelievers."

semin-durr:91-91.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ}: in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is originally an adjective of the maṣdar; when the descriptive word was put in construct with what it describes, it took the accusative that what it describes would have taken. The original is «قَدْره الحق» ("His true measure"), as in their sayings «جَرْدُ قطيفة» ("a worn-out velvet") and «سحق عمامة» ("a threadbare turban"). Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read: «جَرْد قطيفة وسحق عمامة». [Translator's note: this sentence is so in the text; it appears to be a copyist's duplication of the preceding examples combined with the opening of the next sentence.] Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read «قدَّروا» with a doubled dāl and «قَدَره» with the dāl vowelled; it has been stated before that the two are dialectal variants.
His words: «إذ قالوا» is in the accusative by «قَدَروا»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it accusative by «قَدْره», and in Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words there is something suggesting that it is causal. «من شيء» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) in which «مِنْ» was added, because the two conditions for its redundancy are present.
His words: «نوراً» is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and there are two aspects concerning the one it describes. One: it is the hāʾ in «به», so its governing word is «جاء». The second: it is «الكتاب», so its governing word is «أنزل». «للناس» is an adjective of «هدى».
His words: «تَجْعلونه»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with the yāʾ of the third person [«يجعلونه»], and likewise «يُبْدونها» and «يُخْفون»; the rest read with the tāʾ of address in all three verbs. The third person is by construing it with the preceding third person in His words «وما قدروا» to the end. On this view there are two interpretations of His words «وعُلِّمْتُم». One: it is also addressed to them, and it came only by way of a shift (iltifāt). The second: it is addressed to the believers, inserted parenthetically between the command in His words {قُلْ مَنْ أَنزَلَ} and His words {قُلِ الله}.
As for the reading with the tāʾ of address, it has congruence with His words {وَعُلِّمْتُمْ مَّا لَمْ تعلموا أَنتُمْ}, and Makkī and a group preferred it for that reason. Makkī said: "That is better for correspondence and agreement and the connection of the parts of the speech with one another; it is the preferred choice for that reason, and because most of the readers follow it." The Shaykh said: "Whoever says that the deniers were the Arabs or the disbelievers of Quraysh cannot make the address to them; rather, He would have interrupted [the speech] with the Children of Israel, saying in the course of the question and answer: you make it into sheets. Such a thing is unlikely to occur, because it breaks apart the arrangement, making the beginning of the speech addressed to the disbelievers and its end addressed to the Jews." He said: "It has been answered that since all of them shared in denying the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, part of the speech came addressed to the Arabs and part addressed to the Children of Israel."
His words: «تَجْعلونه قراطيس»: «جعل» may mean "to make into (ṣayyara)," or may mean "to put," i.e. "you put it in paper." This clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, either from «الكتاب» or from the hāʾ in «به», as stated for «نوراً وهدى».
His words: «قراطيس»: there are three [aspects]. The first: it is by omission of the preposition, i.e. "in sheets and paper"; so it resembles a vague adverb (ẓarf mubham), which is why the verb reaches it by itself. The second: it is by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "you make it possessing sheets." The third: they treated it as if it were sheets. The explanation of «القراطيس» has been given. The clause «تبدونها» is in the position of an accusative as an adjective of «قراطيس». As for «تُخْفون», Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It too is an adjective of it," and he implied an omitted pronoun, i.e. "and you conceal much of them." As for Makkī, he said: "«وتُخْفون» is a new beginning (mubtadaʾ) that has no grammatical position." End of quotation. It is as though, when he saw that [this clause] lacked [a pronoun] referring to «قراطيس», he forbade its being an adjective; but it has been stated that it is implied, i.e. "of them," and this is better. Al-Wāḥidī allowed «تبدون» to be a ḥāl from the pronoun of «الكتاب» in His words «تجعلونه قراطيس», "on the basis that you make the Book the sheets in meaning, because it is written in them." End of quotation. His saying "on the basis that you make" is an excuse for its pronoun coming in the feminine; in short, it is far-fetched or impossible.
His words: «وعُلِّمْتُمْ»: on the third-person reading of «يجعلونه» and what is conjoined to it, it may be resumptive or a ḥāl, and it only came in the second person for the sake of the shift (iltifāt). On the reading with the tāʾ of address it is a ḥāl, and those who require «قد» with a past verb serving as a ḥāl imply it here, i.e. «وقد عُلِّمْتُمْ».
His words: «قلِ اللهُ»: two aspects are possible in the Majestic Name. One: that it be the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, i.e. "say: He sent it down"; this is the correct one, because the verb is explicit in His words {لَيَقُولُنَّ خَلَقَهُنَّ العزيز} [al-Zukhruf: 9]. The second: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "Allah sent it down"; the reason for its fittingness is the correspondence of the answer to the question, since the question clause is nominal, so let the answer clause be likewise.
His words: {فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ}: «في خوضهم» may be attached to «ذرْهُم», or to «يَلْعبون», or it may be a ḥāl from the object of «ذَرْهم», or a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يَلْعبون»; these are four aspects. As for «يلعبون», it may be a ḥāl from the object of «ذرهم»; and whoever forbids multiple ḥāls for one thing will not then allow «في خوضهم» to be a ḥāl from the object of «ذرهم», but will make it either attached to «ذَرْهُمْ», as stated, or to «يَلْعبون», or a ḥāl from its fāʿil. «يلعبون» may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun of «خَوْضهم»; that is permissible because it is effectively an agent, since the maṣdar is in construct with its agent, the implied form being: "leave them to wade, playing." And it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «خوضهم» [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably meaning the pronoun latent in «في خوضهم»] if we make that a ḥāl, because it contains the meaning of settledness (istiqrār); so it would be an overlapping ḥāl (mutadākhila).

semin-durr:92-92.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وهذا كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ}: in it there is evidence for placing a non-explicit adjective [i.e. a clause] before an explicit one [a single word]. It has been answered that «مبارك» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); the verification of this was given at His words {بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 54]. Makkī said: "«مصدِّقُ الذي» is an adjective of «الكتاب», with the tanwīn omitted because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters, and «الذي» is in the position of an accusative; if the omission of the tanwīn is not assumed, «مصدق» is a khabar after a khabar and «الذي» is in the position of a genitive." What he said is a gross error, because the omission of the tanwīn is only for the verbal (lafẓī) genitive construct, even though the active participle is intended as separate; omission of the tanwīn because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters only occurs in poetic necessity or rarely, as in his saying:
1980 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا ذاكرَ اللهَ إلا قليلا
(…nor one remembering Allah except a little.)
All the grammarians say about «هذا ضاربُ الرجلِ» ("this is the striker of the man") that the tanwīn is omitted for the genitive construct, for lightness; none of them says in such a case that the tanwīn was omitted because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters.
He placed describing it as sent down before describing it as blessed, unlike His words {وهذا ذِكْرٌ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 50]. They said: because the more important thing here is describing it as sent down, since it came right after their denial that Allah sends down anything upon a human being, unlike there. The first adjective came as a verbal clause, because sending down is renewed time after time, and the second as an explicit noun, because the noun indicates permanence and stability, and that is intended here, i.e. its blessing is permanent and stable. «مصدِّق» is also an adjective, or a khabar after a khabar on the view that «مبارك» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. It occurred as an adjective of an indefinite noun because it is intended as separate [i.e. its construct is non-defining], as in His words {هذا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا} [al-Aḥqāf: 24] [and his saying]:
1981 - يا رُبَّ غابِطنا لو كان يعرِفُكم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O how many a one envying us, if he knew you…)
Al-Wāḥidī said: "«مبارك» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; they were separated by the clause, and the implied form is: and this is a blessed Book which We sent down, as in His words {وهذا ذِكْرٌ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 50]." What he mentioned only works on the basis that His word «مبارك» is a second khabar of «هذا», and this is very far-fetched. And if that is conceded, then «أنزلناه» for him would be parenthetical, on the apparent sense of his wording; but there is no need for that—rather «أنزلناه» is made an adjective of «كتاب», and on this assumption there is then nothing objectionable. In sum, the right approach is the parsing I gave you before.
His words: «ولتنذرَ»: the majority read it with the tāʾ of address to the Messenger (upon him be peace), and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim with the yāʾ of the third person [«ولينذر»], the pronoun referring to the Quran, which is the apparent sense, i.e. it warns by its admonitions and deterrents; it may also refer to the Messenger (upon him be peace), since he is known. There are two aspects concerning this lām. One: it is attached to «أنزلنا», conjoined to something implied. Abū al-Baqāʾ gave the implied form as "so that they may believe, and so that you may warn." Al-Zamakhsharī gave the implied form, saying: "«ولتنذر» is conjoined to what the description of the Book indicates, as though it were said: We sent it down for blessings, for confirming the books that preceded it, and for warning."
The second: it is attached to an omitted [verb] placed after, i.e. "and so that you may warn, We sent it down."
His words: «أمَّ القرى» may belong to the category of omission, i.e. "the people of the Mother of Towns," or to the category of figurative usage (majāz), applying [the name of] the place to its occupants. Which of the two is preferable, I mean figurative usage or implied omission? People have three views on the question, whose explanation has been given. This is like His words {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82]. There, there is an aspect that is not possible here: namely, that the questioning of the town may be literal, and that this would be a miracle for a prophet. Here that is not feasible; even if the town itself here also spoke, the warning would not take place, because it would be of no benefit.
His words: «ومَنْ حولها» is conjoined to the omitted «أهل», i.e. "and so that you may warn those around the Mother of Towns." It cannot be conjoined to «أم القرى», since the meaning would then necessarily be "and so that you may warn the people of those around it," and no need calls for that, because "those around it" are capable of receiving the warning. The Shaykh said: "And «مَنْ» was not omitted so that «حول» would be conjoined to «أمّ القرى»—even though that would be valid in meaning—because «حول» is an adverb that is not freely declined (lā yataṣarraf); if it were conjoined to «أم القرى», it would be a direct object, by being conjoined to a direct object, and that is not permissible, because the Arabs used it only as an adverb."
His words: «والذين يؤمنون بالآخرة»: two aspects are possible. One: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is «يؤمنون». The subject and predicate are not identical because their attached elements (mutaʿallaq) differ; that is why the khabar could come in the wording of the mubtadaʾ; otherwise it would be impossible to say «الذي يقوم يقوم» ("the one who stands, stands") or «الذين يؤمنون يؤمنون». On this view, mentioning the extra element (faḍla) here is obligatory. The grammarians did not address this, but they addressed parallels to it. The second: it is in the accusative, conjoined to «أم القرى», i.e. "and so that you may warn those who believe"; so «يؤمنون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun, and it is not an emphatic ḥāl, because of what was given you about what permits its occurring as a khabar, namely the difference of the attached element. The hāʾ in «به» refers to the Quran or to the Messenger. {وَهُمْ على صَلاَتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ} is a ḥāl; «على صَلاتهم» was placed first for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila). Abū ʿAlī mentioned in «al-Rawḍa» that Abū Bakr read «على صلواتهم» in the plural.

semin-durr:93-93.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {كَذِباً}: there are four aspects concerning it. The first: it is the object of «افترى», i.e. "he invented and fabricated a lie." The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of it according to the meaning, i.e. "he fabricated a fabrication." This is open to consideration, because what is attested in such cases is only where the maṣdar is a kind of the verb, e.g. «قعد القرفصاء» ("he sat squatting"), or synonymous with it, e.g. «قعدت جلوساً» ("I sat a sitting"); as for where the maṣdar is more general than its verb, e.g. «افترى كذباً» and «تَقَرْفَصَ قعوداً», this is not attested, since there is no benefit in it; and lying is more general than fabricating. Its verification has been given before. The third: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "he fabricated for the sake of lying." The fourth: it is a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "he fabricated, being a liar," and it is an emphatic ḥāl. His words «أو قال» are conjoined to «افترى». «إليّ» [Translator's note: printed «إلى»] is in the position of a nominative because it stands in place of the fāʿil (agent). Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that what stands in place of the agent be the pronoun of the maṣdar; he said: "Its implied form is: the revelation, or the revealing, was revealed to me." The first is better, because it contains a new piece of information, unlike the second, since the meaning of the maṣdar is understood from the verb before it.
His words: {وَلَمْ يُوحَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ}: a ḥāl clause. The agent is omitted here to magnify Him, since the one who reveals is Allah the Exalted. His words «ومن قال» are in a genitive position, because it is conjoined to «مَنْ» which is in the genitive by «مِنْ», i.e. «وممَّن قال» ("and than one who said"). A parallel to this interrogative was given in al-Baqara, and there is a question and its answer there. Abū Ḥaywa read «سَأُنَزِّل» with the doubled form. His word «مثلَ»: two aspects are possible in it. One: it is in the accusative as a direct object, i.e. "I will send down a Quran like what Allah sent down"; «ما» on this view is a nominal relative or a qualified indefinite, i.e. "like that which He sent down" or "like something He sent down." The second: that it be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "I will send down a sending-down like what Allah sent down"; «ما» on this view is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), i.e. "like Allah's sending down." «إذ» is in the accusative by «ترى», and the object of the seeing is omitted, i.e. "and if you could see the disbelievers," or "the liars"; it may also be that no object is implied for it, i.e. "if you were among those who see at this time." The apodosis of «لو» is omitted, i.e. "you would see a tremendous thing." In «الظالمون» the al may be generic or for the previously known (ʿahd), meaning those mentioned before: the polytheists, the Jews, and the lying fabricators.
{فِي غَمَرَاتِ الموت} is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is in the position of a genitive by the adverb [«إذ»]. «الغَمَرات» is the plural of «غَمْرة», which is a horrifying hardship. Its origin is from «غَمَرَهُ الماء», when the water covered him, as though it covers [a person] with its distress and descends upon him. He said:
1982 - ولا يُنْجي من الغَمَراتِ إلاَّ ... بَرَاكاءُ القتالِ أو الفرارُ
(Nothing saves from the overwhelming hardships but steadfast kneeling in battle, or flight.)
It is also pluralised as «غُمَر», like «عَمْرة» [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably «غُمْرة»] and «عُمَر». He said:
1983 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وحان لتالِكَ الغُمَرِ انقشاعُ
(…and the time has come for those overwhelming troubles to clear away.)
And it is related as «انحسار» ("receding"). Al-Rāghib said: "The root sense of «الغَمْر» is removing the trace of a thing; from it abundant water that removes the trace of its course was called «غَمْر» and «غامِر»." Someone other than al-Rāghib recited, for «غامر»:
1984 - نصفَ النهارُ الماءُ غامِرُه ... ورفيقُه بالغيب لا يدري
(The day reached its midpoint while the water was covering him, and his companion, unseen, did not know.)
Then he said: "«الغَمْرَة» is the bulk of the water, because it covers its bed; and it was made a figure for ignorance that overwhelms the one who has it." «الغَمْر» is one who has not experienced affairs, and its plural is «أغمار». «الغِمْر» with kasra is rancour; «الغَمْر» with fatḥa is abundant water; «الغَمَر» with fatḥa on the ghayn and the mīm is the smell of grease that overwhelms all other smells, and from it is the hadith: "Whoever spends the night with «غَمَر» on his hands…"; one says «غَمِرَت يده», and «غَمِر عرضَه دنسٌ» ("his honour was overwhelmed with defilement"); and "they entered into the throng (ghumār) of people and their multitude (khumār)." «الغُمْرَة» is the saffron with which [the face] is smeared; and from it the cup with which water is taken was called «غُمَر». "So-and-so is «مغامِر»" is said when he throws himself into war, either because of his plunging deep and wading into it, or because recklessness (ghamāra) is conceived of in him.
His words: {والملائكة باسطوا}: a clause in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in His words «في غَمَرات». «أيديهم» is genitive in wording and its position is accusative; the nūn was only dropped for lightness.
His words: {أخرجوا}: its position is accusative by an implied saying, and the saying is frequently implied; its implied form is "saying: bring out," as in His words {يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن كُلِّ بَابٍ سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ} [al-Raʿd: 23], i.e. saying: "Peace be upon you." That implied saying is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «باسطو».
His words: {اليوم تُجْزَوْنَ}: there are two aspects concerning this adverb. One: it is in the accusative by «أخْرِجوا», meaning "bring them out of your bodies"; so this saying is in this world. It may also be on the Day of Resurrection, the meaning being "free yourselves from the punishment." So the pause is on His word «اليوم», and the new start is with His words {تُجْزَوْنَ عَذَابَ الهون}. The second: it is in the accusative by «تُجْزون», and the pause is then on «أنفسَكم» and the new start with His word «اليوم». What is meant by «اليوم» may be the time of death-throes, or it may be the Day of Resurrection. «عذابَ» is the second object, and the first stands in place of the agent. «الهُون» is humiliation (al-hawān). Allah the Exalted said: {أَيُمْسِكُهُ على هُون} [al-Naḥl: 59]. Dhū al-Iṣbaʿ said:
1985 - اذهَبْ إليك فيما أمي براعيةٍ ... ترعى المَخَاضَ ولا أُغْضي على الهُون
(Be off with you! My mother is no herdswoman pasturing pregnant camels, and I do not shut my eyes to humiliation.)
And al-Khansāʾ said:
1986 - يُهينُ النفوسَ وهُونُ النفو ... سِ يومَ الكريهة أَبْقَى لها
(He holds lives cheap — and holding lives cheap on the day of battle better preserves them.)
He put «العذاب» in construct with «الهُون» to signal that it is firmly established in it; for not every punishment contains humiliation, since it may be by way of deterrence and discipline. It may also belong to the category of putting the thing described in construct with its adjective, since the original is «العذاب الهون»; He described it with it for intensification, then put it in construct with it in the manner of their saying «بقلة الحمقاء» ("the foolish herb," purslane) and the like. What shows that «الهُون» means «الهوان» is the reading of ʿAbd Allah [ibn Masʿūd] and ʿIkrima, who read it so [«الهوان»].
His words: {بِمَا كُنتُمْ}: «ما» is maṣdar-forming, i.e. "because of your being sayers of other than the truth, and your being arrogant." The bāʾ is attached to «تُجْزون», i.e. because of it. «غير الحق» is in the accusative in two ways. One: it is a direct object, i.e. "you mention other than the truth." The second: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "you say speech other than the truth." His words «وكنتم»: two aspects are possible. One, which is the apparent one: it is conjoined to the first «كنتم», so it is part of the ṣila of «ما», as stated. The second: it is a resumptive clause brought to state that. «عن آياته» is attached to the khabar of «كان», and was placed first for the sake of the verse-endings.

semin-durr:109-109.t:
