The words of the Exalted: {جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ}: Discussion of it has preceded in al-Māʾida. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read: «لَيُؤْمَنَنْ», in the passive, emphasised with the light nūn. His words «وما يُشْعِركم»: «ما» is interrogative and a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause after it is its khabar (predicate); the agent of «يشعر» refers back to it. It is transitive to two objects: the first is the pronoun of address, and the second is omitted, i.e. and what makes you know their faith when the signs they proposed come to them?
The generality read «أنها» with fatḥa of the hamza, and Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr (with disagreement from him) with its kasra. As for the reading with kasra, it is clear, and people — al-Khalīl and others — found it excellent, because its meaning is a fresh start informing of the absence of faith of those whose hearts have been sealed, even if every sign came to them. Sībawayh said: "I asked al-Khalīl about this reading" — meaning the reading with fatḥa — "and said: what prevents it from being like your saying: ما يدريك أنه لا يفعل? He said: that is not good in this place; He only said «وما يُشْعركم», then He began afresh and affirmed, saying {إِنَّهَآ إِذَا جَآءَتْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}; and had He used fatḥa, saying {وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ أَنَّهَآ إِذَا جَآءَتْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}, it would have been an excuse for them." People explained al-Khalīl's statement and clarified it. Al-Wāḥidī and others said: "Because if you gave «أنَّ» fatḥa and made it the one in something like «بلغني أن زيداً منطلق», it would be an excuse for those of whom it was reported that they do not believe; for when someone says: 'Zayd does not believe', and you say: 'and what makes you know that he will not believe?', the meaning is that he will believe; and if that is so, it is an excuse for the one of whom faith was denied. But the intent of the noble verse is not to establish their excuse and the existence of their faith." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And «إنها» was read with kasra, on the basis that the speech was complete before it, in the sense: and what makes you know what will come from them? Then He informed them of His knowledge about them, saying: إنها إذا جاءت لا يؤمنون."
As for the reading with fatḥa, people have justified it in six ways. The most apparent: that it is in the sense of laʿalla ("perhaps"). Al-Khalīl related «أتيت السوق أنك تشتري لنا منه شيئاً» ("Go to the market, perhaps you will buy us something from it"), i.e. laʿallaka. So this, from the speech of the Arabs, as al-Khalīl related it, is evidence that «أنَّ» can be in the sense of laʿalla. Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās recited:
2027 - أريني جواداً مات هُزْلاً لأَنَّني ... أرى ما تَرَيْنَ أو بخيلاً مُخَلَّدا
(Show me a generous man who died of leanness — perhaps I will see what you see — or a miser who lived forever.)
Imruʾ al-Qays said — al-Zamakhsharī recited it:
2028 - عُوجا على الطلل المُحيلِ لأنَّنا ... نبكي الديار كما بكى ابنُ حِذامِ
(Turn aside, you two, to the long-deserted ruin, that perhaps we may weep over the abodes as Ibn Ḥidhām wept.)
And Jarīr said:
2029 - هلَ أنتمْ عائجون بنا لَعَنَّا ... نرى العَرَصاتِ أو أثرَ الخيام
(Will you turn aside with us — perhaps we may see the courtyards or the traces of the tents.)
And ʿAdī ibn Zayd said:
2030 - أعاذلَ ما يُدْرِيكَ أن منيَّتي ... إلى ساعةٍ في اليوم أو في ضحى الغد
(O censuring woman, what makes you know — perhaps my death is at some hour today or in tomorrow's forenoon.)
And another said:
2032 - قلت لشيبانَ ادنُ مِنْ لِقائِهْ ... أنَّا نُغَذِّي الناسَ مِنْ شوائِهْ
(I said to Shaybān: draw near to meet it, perhaps we will feed the people from its roast.) [Translator's note: the source numbers this verse 2032 (no 2031 appears), and the next verse is also numbered 2032; the numbering is kept as written.]
So «أنَّ» in all these places is in the sense of laʿalla. They said: this is indicated by the fact that in the codex and reading of Ubayy it is «وما أدراكم لعلَّها إذا جاءت لا يؤمنون», and from him was transmitted: {وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ لعلها إِذَا جَآءَتْ}; Abū ʿUbayd and others mentioned that. They also preferred it because «لعل» frequently occurs in a construction like this, as in the words of the Exalted: {وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ الساعة قَرِيبٌ} [al-Shūrā: 17], {وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يزكى} [ʿAbasa: 3]. Among those who also made «أنَّ» in the sense of «لعل» is Yaḥyā ibn Ziyād al-Farrāʾ.
Al-Zajjāj preferred it, saying: "Sībawayh claimed from al-Khalīl that its meaning is «لعلها»"; he said: "And this aspect is stronger and better in Arabic." / He attributed the reading to the people of Medina, and so did Abū Jaʿfar. I say: it is also the reading of the Kufans and the Syrians. However, Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī weakened this view, which people found excellent and strengthened as an explanation of this reading, saying: "The expectation indicated by «لعلَّ» does not fit the reading with kasra, because it indicates His judgment upon them that they do not believe." But when he refused its being in the sense of «لعل», he did not make it governed by «يُشْعِركم»; rather he made it on the omission of the lām of cause, i.e. «لأنها», the implied form according to him being: Say: the signs are only with Allah, because when they come they do not believe; so He does not bring them, because of their persistence in their disbelief. It would thus be a parallel of {وَمَا مَنَعَنَآ أَن نُّرْسِلَ بالآيات إِلاَّ أَن كَذَّبَ بِهَا الأولون} [al-Isrāʾ: 59], i.e. with the proposed signs. On this view His words «وما يُشْعركم» are parenthetical between the cause and the thing caused.
The second: that «لا» is redundant (zāʾida). This is the opinion of al-Farrāʾ and his teacher [al-Kisāʾī]. He said: "Its like is {مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 12], i.e. that you prostrate." So the implied form is: and what makes you know that when they come they will believe? — and the meaning on this view is: had they come, they would not have believed. What led him to take it as redundant is what preceded: that if it were not reckoned redundant, the apparent sense of the speech would be an excuse for the disbelievers and [imply] that they would believe, as you learned in its verification earlier. [Translator's note: the source reads «لو تُقَدَّر زائدةً» ("if it were reckoned redundant"); the argument requires "if it were not reckoned redundant", and it is rendered accordingly.] However, al-Zajjāj attributed that to error, saying: "Whoever mentioned that «لا» is superfluous (laghw) is in error, because what is superfluous cannot be non-superfluous, and whoever reads with kasra — there is consensus that «لا» is not superfluous." So it is not permissible for the meaning of a word to be negation at one time and affirmation at another in one context.
Al-Fārisī supported al-Farrāʾ's view and denied the error in it, for he said: "It is permissible for «لا» to be redundant in one interpretation and not redundant in another, like the poet's saying:
2032 - أبى جودُه لا البخلَ واستعجلَتْ نَعَمْ ... به مِنْ فتى لا يمنع الجودَ نائِلُهْ
(His generosity refused "no" — miserliness — and "yes" hastened [to come] from a young man whose giving does not withhold generosity.)
It is recited in both ways, i.e. with «البخل» in the accusative and in the genitive. Whoever made it accusative, [«لا»] was redundant, i.e. his generosity refused miserliness; and whoever made it genitive, it was not redundant, and he put «لا» in construct with البخل." I say: on the assumption of the accusative its redundancy is not required, since «لا» may be the direct object, with البخل a badal (substitute) of it, i.e. his generosity refused the word «لا», and the word «لا» is miserliness.
A portion of this has preceded for you in verified form at the words of the Exalted {وَلاَ الضآلين} [al-Fātiḥa: 7] at the beginning of this work, and you will come across places of it, like the words of the Exalted: {وَحَرَامٌ على قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَآ أَنَّهُمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 95] — they said it admits redundancy and its absence — and likewise {مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 12] and {لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الكتاب} [al-Ḥadīd: 29].
The third: that the fatḥa is on the implication of the lām of cause, the implied form being: the signs that they propose are only with Allah, because when they come they do not believe; and «وما يُشْعركم» is parenthetical — as the verification of that from Abū ʿAlī preceded, making repetition unnecessary. The meaning becomes: the signs — i.e. the proposed ones — are only with Allah; He does not bring them because of the absence of their faith and their persistence in their disbelief.
The fourth: that in the speech there is the omission of something conjoined to what precedes. Abū Jaʿfar [al-Naḥḥās] said in his Maʿānī: "And it was said: in the speech there is an omission; the meaning is: and what makes you know that when they come they will not believe, or will believe?" This was omitted because the hearer knows it. Others implied it as: what makes you know of the absence of faith or its occurrence?
The fifth: that «لا» is not redundant and there is no omission in the speech; rather the meaning is: and what makes you know the absence of their faith? This would be an answer to whoever judged them to be disbelievers forever and despaired of their faith. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وما يشعركم», and what makes you know that they — that the signs they propose — when they come, they will not believe in them; meaning: I know that when they come they will not believe in them, and you do not know that. That is because the believers were eager for their faith and hopeful of it when that sign came, and wished for its coming; so He, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'and what makes you know that they will not believe', in the sense: you do not know what My knowledge of them has foreknown, that they will not believe. Do you not see His words: {كَمَا لَمْ يُؤْمِنُواْ بِهِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ} [al-Anʿām: 110]?" End of quote. I say: the elaboration of his statement that they were hopeful of their faith is what came in the exegesis: that the polytheists said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Send down upon us the sign about which Allah said {إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّنَ السمآء آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ}, and by Allah we will believe"; so Allah the Exalted sent down: «وما يُشْعركم» to its end/. This aspect is the choice of the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān], for he said: "The speech needs neither the redundancy of «لا», nor this implication" — meaning the omission of the conjoined element — "nor «أنَّ» in the sense of لعلَّ; all of this is departing from the apparent sense without necessity. Rather, taking it in its apparent sense is preferable, and it is clear and acceptable, i.e. and what makes you perceive and know the absence of their faith? You have no way to perceive it."
The sixth: that «ما» is a particle of negation, meaning that He negated their perceiving that. On this view an agent is sought for «يُشْعركم».
It was said: it is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, implied because [the context] indicates it — and there is far-fetched artificiality in it — i.e. Allah does not make you know that when the proposed signs come they will not believe. The manner of Abū ʿAmr's reading of {يُشْعِرُكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 109], {يَنصُرْكُمُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 160] and the like has preceded in al-Baqara at His words {إِنَّ الله يَأْمُرُكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 67]; its upshot is three ways: full ḍamma, slurring (ikhtilās), and pure sukūn.
The majority read: «لا يؤمنون» with the yāʾ of the third person, and Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamza with the tāʾ of address. They both also read in al-Jāthiya [verse 6] {فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَ الله وَآيَاتِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ} with address, and al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim agreed with them in it, while the rest read with the yāʾ of the third person. The upshot of that is that Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamza read with address in both places; Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim with the third person in both places; and al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim with the third person here and with address in al-Jāthiya — so they agreed with one of the two groups in one of the two sūras and with the other in the other.
As for the reading with address here, the apparent sense of the address in His words «وما يشعركم» is that it is to the disbelievers. The meaning of this reading becomes clear on the redundancy of «لا», i.e. and what makes you know that you will believe when the signs you requested come, as you swore to? It also becomes clear on «أنَّ» being in the sense of laʿalla with «لا» negating; and on its being a cause with the omission of the lām implied, i.e. the signs are only with Allah, so He does not bring them to you, because when they come you will not believe in them. It also becomes clear on the conjoined element being omitted, i.e. and what makes you know of your not believing when the signs come, or of its occurrence? For the outcome of your affair is hidden from you, so how do you swear to believe upon the coming of the signs? It is only problematic if we make «أنَّ» governed by «يُشْعركم» and make «لا» negating, not redundant, since the meaning would be: and what makes you know, O polytheists, of the absence of your faith when they come to you? This difficulty is removed by [taking] the meaning as: what thing makes you know of your not believing when the signs you proposed come to you? Meaning: this does not cross your minds; rather you are certain of believing upon their coming, with nothing to turn you away from it, while I know that you will not believe at the time of their coming, because your hearts are sealed.
As for the reading with the third person, the hamza with it is with kasra — the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim — and with fatḥa — the reading of Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim.
On the reading of Ibn Kathīr and those with him, two aspects are permissible regarding the address in «وما يشعركم». One of them: that it is an address to the believers, i.e. and what makes you know, O believers, their faith? Then He began afresh, informing about them that they will not believe, so do not hope for their faith. The second: that it is to the disbelievers, i.e. and what makes you know, O polytheists, what will come from you? Then He began afresh, informing about them of the absence of faith because of His prior knowledge of them; on this view there is iltifāt (a shift) in the speech from address to the third person.
On the reading of Nāfiʿ, the address is to the disbelievers, and «أنَّ» is in the sense of laʿalla [Translator's note: the source has «بمنى», a misprint for «بمعنى»]; so said Abū Shāma and others.
The Shaykh said regarding this reading: "The apparent view is that the address is to the believers, and the meaning is: and what makes you know, O believers, that the sign you propose, when it comes, they will not believe?" — meaning: I know that when it comes they will not believe in it. Then he quoted exactly the words of al-Zamakhsharī that I mentioned from him in the fifth aspect, and said: "It is very far-fetched that the address in «وما يشعركم» should be to the disbelievers." I say: he only considered it far-fetched because he did not hold that this «أنَّ» is in the sense of laʿalla, as I related from him. The Shaykh made, for the whole of {أَنَّهَآ إِذَا جَآءَتْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}, with respect to kasra and fatḥa of the hamza and address and third person, four readings. He said: "Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, al-ʿUlaymī and al-Aʿshā from Abū Bakr read …; and Ibn/ ʿAṭiyya said: 'Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Dāwūd al-Iyādī: «إنها» with kasra of the hamza, and the rest of the Seven read it with fatḥa; and Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamza read «لا تؤمنون» with the tāʾ of address, and the rest with the yāʾ of the third person.' So four readings result. The first: kasra of the hamza and the yāʾ; it is the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Abū Bakr with disagreement from him regarding the kasra of the hamza." Then he said: "The second reading: kasra of the hamza and the tāʾ; it is the transmission of al-ʿUlaymī and al-Aʿshā from Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim. What is fitting is that the address in this reading be to the disbelievers, as if it were said: and what makes you know, O disbelievers, what will come from you? Then He informed them decisively that they will not believe on the supposition of its coming. It is very far-fetched that the address in «وما يُشْعركم» be to the believers and in «تؤمنون» to the disbelievers." Then he mentioned the third reading [and the fourth]. [In this there is] an evident objection [Translator's note: the source text reads «ثم ذكر القراءة الثالثة نظرٌ لا يخفى», which appears to have lost some words; it is rendered according to its evident sense]: when he related the reading with address in «تؤمنون», he related it only from Ḥamza and Ibn ʿĀmir, and did not include Abū Bakr with them, either by way of al-ʿUlaymī and al-Aʿshā or by any other way. And it is given that Ḥamza and Ibn ʿĀmir read the hamza of «أنها» with fatḥa, and Abū Bakr reads it with kasra and fatḥa but reads «يؤمنون» only with the yāʾ of the third person. So whence would we get a reading with kasra of the hamza and address? I have brought his words in their entirety only so that the point taken against him may be known. Then I allowed that this might be a transmission he had related, so I examined his book on the readings — he had devoted in it a section to what al-ʿUlaymī was alone in transmitting — and he did not mention at all that he read «تؤمنون» with address. Then I examined numerous books on the readings, and did not see them mention that. So I knew that when he saw two states for the hamza and two states for the imperfect prefix in «يؤمنون», he multiplied two by two and four readings came out of it — but one of them is unattested.
And His words «لا يُؤْمنون»: what it is attached to is omitted because it is known, i.e. they will not believe in them.
His words: {ونُقَلِّب}: In this clause there are two aspects. One of them — and al-Zamakhsharī said nothing else — is that it, and what is conjoined to it, namely His words «وَيذَرُهم», are conjoined to «يُؤْمنون», falling under the ruling of «وما يُشْعركم», in the sense: "and what makes you know that they will not believe, and what makes you know that We turn their hearts and their eyes, and what makes you know that We leave them." This is supported by what came in the exegesis from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd. The second: that it is a fresh statement; the Shaykh made it the apparent view, but the apparent view is what preceded.

semin-durr:110-110.t:
And al-afʾida: the plural of fuʾād, which is the heart; it is also applied to the intellect. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-fuʾād is like al-qalb, but it is called fuʾād when the sense of tafaʾʾud, i.e. burning (tawaqqud), is regarded in it; one says: faʾadtu al-laḥm, I roasted the meat, and from it laḥm faʾīd, i.e. roasted." The apparent sense of this is that al-fuʾād is other than al-qalb. It is also said fuwād with a pure wāw, which is a substitute for the hamza, because it is an analogical lightening; Warsh reads it so, in it and its parallels, in connection and in pause, and Ḥamza in pause. It is pluralised as afʾida, an analogical plural like ghurāb and aghriba; and afyida, with a yāʾ after the hamza, is permissible — Hishām read it so in Sūrat Ibrāhīm, and it will come.
His words: {كَمَا لَمْ يُؤْمِنُواْ}: The kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and «ما» is maṣdariyya. The implied form, as Abū al-Baqāʾ said, is: a turning like their disbelief, a punishment equal to their disobedience. Al-Ḥawfī implied it as: they will not believe in it with a firm faith, just as they did not believe in it the first time. And it was said: the kāf here is for causation, i.e. We turn their hearts and their eyes because of their not believing in it the first time. And it was said: there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: so they will not believe in it a second time, just as they did not believe in it the first time. Some exegetes said: "The kāf here means requital (mujāzāt), i.e. since they did not believe in it the first time, We requite them by turning their hearts away from guidance and sealing their hearts; it is as if it were said: and We turn their hearts in requital for their not believing in it the first time"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It is the meaning of causation we mentioned, except that his calling it 'requital' is strange and not familiar in the speech of the grammarians." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya was preceded to this expression. Al-Wāḥidī said: "Some said: the meaning of the kāf in {كَمَا لَمْ يُؤْمِنُواْ} is the meaning of requital, and the meaning of the verse is: and We turn their hearts and their eyes as a punishment for them for abandoning faith the first time." The hāʾ in «به» refers back to Allah the Exalted, or to His Messenger, or to the Qur'an, or to the turning indicated by the verb, and that is the most far-fetched of them./ And «أول مرة» is accusative as an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān); its verification has preceded.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī read «ويُقَلِّب ويَذَرُهم» with the yāʾ, the agent being the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted. Al-Aʿmash read: «وتُقَلَّبُ أفئدتهم وأبصارهم» in the passive, with what follows in the nominative as standing in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil) — so al-Zamakhsharī related it from him, though the one well known for this reading is likewise al-Nakhaʿī — and «ويذرهم» was related from him with the yāʾ of the third person, as preceded, and with sukūn of the rāʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ explained this sukūn in two ways. One of them: the sukūn is because of the succession of vowels. The second: that it is jussive, conjoined to «يؤمنوا», "and the meaning is: a requital for their disbelief, and that He did not leave them in their transgression but made things clear to them." This second one is not apparent. And «يَعْمَهون» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a second object, because leaving (tark) here is in the sense of making into (taṣyīr).

semin-durr:123-123.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وكذلك جَعَلْنَا}: it was said: «كذلك» is conjoined to the «كذلك» before it, so what applies to that applies to this. Al-Zamakhsharī gave its implied meaning as: "Just as We placed in Mecca its chiefs so that they might plot in it, so We placed in every town the greatest of its criminals." The lām in «ليمكروا» may be for consequence (ʿāqiba), or for cause, figuratively. «جَعَلَ» is of transformation (taṣyīr), so it takes two objects, and there is disagreement on how to identify them. The correct view is that {فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ} is the second object placed before the first, and the first is «أكابرَ», annexed to «مجرميها». The second: that {فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ} is also an object placed first, «أكابر» is the first, and «مجرميها» is a badal (substitute) for «أكابر»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this. The third: that «أكابر» is a second object placed first and «مجرميها» is a first object placed after, the implied form being: "We made the criminals in every town the greatest", so the preposition and its noun are attached to the verb itself before them; Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned this.

The Shaykh said: "What these two" — meaning Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya — "permitted is a mistake and an oversight of a grammatical rule, namely: afʿal of preference, when it is with «مِنْ» expressed or implied, or annexed to an indefinite, is singular and masculine in every case, whether it is for a masculine or a feminine, a singular, a dual or a plural; and when it is put in the dual or plural or feminine, it agrees with what it is for, and one of two things is then necessary for it: either the definite article, or annexation to a definite noun. Once that is established, the opinion that «مجرميها» is a badal, or that it is a first object and «أكابر» a second object, is a mistake, because it entails «أكابر» remaining plural without the definite article and without being annexed to a definite noun." He said: "Al-Kirmānī was aware of this rule, for he said: 'He annexed «أكابر» to «مجرميها» because afʿal is not put in the plural except with the definite article or with annexation.'" The Shaykh said: "He should have qualified it as annexation to a definite noun."

I say: as for this rule, it is conceded; but Makkī mentioned exactly what Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned, and I think he [Ibn ʿAṭiyya] took it only from him. Likewise al-Wāḥidī too, and he refused to allow the annexation of «أكابر» to «مجرميها». He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The verse involves a fronting and a postponing, its implied form being: We made its criminals the greatest. It is not permissible for الأكابر to be annexed, because the meaning would not be complete, and it would need an implied second object for «الجعل», since if you say «جعلت زيداً» ('I made Zayd') and stop, the speech is not informative until you say: a chief, or a guide, or the like; and because if you annex الأكابر, you will have annexed the adjective to the noun it qualifies, and that is not permissible according to the Basrans." I say: these two arguments by which al-Wāḥidī rejected it are nothing. As for the first, we do not concede that we imply the second object and that the speech becomes uninformative; and the examples he adduced are not analogous, because we say that the second object here is mentioned explicitly / — namely the preceding preposition and its genitive noun.

As for the second, we do not concede that it is of the category of annexing an adjective to the noun it qualifies, because criminals are great and small; so he annexed it for clarification, not with the intent of qualification.

The fourth: that the second object is omitted. They said: its implied form is: "We made in every town the greatest of its criminals transgressors, so that they might plot". This is nothing, because nothing is omitted except on evidence, and the evidence for what they mentioned is not clear. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "And one says أكابِرَة, just as one says أحمر and أحامرة." The poet said:

2048 - إن الأحامرة الثلاثة أتلفتْ ... ما لي وكنت بهنَّ قِدْماً مُوْلَعا
(The three red things have consumed my wealth, and of old I was infatuated with them.)

The Shaykh said: "I know of no one who permitted أفاضلة as the plural of أفضل; rather the grammarians stated explicitly that afʿal of preference forms its masculine plural as الأَفْضَلِين or الأفاضل." I say: the grammarians mention this tāʾ [on the grounds] that it indicates lineage in such a pattern; they said: الأزارقة and الأشاعثة, for al-Azraq and his clan and al-Ashʿath and his sons. It is not regular, and this [i.e. أكابرة] has nothing to do with that. The majority read «أكابر» as a plural. Ibn Muslim read: «أكبر مجرميها» in the singular, and that is permissible, because afʿal of preference, when annexed to a definite noun and meant for other than the singular masculine, may agree, as in the well-known reading here, and in the ḥadīth: «أحاسنكم أخلاقا» ("the best of you in character"); and it may be singular, and there is consensus on that in His saying: {وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ أَحْرَصَ الناس} [al-Baqara: 96].

semin-durr:124-124.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ}: there are two views about this «حيث». The first: that it has left adverbial use and become a direct object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), and the governing word is not this «أعلم», because, as stated earlier, afʿal does not put a direct object in the accusative. Abū ʿAlī said: "It is not permissible for the governing word of «حيث» to be this overt «أعلم», and it is not permissible for «حيث» to be an adverb, because the implied form would become: Allah is most knowing in this place; and Allah the Exalted is not described as being most knowing in some places and times, since His knowledge does not vary with the variation of places and times. That being so, the governing word of «حيث» is a verb indicated by «أعلم», and «حيث» is not an adverb but a noun, and its accusative is as a direct object by extension. Like this, in the accusative of «حيث» as a direct object by extension, is the saying of al-Shammākh:

2049 - وحَلأَّها عن ذي الأراكةِ عامرٌ ... أخو الخُضْرِ يَرْمي حيث تُكْوى النواحِزُ
(ʿĀmir, brother of the Khuḍr, drove them away from Dhū al-Arāka, shooting at the spot where the coughing camels are cauterised.)

So «حيث» is an object, because he does not mean that he shoots something at the place where the coughing camels are; he only means that he shoots at that very spot." People followed al-Fārisī in this opinion. Al-Ḥūfī said: "It is not an adverb, because He, Exalted is He, is not more knowing in one place than in another place; and if it is not an adverb, it is a direct object by extension; and if it is an object, «أعلم» does not govern it, because «أعلم» does not govern a direct object, so a verb is implied for it." The wording of Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ is similar to this. Al-Tibrīzī took al-Fārisī's words, transmitted them and cited the verse given above.

The second: that it remains an adverb by way of figurative usage. This opinion is nothing, but the Shaykh permitted it, preferring it, according to what preceded. He said: "What they permitted — that it is a direct object by extension, or a direct object not by extension — is refused by the rules of grammar, because the grammarians stated explicitly that «حيث» is among the adverbs that are not inflectionally versatile (lā tataṣarraf); the annexation of «لدى» to it and its being made genitive by the bāʾ and by «في» are irregular; and they stated explicitly that an adverb used by extension can only be a versatile one. That being so, it is impossible to make «حيث» accusative as a direct object, whether by extension or otherwise.

What appears to me is to keep «حيث» as a figurative adverb, on the basis that «أعلم» is made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of something that reaches an adverb, so the implied form is: Allah is most penetrating in knowledge where He places His messages, i.e. He is penetrating in knowledge in the place in which He places His messages; and the adverb here is figurative, as we said." I say: he has abandoned what the majority said and followed one after another, and interpreted something graver than what the majority fled from. For it follows, on what he implied, that Allah's knowledge in itself varies in relation to places, so that it is more far-reaching in one place than in another; and his claim of figurative adverbial use does not help him against the problem I have mentioned. How can such a thing be said? And his saying "the grammarians stated explicitly that it is not versatile" is also countered by the fact that they stated explicitly that it may be used versatilely in ways other than what he mentioned of its being made genitive by «لدى», «إلى» or «في». Among them: it occurred as the noun of «إنّ» in the poet's saying:

2050 - إنَّ حيث استقرَّ مَنْ أنت راجي ... هِ حِمَىً فيه عزةٌ وأمانُ
(The place where the one you place your hope in has settled is a sanctuary in which there is might and safety.)

So «حيث» is the noun of «إنّ» and «حمى» its khabar (predicate), i.e. the place in which the one you tend [Translator's note: the source reads «راعيه» here, whereas the verse has «راجيه», "the one you hope in"] has settled is a place in which might and safety are protected. And of its occurring genitive with «إلى» is his saying:

2051 - فشدَّ ولم يَنْظر بيوتاً كثيرة ... إلى حيث أَلْقَتْ رَحْلَها أَمُّ قَشْعَمِ
(He charged without waiting for many houses, to where the mother of Qashʿam [i.e. death] had cast down her saddle.)

The problem that I raised against him may be answered by saying that he did not intend preference by his saying «أنفذ علماً», even though that is the apparent sense, but intended mere description; what shows this is his saying: "i.e. He is penetrating in knowledge in the place in which He places His messages". But he ought to have stated this explicitly by saying: and preference is not intended. «حيثَ يجعل» has been transmitted with fatḥa on the thāʾ, and this admits two possibilities. The first: that it is a fatḥa of indeclinability (bināʾ), for regularity of the pattern. The second: that it is a fatḥa of declension (iʿrāb), because it is declinable in the dialect of Banū Faqʿas; al-Kisāʾī reported this.

Ibn Kathīr, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, read «رسالته» in the singular, and the rest «رسالاته» in the plural. The rationale of that was given in al-Māʾida, except that some of those who read the plural there — namely Ḥafṣ — read the singular here, and some of those who read the singular there — namely Abū ʿAmr, the two brothers, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim — read the plural here.

His saying: {عِندَ الله} may be accusative by «يصيب», and it may be accusative by «صَغار», because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). They also permitted it to be an adjective of «صَغار», so it is attached to something omitted; al-Zajjāj gave its implied form as: "established with Allah". Al-ṣaghār is abasement and humiliation. One says of it: صَغُر يَصْغُر صُغْراً وصَغْراً وصَغاراً, so he is ṣāghir (abased). As for the opposite of bigness, one says of it: صَغَر يَصْغَر صِغْراً, so he is ṣaghīr (small). This is the opinion of al-Layth; so the difference between the two meanings falls in the maṣdar and the verb. Others said that both صَغُر and صغَر are said of abasement.

The "with-ness" (ʿindiyya) here is figurative, for their being gathered on the Day of Resurrection, or for His judgement and decree of that, as when you say: «ثبت عند فلان القاضي» ("it was established with so-and-so the judge"), i.e. in his ruling. For that reason He put the abasement before the punishment, because it befalls them in this world. In «بما كانوا» the bāʾ is causal and «ما» is maṣdariyya; it may also be in the sense of «الذي» (that which).

semin-durr:94-94.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فرادى}: in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «جئتمونا». In «جئتمونا» there are two aspects. One: it has the sense of the future, i.e. "you will come to Us," and it was only presented in the form of the past because of its certainty, as in the words of Allah the Exalted {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1] and {ونادى أَصْحَابُ الجنة} [al-Aʿrāf: 44]. The second: it is a past, and what is meant by it is the narration of the state before Allah the Exalted on the day this is said to them; on that day their coming is past relative to that day.
People differed about «فُرادى»: is it a plural or not? Those who say it is a plural differed about its singular. Al-Farrāʾ said: "«فُرادى» is the plural of «فَرْد», «فريد», «فَرِد» and «فَرْدان»," so he allowed it to be the plural of these things. Ibn Qutayba said: "It is the plural of «فَرْدان», like «سَكْران» and «سُكارى», and «عَجلان» and «عُجالى»." Some said: it is the plural of «فريد», like «رديف» and «رُدَافى», and «أسير» and «أُسارى»; al-Rāghib said this. It is said: it is the plural of «فَرَد» with fatḥa on the rāʾ, and it is said: with sukūn on it. On this view its alif is for the feminine, like the alif of «سُكارى» and «أُسارى», and that is why it is diptote. It is also said: it is a quasi-plural (ism jamʿ), because «فَرْد» is not pluralised as «فُرادى»; and whoever said it is its plural only means in meaning. The meaning of «فُرادى» is "one by one"; when you say «جاء القوم فُرادى», it means "one by one." The poet said:
1987 - ترى النَُعَراتِ الزُّرْقَ تحت لَبانِه ... فُرادى ومثنى أَثْقَلَتْهَا صواهِلُهْ
(You see the blue gadflies under its breast, singly and in pairs; its neighing has weighed them down.)
One says «فَرِد يَفْرُد فُروداً فهو فارِدٌ» ("he was alone … so he is alone"), and «أفردته أنا» ("I singled him out"); and «رجل أفرد» and «امرأة فرداء», like «أحمر» and «حمراء»; the plural on this view is «فُرْد», like «حُمْر». One also says, instead of «فرادى», «فُراد» on the pattern fuʿāl, which is triptote; this is the dialect of Tamīm, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Abū Ḥaywa read with it: {ولقد جِئْتُمونا فُرَاداً}. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It has been read anomalously (fī al-shādhdh) with tanwīn, as a sound noun; in the nominative one says «فُراد», like «نُوام» and «رُجال», and it is a rare plural." End of quotation. One also says «جاء القوم فُرادَ», diptote, so it is like «أُحاد» and «رُباع» in being a deflected (maʿdūl) adjective; this is an anomalous reading here. Khārija related from both Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr that they read «فَرْدى», like «سَكْرى», with regard to the femininity of the group, as in the words of Allah the Exalted {وَتَرَى الناس سكرى وَمَا هُم بسكرى} [al-Ḥajj: 2]. So these are four readings: the well-known «فرادى», and three anomalous ones: «فُراداً» like «رُجال», «فُرادَ» like «أُحادَ», and «فَرْدَى» like «سكرى».
His words: {كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ}: there are several aspects concerning this kāf. The first: its position is accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «جئتمونا». Those who allow multiple ḥāls allow that without reinterpretation, and those who forbid it make the kāf a badal (substitute) from «فُرادى». The second: it is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "[your] coming to Us like your coming on the day We created you." Makkī gave the implied form as: "being alone with an aloneness like your state the first time." The first is better, because the verb's indication of the maṣdar is stronger than the adjective's indication of it. The third: the kāf is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in «فرادى», i.e. "resembling the beginning of your creation"; so Abū al-Baqāʾ gave its implied form. This is open to consideration, because they were not likened to the beginning of their creation; the correct way is to imply a muḍāf, i.e. "your state resembling the state of the beginning of your creation."
His words: {أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ}: in the accusative as an adverb of time, and its governing word is «خلقناكم». «مرة» is originally a maṣdar of «مرَّ يَمُرُّ مَرَّة» ("to pass"); then its usage was extended and it became a [word of] time. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This shows the strength of the resemblance of time to the verb." The Shaykh said: "«أول مرة» is in the accusative as an adverb, i.e. the first time; it is not to be implied as 'the first creating,' because a first creating calls for a second creating, and He does not create a second time; that is only restoration, not creation." That is, «المرة» cannot keep its basic maṣdar sense with the implied form "the first instance of creation," for the reason he mentioned.
His words: {وَتَرَكْتُمْ}: there are two aspects concerning it. One: it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «جِئْتُمونا», with «قد» implied according to one view, i.e. «وقد تركتم». The second: it has no grammatical position because it is resumptive. «ما» is the object of «ترك»; and «مَنْ» [Translator's note: so in the text; «ما» is evidently meant] is a nominal relative, and making it a qualified indefinite is weak; the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. «ما خوَّلْناكموه» ("what We conferred on you"). «ترك» here takes one object [Translator's note: printed «لواجد», for «لواحد»], because it means "leaving"; if it were made to include the meaning of «صيَّر» ("to make into"), it would take two. «خَوَّل» takes two objects, because it means "to give" and "to grant possession."
«الخَوَل» is what Allah has given of blessings. Abū al-Najm said:
1988 - كُومُ الذُّرَى من خَوَلِ المُخَوَّلِ ...
(…high-humped [camels], from the bounty of the One who bestows bounty.)
So the meaning of «خَوَّلْته كذا» is "I gave him possession of the khawal in it," like their saying «مَوَّلته», i.e. "I gave him possession of wealth." Al-Rāghib said: "«التخويل» originally means giving khawal; and it is said: giving what becomes khawal for him; and it is said: giving what needs to be looked after, from their saying «فلانٌ خالُ مالٍ» and «خائل مال», i.e. good at tending it."
His words: {وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِكُمْ} is attached to «تَرَكْتُم». «ترك» here may also be made to include the meaning of «صَيَّر», so that it takes two objects, the first being the relative noun and the second this adverb, which is then attached to an omitted [word], i.e. "and you made the thing left, which We conferred on you, to be behind your backs."
His words: {وَمَا نرى}: the apparent sense is that it is the one taking one object, so it is visual; on this view «معكم» is attached to «نرى». It may also mean "to know," so that it takes two objects, the second of which is the adverb, which is then attached to an omitted [word], i.e. "We do not see them [to be] with you," i.e. accompanying you. However, Abū al-Baqāʾ considered this aspect weak, and it is as he said, since the meaning would become "and your intercessors with you are not known," and that is certainly not the meaning. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And «معكم» cannot be a ḥāl from «الشفعاء», since the meaning would become that their intercessors are with them and We do not see them." What he said is evidently open to consideration. That is because when negation enters upon an entity with a qualification, there are two possibilities. One: negation of that entity with its qualification. The second: negation of the qualification only, without negating the entity. When you say «ما رأيت زيداً ضاحكاً» ("I did not see Zayd laughing"), it may be that you did not see Zayd at all, and it may be that you saw him without laughing. So also here, since the implied form is "and We do not see your intercessors accompanying you": it may be that they did not see the intercessors at all, and it may be that they saw them without their accompanying them. So from where does it follow from this construction that they are with them and they do not see them? The verification of this rule was given early in al-Baqara and at His words
{لاَ يَسْأَلُونَ الناس إِلْحَافاً} [al-Baqara: 273].
«أنهم» fills the place of the two objects of «زعم». «فيكم» is attached to «شركاء» itself. The meaning is: "those whom you claimed were partners of Allah in you," i.e. in your worship or in your creation, because you associated them with Allah in your worship and your creation. It is said that «في» means «عند» ("with"), but there is no need for that. It is also said: the meaning is that they bear for you a share of the punishment, i.e. partners in your punishment, since you used to believe of them that if a calamity befell you they would share it with you.
His words: «بينكم»: Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Ḥafṣ from him read «بينَكم» in the accusative, and the rest «بينُكم» in the nominative. In the first reading there are seven aspects. The best of them: the fāʿil is an implied pronoun referring to "the connection." Although the connection has not been mentioned so that a pronoun could refer to it, something indicating it has preceded, namely the word «شركاء», for partnership suggests connection. The meaning is: "the connection between you has been cut off," so «بينكم» is in the accusative as an adverb. The second: the fāʿil is «بينكم», and it only stayed in its accusative state by being construed according to its most frequent states; this is the doctrine of al-Akhfash. They also counted among such cases His words {يُفَصَلُ بَيْنَكُمْ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 3] in the reading of those who made it passive, and likewise the words of Allah the Exalted {وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَلِكَ} [al-Jinn: 11]. Al-Wāḥidī said: "Just as it ran in their speech in the accusative as an adverb, they left it as it is in most speech." Then he said: "In His words «ومنَّا دون ذلك», «دون» is in the position of a nominative according to him, even though it is accusative in wording; do you not see that you say «منا الصالحون ومنا الطالحون» ('among us are the righteous and among us the wicked')?"
However, when people reported this doctrine they did not address the indeclinability (bināʾ) of this adverb; rather they stated explicitly that it is declinable, in the accusative, and nominative in position. They said: it only remained in the accusative out of regard for its most frequent states. In the Shaykh's words, when he reported al-Akhfash's doctrine, there is something stating explicitly that it is indeclinable, for he said: "Al-Akhfash explained it as being the fāʿil, but indeclinable, by being construed according to most of the states of this adverb." This is open to consideration, because that is not fit to be a cause of indeclinability, and the causes of indeclinability are limited, and this is not among them. Then the Shaykh said: "It may be said [that it is indeclinable] because of its being in construct with an indeclinable, as in His words {وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَلِكَ} [al-Jinn: 11]." This is clear in that he made its being construed according to most of its states a cause of its indeclinability, as stated.
The third: the fāʿil is omitted, and «بينكم» is an adjective of it standing in its place, the implied form being: "a connection between you has been cut off"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The Shaykh rejected it on the grounds that the fāʿil is not omitted; but this is no refutation of him, for by omission he means its not being mentioned in wording, while something stands in its place, so it is as though it were not omitted.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The verb is attributed to something omitted, i.e. the connection between you, and the bond, and the like, has been cut off." This is a clear aspect, and people interpreted it accordingly. The Shaykh rejected it with what has been said. It may be answered that he expressed implication (iḍmār) with [the word] omission, because neither of them is present in wording. The fourth: «بينَكم» is the fāʿil, and it was only made indeclinable because of its being in construct with an uninflectable (ghayr mutamakkin) word, as in the words of Allah the Exalted {إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 23], where «مثل» has fatḥa while it follows «حق», which is nominative; but it was made indeclinable because of its being in construct with an uninflectable word. This will come in its place. Like it is the saying of the other:
1989 - تَتَداعى مَنْخِراه بدَمٍ ... مثلَ ما أثمرَ حُمَّاضُ الجَبَلْ
(His nostrils pour forth blood, like what the mountain sorrel has borne [i.e. red].)
with fatḥa on «مثل», although it follows «دمٍ». And like it is the saying of the other:
1990 - لم يمنعِ الشُّربَ منها غيرَ أَنْ نطقَتْ ... حمامةٌ في غصونٍ ذاتِ أوقال
(Nothing prevented [her] from drinking from it except that a dove cooed among branches with heavy fruit.)
with fatḥa on «غير», though it is the fāʿil of «يمنع». And like it is the saying of al-Nābigha:
1991 - أتاني أبيتَ اللعنَ أنك لُمْتني ... وتلك التي تَسْتَكُّ منها المسامعُ
مقالةَ أَنْ قد قلتَ سوف أنالُه ... وذلك مِنْ تلقاء مثلِك رائِعُ
(It reached me—may you refuse curse—that you blamed me, and that is something from which the ears are deafened: the statement that you said "I shall get him," and that, coming from one like you, is alarming.)
«مقالة» is a badal from «أنك لمتني», which is a fāʿil, and the transmission is with fatḥa on the tāʾ of «مقالة», because of its being in construct with «أَنْ» and what is in its scope.
The fifth: the question belongs to the topic of iʿmāl (competition of governing words), since «تَقَطَّع» and «ضَلَّ» both bear on «ما كنتمْ تزعُمون», each of them requiring it as fāʿil. So the question may be one of giving government to the second, or of giving government to the first, because there is no contextual indication here that determines that. However, you have learned from what preceded that the doctrine of the Basrans is to prefer giving government to the second, and the doctrine of the Kufans the reverse; this was set out in al-Baqara. On the Basrans' preference, «ضَلَّ» is what puts «ما كنتم تزعمون» in the nominative [Translator's note: printed «الرفع», for «الرافع»], and the first needed a fāʿil, so we gave it its pronoun, which is latent in it. On the Kufans' preference, «تقطَّع» is what puts «ما كنتم تزعمون» in the nominative, and in «ضلَّ» there is its pronoun as fāʿil. On both views «بينكم» is in the accusative as an adverb, governed by «تقطَّع».
The sixth: the adverb is the ṣila (relative clause) of an omitted relative noun, its implied form being «تقطع ما بينكم» ("what was between you has been cut off"); the relative noun, namely «ما», was omitted. It has been stated that this is the view of the Kufans, and what they cited in support of it from the Quran and the verses of the Arabs has been given. The proponent of that cited the poet's saying:
1992 - يُدِيرونني عن سالمٍ وأُديرُهمْ ... وجِلْدَةُ بين الأنف والعينِ سالمُ
(They try to turn me away from Sālim, and I turn them away—Sālim is [to me] the skin between the nose and the eye.)
and the saying of the other:
1993 - ما بين عَوْفٍ وإبراهيمَ مِنْ نَسَبٍ ... إلا قرابةُ بين الزنج والرومِ
(There is no kinship between ʿAwf and Ibrāhīm except the kinship between the Zanj and the Byzantines.)
the implied form being «وجلدة ما بين» and «إلا قرابة ما بين». This is indicated by the reading of ʿAbd Allah [ibn Masʿūd], Mujāhid and al-Aʿmash: {لقد تقطَّع ما بينكم}.
The seventh: al-Zamakhsharī said: "«لقد تقطع بينكم»: the cutting has occurred between you, as you say «جمع بين الشيئين», meaning he effected the joining between them; [this is] on the basis of attributing the verb to its own maṣdar with this interpretation." End of quotation. His saying "with this interpretation" is a good statement, because if the pronoun of the maṣdar understood from «تقطع» were implied in it, the implied form would become "the cutting was cut between you," and if the cutting were cut between them, connection would result, which is the opposite of what is intended; so he needed to say that the verb was attributed to its maṣdar with the interpretation mentioned. However, the Shaykh objected, saying: "Its apparent sense is not good. Put precisely: he attributed the verb to the pronoun of its maṣdar, implying it in it, because if he attributed it to the explicit maṣdar, it would be omitted, and omission of the fāʿil is not permissible. And even with this implied form it is not correct, because the condition of attribution (isnād) is lacking in it, namely that the judgement and the thing judged be different." He means that the verb and the agent may not be identical in one word without benefit; you do not say «قام القائم» ("the stander stood") or «قعد القاعد». So you say: when the verb is attributed to its maṣdar—if to its explicit maṣdar without implication, omission of the fāʿil follows; and if to its pronoun, there remains "the cutting was cut," which is like «قام القائم», and that is not permissible; besides which, corruption of the meaning also follows from it, as stated, namely that it entails their attaining connection. This objection the Shaykh raised, which I have set out from his words so that it is understood, does not apply, because of al-Zamakhsharī's statement mentioned earlier, "on the basis of attributing the verb to its maṣdar with this interpretation"; and that interpretation has been given.
As for the second reading, there are three aspects in it. The first: the usage of this adverb was extended, and the verb was attributed to it, so it became a noun like other freely declined nouns. This is indicated by the words of Allah the Exalted {وَمِن بَيْنِنَا وَبَيْنِكَ حِجَابٌ} [Fuṣṣilat: 5], where He used it in the genitive with «مِنْ», and the words of Allah the Exalted {فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنِكَ} [al-Kahf: 78], {مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا} [al-Kahf: 61] and {شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 106]. Sībawayh reported: «هو أحمر بين العينين» ("he is red between the eyes"). ʿAntara said:
1994 - وكأنما أَقِصُ الإِكامَ عشيةً ... بقريب بينِ المَنْسِمَيْنِ مُصَلَّمِ
(It is as though in the evening I crush the hillocks with one [i.e. an ostrich] whose two toes are close together, with clipped ears.)
And Muhalhil said:
1995 - كأنَّ رماحَنا أشطانُ بئرٍ ... بعيدةِ بين جالَيْها جَرُورِ
(As though our spears were the ropes of a well, wide between its two sides, deep.)
So in all these places it was used as a muḍāf ilayhi and freely declined; so here too. And like it his saying:
1996 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وجِلْدَةُ بين الأنف والعين سالم
(…and Sālim is [to me] the skin between the nose and the eye.)
and his saying:
1997 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... إلا قرابةُ بين الزنج والروم
(…except the kinship between the Zanj and the Byzantines.)
and his saying:
1998 - ولم يَتْرك النبلُ المُخالِفُ بينها ... أخاً لاح [قد] يُرْجى وما ثورةُ الهندِ
(And the arrows, crossing between them, did not leave a brother… [Translator's note: the second hemistich is corrupt in the text and its sense is unclear; it is left untranslated.])
It is related with «بينها» in the nominative and with fatḥa, as the fāʿil of «مخالف»; it was only made indeclinable because of its being in construct with an indeclinable. Like it in that respect are «أمام» and «دون», as in his saying:
1999 - فَغَدَتْ كلا الفَرْجَيْنِ تحسب أنَّه ... مَوْلَى المخافةِ خَلْفُها وأمامُها
(So she set off in the morning, thinking each of the two openings to be the place of danger—behind her and before her.)
with «أمام» in the nominative; and his saying:
2000 - ألم تَرَ أني قد حَمَيْتُ حقيقي ... وباشَرْتُ حدَّ الموتِ والموتُ دونُها
(Have you not seen that I protected what I must protect, and met the edge of death, with death before it?)
with «دون» in the nominative.
The second: «بين» is a noun, not an adverb, and its meaning is "connection," i.e. "your connection has been cut off." Then people have, after that, two expressions [Translator's note: so in the text]: one suggesting that «بين» is the maṣdar of «بان يبين بَيْناً» meaning "to be far apart," so that it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād), i.e. homonymous, used for connection and separation, like «الجَوْن» for black and white; this is ascribed to Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Jinnī, al-Mahdawī and al-Zahrāwī. Abū ʿUbayd said: "Abū ʿAmr used to say: the meaning of «تقطَّع بينكم» is 'your connection has been cut off'; so here it became a noun without «ما» being with it." Al-Zajjāj said: "The nominative is better, and its meaning is: your connection has been cut off." So these [scholars] stated without qualification that «بَيْن» means connection, and the basic assumption with unqualified usage is literal meaning.
However, Ibn ʿAṭiyya impugned it and claimed that «البين» meaning connection has not been heard from the Arabs, and that it was only extracted from this verse; or that what is meant by «البين» is separation, and that is figurative for the distant thing, the meaning being: the distance between you has been cut off because of its length, so this was expressed by «البين». I say: the apparent sense of Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words suggests that he understood it to mean connection literally, and then rejected that because it has not been heard from the Arabs. This is not acceptable from him, because Abū ʿAmr, Abū ʿUbayd, Ibn Jinnī, al-Zahrāwī, al-Mahdawī and al-Zajjāj are authorities whose word is accepted. His saying "it was only extracted from this verse" is not granted; rather that is understood from the language of the Arabs, and even if no one but Abū ʿAmr had transmitted it, he would suffice. And his [other] expression suggests that it is figurative. The reasoning of the figure, as al-Fārisī said, is: "Since «بين» was used with two things in contact, as in «بيني وبينك شركَةٌ» ('between me and you is a partnership') and «بيني وبينك رحم وصداقة» ('between me and you is kinship and friendship'), it came, through its use in these places, to mean the bond, the opposite of separation; therefore 'your connection has been cut off' came." Once this is established, saying it is figurative is preferable to saying it is homonymous, because whenever homonymy and figurative usage conflict, the figurative is better according to the majority.
Abū ʿAlī also said: "What shows that this nominative is the one that was used as an adverb is that it must be either the adverb whose usage was extended, or the one that is a maṣdar; and it cannot be this [latter] category, because the implied form would become 'your separation has been cut off,' and this is contrary to the purpose and the meaning; do you not see that what is meant is your connection and what you were united upon? If you ask: how can it mean connection when its origin is separation and distinctness? It is answered: since it was used with two things in contact, as in «بيني وبينك شركة»…"—and he mentioned what I gave above from him about the reasoning of the figure, to the end.
Abū ʿUbayd, al-Zajjāj and a group approved the nominative reading. Abū ʿUbayd said: "Likewise we read it in the nominative, because we have found the Arabs making «بين» a noun without «ما»; this is confirmed by the words of Allah the Exalted {بَلَغَا مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا} [al-Kahf: 61], where He made «بين» a noun without «ما», and likewise His words
{هذا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنِكَ} [al-Kahf: 78]." He said: "And we have heard it in more than one place in their poetry." Then he mentioned what I mentioned from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ. Then he said: "Al-Kisāʾī read it in the accusative, and he used to take as his reference the reading of ʿAbd Allah: «لقد تقطع ما بينكم»." Al-Zajjāj said: "The nominative is better and the accusative is permissible; the meaning is: what partnership there was between you has been cut off." The third: this is speech construed according to its meaning, since the meaning is "your gathering has been dispersed and scattered"; but this is not fit to be an explanation of the parsing.
His words: {مَّا كُنتُمْ}: «ما» may be a nominal relative, a qualified indefinite, or maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya). The referent pronoun on the first two aspects is omitted, unlike the third. The implied form is "you claimed them to be partners" or "intercessors"; so the referent pronoun is the first object and «شركاء» is the second. So both objects are omitted for brevity (ikhtiṣāran), because they are indicated, if we say that «ما» is a nominal relative or a qualified indefinite. And the omission may be an omission of restriction (iqtiṣāran) if we say it is maṣdar-forming, because the maṣdar-forming one does not need a referent pronoun, unlike the others, which require a referent pronoun, so it must be taken into account, and then implying the second object is necessary. Of omission for brevity is his saying:
2001 - بأيِّ كتابٍ أم بأية سنةٍ ... ترى حبَّهم عاراً علي وتحسبُ
(By what scripture, or by what sunna, do you consider loving them a shame upon me, and reckon [it so]?)
i.e. "and you reckon loving them a shame upon me."

semin-durr:125-125.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: {فَمَن يُرِدِ الله أَن يَهْدِيَهُ} is like His saying: {مَن يَشَإِ الله يُضْلِلْهُ} [al-Anʿām: 39]. «مَنْ» may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or accusative by a verb implied after it, by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), i.e. whomever Allah grants success, He wills to guide him. «أن يهديه» is the object of the willing. Al-sharḥ is spreading out and widening; al-Layth said this. Ibn Qutayba said: "It is opening; from it is «شَرَحْتُ اللحم», i.e. I opened [cut open] the meat." «شرحَ الكلامَ» means he spread out the speech and opened what was closed in it; it is a metaphor (istiʿāra) in abstract meanings and literal in concrete things. «للإِسلام» means: for accepting it.

His saying: «يَجْعَلْ» may be the jaʿala of transformation (taṣyīr), or of creation, or in the sense of "to name". This third is what the Muʿtazila resort to, such as al-Fārisī and others of the Muʿtazilī grammarians, because [in their view] Allah does not make or create anyone thus. On the first view, «ضيقاً» is an object, both for those who doubled its yāʾ — the majority, other than Ibn Kathīr — and likewise for those who lightened it with sukūn; it would have two dialectal forms, doubled and light, like ميِّت and مَيْت, and هيِّن and هين. And it was said: the light form is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «ضاق يضيق ضَِيقاً», as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ} [al-Naḥl: 27] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Naḥl 127]. One says: «ضاق يضيق ضَيقاً وضِيقاً», with fatḥa and kasra on the ḍād; Ibn Kathīr read with kasra in al-Naḥl and al-Naml. If it is made a maṣdar, then the three views applying to a maṣdar used as a description of a concrete being, as in «رجل عدل» ("a just man", lit. "a man of justice"), come into it: namely the omission of a muḍāf, or hyperbole, or its standing in the place of an active participle; i.e. He makes his breast possessed of narrowness, or narrowing, or narrowness itself by way of hyperbole. What appears from the reading of Ibn Kathīr is that in his view it is a noun-adjective lightened from the fayʿil pattern; that is because his reading of the maṣdar of this verb stood out [Translator's note: the source has «استغرب قراءته», literally "found his reading strange"; the sense required seems to be that his reading of the maṣdar was distinctive, i.e. with kasra] — not with fatḥa — in Sūrat al-Naḥl and al-Naml; so had this been a maṣdar in his view, the apparent thing in his reading would have been kasra, as in the two places indicated. This is one of the fine points of the science of grammar and the readings. The disagreement found here is also found in al-Furqān. Al-Kisāʾī said: / "الضَّيِّق with the doubling is for bodies, and with the lightening for abstract meanings."

The pattern of ضيّق is fayʿil, like ميّت and سيّد, according to the majority of grammarians; then it was assimilated, and it may be lightened, as was set out earlier. Al-Fārisī said: "The yāʾ is like the wāw in being dropped, even if it does not undergo weakening by change as the wāw did; the yāʾ was made to follow the wāw in this, as it was made to follow in their saying «اتَّسر» from اليسر, and so was treated like اتَّعد." Ibn al-Anbārī said: "Those who double the yāʾ say its pattern, in terms of the verb, is faʿīl, its original being ضَييق on the model of كريم and نبيل. They made the first yāʾ an alif because it was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, inasmuch as they weakened ضاق يضيق; then they dropped the alif because of its sukūn and the sukūn of the yāʾ of faʿīl. They then feared that faʿīl would be confused with faʿl, so they added a yāʾ to the yāʾ by which the structure of the word is completed and by which a distinction arises between faʿīl and faʿl. Those who lightened the yāʾ said: confusion is avoided, because the origin of this word is known, so confidence in knowing it prevents confusion.

The Basrans said: its pattern, in terms of the verb, is fayʿil; the yāʾ was assimilated into the one after it and so doubled; then the lightening came." He said: "Al-Farrāʾ and his companions rejected this against the Basrans, and said: no noun on the pattern fayʿil — meaning with kasra on the middle radical — is known in the speech of the Arabs; only fayʿal — meaning with fatḥa — is known, as in صيقَل and هيكل. Whenever someone claims for a weak noun what is not known in the sound ones, his claim is rejected." I say: the verification of these opinions preceded at His saying: {أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ} [al-Baqara: 19], so let it be consulted there. If we say it is lightened from the doubled form, is the omitted letter the first yāʾ or the second? There is disagreement, parallels of which have passed.

If «يَجْعَل» is in the sense of "creates", then «ضيقاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and if it is in the sense of «سَمَّى» ("names"), it is a second object; and the discussion of it with respect to doubling and lightening and the implied meanings is like the discussion of it first.

حَرَجاً and حَرِجاً, with fatḥa and kasra on the rāʾ: it is that which is increasing in narrowness, so it is more specific than the first; every ḥaraj is narrow but not vice versa. On this view, the forms with fatḥa and with kasra have one meaning; one says: «رجل حَرِج وحَرَج». The poet said:

2052 - لا حَرِجُ الصدرِ ولا عنيفُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Neither narrow of breast nor harsh…)

Al-Farrāʾ said: "In its kasra and its fatḥa it is like الوحَد and الوِحد, الفرَد and الفرِد, and الدَّنَف and الدَّنِف." Al-Zajjāj and al-Fārisī distinguished between them, saying: the one with fatḥa is a maṣdar and the one with kasra is an active participle. Al-Zajjāj said: "Al-ḥaraj is the narrowest narrowness. Whoever says «رجل حرَج» — meaning with fatḥa — means one with ḥaraj in his breast; and whoever says حرِج — meaning with kasra — made it an agent; likewise دنَف and دنِف." Al-Fārisī said: "Whoever gives fatḥa to the rāʾ, it is a description by means of the maṣdar, like قَمَن [Translator's note: the source prints «فَمَن»], حَرَىً, دنَف and the like among the maṣdars used as descriptions; and it is not like بطل, because the active participle in general comes only on faʿil. Whoever reads حَرِجاً — meaning with kasra on the rāʾ — it is like دنِف and فَرِق with kasra on the middle radical." And it was said: الحَرَج with fatḥa is the plural of حَرَجة, like قصبة and قصب, and the form with kasra is an adjective like دَنِف. The origin of the root is intertwining and intense narrowness, for al-ḥaraja is a thicket of salam trees, so intertwined that no one can reach it. Al-ʿAjjāj said:

2053 - عايَنَ حَيَّاً كالحِراج نَعَمُهْ ...
(He beheld a tribe whose livestock were [dense] like thickets.)

الحِراج is the plural of حِرْج, and حِرْج is the plural of حَرَجة. Among the curious things reported is that Ibn ʿAbbās recited this verse and said: "Is there anyone here from Banū Bakr?" A man said: "Yes." He said: "What is al-ḥaraja among you?" He said: "The valley with many trees, dense, with no path through it." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Thus is the heart of the disbeliever." This is the report of ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr. Abū al-Ṣalt al-Thaqafī reported this story at greater length from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb; he said: "ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb recited this verse and said: Find me a man of Banū Kināna, and let him be a herdsman. So they brought him to him, and ʿUmar said to him: Young man, what is al-ḥaraja among you? He said: Al-ḥaraja among us is the tree surrounded by trees, so that neither / grazing animal nor wild beast can reach it.

ʿUmar said: Likewise the heart of the disbeliever: nothing of good reaches it."

Some report this story from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, as though supporting those who read with kasra. He said: "One of ʿUmar's companions recited it to him with kasra, and he said: Find me a man of Kināna who is a herdsman, and let him be of Banū Mudlij. They brought him to him, and he said: Young man, what is the ḥaraja that is among you? He said: A tree that is among the trees which neither grazing animal nor wild beast can reach. He said: Likewise the heart of the disbeliever: nothing of good reaches it." The Shaykh said: "This is an indication — and Allah knows best — of deriving the verb from a concrete noun, like استنوق and استحجر." I say: this has nothing to do with the category of استنوق [Translator's note: the source prints «التنوق»] and استحجر, because this is an independent meaning and an independent, inflectionally versatile root, as in «حَرِجَ يَحْرَج فهو حَرِج وحارج»; unlike those words, whose meaning compels taking them from inert (jāmid) nouns. For the meaning of your saying «استنوق الجمل» is: the camel became like a she-camel; and «استحجر الطين»: the clay became like stone; and we have no root inflected into verb forms from the words الحجر and الناقة. When you say «حَرِج صدرُه», there is no necessity for you to say: it became like a ḥaraja; rather its meaning is: its narrowness increased. As for the comparison drawn by ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, it is to bring out meanings in the moulds of concrete things, for the sake of emphasis in explanation.

Nāfiʿ, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, read «حَرِجاً» with kasra on the rāʾ, and the rest with fatḥa [Translator's note: the source misprints «بتفحها» for «بفتحها»]; both have been explained. On the reading with fatḥa, if it is a maṣdar, the three views given above for its parallels apply to it; and if it is made an adjective, no interpretation is needed.

Its accusative, on both readings, is either as an adjective of «ضيقاً», or as an additional object [of multiple objects]. That is because the abrogating verbs, when they enter on a mubtadaʾ and khabar, leave the two predicates as they were; so just as multiple khabars are permissible — absolutely, or by interpretation — with an explicit mubtadaʾ and khabar, so also with the abrogated ones. You say: «زيدٌ كاتب شاعر فقيه» ("Zayd is a writer, a poet, a jurist"), then you say: «ظننتُ زيداً كاتباً شاعراً فقيهاً», and you say: «زيداً» is the first object, «كاتباً» the second object, «شاعراً» a third object, «فقيهاً» a fourth object, just as you say: second, third and fourth khabar. It does not follow from this that the verb takes three or four objects, because that is with respect to the multiplicity of words; so this is not like your saying «أعلمْتُ زيداً عمراً فاضلاً», since the third object there is not a repetition for a single thing. I have explained this only because some people erred in understanding it. It has become clear to you from what preceded that His saying «ضيقاً حَرَجاً» contains no repetition. Makkī said: "The meaning of حَرِج — meaning with kasra — is like the meaning of ضيق; it was repeated, because its wording differs, for emphasis." I say: it would be for emphasis only where no distinguishing difference appears between them, so you say: it was repeated because of the difference of wording, as in His saying: {صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ} [al-Baqara: 157], [and his saying]:

2054 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وألفَى قولَها كَذِباً ومَيْنا
(…and he found her speech to be lying and falsehood.)

[and his saying]:

2055 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وهندٌ أتى مِنْ دونها النَّأْيُ والبُعْدُ
(…and Hind — remoteness and distance have come between us and her.)

But here the difference between them has been given above, as general and specific, or otherwise. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it was said: it is the plural of «حَرَجَة», like قَصَبَة and قَصَب, and the hāʾ in it is for hyperbole." I do not know how he imagined this hāʾ — which indicates the single unit in the singular of collective nouns, as in ثمرة, بُرّة and نَبِقة — to be for hyperbole, like the one in راوية, نَسَّابة and فَرُوْقة.

His saying: «كأنما»: this «ما» prepares for the entry of «كأنّ» on verbal clauses, like the one in {وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوْنَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 185].

Ibn Kathīr read «يَصْعَد», with sukūn on the ṣād and the ʿayn undoubled, the imperfect of صَعِد, i.e. "rises". Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «يصَّاعد», with doubled ṣād followed by an alif; its origin is يتصاعد, i.e. he undertakes the ascent and labours at it; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād for lightness. The rest read «يَصَّعَّد», with doubled ṣād and ʿayn without an alif between them, from يصَّعَّد, i.e. he performs the ascent and is burdened with it; the origin is يتصعَّد, and it was assimilated as in the reading of Shuʿba [Translator's note: i.e. Abū Bakr]. This simile clause may be resumptive, in which the state of the one whose breast Allah has made narrow and constricted is likened to one who seeks to ascend to the overarching sky, or to a high and rugged place like a steep mountain pass.

They permitted two other views about it. The first: that it is another of the multiple objects, as what precedes it is multiple. The second: that it is a ḥāl, and as to its possessor there are two possibilities: the first, the pronoun latent in «ضيِّقا»; the second, the pronoun in «حَرَجا». «في السماء» is attached to what precedes it.

His saying: {كذلك يَجْعَلُ} is like its parallels. Al-Zajjāj gave its implied form as: "Like what We have narrated to you, He makes", i.e. it would be a mubtadaʾ and khabar, or the adjective of an omitted maṣdar; so you may put «مثل» in the nominative or the accusative, on the two considerations in his view. The best is to imply for it a suitable maṣdar, as people have implied, namely: like that making — i.e. the making of the breast narrow and constricted — Allah makes the defilement (al-rijs); so Makkī and others implied it. «يجعل» may be in the sense of «ألقى» ("casts"), which is the apparent view; it then takes one object by itself and the other by a preposition, and that is why it takes «على» here; the meaning is: thus Allah casts the punishment on those who do not believe. It may also be in the sense of «صَيَّر», i.e. He makes it lie over them, encompassing them; the technical implied form is: "settled upon them".

semin-durr:126-126.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: {مُسْتَقِيماً} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «صراط», and what governs it is one of two things: either «ها», because of the meaning of drawing attention that it contains, or «ذا», because of the meaning of pointing that it contains. It is a corroborative ḥāl, not an explanatory one, because the path of Allah can only be like that.

semin-durr:127-127.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لَهُمْ دَارُ}: this clause may be resumptive and so have no grammatical position, as though someone asked about what Allah has prepared for them, and that was said to him. It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَذَّكَّرون», and it may be an adjective of «قوم». On these two views, the ḥāl or the adjective may be the preposition and its genitive noun alone, with «دار السلام» nominative as its agent; this is preferable in their view, because it is closer to a single word than a clause is, and the basic form in the adjective, the ḥāl and the khabar is the single word, so what is closer to it is preferable.

{عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ} is a ḥāl from «دار», and what governs it is the [notion of] settledness in «لهم». السلام and السَّلامة have one meaning, like اللَّداد and اللَّدادة. «عند» may be accusative by «السلام» itself, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. they are greeted with peace in the presence of their Lord, i.e. in His Garden; and it may be accusative by the settledness in «لهم». His saying «وهو وليُّهم» may also be resumptive [Translator's note: the source misprints «الاسنئناف»], or a ḥāl, i.e. theirs is the abode of peace, while Allah is their protecting friend and helper. In «بما كانوا» the bāʾ is causal and «ما» is in the sense of «الذي» (that which), or an indefinite, or maṣdariyya.

semin-durr:128-128.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَيَوْمَ يِحْشُرُهُمْ}: it may be accusative by an implied verb. Abū al-Baqāʾ gave its implied form at one time as «اذكر» ("remember"), and at another time as the omitted verb of saying that governs the vocative clause in His saying «يا مَعْشَر», i.e. "and He says: O company…, on the day We gather them". Al-Zamakhsharī gave its implied form as: "And on the day He gathers them, and We say [O company of jinn…], there will be what cannot be described for its horror." The Shaykh said: "What we said is preferable" — meaning its being accusative by «يقول», by which the vocative clause is reported — and he said: "because his [view] entails the omission of two clauses, one of them the clause «وقلنا» and the other the one governing the adverb." Al-Zajjāj gave its implied form with a passive verb of saying: "It will be said to them: O company…, on the day We gather them." This is a good meaning; it is as though he looked to the meaning of His saying «ولا يُكَلِّمهم ولا يزكِّيهم» ("and He will not speak to them nor purify them") and so made it passive. «يوم» may also be accusative by His saying «وليُّهم», because of the verbal meaning in it, i.e. He befriends them because of what they used to do, and befriends them on the day He gathers them. «جميعاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or tawkīd (emphasis) according to the opinion of some grammarians. Ḥafṣ read «يحشرهم» with the yāʾ of the third person, referring back to His saying «ربهم», i.e. and on the day their Lord gathers them.

His saying: {يَا مَعْشَرَ} is in the position of accusative by that implied verb of saying, i.e. "He says" or "We said". On al-Zajjāj's implied form, it is in the position of nominative, because it stands in the place of the agent that is substituted for. Al-maʿshar is a group; the poet said:

2056 - وأبغضُ مَنْ وضعتُ إليَّ فيه ... لساني معشرٌ عنهم أذودُ
(The most hateful of those against whom I have turned my tongue are a company whom I [nonetheless] defend.)

Its plural is maʿāshir, as in his saying, upon him be peace: «نحن معاشرَ الأنبياء لا نورث» ("We, the companies of prophets, are not inherited from"). Al-Awdī said:

2057 - فينا معاشرُ لن يَبْنوا لقومِهمُ ... وإن بَنى قومُهمْ ما أفسدوا عادوا
(Among us are companies who will never build for their people; and if their people build what they have ruined, they return [to ruin it].)

His saying {مِّنَ الإنس} is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. their friends, being of mankind. «مِنْ» may also be for explaining the genus, because their friends were men and jinn; the implied form is: their friends who are mankind. From «ربَّنا» the vocative particle has been omitted. The majority read «أَجَلَنا» in the singular, because of His saying «الذي». It was also read «آجالنا», in the plural on the pattern afʿāl, with «الذي» singular / and masculine, it being an adjective of the plural. Abū ʿAlī said: "It is a genus; he put «الذي» in the place of «التي»." The Shaykh said: "Its parsing, in my view, is as a badal (substitute), as though it were said: the time which; it is then a genus, and its parsing is not as an adjective, because of the lack of agreement between them."

His saying «خَالِدِينَ» is accusative as a ḥāl, and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). As to what governs it, there are three views. The first: that it is «مثواكم», because here it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), not a noun of place; the meaning is: the Fire is the [place] of your abiding, i.e. your residing in this state. For that reason al-Fārisī rejected al-Zajjāj's saying: «المثوى» is the abode, i.e. the Fire is the place of your abiding, i.e. your residing. Al-Fārisī said: "Al-mathwā in the verse is, in my view, the noun of the maṣdar, not of the place, because the ḥāl is governed [by it], and the noun of place does not operate as the verb does, since there is no verbal meaning in it. If it is not a place, it is established that it is a maṣdar, and the meaning is: the Fire is [the place] of your residing in it eternally. So the kāf and mīm are in meaning agents, even if in wording they are genitive by the construct. Like this is the poet's saying:

2058 - وما هي إلا في إزارٍ وعِلْقَةٍ ... مُغَارَ ابنِ هَمَّامٍ على حَيّ خَثْعما
(She was only in a waist-wrapper and a sleeveless shift at the time of Ibn Hammām's raid on the tribe of Khathʿam.)

This indicates the omission of a muḍāf; the meaning is: she was only [in] a waist-wrapper and a shift at the time of the raiding of Ibn Hammām. For that reason he made it transitive with «على»; had it been a place, he would not have made it transitive. So it is established that it is a noun of the maṣdar, not of place; and it is like your saying: «آتيك خفوقَ النجم ومقدَمَ الحاج» ('I will come to you at the setting of the star and at the arrival of the pilgrims')." Then he said: "This is good in maṣdars only because of their correspondence to time; do you not see that it passes away and does not remain, just as time is like that?" He mentioned much discussion, which I have abridged.

The second: that what governs it is an omitted verb, i.e. they will abide in it eternally; «مثواكم» indicates this implied verb, and by «مثواكم» the place of abiding is meant. This is an answer to the objection al-Fārisī made against al-Zajjāj.
