The third, said by Abū al-Baqāʾ: that what governs it is the meaning of the construct; but the meaning of the construct is not at all fit to be a governing agent, so this is nothing.

His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ الله}: they differed over what it is excepted from. The majority said: it is the clause that it follows, namely His saying {النار مَثْوَاكُمْ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَآ}; its explanation will come shortly. Abū Muslim said: "It is excepted from His saying «وبلغْنا أجَلَنا الذي أجَّلْتَ لنا», i.e. except those whom You destroyed and cut off before the term You named, because of their disbelief and straying."

People rejected this doctrine of his on technical grounds and on grounds of meaning. As for the technical, it is from two angles. The first: had the matter been so, the construction would have been «إلا ما شئت» ("except what You willed"), to correspond to His saying «أجَّلْتَ». The second: he would have separated the excepted from what it is excepted from by His saying «قال النار مثواكم خالدين فيها», and such a thing is not permissible. As for the meaning, it is because the doctrine of two terms — the term of being cut off and the named term — is false, by proofs established elsewhere than this place.

Then they differed over this exception: is it connected (muttaṣil) or disconnected (munqaṭiʿ)? There are two opinions. Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and Abū al-Baqāʾ in one of his two opinions, held that it is disconnected, the meaning being: He said: the Fire is your abode, except those of you who believed in this world; like His saying: {لاَ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الموت إِلاَّ الموتة الأولى} [al-Dukhān: 56], i.e. but [not] the first death, for they have already tasted it in this world. So too this: but those of you whom Allah willed to believe in this world. This is far-fetched. Others held that it is connected, and then they differed over what it is excepted from. Some said: it is the pronoun of those addressed in His saying «مَثْواكم», i.e. except those who believed in this world after having been among these disbelievers. «ما» here is in the sense of «مَنْ», which is for rational beings, and its occurrence here is acceptable because what is meant by the excepted is a type and kind, and «ما» applies to types of rational beings; the verification of this preceded at His saying {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ النسآء} [al-Nisāʾ: 3].

But this was considered far-fetched, in that the excepted differs from what it is excepted from in the time of the judgement made on them, and the two must share / in time. If you said «قام القوم إلا زيداً» ("the people stood except Zayd"), its meaning would be: except Zayd, for he did not stand; it would not be valid for the meaning to be: for he will stand in the future. And if you said «سأضرب القوم إلا زيداً» ("I will strike the people except Zayd"), its meaning would be: for I will not strike him in the future; it would not be valid for the meaning to be: for I struck him in the past — unless it is made a disconnected exception, as its explanation has preceded.

Some held that what it is excepted from is a time, and then those holding this differed. Some of them said: that time is the period of their residence in the barzakh, i.e. the graves. And it was said: it is the period between their being gathered and their entering the Fire; this is the opinion of al-Ṭabarī. He said: "That is acceptable, since the expression in His saying «النار مَثْواكم» does not restrict it to future time to the exclusion of other times." Al-Zajjāj said: "It is the two times together, i.e. the period of their residence in the graves and the period from their gathering to their entering the Fire." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إلا ما شاء الله» means: they will remain eternally in the punishment of the Fire for all eternity, except what Allah wills — except the times in which they are moved from the punishment of the Fire to the punishment of the zamharīr (bitter cold); for it is reported that they enter a valley in which there is such zamharīr as severs their joints, and they howl to one another and ask to be returned to Hell." Some said: "«إلا ما شاء الله» refers to the sinners of the people of tawḥīd who enter the Fire; «ما» was applied to them because they are a type, as though it were said: except the type of sinners that entered it, for they do not remain in it eternally." The apparent view is that this is a real exception; indeed it must be so. Al-Zamakhsharī claimed that it may be of the category of the saying of the aggrieved man who has got hold of the one who wronged him, and who keeps gnashing his teeth at him, when the other asks him to loosen his grip on his throat: "May Allah destroy me if I let you breathe — except if I wish"; and he knows that he will not wish that, but only to slake his rage on him with the utmost severity and harshness he is able to; so his saying "except if I wish" is among the most severe threats, together with mockery. I say: there is no need to claim that, given the evident meaning of exception in it, and [to commit] figurative usage and to present what has not occurred in the form of what has occurred. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: "«إلا ما شاء الله» means: of their being in this world without punishment"; so he made the excepted the time of their life, and this is more far-fetched than what preceded.

Al-Farrāʾ said — and al-Zajjāj inclined to it: "The meaning is: except what Allah wills of increase [Translator's note: the source misprints «زياةٍ» for «زيادةٍ»] in the punishment." Others said: except what Allah wills of exemplary punishment. All of this works only on the basis of a disconnected exception.

The Shaykh said: "This goes back to the exception from the maṣdar indicated by the meaning of the speech, since the meaning is: they will be punished in the Fire, remaining in it eternally, except what Allah wills of punishment in excess of the Fire, for He will punish them with it. It is then a disconnected exception, since the punishment in excess of the punishment of the Fire is not included under the punishment of the Fire." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is plausible in my view that this exception is an address to the Prophet ﷺ and his nation, and not part of what will be said on the Day of Resurrection; the excepted being those of the disbelievers at that time [i.e. now] who will believe in the knowledge of Allah. It is as though, when He informed them that it will be said to the disbelievers 'The Fire is your abode', He excepted for them those who might believe among those they see as disbelievers at that time; «ما» applies to an attribute of rational beings. This interpretation is also supported by His saying {إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ عَليمٌ}, i.e. [knowing] of those of them who might believe." The Shaykh said: "It is a good interpretation" — yet he had said before that: "The apparent view is that this exception is part of Allah the Exalted's speech to those addressed, and the interpretations of the exception came on that basis; and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said…" — and then he quoted it to the end. So how can he approve of something that he has judged to be contrary to the apparent sense, without a strong indication removing the wording from its apparent sense?

semin-durr:129-129.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {وكذلك نُوَلِّي}: i.e. just as We forsook the disobedient among mankind and jinn until some of them enjoyed others, so We leave some of them to others for help and support. So it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); or it is in the position of nominative, i.e. the matter is like the putting of some / of the wrongdoers in charge of others — this is the opinion of al-Zajjāj in more than one place. {بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكْسِبُونَ} is evident, like its parallels.

semin-durr:130-130.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مِّنْكُمْ} is in the position of nominative as an adjective of «رسل», so it is attached to something omitted. His saying «يَقُصُّون» may be a second adjective, and it has come thus in a good way, since what is close to a single word has been placed before the clause. It may also be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and as to its possessor there are two views. The first: it is «رسل»; this is permissible even though it is indefinite [Translator's note: the source misprints «مكرة» for «نكرة»], because it is specified by the adjective. The second: that it is the latent pronoun in «منكم».

His saying {رُسُلٌ مِّنْكُمْ}: al-Farrāʾ claimed that the verse contains the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "Did there not come to you messengers from one of you" — meaning from the genus of mankind. He said: "Like His saying: {يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا الُّلؤْلُؤُ وَالمَرْجَانُ} [al-Raḥmān: 22], whereas they come out only from the salt water; and {وَجَعَلَ القمر فِيهِنَّ نُوراً} [Nūḥ: 16], whereas it is only in some of them. So the implied form is: comes out from one of the two, and He made the moon in one of them; it was omitted because it is known." Al-Farrāʾ needed this only because in his view messengers are exclusive to mankind; that is, he did not believe that Allah sent the jinn a messenger from among themselves, but rather that He sent mankind to them, as is reported in the exegesis. And on this there is consensus: that the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ was sent to mankind and jinn. This is the truth — I mean that no one of the jinn was sent except by means of the message of mankind, as came in the ḥadīth about the jinn who, when they heard the Qurʾān, turned back to their people. But there is no need to imply a muḍāf, even if we say that the messengers of the jinn are from mankind, for the reason I mentioned, namely that they are called messengers figuratively, being messengers by means of the message of mankind. Some claimed that Allah sent the jinn a messenger from among themselves named Yūsuf.

semin-durr:131-131.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {ذلك أَن لَّمْ يَكُنْ رَّبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ} admits three views. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. that is the matter. The second: the reverse, i.e. the matter is that. The third: that it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. We did that. The meaning becomes clear only when what is pointed to is known. It may be the coming of the messengers narrating the signs and warning of the gathering and the recompense; or it may be that which We have narrated of the affair of the messengers and the affair of those who denied; and it may be a pointing to the question understood from His saying «ألم يأتكم».

His saying «أن لم يكن» admits two views. The first: that it is on the omission of the lām of cause, i.e. that matter which We have narrated, or that coming, or that questioning, is because [your Lord] would not; when the lām was omitted, its position could be genitive or accusative, as has been known more than once. The second: that it is a badal (substitute) for «ذلك».

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "You may make it a badal for «ذلك», as in His saying: {وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ الأمر أَنَّ دَابِرَ هَؤُلآءِ مَقْطُوعٌ مُّصْبِحِينَ} [al-Ḥijr: 22]" [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Ḥijr 66] — end of quotation. So it may be in the position of nominative or accusative, according to what preceded regarding «ذلك»; except that al-Zamakhsharī, who holds the badal view, mentioned for the position of «ذلك» only the nominative, as khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. «أَنْ» may be the one that makes the imperfect accusative, or the lightened one whose noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), with «لم يكن» in the position of nominative as its khabar; it is analogous to His saying {أَلاَّ يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلاً} [Ṭāhā: 89] and his saying:

2059 - في فتيةٍ كسيوف الهند قد عَلِمُوا ... أنْ هالكٌ كلُّ مَنْ يَحْفَى ويَنْتَعِلُ
(Among young men like Indian swords, who know that everyone who goes barefoot or shod will perish.)

«بظلمٍ» admits two views. The more evident of them: that it is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ربك» or from the pronoun in «مُهْلِكَ», i.e. He would not be the destroyer of the towns while doing wrong. It may also be a ḥāl from «القرى», i.e. while they are involved in their sins; both meanings are transmitted in the exegesis. The second: that it is attached to «مُهْلِك» as an object; this is far-fetched, and Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. His saying: «وأهلُها غافلون» is a circumstantial clause.

semin-durr:132-132.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلِكُلٍّ}: the muḍāf ilayhi was omitted because it is known, i.e. and for each party of the jinn and mankind. His saying: «مما عملوا» is in the position of nominative as an adjective of «درجات». And it was said: and for each of the believers specifically. And it was said: and for each of the disbelievers specifically, because it came right after the address to the disbelievers; but His saying «درجاتٌ» (degrees) makes this unlikely — though it may be said that what is meant by it here is ranks, even if its use is predominantly for good. His saying «عمَّا يعملون»: the majority read it in the third person, referring back to His saying «ولكل درجات». Ibn ʿĀmir read it in the second person, in keeping with what follows it in His saying «يُذْهِبْكم», «من بعدكم», «أنشأكم».

semin-durr:133-133.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَرَبُّكَ الغني}: «الغنيُّ» and «ذو الرحمة» may be two khabars (predicates) or two adjectives, with «إن يشأ» and what follows it as the khabar of the first [i.e. of the mubtadaʾ]; or «الغنيّ» may be an adjective and «ذو الرحمة» the khabar, the conditional clause being a second khabar or resumptive. His saying «ما يشاء»: «ما» may apply to what is of the genus of human beings, and He used «ما», which is for non-rational beings, only because of the vagueness that results. It may apply to non-rational beings, meaning that He will bring another genus; and it may apply to a type of rational beings, as has preceded.

His saying {كَمَآ أَنشَأَكُمْ} admits two views. The first: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) not of the same root [Translator's note: the source reads «على غير الصدر», a misprint for «على غير المصدر»] as His saying «ويَسْتخلف», because the meaning of «يستخلف» is «يُنْشئْ» (brings into being). The second: that it is the adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: a succession like that by which He brought you into being. His saying {مِنْ ذرِّيَّة} is attached to «أنشأكم». There are several views about this «مِنْ». The first: that it is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. He began your bringing into being from the offspring of a people. The second: that it is partitive; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The third: in the sense of substitution (badal). Al-Ṭabarī said, and Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib followed him: "It is like your saying «أخذت من ثوبي درهماً» ('I took a dirham for my garment'), i.e. in exchange and compensation for it." The use of «مِنْ» in the sense of substitution is rare or impossible, and what occurs of it is interpreted, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {لَجَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ مَّلاَئِكَةً} [al-Zukhruf: 60] and his saying:

2060 - جاريةٌ لم تَأْكُلِ المرقَّقَا ... ولم تَذُقْ من البقول الفُسْتُقا
(A girl who has not eaten thin bread, nor tasted pistachios in place of herbs.)

i.e. instead of you and instead of herbs. The meaning is: from the children of an earlier people whose origin is Ādam. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From the children of another people who were not of your description, namely the people of Noah's ark." Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read «ذَرِّيَّة» with fatḥa on the dhāl; Abān ibn ʿUthmān read «ذَرِيَّة» with the rāʾ undoubled and with kasra, and «ذَرْية», on the pattern of ضَرْبَة, is also reported from him. The verification of this has preceded.

semin-durr:134-134.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {إِنَّ مَا تُوعَدُونَ لآتٍ}: «ما» is in the sense of «الذي» (that which) and is not the restraining «ما» (al-kāffa); «توعدون» is its ṣila (relative clause) and the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. «إنَّ ما توعدونه»; «لآتٍ» is the khabar (predicate), emphasised by the lām. The two brothers [Translator's note: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read here «مَنْ يكون له عاقبة الدار», and in al-Qaṣaṣ, with the yāʾ, and the rest with the tāʾ (dots above). Both are clear, for its femininity is not real; that preceded at His saying: {وَلاَ تَنفَعُهَا شَفَاعَةٌ} [al-Baqara: 123].

semin-durr:135-135.t:
The majority read {على مَكَانَتِكُمْ} here and throughout the Qurʾān in the singular, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «مكاناتكم» in the plural in all of them. Whoever read the singular did so to intend the genus; whoever read the plural did so to agree with what follows it, for those addressed are a group and it has been annexed to them, and it is known that each one has his own position. There is disagreement about the mīm of «مكان» and «مكانة». It was said: it is a radical, and both are from مكن يمكن. And it was said: both are from الكون (being), so the mīm is extra. On the first, the meaning is: act according to your ability over your affair and the utmost of your capacity and power — Abū Isḥāq said its meaning; on the second: act according to your direction and the state you are in.

His saying: {مَن تَكُونُ لَهُ}: this «مَنْ» admits two views. The first: that it is a relative noun, which is the apparent view, so it is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «علم» here takes one object, because it is in the sense of recognising (ʿirfān). The second: that it is interrogative, so it is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). {تَكُونُ لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ الدار}: «تكون» with its noun and khabar is in the position of nominative as its khabar (predicate), and it [the mubtadaʾ] with its khabar is in the position of accusative, either because it fills the place of one object if «علم» is of recognition, or because it fills the place of two if it is of certainty.

semin-durr:136-136.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ}: «جعل» here is in the sense of «صيَّر» (to make into), so it takes two objects, the first of them being His saying «نصيباً» and the second His saying «لله». «ممَّا ذَرَأ» may be attached to the verb «جعل», or attached to something omitted, because it was originally an adjective of «نصيباً», and when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the implied form is: and they assigned a portion of what He produced to Allah. «من الحَرْث» may be a badal (substitute) for «ممَّا ذرأ» with repetition of the governing element, as though it were said: and they assigned to Allah a portion of the crops and the livestock. It may be attached to «ذرأ», or attached to something omitted as a ḥāl, either from the relative «ما» or from its omitted referent pronoun. In the speech there is the omission of an object required by the division, the implied form being: and they assigned to Allah a portion of such-and-such and to their partners a portion of it; what follows indicates it, in His saying: {فَقَالُواْ هذا للَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ وهذا}. «هذا لله» is a clause whose position is accusative by the verb of saying, and likewise His saying «وهذا لشركائنا».

His saying: {بِزَعْمِهِمْ} admits two views. The first: that it is attached to «قالوا», i.e. they said that saying by assertion, not by certainty and insight. And it was said: it is attached to what the [notion of] settledness in His saying «لله» is attached to. The majority read «زَعمهم» with fatḥa on the zāy in both places; this is the dialect of the Ḥijāz [Translator's note: the source misprints «الحداز» for «الحجاز»], and it is the most eloquent. Al-Kisāʾī read «بزُعمهم» with ḍamma, / which is the dialect of Banū Asad. Are the fatḥa and the ḍamma of one meaning, or is the form with fatḥa a maṣdar (verbal noun) and the form with ḍamma a noun? There is a well-known disagreement. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «بزَعَمهم», with fatḥa on the zāy and the ʿayn. There is a fourth dialectal form, of some of Qays and Banū Tamīm, namely kasra on the zāy; it has not been read in this dialect as far as I know. The verification of al-zaʿm has preceded.

His saying {لِشُرَكَآئِنَا} admits two views. The first: that الشركاء is from الشرك (associating partners), and by them they mean their gods whom they associated with the Creator, Exalted is He, in worship. The construct is then neither to an agent nor to an object, but is a construct of specification; the meaning is: the partners whom they associated between themselves and Allah in worship [Translator's note: so in the source]. The second: that الشركاء is from الشركة (partnership), and the meaning of their calling their gods their partners is that they made them partners in their wealth, crops, livestock, trade and other things. The construct is then a verbal (lafẓī) construct, either to the object, i.e. our partners who shared with us in our wealth, or to the agent, i.e. those whom we made partners in our wealth.

His saying: {سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ}: its parallel has preceded more than once. Al-Ḥūfī parsed it here, saying: "«ما» is in the sense of «الذي», the implied form being: evil is that which they judge — their judgement; so «حكمُهم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate), and it was omitted because «يحكمون» indicates it. «ما» may also be a tamyīz (specification), on the doctrine of those who allow that in «بئسما», so it is in the position of accusative, the implied form being: evil as a judgement is their judgement. «يحكمون» is not then an adjective of «ما», because the purpose is vagueness; but there is an omission in the speech indicated by «ما», the implied form being: «ساء ما ما يحكمون», and the second «ما» was omitted." I say: if this «ما» is a relative, the doctrine of the Basrans is that omission of the relative is not permissible, as is known; and if it is an indefinite qualified by an adjective, it is open to question, because omission of «ما» as an indefinite qualified by an adjective is not attested.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«ما» is in the position of nominative, as though He said: evil is that which they judge. It does not seem plausible to me that «ساء» here should be treated like نِعْم and بئس, because what is explained here is implied (a pronoun), and by agreement of the grammarians it must be made overt. It is plausible for it to be treated like بئس only in His saying {سَآءَ مَثَلاً القوم} [al-Aʿrāf: 177], because what is explained is overt in the speech." The Shaykh said: "These are the words of one whose foot is not firmly planted in Arabic, but who has picked up a little of it; because when «ساء» is treated like بئس, its rule is exactly like its rule, differing in nothing whatsoever, whether as to an overt or implied agent, or the tamyīz; and there is no disagreement about the permissibility of omitting the one specified for praise or blame (al-makhṣūṣ), and the tamyīz with it, when the speech indicates it. So his saying 'because what is explained here is implied, and by agreement it must be made overt' is a statement that falls; and his claim of agreement on that, when agreement is on the contrary, is an astonishing wonder."

semin-durr:137-137.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وكذلك زَيَّنَ}: this is in the position of accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), like its parallels. Al-Zamakhsharī gave two implied forms for it, saying: "And like that adorning — namely the adorning of shirk in dividing the offering between Allah and the gods — or: and like that far-reaching adorning which is known from the devils." The Shaykh said: "Ibn al-Anbārī said: «كذلك» may be resumptive, not pointing to what precedes it, so that the meaning is: and thus [the partners] made attractive." I say: what is transmitted from Ibn al-Anbārī is that it points to what precedes it. Al-Wāḥidī transmitted from him that he said: "«ذلك» points to what Allah reproached them for, of their dividing what they divided out of ignorance; it is as though it were said: and like that which they did in the division, out of ignorance and error, [their partners] made attractive to many of the polytheists. So He likened the partners' adorning to their mistake [Translator's note: the source reads «بخطابهم» ("their address"), evidently for «بخطئهم» ("their error")] in the division." This is the meaning of al-Zajjāj's saying.

In this verse there are many readings, of which two are mutawātir. The first: the majority read «زَيَّنَ» as active, «قَتْلَ» accusative as object, «أولادهم» genitive by the construct, and «شركاؤهم» nominative as agent; this reading is clear in meaning and construction. Ibn ʿĀmir read: «زُيِّن» as passive, «قَتْلُ» nominative as that whose agent is not named [i.e. nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent], «أولادَهم» accusative as the object of the maṣdar, and «شركائهم» genitive, the maṣdar being annexed to it as its agent. This reading is mutawātir and sound. Many people have been bold against its reader in ways that are not fitting, whereas he is the highest of the seven readers in chain of transmission and the earliest of them in emigration. As for the height of his chain: he read with Abū al-Dardāʾ, Wāthila ibn al-Asqaʿ, Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd, Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān and al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī, and Yaḥyā al-Dhimārī transmitted that he read with ʿUthmān himself. As for the earliness of his emigration: he was born in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. And it suffices you regarding him that Hishām ibn ʿAmmār, one of the teachers of al-Bukhārī, took from the companions of his companions. His biography is extensive; I mentioned it in «شرح القصيد» (the Commentary on the Qaṣīda). I have mentioned this brief note here only to draw attention to the error of those who rejected his reading and attributed it to a solecism, or to merely following the written form.

Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās said: "This" — meaning separation between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi by an adverb or other — "is not permissible in poetry or elsewhere." This is a mistake on the part of Abū Jaʿfar, because of what we will mention from the language of the Arabs. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: "This is ugly and rare in usage; had he" — meaning Ibn ʿĀmir — "turned away from it, it would have been better, because they did not separate between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi by an adverb in [ordinary] speech, despite their latitude with adverbs; they permitted it only in poetry." He said: "They have separated with it — i.e. with the adverb — in many places, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوْماً جَبَّارِينَ} [al-Māʾida: 22], and the poet's saying:

2061 - على أنني بعدما قد مَضَى ... ثلاثون للهَجر حَوْلاً كميلا
(Even though, after thirty full years of separation have passed…)

and another's saying:

2062 - فلا تَلْحَنِي فيها فإنَّ بحبِّها ... أخاك مصابُ القلب جَمٌّ بلابلُه
(So do not blame me concerning her, for with love of her your brother is stricken in heart, his anxieties many.)

So he separated between «إنَّ» and its noun by what is attached to its khabar (predicate). Had it been by other than an adverb, it would not have been permissible; do you not see that if you said «إن زيداً عمراً ضارب», intending «زيداً» to be accusative by «ضارب», it would not be permissible? So if they did not permit separation between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi in speech by an adverb, despite their latitude with it in speech, and it is permissible only in poetry, as in his saying:

2063 - كما خُطَّ الكتابُ بكفِّ يوماً ... يهوديٍ يقارِبُ أو يُزيلُ
(As writing is traced one day by the hand of a Jew, bringing [lines] close together or setting them apart.)

then it is all the more fitting that it not be permissible with a direct object, with which no latitude for separation is taken. The justification of it, despite its weakness and rarity of usage, is that it has occurred in poetry in the manner in which he read it. Al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:

2064 - يَطُفْنَ بحوزيِّ المراتعِ لم تَرُعْ ... بواديه مِنْ قَرْعِ القِسِيَّ الكنائِنِ
(They circle around a [bull] that has the pastures to itself, in whose valley the quivers' knocking against the bows has never caused alarm.)

And Abū al-Ḥasan cited:

2065 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... زجَّ القَلوصَ أبي مزادَهْ
(…as Abū Mazāda drives on the young she-camel.)"

Abū ʿUbayd said: "ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir and the people of Syria used to read it «زُيِّن» with ḍamma on the zāy, «قتلُ» in the nominative, «أولادَهم» in the accusative and «شركائهم» in the genitive, interpreting it as 'their partners' killing of their children', thus separating between the verb [i.e. the maṣdar] and its agent." Abū ʿUbayd said: "I do not like this reading, because of the forcedness in it; the reading [of the majority], in our view, is preferable, because of its soundness in Arabic together with the consensus of the people of the two Sanctuaries and the two cities of Iraq upon it." Sībawayh said about their saying «يا سارق الليلةِ أهلَ الدار» ("O you who robbed the people of the house this night"), with «الليلة» in the genitive by extension and «الأهل» accusative as object: "And «يا سارقَ الليلةَ أهلِ الدار» is not permissible except in poetry, out of dislike of separating between the governing genitive and the genitive." Then he said: "Among what has come in poetry, where separation was made between it and the genitive, is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Qamīʾa:

2066 - لمَّا رأت ساتيدَ ما استعبرتْ ... لله درُّ اليومَ مَنْ لامها
(When she saw Sātīdamā, she wept; how excellent, today, is the one who blamed her!)"

And he mentioned other verses which will come. Then he said: "This is ugly; and on this basis it is permissible in poetry to say: «مررت بخيرِ وأفضلِ مَنْ ثَمَّ» ('I passed by the best and most excellent of those there')." Abū al-Fatḥ Ibn Jinnī said: "Separation between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi by an adverb, or by a preposition and its genitive noun, is frequent, but it is of the poet's necessity (ḍarūra)." Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: "Whoever read this reading, putting «الأولاد» in the accusative and «الشركاء» in the genitive — it is a remote reading. It has been transmitted from Ibn ʿĀmir, and its justification is separation between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi by the object; and that is permissible according to the grammarians only in poetry, and most often with an adverb." Ibn ʿAṭiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "This is a weak reading in the usage of the Arabs. That is because he annexed the verb [i.e. the maṣdar] to the agent, which is الشركاء, then separated between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi by the object; and the leading authorities on Arabic do not permit separation with adverbs in such a case except in poetry, as he said:

2067 - كما خُطَّ الكتابُ بكفِّ يوماً ... يهوديٍ. . . . . . . . . . . . .

/ — the verse. So how then with the object, in the most eloquent speech? But its justification, despite its weakness, is that it occurred in an irregular verse cited by Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash:

2068 - فَزَجَجْتها بمَزَجَّةٍ ... زجَّ القَلوصَ أبي مزادَهْ
(I thrust at her with a short spear, as Abū Mazāda drives on the young she-camel.)

and in the verse of al-Ṭirimmāḥ, namely his saying:

2069 - يَطُفْنَ بحُوزِيِّ المراتع لم تَرُعْ ... بواديه من قَرْع القِسيَّ الكنائِنِ"

Al-Zamakhsharī spoke harshly and expressed himself badly: "As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, which he mentioned, it is something that, were it in the place of necessity, namely poetry, would be ugly [Translator's note: the source prints «سَمِيحاً», a misprint for «سَمِجاً», "ugly", as the following «سَمُج» shows] and rejected, just as … زجَّ القَلوصَ أبي مزادَهْ was found ugly and rejected. So how then in prose speech? And how then in the Qurʾān, which is inimitable in the beauty of its arrangement and its eloquence? What led him to that was that he saw «شركائهم» written with a yāʾ in some copies of the muṣḥaf. Had he read «الأولاد» and «الشركاء» both in the genitive — since children are their partners in their wealth — he would have found in that a way out of committing this." I say: there will come an explanation of what Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] wished Ibn ʿĀmir had read, and that he did in fact read it; it seems al-Zamakhsharī did not come across that, and so he wished for it.

All these opinions I have mentioned should not be paid attention to, because they are an attack on what is mutawātir, even if they issued from [Translator's note: the source has «على», for «عن»] great imāms. Moreover, those of equal standing have defended it and adduced from the language of the Arabs, its verse and its prose, what testifies to the soundness of this reading linguistically. Abū Bakr Ibn al-Anbārī said: "This is a sound reading. Since the Arabs have separated between two terms of a construct by a clause, in their saying «هو غلامُ إن شاء الله أخيك» — meaning: he is the servant, Allah willing, of your brother — separating by a single word is easier." End of quotation. Al-Kisāʾī heard one of them say: «إن الشاةَ لتجترُّ فتسمع صوتَ واللهِ ربِّها» ("the sheep chews the cud and hears the voice — by Allah — of its owner"), i.e. the voice of its owner, by Allah; so he separated with the oath, which has the force of a clause. One of the early generations read: {فَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ الله مُخْلِفَ وَعْدَه رُسُلِهُ} [Ibrāhīm: 47], with «وعدَه» accusative and «رسله» genitive. In the ḥadīth from him, upon him be peace: «هل أنتم تاركو لي صاحبي، تاركو لي امرأتي» ("Will you leave to me my companion? Will you leave to me my wife?") [Translator's note: so in the source; the well-known wording is «تاركو لي صاحبي» only], i.e. leave my companion to me, leave my wife to me.

Ibn Jinnī said in al-Khaṣāʾiṣ: "Chapter on what is reported from an Arab in contradiction to the majority. If something of that occurs, that Arab and what he brought are examined: if he is eloquent and what he brought is acceptable to analogy, one thinks well of him, because it may have reached him from an ancient dialect whose time has long passed and whose traces have faded. Abū Bakr Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ḥajjāj informed us from Abū Khalīfa al-Faḍl ibn al-Ḥubāb, who said: Ibn ʿAwn said from Ibn Sīrīn: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Poetry was the knowledge of a people who had no knowledge sounder than it. Then Islam came, and the Arabs became occupied away from it with jihād and with raiding Persia and Byzantium, and were distracted from poetry and its transmission. When Islam spread, the conquests came and the Arabs settled in the garrison cities, they went back to transmitting poetry, but they could not resort to a compiled dīwān or a written book. They had grown used to that [i.e. oral transmission], and those of the Arabs who perished had perished by death and killing; so they preserved the lesser part of it and the greater part of it was lost to them.'

He said: Abū Bakr told us from Abū Khalīfa from Yūnus ibn Ḥabīb from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: 'Only the lesser part of what the Arabs said has reached you; had it come to you in full, much knowledge and poetry would have come to you.'" Abū al-Fatḥ said: "If the matter is so, we do not decide that an eloquent person is mistaken [when] something contrary to the majority is heard from him, as long as there is a way to accept what he reports — except [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense seems to be "especially"] when analogy supports it." I say: and the reading of this imām would be in this position — indeed all the more so and the more fittingly — even if it were not mutawātir; so how, when it is mutawātir?

Ibn Dhakwān said: "Al-Kisāʾī asked me about this word and what had reached him of our reading, and I saw that he seemed to admire it, and he chanted this verse:

2070 - تَنْفي يداها الحصَى في كل هاجرة ... نَفْيَ الدَّراهيمَ تَنْقادِ الصيارِيف
(Her forelegs scatter the pebbles in every midday heat, as the money-changers' testing scatters the dirhams.)"

— with «الدراهيم» accusative and «تنقاد» genitive. It is also transmitted with «الدراهيم» genitive and «تنقاد» nominative, which is the basic form and the well-known one in transmission. Al-Kirmānī / said: "The reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, even if weak in Arabic because of the interposition between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi, is strong and lofty in transmission." End of quotation. And it was heard from one whose Arabic is trusted: «تَرْكُ يوماً نفسِك وهواها سَعْيٌ في رَداها», i.e. leaving your soul one day with its desire is striving towards its ruin. As for what has occurred in verse of separation between two terms of a construct by an adverb, a preposition, or an object, it is frequent, and by other than that it is rare. Of separation by an adverb is the poet's saying:

2071 - فَرِشْني بخيرٍ لا أكونَنْ ومِدْحتي ... كناحتِ يوماً صخرةٍ بعسيل
(So feather me [i.e. reward me] with good, lest I and my praise be like one who one day carves a rock with a brush.)

Its implied form is: «كناحت صخرةٍ يوماً». And like it is another's saying:

2072 - كما خُطَّ الكتابُ بكف يوماً ... يهوديٍّ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

and another's saying:

2073 - قد سَأَلَتْني أمُّ عمروٍ عن ال ... أرضِ التي تجهل أَعْلامَها
لَمَّا رَأَتْ ساتِيْدَ ما اسْتَعْبَرَتْ ... للهِ دَرُّ اليومَ مَنْ لامها
تَذَكَّرَتْ أرضاً بها أهلَها ... أخوالَها فيها وأعمامَها
(Umm ʿAmr asked me about the land whose landmarks she does not know; when she saw Sātīdamā she wept — how excellent, today, is the one who blamed her! She remembered a land in which were her people, her maternal and paternal uncles.)

He means: «لله دَرُّ مَنْ لامَها اليوم». As for «ساتيد ما», it was said: it is a compound, the original being «ساتي دما» ("thirsting for blood"), and then this mountain was named with it because [someone] was killed near it; it was said: the slain never cease to be near it. And it was said: «ساتيد» is the whole name and «ما» is redundant. An example of separation by a preposition is his saying:

2074 - هما أخوا في الحرب مَنْ لا أخاله ... إذا خافَ يوماً نَبْوَةً فدعاهما
(They are, in war, the two brothers of the one who has no brother, if one day he fears a setback and calls upon them.)

and his saying:

2075 - لأنتَ مُعْتادُ في الهيجا مصابَرَةٍ ... يَصْلى بها كلُّ مَنْ عاداك نيرانا
(You are accustomed, in battle, to endurance, by which everyone who shows you enmity is roasted in fires.)

and his saying:

2076 - كأنَّ أصواتَ مِنْ إيغالِهِنَّ بنا ... أواخِرِ المَيْسِ أصواتُ الفراريج
(As though the sounds — from their rushing on with us — of the hind parts of the saddle-wood were the cries of chicks.)

and his saying:

2077 - تَمُرُّ على ما تَسْتَمِرُّ وقد شَفَتْ ... غلائلَ عبدُ القيسِ منها صدورِها
(She passes on as she persists, and ʿAbd al-Qays has cured by her the rancours of their breasts.)

He means: they are the two brothers of the one who has no brother, in war; you are accustomed to endurance in battle [Translator's note: the source here writes «الهجاء» ("satire") for «الهيجا» ("battle") of the verse]; as though the sounds of the hind parts of the saddle-wood; and the rancours of their breasts.

Of separation by an object is the poet's saying:

2078 - فَزَجَجْتُها بمَزَجَّةٍ ... زجَّ القَلوصَ أبي مزادَه

It is also transmitted as «فَزَجَجْتها فتدافعَتْ» and as «فزجَجْتها متمكناً». This verse, as stated, was cited by al-Akhfash with «القلوص» accusative, separating between the maṣdar and its notional agent. However, al-Farrāʾ said after citing this verse: "The grammarians of the people of Medina cite this verse" — meaning with «القلوص» accusative. He said: "The correct form is «زَجَّ القلوصِ», with the genitive." I say: his saying "the correct form" may be from the point of view of transmission, i.e. the correct thing is its genitive according to the sound transmission; or from the point of view of analogy, even if it was transmitted only with the accusative. He said in another place of his book Maʿānī al-Qurʾān: "This is among what the grammarians of the people of the Ḥijāz used to say, and we have not found its like in Arabic." Abū al-Fatḥ said: "He separated between them by the direct object, though he was able to say «زج القلوصِ أبو مزادة», as in your saying «سَرَّني أكلُ الخبزِ زيدٌ» ('Zayd's eating of the bread pleased me')" — meaning that he should have annexed the maṣdar to its object, leaving the agent nominative as it originally is; and this is the meaning of al-Farrāʾ's first saying, "the correct form is the genitive of القلوص", meaning with the agent nominative. Then Ibn Jinnī said: "In this verse there is, in my view, evidence of the strength among them of annexing the maṣdar to the agent, and that in their minds it is stronger than annexing it to the object; do you not see that he committed this licence while able to avoid it, for no reason other than the desire to annex the maṣdar to the agent rather than the object?" Of separation by the direct object also is another's saying:

2079 - وحِلَقِ الماذيِّ والقوانِسِ ... فداسَهم دونسَ الحصادَ الدائِسِ
(…and the rings of the bright mail and the helmet-crests; and he trampled them as the thresher tramples the harvest.)

i.e. «دوس الدائس الحصادَ» [Translator's note: the verse in the source prints «دونسَ», a misprint for «دَوْسَ»]. And like it also:

2080 - يَفْرُك حَبَّ السنبلِ الكُنَافِجِ ... بالقاع فَرْكَ القطنَ المحالجِ
(He rubs out the grain of the full ear on the plain, as the ginning-tools rub the cotton.)

He means: «فَرْك المحالجِ القطنَ». And the saying of al-Ṭirimmāḥ:

2081 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بواديه من قَرْع القِسِيَّ الكنائنِ

He means: «قرع الكنائنِ القسيَّ» (the quivers' knocking against the bows). Ibn Jinnī said about this verse: "We find in it no escape from the separation, because the rhymes are genitive." And he said about «زجَّ القلوصَ»: "He separated between them by the direct object, / though he was able…", to the end of his words given above. He means that had he cited al-Ṭirimmāḥ's verse with «القسيّ» genitive and «الكنائن» nominative, it would not have been permissible, because the rhymes are genitive; unlike al-Akhfash's verse, for had he put «القلوص» in the genitive and «أبو مزادة» in the nominative, its rhyme would not have varied nor its metre broken. I say: had he put «الكنائن» in the nominative in the verse, it would have been permissible, even though the rhymes are genitive, and that would be iqwāʾ, which is that some rhymes are genitive and some nominative, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

2082 - تَخْدي على العِلاَّتِ سامٍ رأسُها ... رَوْعاءُ مَنْسِمُها رثيمٌ دامِ
(She paces briskly despite her ailments, her head held high, spirited, her toe-pad bruised and bleeding.)

Then he said:

جالَتْ لتصرَعني فقلت لها اقصِري ... إني امرؤٌ صَرْعي عليك حرامُ
(She swerved to throw me, and I said to her: Stop! I am a man whose throwing is forbidden to you.)

So the mīm is genitive in the first and nominative in the second. If it is said: this is a defect in poetry — it is said: that does not fall short of being like this [separation] for the sake of necessity; and the truth is that iqwāʾ is more hideous and more defective than the separation mentioned. Of that also is:

2083 - فإن يكنِ النِّكاحُ أَحَلَّ شيءٍ ... فإنَّ نكاحها مطرٍ حرامُ
(If marriage is the most lawful of things, then Maṭar's marrying her is forbidden.)

i.e. «فإن نكاحِ مطرٍ إيَّاها». When the object was placed first, separating between the maṣdar and its agent, it became attached to its governing word, because it could be attached, so it did not resort to the detached form. In the poetry of Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī] there occurs separation between the maṣdar annexed to its agent by the object, as in his saying:

2084 - بعثتُ إليه من لساني حديقة ... سقاها الحيا سَقْيَ الرياضَ السحائبِ
(I sent him from my tongue a garden, watered by the rain as the clouds water the meadows.)

i.e. «سقي السحائبِ الرياضَ». As for separation by other than what has preceded, it is rare. Of it is separation by the agent, as in his saying:

2085 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... غلائلَ عبدُ القيس منها صدورِها

So «غلائل» was separated from «صدورها» by the agent, which is «عبد القيس», and by the preposition, which is «منها», as explained earlier. Like it is another's saying:

2086 - نرى أسهماً للموت تُصْمي ولا تُنْمي ... ولا تَرْعوي عن نقضِ أهواؤنا العزمِ
(We see arrows of death that kill on the spot and do not miss, yet our desires do not desist from breaking resolve.)

So «أهواؤنا» is an agent of the maṣdar «نَقْض», and by it separation was made between the maṣdar and the muḍāf ilayhi, which is «العزم». Like it is another's saying:

2087 - أَنْجَبَ أيام والداهُ به ... إذ نَجَلاه فنِعْمَ ما نَجَلا
(His parents were blessed with noble offspring in him in the days when they begot him — how excellent is what they begot!)

He means: «أيام إذ نجلاه»; so he separated by the agent «والداه», which is nominative by «أنجب», between the two terms of the construct, which are «أيام إذ ولداه» [Translator's note: so in the source, «ولداه» for «نجلاه»]. Ibn Kharūf said: "Separation between the maṣdar and the muḍāf ilayhi by the object is permissible, because it is not in its own place, but it is not permissible by the agent, because it is in its own place; and on this is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir." I say: this is a distinction between the agent and the object, in that separation by the object was considered good but not by the agent. Of separation by other than what preceded is also separation by the vocative, as in his saying:

2088 - وفاقُ كعبُ بُجَيْرٍ منقِذٌ لك من ... تعجيل مُهْلِكَةٍ والخلدِ في سَقَرَ
(Agreeing with Bujayr, O Kaʿb, will save you from a hastened destruction and from eternity in Saqar.)

and another's saying:

2089 - إذا ما أبا حفصٍ أَتَتْكَ رَأَيْتَها ... على شعراء الناس يعلو قصيدها
(When it comes to you, O Abū Ḥafṣ, you see its odes rise above the poets of mankind.)

and another's saying:

2090 - كأنَّ بِرْذَوْنَ أبا عصامِ ... زيدٍ حمارٌ دُقَّ باللِّجامِ
(As though Zayd's nag, O Abū ʿIṣām, were a donkey hammered into a bridle.)

He means: «وفاق بجيرٍ يا كعب», «وإذا ما أتتك يا أبا حفص», and «وكأن بِرْذون زيدٍ يا أبا عصام». Of separation also is separation by the adjective, as in the saying of Muʿāwiya addressing ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ:

2091 - نَجَوْتَ وقد بَلَّ المُراديُّ سيفَه ... من ابن أبي شيخ الأباطح طالبِ
(You escaped, while the Murādī had wetted his sword with the blood of the son of Abū — the elder of the valleys — Ṭālib.)

and another's saying:

2092 - ولئن حَلَفْتُ على يديكَ لأحْلِفَنْ ... بيمينِ أصدقَ مِنْ يمينك مُقْسِمِ
(If I swear by your hands, I shall swear with the oath — truer than your oath — of one who swears.)

He means: «من ابن أبي طالب شيخ الأباطح»; «شيخ الأباطح» is an adjective of «أبي طالب», by which he separated between «أبي» and «طالب». And he means: «لأحلفن بيمينٍ مقسم أصدقَ مِنْ يمينك»; «أصدق» is an adjective of his saying «بيمين», by which he separated between «يمين» and «مقسم». Of separation also is separation by a cancelled (mulghā) verb:

2093 - ألا يا صاحِبَيَّ قِفا المَهارى ... نسائلْ حيَّ بثنةَ أين سارا
بأيِّ تَرَاهُمُ الأرَضينَ حَلُّوا ... أالدبران أم عَسَفُوا الكِفارا
(O my two companions, halt the swift camels, that we may ask where Buthayna's tribe has gone: in which — do you think — of the lands have they settled? At al-Dabarān, or have they struck out across the wastes?)

He means: «بأي الأرضين تراهم حلُّوا»; so he separated by his saying «تراهم» between «أيّ» and «الأرضين».

Of separation also is separation by an object that is not governed by the maṣdar annexed to its agent, as in the poet's saying:

2094 - تَسْقي امتياحاً ندى المسواكَ ريقتِها ... كما تَضَمَّن ماءَ المُزْنَةِ الرَصفُ
(She gives the tooth-stick to drink, as one draws water, of the dew of her saliva, as the stones of a channel hold the rain-cloud's water.)

i.e. «تسقي ندى ريقتها المسواكَ»; «المسواك» is a direct object made accusative by «تسقي», by which he separated between / «ندى» and «ريقتها». Now that you know this, know that the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir is sound from the point of view of language just as it is sound from the point of view of transmission. No attention is to be paid to the saying of those who said that he relied in this on the script of the Syrian muṣḥaf which ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him, sent, because nothing was found in it except the writing of «شركائهم» with a yāʾ. Even if this suffices to indicate the genitive of «شركائهم», there is nothing in it indicating the accusative of «أولادهم», since the muṣḥaf is devoid of vowel marks and dots; so no proof remains to him for the accusative of «الأولاد» except pure transmission.

It has been transmitted from Ibn ʿĀmir that he read «الأولاد» in the genitive, as its explanation and justification will come. Moreover, the writing «شركائهم» with yāʾ is not exclusive to the Syrian muṣḥaf; rather it is so too in the muṣḥaf of the people of the Ḥijāz. Abū al-Barhasam said: "In Sūrat al-Anʿām, in the master copy (imām) of the people of Syria and the people of the Ḥijāz, «أولادهم شركائهم» is with yāʾ, and in the master copy of the people of Iraq «شركاؤهم». The people of the Ḥijāz did not read «شركائهم» in the genitive, because the script is a followed sunna which the recitation may agree with and may not." However, Shaykh Abū Shāma said: "I say: it was written so only in consideration of two readings: the [form] with ḍamma supports the reading of most readers"; then he said: "As for «شركائهم» in the genitive, it accommodates the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir." This statement of Abū Shāma will come in full in its place; I have taken from it only [as much as] needed here. His saying that every reading follows the script of its muṣḥaf is problematic in view of what I mentioned to you, that the muṣḥaf of the Ḥijāzīs has the yāʾ although they did not read so. Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī transmitted that «شركائهم» with yāʾ is only in the Syrian muṣḥaf, not the muṣḥafs of the other cities; he said: "In the muṣḥafs of the people of Syria «أولادهم شركائهم» is with yāʾ, and in all the other muṣḥafs «شركاؤهم» with wāw." I say: this is what is well known among people — I mean that the yāʾ is exclusive to the Syrian muṣḥafs [Translator's note: the source misprints «الضام» for «الشام»] — but Abū al-Barhasam is also trustworthy, so we accept what he transmits. Al-Zamakhsharī's saying has preceded: "What led him to that was that he saw «شركائهم» written with a yāʾ in some copies of the muṣḥaf."

Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma said: "There is nothing far-fetched in what the grammarians considered far-fetched from the point of view of meaning. That is because the precedence of the object over the agent that is nominative in wording is well known, so this rank continued for it with the agent that is nominative by implication; for if the maṣdar had tanwīn, it would be permissible to put the object before its agent, as in «أعجبني ضربٌ عمراً زيدٌ» ('Zayd's striking of ʿAmr pleased me'), and likewise in the construct. And the permissibility of separation between a preposition and its genitive has been established, despite the bond between them being stronger than the bond between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مَّيثَاقَهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 155] and {فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 159]. «ما» is redundant in wording, so it is as though dropped from it, since it is dropped in meaning; and the object placed first is, in meaning, not in its place, so it is as though placed after in wording. No attention is to be paid to the saying of those who claimed that its like has not come in prose speech, because he is a negator, whereas whoever transmitted this reading with a chain is an affirmer, and affirmation is preferred over negation by consensus. Had it been transmitted to this claimant that some Arab used it in prose, he would have gone back to it; so what is the matter with him that he is not content with the transmitter of the reading from the Successors from the Companions? Then what Ibn al-Anbārī reported" — meaning what was reported earlier of their saying «هو غلامُ إن شاء الله أخيك» — "contains separation outside poetry by a clause."

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, and ʿAbd al-Malik, the judge of the army [Translator's note: «قاضي الجند»; possibly al-Jund in Yemen], the companion of Ibn ʿĀmir, read: «زُيِّن» as passive, «قَتْلُ» nominative as above, «أولادِهم» genitive by the construct, and «شركاؤهم» nominative. There are two explanations of its nominative. The first, the explanation of Sībawayh: that it is nominative by an implied verb, its implied form being «زَيَّنه شركاؤهم» ("their partners made it attractive"); so it is the answer to an implied question, as though it were said: Who made it attractive to them? And it was said: their partners. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: «يُسَبَّح له فيها بالغدوّ والآصال رجال», i.e. men glorify Him; and another's saying:

2095 - ليُبْكَ يزيدٌ ضارعٌ لخصومةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Let Yazīd be wept for — [let] one humbled in a dispute [weep for him]…)

The second, the explanation of Quṭrub: that «شركاؤهم» is nominative as the agent of the maṣdar, the implied form being: "it was made attractive to the polytheists that their partners should kill their children", as you say: / «حُبِّب لي ركوبُ الفرسِ زيدٌ» ("Zayd's riding of the horse was made dear to me"), its implied form being: "it was made dear to me that Zayd should ride the horse". The difference between the two explanations is that the first leads to this reading being, in meaning, like the reading ascribed to the majority, in that the partners make the killing attractive and are not the killers; while the second is [that] the partners are the killers, but that is by way of figurative usage, because when they made their killing attractive to the fathers and were a cause of it, the killing was attributed to them figuratively. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is possible that the killing occurred from them in reality." This is open to question, because of His saying «زُيّن»; a person has only his own action made attractive to him, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {أَفَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُ سواء عَمَلِهِ فَرَآهُ حَسَناً} [Fāṭir: 8].

Someone other than Abū ʿUbayd said: "The people of Syria read like the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, except that they put «الأولاد» in the genitive too." Its explanation is easy: namely that you make «شركائهم» a badal (substitute) for «أولادهم», in the sense that they share with them in lineage, wealth and other things. Al-Zajjāj said: "«شركايهم» with yāʾ has been transmitted in some muṣḥafs, but it is not permissible except on the basis that «شركاؤهم» is an adjective of the children, because their children are their partners in their wealth."

Al-Farrāʾ said, after mentioning the reading of the majority — namely «زَيَّن» as active and «شركاؤهم» nominative as its agent — and the reading of «زُيِّن» as passive with «شركاؤهم» nominative, on the basis given above that it is by an implied verb: "In the muṣḥaf of the people of Syria it is «شركايهم» with yāʾ. If it is established from the earlier generations, then it ought to be read «زُين», and the partners would be the children, because they are of them in lineage and inheritance. If they read «زَيَّن»" — meaning with fatḥa on the zāy — "then I do not know its rationale, unless they were following in it the dialect of a people who say «أتيتها عشايا» and say in the dual of حمراء «حمرايان»; this would be a rationale for their having meant: «زين لكثير من المشركين قتل أولادهم شركايُهم»" — meaning with a yāʾ bearing ḍamma, because «شركاؤهم» is the agent, as in the majority reading. He said: "And if you wish, you can make «زين» a verb which, when you give it fatḥa, causes no confusion, then put «الشركاء» in the genitive by following «الأولاد»." Abū Shāma said: "I say: he means the implied speech is «زَيَّن» in the place of «زُين»; so it is plausible for «شركائهم» in the genitive to be an adjective of «الأولاد», whether «زين» is read with fatḥa or ḍamma."

A group of the people of Syria read — and it is also transmitted from Ibn ʿĀmir — «زِيْنَ», with kasra on the zāy followed by a quiescent yāʾ, as a past passive verb on the model of «قيل» and «بيع»; and «قتلُ» [Translator's note: the source has «وقيل: مرفوعٌ», evidently for «وقتلُ مرفوعٌ»] nominative as that whose agent is not named, «أولادَهم» accusative and «شركائِهم» genitive. The rationale is clear from what preceded; it and the first reading are the same; the most that can be said is that it was taken from the three-letter «زان» and made passive, then underwent the weak-letter change you learned at the beginning of al-Baqara.

The lām in His saying «لكثير من المشركين» is attached to «زين», and likewise the lām in His saying «ليُرْدُوهم». If it is said: how can you attach two prepositions of the same wording and the same meaning to one governing word, without substitution or conjunction? The answer is that their meanings differ: the first is for making transitive and the second for causation. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If the adorning is from the devils, it is for real causation; and if it is from the custodians [of the idols], it is for outcome (ṣayrūra)." He means that Satan performs the adorning and his aim in it is ruin, so the causation in it is clear; whereas the custodians did not make that attractive to them with their aim being to destroy them, but since the end of their state was ruin, He used the lām that indicates consequence and outcome.

His saying «وليَلْبِسوا» is conjoined to «ليُرْدوا»; He gave two causes for the adorning: ruin, and confusing and introducing doubt into their religion. The majority read «وليَلْبِسوا» with kasra on the bāʾ, from «لبَسْت عليه الأمر ألبِسُه», with fatḥa on the middle radical in the past and kasra in the imperfect, when you introduce doubt into it for him and confuse him in it. Its explanation preceded at His saying {ولَلَبَسْنا عليهم ما يَلْبِسون} [al-Anʿām: 9]. Al-Nakhaʿī read «وليلبَسوا» with fatḥa on the bāʾ. It was said: it is a dialectal form in the meaning mentioned; you say «لَبَِسْتُ عليه الأمر», with fatḥa and kasra on the bāʾ, «ألبِسه» and «ألبَسه». The correct view is that لَبِس with kasra is in the sense of / wearing clothes, and with fatḥa in the sense of confusing. So the correct view is that He borrowed [the idea of] clothing for the intensity of the intermingling arising between them and the confusion, until it was as though they wore it like clothes and it became something encompassing them.

His saying: «ما فعلوه»: the nominative pronoun is for «الكثير» and the accusative for the killing, because it is explicitly mentioned and because it is what the discourse is driven to speak about. And it was said: the nominative is for the partners and the accusative for the adorning. And it was said: the accusative is for the confusing understood from the verb before it; this is far-fetched. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "[Had Allah willed,] the polytheists would not have done what was made attractive to them of the killing; or the devils or the custodians would not have done the adorning, or the ruining, or the confusing, or all of that, if you make the pronoun function like a demonstrative."

His saying {فَذَرْهُمْ وَمَا يَفْتَرُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 112]: its parallel has preceded.

semin-durr:138-138.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَنْعَامٌ}: The majority read it thus, in the plural form; Abān ibn ʿUthmān read «نَعَمٌ» in the singular, which is close, because a generic noun stands in the place of the plural. The majority read «حِجْر» with kasra on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the jīm. al-Ḥasan, Qatāda and al-Aʿraj read it with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the jīm. It is also reported from al-Ḥasan and Qatāda with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the jīm. It is reported from Abān ibn ʿUthmān with ḍamma on both the ḥāʾ and the jīm. Hārūn said: "al-Ḥasan used to put ḍamma on the ḥāʾ of «حجر» wherever it occurs in the Qur'an, except in one place, which is: {وَحِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً} [al-Furqān: 53]." The upshot is that this root indicates prevention and confinement; hence "so-and-so is in the ḥijr of the judge", i.e. in his custody (prevention), and "in my ḥijr", i.e. what the lap of a garment holds back so that nothing slips out of it. The verification of this was given earlier in (Sūrat) al-Nisāʾ. So His saying {وَحَرْثٌ حِجْرٌ} means "forbidden"; so «فِعْل» (fiʿl) has the sense of «مفعول» (passive participle), like «الذِّبْح» and «النِّطْح» in the sense of "slaughtered" and "gored". If it is asked: two things have been mentioned before, namely «أنعام» and «حرث», yet the adjective is brought in the singular? The answer is that in origin it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the maṣdar is kept masculine and singular in every case. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural are alike in being described by it, because its rule is the rule of nouns, not adjectives." I say: by "its rule is the rule of nouns" he means that it is in origin a maṣdar, not an adjective; the noun here is intended to mean the maṣdar, which is the opposite of the adjective.
As for the remaining readings, Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "They are dialectal variants of the word", and he explained its meaning as "forbidden". I say: it is possible that the one with ḍamma on both the ḥāʾ and the jīm is a maṣdar, for among the maṣdars of the triliteral verb there are some on the pattern fuʿul with ḍamma on the fāʾ and on the ʿayn, such as «حُلُم». It is also possible that it is the plural of «حَجْر» with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the jīm, since fuʿul has occurred, rarely, as a plural of faʿl, such as «سَقْف» with plural «سُقُف» and «رَهْن» with plural «رُهُن»; or that it is a plural of fiʿl with kasra on the fāʾ, since fuʿul has also occurred as a plural of fiʿl with kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn, such as «حِدْج» with plural «حُدُج». As for «حُجْر» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the jīm, it is a shortened form of the one with both ḍammas, so it may be a maṣdar, or a plural of «حَجْر» or «حِجْر». Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, ʿIkrima, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār and al-Aʿmash read: «حِرْج» with kasra on the ḥāʾ and a sākin rāʾ placed before the jīm. There are two interpretations of it. One is that it comes from the root «الحَرَج», which is constriction. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Its origin is «حَرِج» with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, but it was lightened and shifted, like «فَخْذ» for «فخِذ»." I say: there is no need to claim that; rather, this came by way of original form on the pattern fiʿl. The second is that it is transposed (maqlūb) from «حجر», the lām of the word being put before its ʿayn, its pattern being filʿ, as they say «ناء» for «نأى» and «معيق» for «عميق»; transposition is rare in their language.
I have already given a good deal on it at His saying, the Exalted, «أشياء» in (Sūrat) al-Māʾida.
His saying: {لاَّ يَطْعَمُهَآ إِلاَّ مَن نَّشَآءُ}: This clause is in the position of nominative as an adjective (naʿt) of «أنعام». They described it with two descriptions: one, that it is forbidden (ḥijr); the second, that none eats it except whom they wish, namely the men and not the women, or the custodians of the idols. «من يشاء» is the agent (fāʿil) of «يَطْعَمُها», and it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), and «بزعمهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), as in its counterpart earlier.
His saying: «افتراءً»: there are four aspects to it. First, which is the view of Sībawayh, that it is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. they said what preceded for the sake of fabricating against the Creator, the Exalted. Second: a maṣdar not from the verb's own root (ʿalā ghayr al-maṣdar), because their saying that is reported of them is a fabrication, so it is like «قعد القرفصاء» ("he sat squatting"); this is the view of al-Zajjāj. Third: a maṣdar whose governing verb, of the same root, is omitted, i.e. "they fabricated that a fabrication". Fourth: a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "they said that while fabricating"; it resembles the confirmatory ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), since this particular statement can only be made by someone fabricating. His saying «على الله» may be attached to «افتراء» according to the first and fourth views; according to the second and third it is attached to «قالوا», not to «افتراء», because a confirmatory maṣdar does not govern. It may also be attached to an omitted word as an adjective of «افتراء», and this is permissible on every one of the preceding views. His saying «بما كانوا»: the bāʾ is causal, and «ما» is either maṣdariyya, or indefinite (mawṣūfa), or has the sense of «الذي» ("that which").

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلنَآ إلى أُمَمٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ}: There is an omission in the discourse, its implied form being: "We sent messengers to nations, and they denied them, so We seized them." This omission is entirely obvious. «مِنْ قبلك» is attached to «أَرْسَلْنا». As for making it an adjective (naʿt) of «أمم», there is discussion that has come before more than once. The explanation of «البأساء» and «الضرَّاء» has also come before; no masculine form on the pattern afʿal is pronounced for either of them.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فلولا إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا تَضَرَّعُواْ}: «إذ» is accusative (manṣūb) by «تَضرَّعوا»; it separates the particle of urging (ḥarf al-taḥḍīḍ) from what it governs, and this is permissible even with a direct object (mafʿūl bihi); you say «لولا زيداً ضَرَبْتَ». It has already been mentioned that the particle of urging with the past tense has the meaning of reproach.

«التضرُّع» is the form taFaʿʿul from «الضراعة», which is abasement and the state caused by submission to obedience. One says «ضَرَع يَضْرَعُ ضَراعة», so he is «ضارعٌ», and also «ضَرِع». The poet said:

192 - 7- لِيُبْكَ يزيدُ ضارعٌ لخصومَةٍ ... ومختبطٌ ممَّا تُطيح الطوائِحُ
(Let Yazīd be wept for by one abased in a dispute, and by one who comes begging, because of what calamities carry away.)

Because of the softness and submissiveness understood from this root, they derived from it a name for the udder and called it «ضَرْعاً».

His saying: {ولكن قَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ}: «لكنْ» here occurs between two opposites, namely gentleness and hardness. That is because His saying «تَضَرَّعوا» signals gentleness and softness. Likewise, if you take submission (ḍarāʿa) to be an expression for faith, and hardness for disbelief, expressing the cause by the effect and the effect by the cause. Do you not see that you say: «آمَنَ قلبُه فتضرَّع» ("his heart believed, so he humbled himself") and «قسا قلبه فكفر» ("his heart hardened, so he disbelieved")? This is better than the statement of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «ولكن» is a correction (istidrāk) in meaning, i.e. "they did not humble themselves, but ...", meaning that the urging has the meaning of negation. This may be given preference by what al-Zamakhsharī said, for he said: "Its meaning is the negation of humbling oneself, as if it were said: 'They did not humble themselves when Our punishment came to them'; but it came with «لولا» to convey that they had no excuse for abandoning humility except the hardness of their hearts and their admiration of their deeds, which Satan made attractive to them."

His saying: {وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ}: This clause admits two aspects. One: that it is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); the Exalted informs about them with that. The second, which is the apparent one: that it falls within the scope of the istidrāk, so it is conjoined to His saying {قَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ}. This is the opinion of al-Zamakhsharī, who said: "They had no excuse for abandoning humility except the hardness of their hearts and their admiration of their deeds," as already mentioned. As for «ما» in His saying {مَا كَانُواّ}, it may be a relative noun (mawṣūl ismī), i.e. "that which they used to do", or it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He made their deed attractive to them", like His saying {زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ} [النمل: 4]. It is remote to make it an indefinite noun with a description.

«Translator's note: the source text reads «الاستدارك» and «استنافية» (for «الاستدراك» and «استئنافية») in this passage; translated as intended.»

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَتَحْنَا}: The majority read «فَتَحْنا» with light (unreduplicated) tā, while Ibn ʿĀmir read «فتَّحنا» with the doubled consonant. The doubling signals intensity or multiplicity, because after it comes «أبواب» ("doors"), so multiplicity is fitting; the light form is the original. Ibn ʿĀmir also read with doubling in al-Aʿrāf {لَفَتَحْنَا} [الآية: 96] and in al-Qamar {فَفَتَحْنَآ أَبْوَابَ} [الآية: 11]; he also doubled {فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ} [الأنبياء: 96]. The disagreement also concerns {فُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا} [الآيتين: 71، 73] in al-Zumar, in both places, and {وَفُتِحَتِ السمآء} [الآية: 19] in al-Nabaʾ; the group agreed with Ibn ʿĀmir in doubling these, and only the Kufans read them with the light form. So Ibn ʿĀmir followed one pattern with this verb, while the others doubled in the three places indicated and lightened elsewhere, combining the two dialects.

His saying: {فَإِذَا هُمْ مُّبْلِسُونَ}: «إذا» is the one of suddenness (fujāʾiyya), and there are three positions about it. The position of Sībawayh is that it is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān); the position of a group of them, among them al-Riyāshī, is that it is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān); and the position of the Kufans is that it is a particle. On the assumption that it is an adverb of place or time, what governs it is the predicate (khabar) of the subject (mubtadaʾ), i.e. "they were made despondent in the place of their residence" or "in its time".

«الإِبلاسُ» is lowering the head (silent dejection); it was also said to be the grief that befalls from the intensity of despair, and from it «إبليس» is derived, which has been dealt with in its place, including whether it is non-Arabic or not.

His saying: {فَقُطِعَ دَابِرُ}: The majority read «فَقُطِع» as passive; «دابر» is nominative (marfūʿ) by it. ʿIkrima read «قطع» as active, the agent being Allah the Exalted, with «دابر» a direct object (mafʿūl bihi); this involves an iltifāt (shift of person), since it is a departure from the first person in «أخذناهم» to the third. «الدابِرُ» is the follower from behind; one says «دَبَر الولدُ والدَه» ("the child followed his father"), and «دَبَر فلان القوم يَدْبُرُهم دُبُوراً ودَبْراً». It was also said: «الدابِر» is the root; one says «قطع الله دابِرَه», i.e. its root; so said al-Aṣmaʿī. Abū ʿUbayd said: "The dābir of a people is their last." They recited the verse of Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt:

192 - 8- فاستُؤْصِلوا بعذابٍ حَصَّ دابِرَهُمْ ... فما استطاعوا له صَرْفاً ولا انتصروا
(So they were uprooted by a punishment that cut off their rear; they were unable to turn it away, nor were they given victory.)

From it: «دَبَر السهمُ الهدفَ», i.e. the arrow fell behind the target.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخَذَ الله}: The first object is omitted, its implied form being: "Have you considered your hearing and your sight, if Allah takes them away?" The interrogative clause is in the position of the second. It has already been mentioned that the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) makes this a case of conflict of governors (tanāzuʿ). The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, along the lines already given. Al-Ḥawfī said: "The conditional particle and what is attached to it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the governor of the ḥāl is «أرأيتم», like your saying «اضربه إن خرج», i.e. 'while going out'; and the apodosis is what precedes, that which the interrogative hamza entered." This is an i'rab that is not apparent.

The address kāf is not brought here, whereas it was brought there, because the threat there is greater, so emphasis by bringing the address kāf was fitting. And since the kāf is not brought, the plural marker must appear in the tāʾ so that there is no confusion; had the kāf been brought with it, it would have sufficed, as already mentioned. The singular «السمع» and the plural «الأبصار» is understood from what came before in al-Baqara.

His saying: {مَّنْ إله}: a subject and predicate (mubtadaʾ and khabar). «مَنْ» is interrogative, «وغيرُ الله» is an adjective of «إلهٌ», and «يأتيكم» is a second adjective. The hāʾ in «به» refers back to «سمعكم». It was also said that it refers to all of them, and is singular following the way of the demonstrative. It was said that it refers to the guidance (hudā) indicated by the meaning. It was said that it refers to what was taken and sealed, which are indicated by the taking and the sealing. The interrogative here is for denial.

His saying: {انظر كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ}: «كيف» is governed by «نصرِّف», and its accusative case is either by resemblance to a ḥāl or by resemblance to an adverb (ẓarf). It suspends the effect (muʿallaqa) of «انظر», so it is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition. All this is apparent from what preceded. «ويَصْدِفون» means "they turn away"; one says «صَدَف عن الشيء صَدْفاً وصُدُوفاً وصدافِيَةً». ʿAdī ibn al-Riqāʿ said:

192 - 9- إذا ذكرْنَ حديثاً قُلْنَ أحسنَه ... وهُنَّ عن كل سوءٍ يُتَّقى صُدُفُ
(When they relate a story, they tell its best; and they turn away from every evil to be guarded against.)

«صُدُف» is the plural of «صَدُوف», like «صُبُر» as the plural of «صبور». It was also said that the meaning of «صدف» is "to incline", taken from «الصَّدَف» in a camel, which is the hoof's inclining from the foreleg toward the hind leg on the outer side. «الصَّدَف» is also the plural of «صَدَفة», the shell in which the pearl is found. He said:

193 - 0- وزادَها عَجَباً أَنْ رُحْتُ في سُبُلٍ ... وما دَرَتْ دَوَرَان الدُّرِّ في الصَّدَفِ
(It increased her wonder that I went along paths, and she knew not the turning of the pearl in the shell.)

«الصَّدَف» and «الصُّدُف», with fatḥa on the ṣād and dāl, or ḍamma on both, and with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the dāl, is a side of the high mountain; more explanation of this will come.

The majority read «به انظر» with kasra on the hāʾ, as the original; al-Musayyibī related from Nāfiʿ «بهُ انظر» with ḍamma on it, looking to the original. The majority also read {نُصَرِّف} with doubling; «نَصْرِف» with kasra on the rāʾ, from the triliteral «صرف», was read as an irregular reading.

His saying: {هَلْ يُهْلَكُ}: This is an interrogative with the meaning of negation; for that reason «إلاَّ» entered, and it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh); the implied meaning: "None is destroyed except the wrongdoing people." This interrogative clause is in the position of the second object of «أرأيتكم», the first being omitted, and this is a case of tanāzuʿ on the Shaykh's view, as its explanation has gone before. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The interrogative here has the meaning of affirmation (taqrīr), therefore it takes the place of the apodosis, i.e. 'if it comes to you, you will be destroyed'," but the apparent is what I presented earlier. Al-Ḥawfī's statement mentioned in the previous verse, about the condition being a ḥāl, comes here too. Ibn Muḥayṣin read {هل يَهْلَكُ} as active (with fatḥa on the yā and lām). The discussion of «بَغْتة», in derivation and i'rab, has also gone before.

«Translator's note: the source says "مبنياً للفاعل" for Ibn Muḥayṣin's reading «يَهْلَكُ»; I have translated it as written and added the vocalization description in parentheses as my own clarification.»

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المرسلين». In this ḥāl is a sense of predominance, i.e. "We did not send them so that signs be demanded of them, but so that they give glad tidings and warn." Ibrāhīm and Yaḥyā read «مُبْشِرين» with the light form; it has already been mentioned that «أَبْشَر» is a dialectal variant of «بَشَّر».

His saying: {فَمَنْ آمَنَ}: «مَنْ» may be conditional (sharṭiyya) or relative (mawṣūla). On both assumptions its position is nominative as a subject (mubtadaʾ), and the predicate is «فلا خوف». If it is conditional, the fāʾ is the fāʾ of the apodosis; if it is relative, the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), because of the resemblance of the relative to the condition. On the first assumption the position of the two clauses is jussive; on the second, the first has no position and the position of the second is nominative. It is treated according to the form, so «آمن» and «اصلَح» are singular, and according to the meaning, so it is plural in {فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ}. That it is relative is strengthened by its being set against the relative after it in His saying {والذين كَذَّبوا}.

semin-durr:49-49.t: ʿAlqama read {نُمسُّهم} with a nūn with ḍamma, from «أَمَسَّه كذا», with «العذابَ» accusative; and al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read «يَفْسِقون» with kasra on the sīn, which has already been mentioned to be a dialect. «ما» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the most apparent view, i.e. "because of their wickedness".

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {ولا أَعْلَمُ الغيب}: There are two aspects regarding the position of this clause. The first: accusative, conjoined to His saying «عندي خزائنُ الله», because it is part of what is said, as if He said: "I do not say this statement to you, nor this statement." So said al-Zamakhsharī. There is something to examine in it, in that it leads to the implied meaning becoming "and I do not say to you: I do not know the unseen", which is not correct. The second: that it is conjoined to «لا أقول», not governed by it, so he was commanded to inform about himself with these three clauses, and they are governed by the command which is «قل». This is the Shaykh's derivation; after reporting the statement of al-Zamakhsharī he said: "What he said is not necessarily so; rather the apparent is that it is conjoined to «ألاَّ أقول» up to the end."

«Translator's note: the source spells al-Zamakhsharī as «الزمشخري» here.»

semin-durr:139-139.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {خَالِصَةٌ}: The majority read «خالصة» with the feminine ending, nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of the relative «ما». The feminine is either by construing according to the meaning, because what is in the bellies of the cattle is cattle, and then construing according to its form in His saying «ومحرَّم»; or because the feminine is for intensification, as in «عَلاَّمة», «نسَّابة» and «راوية»; or because «خالصة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern fāʿila, like «العاقبة» and «العافية». The Exalted said: {بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدار} [Ṣād: 46]. This latter view is that of al-Farrāʾ, and the first is also his and that of Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj; the second is that of al-Kisāʾī. If it is said to be a maṣdar, that is on the omission of a muḍāf (head of a genitive construct), i.e. "possessor of purity", or on the basis of intensification, or on the maṣdar standing in the place of the active participle, as with its counterparts. The poet said:
2096 - وكنتِ أُمْنِيَّتي وكنتِ خالصتي ... وليس كلُّ امرِئٍ بمؤتمنِ
(You were my heart's wish and you were my sincere confidante... yet not every man is to be trusted.)
This is widespread in their speech: "so-and-so is my khāliṣa", i.e. possessor of my sincerity. «لذكورنا» is attached to it, and it may be attached to an omitted word as a description of «خالصة», though that is not strong.
ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd), Ibn Jubayr, Abū l-ʿĀliya, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «خالص» in the nominative, on what has preceded, without the tāʾ marbūṭa. «لذكورنا» is attached to it or to an omitted word, as before. Ibn Jubayr also read, in what Ibn Jinnī reports from him, «خالصاً» in the accusative without the tāʾ; its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its owner (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) has two possibilities, the more apparent being that it is the latent pronoun in the ṣila (relative clause).
