The second: that it is the latent pronoun in «لذكورنا», for on this reading «لذكورنا» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject); this is permissible only according to the school of Abū l-Ḥasan (al-Akhfash), because he allows the ḥāl to precede its governing word when that is abstract (maʿnawī), as in «زيد مستقراً في الدار», whereas the majority forbid it. The verification of this question, with its details and proofs, has already been given.
Ibn ʿAbbās also, and al-Aʿraj and Qatāda, read «خالصةً» in the accusative with the feminine ending; the discussion of its accusative and its feminine is as in its counterpart earlier. al-Zamakhsharī analysed it as a confirmatory maṣdar like «العاقبة». Ibn ʿAbbās also, and Abū Razīn, ʿIkrima and Abū Ḥaywa, read: «خالصُه» with «خالص» nominative, annexed to the pronoun of «ما». Its nominative is in one of two ways: either as a badal (substitute) for the relative, a badal of part from whole (badal baʿḍ min kull), with «لذكورنا» as the khabar of the relative; or as a mubtadaʾ with «لذكورنا» as its khabar, the clause being the khabar of the relative. You have learned from what has preceded that where we say «خالصة» is a maṣdar or is for intensification, there is in the sentence no construing first by meaning and then by form; and if we say that the feminine in it is because of the femininity of what is in the bellies, then in the sentence there is construing by meaning first and then by form in His saying «مُحَرَّمٌ» second, and there is no parallel for this in the Qur'an, I mean construing by meaning first and then by form.
However, Makkī claimed, in a work other than his «Iʿrāb al-Qurʾān», that this verse has parallels, and he listed them; but in his iʿrāb he did not mention that anything else in the Qur'an shares it in this. He said in his iʿrāb: "He made the khabar feminine only because what is in the bellies of the cattle is cattle, so the feminine was construed by meaning; then he said «ومُحَرَّمٌ» in the masculine, construing by the form of «ما». This is rare and has no parallel; what usually happens with «مَنْ» and «ما» is that the speech is first construed by form and then by meaning afterwards. Mark that, for it is rare." And in the other work he said: "This verse, in the reading of the group, came contrary to its counterparts in the Qur'an, because everything that is construed once by form and once by meaning begins first with construing by form, followed by construing by meaning, as in {مَنْ آمَنَ بالله} [al-Baqara: 62], then He said «فلهم أجرُهم»; so it occurs in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs. In this verse construing by meaning came first, so He said «خالصة», and then it was construed by form, so He said «ومُحرَّمٌ». Similar is {كُلُّ ذلك كَانَ سَيِّئُةً} [al-Isrāʾ: 38] in the reading of Nāfiʿ and those who followed him: he made it feminine according to the meaning of «كل», because it is a noun for all that has preceded of the sins that were forbidden, then He said «عند ربك مكروهاً», making it masculine according to the form of «كل». Likewise {مَا تَرْكَبُونَ لِتَسْتَوُواْ على ظُهُورِهِ} [al-Zukhruf: 13]: He made «ظهور» plural, construing by the meaning of «ما», and made the hāʾ singular, construing by the form of «ما». And it is related from the Arabs: «هذا الجرادُ قد ذهب فأراحنا مِنْ أَنْفُسِه» ("This locust swarm has gone and relieved us of its selves"), where he made «الأنفس» plural and made the hāʾ singular and masculine."
I say: As for his saying "so it occurs in the Qur'an", that is correct; but as for his saying "and in the speech of the Arabs", that is not conceded, for in the speech of the Arabs one may begin with construing by meaning and then by form, even if the reverse is the more frequent. As for what he made a parallel to this verse in construing by meaning first and by form second, that too is not conceded; likewise we do not concede that this verse is one in which construing was by meaning first and then by form. The explanation is that someone could say: the ṣila of «ما» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted word, and you would then imply it as predicated of a masculine pronoun, i.e. "what is settled in the bellies of these cattle", while its implication as «استقرَّت» (feminine) is remote. Once this is known, he would have construed first by form in the implied ṣila and then by meaning second. As for «كل ذلك كان سَيِّئةً», he also began there with construing by form in His saying «كان», for he made masculine its latent pronoun in «كان», then construed by meaning in His saying «سيِّئة», making it feminine.
Likewise «لتَسْتَووا»: before it is «ما تركبون», the implied form being «ما تركبونه»; so the omitted returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is construed by form first and then by meaning second. Likewise in their saying «هذا الجراد قد ذهب» it was construed by form, so the pronoun in «ذهب» is singular, and then by meaning second, so he made plural His saying «أنفسه». In these places, construing is first by form, then by meaning, then by form. I had already mentioned that there are three more such places in the Qur'an: the verse of al-Māʾida [verse 60]: {وَعَبَدَ الطاغوت}, Luqmān [verse 6]: {وَمِنَ الناس مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الحديث}, and al-Ṭalāq [verse 11]: {وَمَن يُؤْمِن بالله}.
His saying: {وَإِن يَكُن مَّيْتَةً}: Ibn Kathīr read «يكن» with the yāʾ of the third person masculine and «مَيْتَةٌ» nominative; Ibn ʿĀmir: «تكن» with the feminine tāʾ and «ميتة» nominative; ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Abū Bakr: «تكن» with the feminine tāʾ and «ميتةً» accusative; and the rest: «تكن» like Ibn Kathīr and «ميتةً» like Abū Bakr. The masculine and the feminine are both clear, because «الميتة» is a figurative feminine, since it applies to both the male and the female among animals; whoever made it feminine did so by the form, and whoever made it masculine did so by the meaning. This is according to the one who makes «ميتة» nominative with «تكن». As for the one who makes it accusative, he then assigns the verb to a pronoun, making it masculine in view of the form of «ما» in His saying «ما في بطون», and feminine in view of its meaning. And whoever puts «ميتة» in the accusative does so as the khabar of the incomplete (nāqiṣa) kāna. Whoever makes it nominative has two possibilities: one, that it is the complete (tāmma) kāna, which is the apparent, i.e. "if a dead one exists or comes about"; and that it is the incomplete, in which case its khabar is omitted, i.e. "if there is there, or in the bellies, a dead one"; this is the opinion of al-Akhfash. So the implied form of Ibn Kathīr's reading is "if a dead animal comes about" or "if there is a dead one in the bellies", according to the two implications, complete and incomplete; the implied form of Ibn ʿĀmir's reading is like that of his reading, except that he made the verb feminine in view of the form of its subject; the implied form of Abū Bakr's reading is "if the cattle or the embryos are dead", so he made it feminine by construing by meaning; and the reading of the rest is like the implied form of his reading except that they made it masculine in view of the form. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "What strengthens this reading", meaning the reading with masculine and accusative, "is His saying «فهم فيه» and He did not say «فيها»." This was rejected against Abū ʿAmr, since «الميتة» is for every dead thing, male or female, so it is as though it were said "if it be dead, they are partners in it"; that is, he has no proof in the masculine pronoun in «فيه».
al-Zamakhsharī reported Ibn ʿĀmir's reading from the people of Mecca, saying: "The people of Mecca read «وإن تكنْ ميتةٌ» with the feminine and the nominative." If by the people of Mecca he meant Ibn Kathīr, and I do not think he meant him, then it is not so; and if he meant someone else, it is possible, given that it is possible that Ibn Kathīr also read it with the feminine, though that was not as well known from him as the masculine. Yazīd read «مَيِّتة» with shadda. ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) read: «فهم فيه سواء», and I think it is an explanation, not a reading, because it contradicts the codex (al-sawād).

semin-durr:140-140.t: His saying, the Exalted: {قَدْ خَسِرَ الذين قتلوا}: This is the response to an omitted oath. Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir, and it is the reading of al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, read «قَتَّلوا» with shadda for intensification and multiplication; the rest read it without shadda. «سفهاً» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "possessors of foolishness"; or as a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), though this is remote, because it is not a motivating cause; or as a maṣdar of an implied verb, i.e. "they acted foolishly foolishly"; or as a maṣdar not from the verb's own root, because this killing is foolishness. al-Yamānī read «سُفَهاء» in the plural, and it is a ḥāl; this strengthens the view that the reading of the common people is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, since he made it explicit. «بغير علم» is either also a ḥāl, or an adjective of «سفهاً», though it is not so.

semin-durr:141-141.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مُخْتَلِفاً أُكُلُهُ}: It is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and there are two views on it. One: that it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because the date palm and the crops at the time of their coming forth have no produce (akl) in them, such that it could be said of it that it is uniform or varied; so it is like His saying {فادخلوها خَالِدِينَ} [al-Zumar: 73] and like their saying «مررتُ برجلٍ معه صقرٌ صائداً به غداً» ("I passed a man with a falcon with him, hunting with it tomorrow"), i.e. intending to hunt with it. The second: that it is a concomitant ḥāl, on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "and the fruit of the date palm and the grain of the crops". «أُكُلُه» is nominative by «مختلفاً», because it is an active participle and the conditions for its governing are present. «الأُكُل» is the thing eaten; it has already been mentioned that it is read with ḍamma on the kāf and with sukūn, and its verification was given in (Sūrat) al-Baqara.
As for the pronoun in «أُكُله»: the apparent is that it refers to the crops only, either because a ḥāl was omitted for the date palm, indicated by this one, its implied form being "and the date palm, its produce varied, and the crops, their produce varied"; or because the crops are where the variation is apparent in respect of what is eaten from them, such as wheat, barley, fava beans, chickpeas, lentils and so on. It is also said that it refers to both. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun refers to the date palm, and the crops are included in its rule since they are conjoined to it." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "That is not good, because conjunction with wāw does not allow a singular pronoun for the two conjoined items." al-Ḥawfī said: "The hāʾ in «أكلُه» refers to the mention of these planted things that have preceded", and on what al-Ḥawfī mentioned, the ḥāl is not restricted to the date palm and the crops but belongs to all that has preceded.
The Shaykh said: "If it were as he claims, the construction would be «أكلها» (feminine), unless that is taken on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. 'the fruit of gardens', and this omitted word is respected, so «أُكُلُه» was said in the singular in regard to it; that would then be like His saying «أو كظلمات في بحر لُجِّيٍّ يغشاه موج», i.e. 'or like the possessor of darknesses'; and for that reason he returned the pronoun in «يغشاه» to it." I say: Then the implied form remains "varied, the produce of the fruit of the gardens and of what follows them", and this entails the annexation of a thing to itself, because «الأُكُل», as has been said more than once, is the fruit that is eaten. al-Zamakhsharī said of «الأكل»: "It is its fruit which is eaten." Ibn al-Anbārī said: "«مختلفاً» is accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off), as if he had said: 'the date palm and the crops, whose produce is varied'", and this is the opinion of the Kufans, whose clarification has been given more than once.
And His saying: {والزيتون والرمان} up to His saying: {إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ} has already been clarified.
His saying «حصادِه»: Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, and the rest with kasra; they are two dialectal forms of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as in their saying «جَداد» and «جِداد», «قَطاف» and «قِطاف», «حَران» and «حِران». Sībawayh said: "They brought the maṣdar, when they meant the end of the time, on the pattern fiʿāl, and they sometimes said faʿāl in it." He means that this is a specific maṣdar indicating a meaning additional to the unrestricted maṣdar, for the original maṣdar is only «الحصد»; «الحصد» contains no indication of the end of a time or its absence, unlike «الحَصاد» and «الحِصاد».
al-Farrāʾ attributed the kasra to the people of the Hijaz, and the fatḥa to Tamīm and Najd. Abū ʿUbayd preferred the fatḥa, saying: "for grandness, although the other is widespread and not rejected", and Makkī preferred the kasra, saying: "because it is the original and most of the group follow it."
His saying {يَوْمَ حَصَادِهِ} has two aspects. One: that it is accusative by «آتوا», i.e. "give what is due from it on the day of its harvest". Some people found this problematic, in that the giving takes place only after cleaning, so how can giving be obligatory on the day of harvest? The answer is that there is an omitted word there and the implied form is "until its cleaning"; they said: the harvest is then the cause of the extended obligation, and the cleaning is the cause of payment. Better than this is that the meaning be: "be careful to give the obligatory zakāt on it and intend it on that day."
The second: that it is accusative by the word «حقه», in the sense: "and give what is due from it on the day of its harvest", so the entitlement is established on the day of the harvest and the payment is after cleaning; this is supported by the implication of the omitted word by some, as I have presented. And He said in the counterpart of this verse: {انظروا إلى ثَمَرِهِ} [al-Anʿām: 99], while in this one «كُلُوا». It is said: because the first was set forth to indicate the perfection of His power and the restoration of bodies from the coccyx (ʿajb al-dhanab), so He commanded looking and reflecting on the beginning and the end; whereas this was set forth in the context of the perfection of grace, so the command to eat was fitting. From the two verses together results benefit both in the hereafter and in this world, and this is the reason for looking preceding the command to eat.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {بالغداة}: The majority read «بالغداة» here and in al-Kahf, while Ibn ʿĀmir read {بالغُدْوة} with ḍamma on the ghayn, sukūn on the dāl and fatḥa on the wāw, in both places. This is also the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Mālik ibn Dīnār, Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim al-Laythī. The better-known view about «الغُدْوة» is that it is definite by being a proper name (ʿalam), a generic proper name like «أسامة» among persons, and for that reason it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf). Al-Farrāʾ said: "I heard Abū al-Jarrāḥ say: 'I have never seen the like of ghudwa,' meaning the ghadāh of his day." He said: "Do you not see that the Arabs do not make it the first term of an annexation, and likewise the alif and lām do not enter it? They only say: 'I came to you on the ghadāh of Thursday.'" Al-Farrāʾ said in his book al-Maʿānī, in Sūrat al-Kahf: "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read {بالغُدْوَة والعَشِي}, and I do not know anyone who read it so other than him. The Arabs do not bring the alif and lām into «الغدوة», because it is definite without alif and lām." Then he mentioned it to the end.

Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām criticized this reading and said: "We only see that Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Sulamī read that reading following the script; yet the writing of the wāw in the codex is no evidence for reading with it, for they wrote «الصلاة» and «الزكاة» with a wāw while their pronunciation is without it, and likewise «الغداة»; this is how we found the Arabs." Al-Fārisī said: "The preferable aspect is the reading of the common readers, «بالغداة», because it is used both as indefinite and as definite with the lām. As for «غُدْوَة», it is definite and a proper name set for definiteness, and being so, the alif and lām for definiteness should not enter it, just as they do not enter the other proper names, even if it was written with a wāw, since that does not prove it. Do you not see «الصلاة» and «الزكاة» with the wāw and they are not read with it? Likewise «الغداة». Sībawayh said: 'ghudwa and bukra: each of them was made a name for a time, as they made «أم حُبَيْن» a name for a known animal.'" However, this criticism is not to be heeded. How could one suppose that those of earlier times were making grammatical errors? Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī is among those whose speech, let alone his reading, is cited as evidence; Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, the teacher of the grammarians, took this knowledge from Abū al-Aswad, the fountainhead of the craft; and Ibn ʿĀmir does not know solecism because he was an Arab, and he read to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and other Companions. But Abū ʿUbayd, may Allah have mercy on him, did not know that making «غدوة» indefinite is a second dialect from the Arabs, which Sībawayh and al-Khalīl related.

Sībawayh said: "Al-Khalīl claimed that it is permissible to say «أَتيتُكَ اليوم غُدْوةً وبُكْرة»," making it like «ضَحْوة». Al-Mahdawī said: "Sībawayh and al-Khalīl related that some of them make it indefinite and say «غُدْوةً» with tanwīn, and in this way Ibn ʿĀmir read it, as if he made it indefinite and so brought the alif and lām into it." Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: "The aspect of the alif and lām entering it is that it is permissible, even though it is definite, to make it indefinite, as Abū Zayd related: «لقيته فَيْنَةَ» (not declined), and «الفَيْنَةَ بعد الفينة», i.e. time after time. So the lām of definiteness was attached to what was used as definite. The aspect of that is that indefiniteness and generality is assumed in it, just as it is assumed when it is built."

Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās said: "Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Mālik ibn Dīnār and Ibn ʿĀmir read «بالغُدْوة»." He said: "The rule for ghudwa is that it is definite, except that it can be made indefinite, as proper names are made indefinite; so when made indefinite, the alif and lām for definiteness enter it." Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: "The alif and lām entered «غداة» only because it is indefinite. Most Arabs make «غُدوة» definite and do not give it tanwīn, and all of them make «غداة» indefinite and give it tanwīn; and among them are those who make «غُدْوة» indefinite, and they are the fewer." So these reports which I have mentioned from these leading authorities establish that Ibn ʿĀmir's reading is free from Abū ʿUbayd's criticism, and it is as if he, may Allah have mercy on him, did not preserve it as a dialect.

As for «العَشِيُّ», it is indefinite, and likewise «عَشِيَّة». Is «العَشِيُّ» synonymous with «عِشِيَّة»? That is, does this word have two dialects, masculine and feminine, or is «عَشِيّاً» the plural of «عَشِيَّة» in meaning, along the lines of «قمح وقمحة» and «شعير وشعيرة», so that it is a generic noun? This is a well-known disagreement. The apparent is the first, because of His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بالعشي الصافنات} [ص: 31], since what is meant here is one evening. The codices of the provinces agree on writing this word «الغدوة» with a wāw. It has already been mentioned to you that Ibn ʿĀmir's reading does not rest on mere orthography but on transmission. There are also words on which there is agreement that they are written with a wāw and read with an alif, namely: «الصلاة» and «الزكاة» and «مَنَاة» and «مِشْكاة» and «الربا» and «النجاة» and «الحياة»; and one word on which there is agreement that it is written with a wāw while the reading with alif or wāw differs, namely «الغداة». The origin of «غداة» is «غَدَوَة»: the wāw was vowelled and what precedes it had fatḥa, so it was turned into alif. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «بالغَدَوات والعَشِيَّات», plural of «غداة» and «عشية». It was also transmitted from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān «بالغدوِّ» with doubled wāw and no hāʾ (tā marbūṭa).

His saying: {يُرِيدُونَ}: This clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَدْعون» or from its object; the first is the correct one. There is an omission in the discourse, i.e. "they seek His Face by their supplication at these two times."

His saying: {مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ}: This «ما» may be the Ḥijāzī one that puts the predicate in the accusative, so «عليك» is in the position of accusative as its predicate, according to those who permit its working on a fronted predicate when it is an adverb or a preposition and its genitive noun. But if it is the Tamīmī «ما», or if non-working with a fronted predicate is required absolutely, then «عليك» is in the position of nominative as a fronted predicate, and the subject (mubtadaʾ) is «مِنْ شيء», in which «مِنْ» is redundant.

His saying: {مِنْ حِسَابِهِم}: They said: «مِنْ» is partitive (tabʿīḍiyya) and is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, the owner of the ḥāl being «مِنْ شيء», because if it came after it, it would be an adjective of it, and the adjective of an indefinite, whenever fronted, becomes accusative as a ḥāl. On this basis it is attached to an omitted word, and the governor of the ḥāl is the "settling" (istiqrār) implied in «عليك». It is also permissible that «من شيء» be in the position of nominative as an agent (fāʿil), its raiser being «عليك» since it relies on a negation; and «مِنْ حسابهم» is also a ḥāl from «شيء», governed by the istiqrār, the implied form being: "nothing of their account rests on you." It has also been permitted that «من حسابهم» be the predicate: either of «ما» or of the mubtadaʾ, with «عليك» a ḥāl from «شيء», governed by the istiqrār. On this, it is permissible that «من حسابهم» is what raises the agent in that aspect, and «عليك» is also a ḥāl, as its explanation has gone before. That «من حسابهم» is the predicate and «عليك» the ḥāl is not clear, because the point of the benefit is «عليك».

His saying: {وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ} is like the one before it, except that here some of what was permissible there is excluded. That is because His saying «من حسابك» cannot be accusative as a ḥāl, since this would require it to precede its governor which is a semantic one, which is weak or impossible, especially as it has been fronted here before its governor and before its owner. It has already been mentioned to you that when a ḥāl is an adverb or a preposition with its genitive noun, its being fronted before a semantic governor is better than when it is not so. So here you may make His saying «مِنْ حسابك» an explanation (bayān), neither a ḥāl nor a predicate, in order to escape this objectionable matter. That this «مِنْ» is partitive is not apparent. He put the address to him, peace be upon him, first in both clauses, to honour him. Had the second clause come on the pattern of the first, the construction would have been «وما عليهم مِنْ حسابك من شيء», with the phrase governed by «على» fronted as he fronted it in the first; but he departed from that for what has been mentioned.

In these two clauses is what the people of badīʿ (rhetorical embellishment) call "returning the endings to the beginnings" (radd al-aʿjāz ʿalā al-ṣudūr), as in their saying «عادات السادات سادات العادات» ("the habits of the masters are the masters of habits"), and similar in meaning is the poet's saying:

193 - 1- وليس الذي حَلَّلْتَه بمُحَلَّلٍ ... وليس الذي حَرَّمْتَه بمُحَرَّم
(What you have declared lawful is not thereby lawful, and what you have declared forbidden is not thereby forbidden.)

Al-Zamakhsharī said, after discourse he had put forward on the meaning: "If you say: was His saying {مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ} not sufficient, that He joined to it {وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ شَيءٍ}? I say: the two clauses have been made the equivalent of one clause, and a single purport is intended by them, which is what is meant by His saying {وَلاَ تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أخرى} [الأنعام: 164]; and only the two clauses together suffice for this meaning, as if it were said: neither you nor they will be taken to account for the account of his companion."

The Shaykh said: "His saying 'neither you ... will be taken to account', to the end, is a non-Arabic construction. The pronoun cannot return here as a third person nor as a second person. If it returns as a third person, there has preceded no singular third-person noun for it to return to; only «هم» preceded, and it cannot return to it on the assumption of the singular standing in for the plural, because then the construction would be 'the account of their companion'. And if it is made to return as a second person, no addressee preceded for it to return to; only 'you will not be taken to account' preceded, and it cannot return to that, since it is a second-person pronoun and a third person cannot return to it. And if you made it appear as a second person, the construction would also not be correct. The correction of the construction is to say: 'None of you or of them will be taken to account for the account of his companion', or 'you will not be taken to account for their account, nor they for yours', or 'neither you nor they will be taken to account for your account', giving the addressee priority over the absent, as you say «أنت وزيد تضربان».'" What appears is that al-Zamakhsharī's statement is correct, but there is an omission in it, its implied form being: "Each one will not be taken to account: you, nor they, for the account of his companion", with «أنت ولا هم» a substitute (badal) for «كل واحد», and the pronoun in «صاحبه» returning to His saying «كل واحد». Then he (the Shaykh) fell into another objectionable matter in what he used to correct Abū al-Qāsim's statement, namely that he said: "or neither you nor they will be taken to account for your account." This construction may mean, indeed it is the apparent meaning, the negation of being taken to account for each one's own account in relation to himself, not that each one is not taken to account for the account of another; and the second meaning is the intended one.

The three pronouns, I mean those in His saying {مِنْ حِسَابِهِم} and «عليهم» and «فتطردهم», apparently return to a single kind, namely those who call upon their Lord. So said al-Ṭabarī, except that he explained «الحساب» as worldly provision. Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The first two pronouns return to the polytheists, and the third returns to those who call." The Shaykh said: "It was said: the pronoun in «حسابهم» and «عليهم» returns to the polytheists, and the two clauses are parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ) between the prohibition and its response." The apparent form of his wording is that the two clauses are not parenthetical except on the assumption that the two pronouns in «حسابهم» and «عليهم» return to the polytheists. This is not the case; rather they are parenthetical between the prohibition, which is «لا تَطْرُدِ», and its response, which is «فتكونَ», even if all the pronouns refer to the believers. What indicates this is that he said afterwards regarding «فتكون»: "They allowed it to be the response to the prohibition in His saying {وَلاَ تَطْرُدِ}, and the two clauses and the response of the first are parenthetical between the prohibition and its response." So he made them parenthetical absolutely, without regard to the two pronouns.

By the two clauses he means «وما عليك من حسابهم مِنْ شيء» and «ما من حسابك عليهم من شيء», and by the response of the first, His saying {فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ}.

His saying, the Exalted: {فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ}: There are two aspects in it. One: it is accusative as the response of the prohibition (jawāb al-nahy) in only one of two meanings, namely the negation of expelling because of the negation of their account being upon him and his account upon them, for the effect is negated by the negation of its cause. This is made clear by an example: «ما تأتينا فتحدِّثنا» with «فتحدِّثَنا» accusative, which admits two meanings. One: the negation of coming and the negation of speaking, as if it were said: "No coming happens from you, so how would speaking happen from you?" This meaning is the intent of the noble verse, i.e. "No one is taken to account for the account of another, so how would expulsion occur?" The second meaning: the negation of speaking with the establishment of coming, as if it were said: "You do not come to us speaking; rather you come to us not speaking." This meaning does not suit the noble verse. The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, although they state unrestrictedly that it is accusative as the response to a negation, only mean the first meaning, not the second. The second aspect: that it is accusative as the response of the prohibition.

As for His saying «فتكونَ», there are two aspects in its accusative case, the more apparent being that it is accusative by being conjoined to «فتطردَهم», and the meaning is the report of the negation of their account, of the expulsion, and of the wrong caused by the expulsion. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be conjoined to «فتطردَهم» on the basis of causation, since his being a wrongdoer is caused by his expelling them."

The second of the two accusative aspects: that it is accusative as the response of the prohibition in His saying «ولا تَطْرد». Neither Makkī, nor al-Wāḥidī, nor Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned anything else. The Shaykh said: "They allowed «فتكونَ» to be the response to the prohibition in «لا تَطْرِدِ», like His saying {لاَ تَفْتَرُواْ عَلَى الله كَذِباً فَيُسْحِتَكُم بِعَذَابٍ} [طه: 61], with the two clauses and the response of the first being parenthetical between the prohibition and its response." I say: it has already been mentioned that their being parenthetical does not depend on the pronouns in His saying «مِنْ حسابهم» and «عليهم» returning to the polytheists, as is understood from his saying here, even though his statement before that, as I have reported it from him, suggests it.

«Translator's note: the source reads «بان عطية» (for ابن عطية) and «الخيل» (for الخليل), «مفعلوله» (for مفعوله); translated as intended.»

semin-durr:142-142.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً}: Both are accusative, being conjoined to «جنات», i.e. "and He produced from the cattle beasts of burden". «الحَمولة» is that which can bear a load, of camels, and «الفَرْش» is their young; this is the well-known sense in the language. It is also said: «الحَمولة» are the large cattle, I mean camels, cows and sheep, and «الفَرْش» their young. He said: "What indicates it is that He made His later saying «ثمانية أزواج من الضأن» a badal (substitute) for it", as will come. al-Zajjāj said: "The people of the language are agreed that «الفَرْش» are the young of camels", and he recited:
2097 - أَوْرَثَني حَمولةً وفَرْشاً ... أَمُشُّها في كل يومٍ مَشَّا
(He left me as inheritance beasts of burden and young camels... I stroke them every day with a stroking.)
And another said:
2098 - وَحَوَيْنا الفَرْشَ مِنْ أنعامكم ... والحَمُولاتِ وربَّاتِ الحجالْ
(We seized the young camels from your cattle... and the beasts of burden and the ladies of the bridal chambers.)
Abū Zayd said: "It is possible that they were named by the maṣdar, because «الفَرْش» is in origin a maṣdar." «الفَرْش» is a word shared among many meanings, among them what has preceded, and among them household goods, the wide open space, the slight spreading of a camel's pad, and smooth ground, on the authority of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, and a plant that clings to the ground, of which is the poet's saying:
2099 - كمِشْفَر الناب تلوك الفَرْشا
(Like the lip of the old she-camel, chewing the fresh herbage.)
It is also said: «الحَمُولة» is everything that is loaded, of camels, cows, mules and donkeys, and «الفَرْش» here is what is made from its wool, fur and hair that is spread out as bedding. They recited for al-Nābigha:
2100 - وحَلَّتْ بيوتي في يَفاعٍ مُمَنَّعٍ ... تَخَالُ به راعي الحَمولَةِ طائرا
(My tents settled on a fortified height... in which you would think the herder of the pack animals a bird.)
And ʿAntara said:
2101 - وما راعني إلا حَمُولة أهلها وسطَ الديارِ تَسُفُّ حب الخِمْخِمِ
(Nothing startled me but the pack camels of her people, in the midst of the dwellings, nibbling the grains of khimkhim.)

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وكذلك فَتَنَّا}: The kāf is in the position of accusative as an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied meaning being: "and like that preceding testing, which is understood from the course of the reports of the past nations, We tested some of this nation by others." So the reference by "that" is to the testing indicated by His saying {فَتَنَّا}. For that reason al-Zamakhsharī said: "and like that great testing, some people were tested by others," making the reference to the maṣdar of «فتنَّا». And observe how he did not himself pronounce the attribution of the testing to Allah the Exalted in his discourse, although the Creator, the Exalted, has attributed it; rather he said «فُتِن بعضُ الناس» ("some people were tested"), building it as passive according to the rule of the Muʿtazila.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya made the reference to the request for expulsion, for he said after discourse relating to exegesis: "The reference by 'that' is to what was mentioned of their request that the weak be expelled." The Shaykh said: "This comparison is not coherent, since the implied meaning would become: 'like the request for expulsion We tested some of them by others'; and what comes immediately to mind from your saying «ضربْتُ مثل ذلك» is likeness in the beating, i.e. like that beating, not that the likeness occurs in something other than the beating. It has been mentioned more than once that Sībawayh makes «مثل ذلك» a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the implied maṣdar."

«Translator's note: the source reads «محصل نصب» (for «محل نصب») and «طلب الطرف» (for «الطرد») in the Shaykh's quotation; translated as intended.»

His saying: {ليقولوا}: There are two aspects regarding this lām. The more apparent, which most of the i'rab scholars and exegetes hold, is that it is the lām of purpose (lām kay), the implied meaning being: "and like that testing We tested them so that they would say this statement, as a trial and test from Us." The second: that it is the lām of consequence (lām al-ṣayrūra, i.e. al-ʿāqiba), as in the saying:

193 - 2- لِدُوا للموتِ وابنُوا للخراب ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Bear children for death, and build for ruin ...)

and {فالتقطه آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً} [القصص: 8]; and their saying «أهؤلاء», to the end, would then be uttered by way of belittling.

His saying: {أهؤلاء}: Two aspects are permissible for it. The more apparent: it is accusative in position by preoccupation (ishtighāl) with an omitted verb that the overt verb explains, the one governing its pronoun by means of «على», the explainer being so in meaning and not in wording, the implied form being: "Did Allah favour these, bestow favour upon them?" or "Did He choose these, bestow favour upon them?" The clause {مَنَّ الله عَلَيْهِم} has no position, being explicative. The implying of the verb is preferred here only because it occurs after a particle which is usually followed by a verb. The second: that it is nominative in position as a subject (mubtadaʾ), and the predicate is «مَنَّ الله عليهم». Although this is free from the implying found in the previous aspect, it is the less preferred one, for the reason given; and «عليهم» is attached to «مَنَّ».

{مِّن بَيْنِنَآ} may also be attached to it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. He distinguished them above us; and it may be a ḥāl." Abū al-Baqāʾ also said: "i.e. He favoured them while they were alone." These two explanations are explanations of meaning, not of i'rab, except that he presented them as if they were explanations of i'rab. The clause of His saying {أهؤلاء مَنَّ الله} is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying.

His saying {بِأَعْلَمَ بالشاكرين}: As for the difference between the two bāʾs: the first has no attachment, being redundant in the predicate of «ليس»; the second is attached to «أعلم», and the knowing is made transitive by it because of the meaning of encompassing included in it. This often occurs in the wording of scholars, who say «عَلِم بكذا» and «العِلْم بكذا», for the reason given.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذَا جَآءَكَ}: «إذا» is accusative by its apodosis, i.e. "then say: 'Peace be upon you'" at the time of their coming; that is, make this whole saying occur at the time of their coming to you. This is a clear meaning. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The governor of «إذا» is the meaning of the apodosis, i.e. 'when they come to you, greet them'." There is no need that calls for that, with the loss of strength of meaning, because his conveying the greeting to them, and informing them that He has prescribed mercy upon Himself and that whoever does evil in ignorance He forgives, is not matched by the greeting alone, and his implied form leads to that.

His saying: {سَلاَمٌ}: a subject (mubtadaʾ). Starting with it is permissible even though it is indefinite, because it is a supplication, and supplication is among the justifications. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "because of the verbal meaning in it." This is not the position of the majority of the Basrans; it is something reported from al-Akhfash, that if an indefinite noun has the meaning of a verb, it may be the start of a sentence and its raising the agent is permissible, as in «قائمٌ أبواك». Ibn Mālik reported that Sībawayh hinted at its permissibility, and al-Akhfash cited as evidence the saying:

193 - 3- خبيرٌ بنو لِهْبٍ فلاتك مُلْغِياً ... مقالةَ لِهْبِيِّ إذا الطيرُ مَرَّتِ
(The Banū Lihb are experts, so do not disregard the word of a Lihbī when the birds pass by.)

There is no evidence in it, because the form faʿīl occurs in a single wording for the singular and others, so «خبير» is a fronted predicate. He also cited as evidence for it the saying of another:

193 - 4- فخيرٌ نحنُ عند الناسِ منكمْ ... إذا الداعي المثوِّبُ قال يالا
(We are better in the eyes of the people than you, when the caller who repeats the call says "Yā lā ...")

So «خير» is a subject and «نحن» an agent standing in the place of the predicate.

If it is asked: why is it not permissible that «خير» be a fronted predicate and «نحن» a postponed subject? It is said: so that there is no necessary separation between afʿal and «مِنْ» by a foreigner, unlike making it an agent, for the agent is like the predicate, unlike the subject. This much is sufficient in this place; I have established the question elsewhere. «عليكم» is its predicate. «سلام عليكم» is more eloquent than «سلاماً عليكم» with accusative, and this was established at the beginning of al-Fātiḥa in connection with the readings «الحمدُ» and «الحمدَ».

His saying: {كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ}: in the position of accusative as the content of the saying, because it is like an explanation of His saying {سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ}.

His saying {أنَّه، فأنَّه}: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read both with fatḥa; Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read both with kasra; and Nāfiʿ read the first with fatḥa and the second with kasra. These three readings are among the mutawātir ones. Al-Aʿraj read the first with kasra and the second with fatḥa, the reverse of Nāfiʿ's reading; this is the transmission of al-Zahrāwī from him, and likewise al-Dānī. As for Sībawayh, he transmitted his reading as the reading of Nāfiʿ, so it is possible that there are two transmissions from him. As for the first reading: the fatḥa of the first has four aspects. The first: it is a substitute (badal) for «الرحمة», a substitute of a thing for a thing, the implied meaning being: "He has prescribed upon Himself that whoever does ..." to the end, since the very clauses that include the report of this are mercy. The second: it is in the position of nominative as a subject, the predicate omitted, i.e. "upon Him is that whoever does ..." to the end.

The third: that it has fatḥa on the assumption of omission of the preposition, the implied meaning being "because whoever does ..."; when the lām was omitted, the well-known disagreement applied to its position. The fourth: that it is the object (mafʿūl) of «كتب» and «الرحمة» is an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), i.e. "He prescribed that whoever does ..., for the sake of His mercy toward you." The Shaykh said: "It should not be permitted, because in it the governor is prepared for work and then cut off from it."

As for the fatḥa of the second: five aspects. The first: it is in the position of nominative as a subject and the predicate is omitted, i.e. "so His forgiveness and mercy are attained or exist", or "upon Him are His forgiveness and mercy." The reciters have agreed on the fatḥa of what follows the fāʾ of the apodosis in His saying: {أَلَمْ يعلموا أَنَّهُ مَن يُحَادِدِ الله وَرَسُولَهُ فَأَنَّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ} [التوبة: 63] and {كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ مَن تَوَلاَّهُ فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّه} [الحج: 4], just as they agreed on kasra in His saying: {وَمَن يَعْصِ الله وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ} [الجن: 23]. The second: it is in the position of nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "his matter or case is that He is Forgiving, Merciful." The third: it is a repetition of the first, repeated when the discourse became long, and conjoined to it with the fāʾ; this is reported from Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās. This is a gross error, because one of two objectionable consequences follows from it: either a subject remains without a predicate or a condition without an apodosis. The explanation: «مِنْ» in His saying {أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ} is either relative or conditional, and in both cases is in the position of nominative as a subject; so if we made the second «أن» conjoined to the first, the subject would lack a predicate and the condition an apodosis, which is not permissible.

This objection was mentioned, and answered, by Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma, who said: "Among them are those who made the second a repetition of the first because of the length of the discourse, along the lines of His saying: {أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتٌّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُّخْرَجُونَ} [المؤمنون: 35]; and the fāʾ entered «فأنه غفورٌ» as it entered {فَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ بِمَفَازَةٍ} [آل عمران: 188] according to the one who made it a repetition of His saying {لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ الذين يَفْرَحُونَ} [آل عمران: 188]. Except that this is not like «أيعدكم أنَّكم», because that has no condition in it and this has a condition, so it remains without an apodosis. It was said: the apodosis is omitted because the discourse indicates it, its implied form being: 'He forgave them.'" End of quotation. There is remoteness in it, and this answer will also come in the second reading, reported from Abū al-Baqāʾ; he should have answered with it here but did not, and no difference between the two cases has become apparent.

The fourth: it is a substitute for the first «أنَّ», and this is the statement of al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj. This is rejected for two reasons. One: that a conjunction particle does not enter a substitute, and this is accompanied by a conjunction particle, so it is impossible that it be a substitute. If it is said: we make the fāʾ redundant; the answer is that its redundancy is not permissible, it being something al-Akhfash held, and even granting it, that is not permissible for another reason: the subject or condition lacking a predicate or apodosis.

The second of the two reasons: the subject or condition lacking the predicate or apodosis, as its explanation has gone before. If it is said: we make the apodosis omitted, as reported earlier from Abū Shāma, it is said: this is remote from understanding.

The fifth: that it is nominative as an agent, its implied form being: "so there settles for him that He is Forgiving", i.e. there settles and is established for him His forgiveness. It is also permissible in this aspect to imply a preposition and its genitive noun raising this agent according to al-Akhfash, the implied form being "so upon him is that He is Forgiving", because it raises with it even if it does not rely on anything; its verification has gone before more than once.

As for the second reading: the kasra of the first has three aspects. The first: it is resumptive and the discourse is complete before it, and it and what follows are brought as an explanation of His saying: {كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ على نَفْسِهِ الرحمة}. The second: it has kasra after an implied saying, i.e. "Allah said that", which in meaning is like the one before. The third: that "kataba" is treated like "qāla", so it takes kasra after it as it does after an explicit saying; this does not go along the principles of the Basrans. As for the kasra of the second, there are two aspects. One: that it is resumptive, meaning it is at the head of a clause that occurred as the predicate of the relative «مَنْ», or as its apodosis if it is conditional. The second: that it is conjoined to the first and a repetition of it; this is objected to, in that the subject remains without a predicate or the condition without a consequence, as already stated for the two with fatḥa.

Abū al-Baqāʾ answered that here by saying that the predicate of «مَنْ» is omitted and the discourse indicates it. I have already presented to you that he should have given this answer for the two with fatḥa, for the one who made the second a repetition of the first or a substitute for it. Then he said: "It is also permissible that the returning pronoun be omitted, i.e. 'He is Forgiving to him'." I say: his saying "it is permissible" is not good; rather he should have said "it is obligatory", because a pronoun returning to the subject from the predicate clause is necessary, or what stands in its place if it is not the very subject.

As for the third reading: the fatḥa of the first and kasra of the second are derived from what has been said about their kasra and fatḥa, as appropriate, and this is apparent.

As for the fourth reading, it is likewise. Abū Shāma said: "Al-Zajjāj allowed kasra on the first and fatḥa on the second, even though it was not read." I say: I have presented that this is the reading of al-Aʿraj, and that al-Zahrāwī and Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī transmitted it from him, so it seems that the Shaykh was not aware of it. I also presented to you that Sībawayh transmitted nothing from al-Aʿraj except as Nāfiʿ's reading, which may serve as an excuse for al-Zajjāj; as for Abū Shāma, he is later, so his lack of awareness is surprising.

The hāʾ in «أنَّه» is the pronoun of the matter and the story (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-qiṣṣa). «مَنْ» may be conditional or relative, and in either case it is a subject; the fāʾ and what follows are in the position of jussive as the apodosis if it is conditional, otherwise in the position of nominative as the predicate if it is relative, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "Forgiving to him."

The hāʾ in «بعده» may return to «السوء» and may return to the deed understood from the verb, as in His saying: {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [المائدة: 8]; the first is preferable because it is more explicit. «منكم» is attached to an omitted word, as it is a ḥāl from the agent of «عمل»; and it is permissible that «مِنْ» is explicative (lil-bayān), in which case an implied «أعني» ("I mean") governs it.

His saying {بِجَهَالَةٍ} has two aspects. One: that it is attached to «عمل», with the bāʾ denoting causation, i.e. "his doing it by reason of ignorance." Abū al-Baqāʾ expressed this in this aspect as a direct object, which is not clear. The second, which is the apparent: that it is for circumstance, i.e. "his doing it accompanied by ignorance." «ومِنْ» in «مِنْ بعده» is for the beginning of the range.

«Translator's note: the source contains several misprints («الثاينة», «القاراءتُ», «مفول», «غفول له»); translated as intended.»

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَكَذَلِكَ نفَصِّلُ}: The matter of the kāf is clear, in that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of that maṣdar, as is the opinion of Sībawayh. The reference by «ذلك» is to the preceding detailing; the implied meaning: "like that clear detailing, namely what preceded of the circumstances of the nations, We detail the verses of the Qurʾān." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The reference by His saying «وكذلك» is to what preceded, of the prohibition of expelling the believers and the explanation of the corruption of the approach of those who oppose that; and detailing the verses is making them clear and explaining them." This is similar to what he said before regarding His saying {وكذلك فَتَنَّا} [الأنعام: 53], and it was mentioned that it is not apparent.

His saying: {وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ}: The Two Brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū Bakr read «وليستبين» with yāʾ (two dots below) and «سبيلُ» with nominative; Nāfiʿ read «ولتستبين» with tāʾ (two dots above) and «سبيلَ» with accusative; and the rest read with tāʾ and «سبيل» nominative. These readings revolve around the masculine and feminine use of «السبيل» and the transitivity and intransitivity of «استبان». To clarify this: the dialect of Najd and Tamīm makes «السبيل» masculine, and on it is His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن يَرَوْاْ سَبِيلَ الرشد لاَ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلاً وَإِن يَرَوْاْ سَبِيلَ الغي يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلاً} [الأعراف: 146]; the dialect of the Ḥijāz makes it feminine, and on it is {قُلْ هذه سبيلي} [يوسف: 108] and the saying:

193 - 5- خَلِّ السبيل لمَنْ يبني المنار بها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Leave the way to whoever builds the signposts along it ...)

As for «استبانَ», it can be transitive, as in «استَبَنْتُ الشيءَ», and intransitive, as in «استبان الصبح», meaning "became clear". So whoever read with yāʾ and nominative ascribed the verb to «السبيل»; its nominative is because it is masculine and the verb intransitive. Whoever read with tāʾ and nominative did likewise but on the feminine dialect. Whoever read with tāʾ and accusative «السبيلَ» ascribed the verb to the addressee and put «السبيل» in the accusative as an object, on the basis of the verb's transitivity, i.e. "so that you may make clear the way of the criminals". So the tāʾ in «لتستبينَ» differs in meaning: in one of the two readings it is for the address, in the other for the feminine; in both cases it is the tāʾ of the imperfect. «تستبين» is accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām of purpose (lām kay). As to what this lām is attached to, there are two aspects. One: it is conjoined to an omitted reason, which is governed by His saying {نفَصِّلُ}, and the meaning: "and thus We detail the verses so that it becomes clear to you, and so that ... becomes clear."

The second: it is attached to an implied word after it, i.e. "so that the way of the criminals becomes clear, We detailed them with that detailing." In the discourse there is, on one view, an omitted conjoined term, i.e. "and the way of the believers", like His saying, the Exalted: {سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [النحل: 81]. It was also said that this is not needed, because the context requires mentioning the criminals only, since they are the ones who stirred up what was mentioned before.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَنْ أَعْبُدَ}: Regarding the position of «أَنْ» is the well-known disagreement, since it is on the omission of a preposition, the implied meaning: "I have been forbidden from worshipping." His saying {قَدْ ضَلَلْتُ}: «إذن» is a particle of response and consequence (ḥarf jawāb wa-jazāʾ) with no effect here, for lack of a verb for it to work on. The meaning: "If I follow your desires, I will have gone astray and will not be guided"; so it has the force of condition and consequence.

The majority read {ضَلَلْتَ} with fatḥa on the first lām. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Yaḥyā and Ṭalḥa read it with kasra on it, and it has already been mentioned that this is a dialect. The author of al-Taḥrīr [reported from Yaḥyā and Ibn Abī Laylā that they read] here, and in Alif Lām Mīm al-Sajda, {أَإِذَا ضَلَلْنَا} with an undotted ṣād. One says «صَلَّ اللحمُ», i.e. it rotted. This has some fittingness in the verse of al-Sajda, but here its meaning is remote or impossible. Al-ʿAbbās related from Ibn Mujāhid in his book al-Shawādhdh: «صُلِلْنا في الأرض», i.e. "we were buried in the ṣalla", which is the hard ground. His saying {وَمَآ أَنَاْ مِنَ المهتدين} is an emphasis of His saying {قَدْ ضَلَلْتُ}; the first was brought as a verbal clause to indicate renewal and occurrence of the action, and the second as a nominal clause to indicate permanence.

«Translator's note: the source says «ألم السجدة» (Alif Lām Mīm al-Sajda, i.e. Sūrat al-Sajda) and quotes the verb in the verse with the form «ضَلَلْنَا»; translated as written. The bracketed text "[reported from Yaḥyā and Ibn Abī Laylā that they read]" is in the source.»

semin-durr:143-143.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ}: There are six aspects to its accusative. The best of them: that it is a badal (substitute) for «حَمولة وفرشاً», were it not for the consensus reported by al-Zajjāj earlier; but that does not state that this is restricted to camels. The view of badal is the view of al-Zajjāj and al-Farrāʾ. The second: that it is accusative by the «كلوا» before it, i.e. "eat eight pairs", with His saying «ولا تَتَّبِعُوا» to the end being as a parenthesis between the verb and its object; this is the view of ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān, who implied it as "eat the meat of eight". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is accusative by «كلوا», its implied form being: 'eat of what Allah has provided you, eight pairs', and «ولا تُسْرفوا» is a parenthesis between them." I say: the correct form is for him to say «ولا تتَّبعوا» in place of «ولا تسرفوا», because the «كُلوا» that is followed by «ولا تسرفوا» does not govern the accusative on this view, for it is distant from it, and because after it is something more entitled to govern than it; and it is possible that the copyist made an error with him, and that he himself said «ولا تَتَّبعوا». What indicates this is that he said "its implied form being: eat of what Allah has provided you", and the first «كلوا» is not followed by «مما رزقكم»; that comes only after the second. Third: that it is conjoined to «جنات», i.e. "He produced gardens and He produced eight pairs", then the verb and the conjunction were omitted; this is the school of al-Kisāʾī. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak." I say: the matter is so; yet it has been heard in their speech, in prose and verse. In prose, their saying: «أكلت لحماً سمكاً تمراً» ("I ate meat, fish, dates"); and in their verse, the poet's saying:
2102 - ... كيف أصبحتَ كيف أَمْسَيْتَ مِمَّا
يزرَعُ الودَّ في فؤاد الكريمِ
(... How did you wake, how did you spend the evening, of the things that plant affection in the heart of the generous man.)
That is: "I ate meat and fish and dates", and "how did you wake and how did you spend the evening"; and this is according to one of the two views on that. The second view is that it is a badal of retraction (badal badāʾ). Of this is the hadith: «إن الرجلَ ليصلِّي الصلاة، وما كُتِبَ له نصفُها ثلثُها ربعُها إلى أن وصل إلى العَشْر» ("A man prays the prayer and only half of it is recorded for him, a third of it, a quarter of it", until he reached a tenth). Fourth: that it is accusative by an omitted verb indicated by what is in the wording, its implied form being: "eat eight pairs"; and this is weaker than what precedes. Fifth: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being "varied" or "numerous", and the owner of the ḥāl is «الأنعام»; the governor of the ḥāl is what the preposition is attached to, namely «مِنْ». Sixth: that it is accusative as a badal for the position of «ممَّا رزقكم الله».
His saying: {مَّنَ الضأن اثنين}: there are two aspects to the accusative of «اثنين». One: that it is a badal for «ثمانية أزواج», and this is the apparent meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's saying, for he said: "and the proof of it is «ثمانية أزواج»", then he explained it by His saying «من الضأن اثنين» (the verse). Abū l-Baqāʾ stated it explicitly, saying: "«واثنين» is a badal from the eight, and the remainder of the eight is conjoined to it."
The second: that it is accusative by an implied «أنشأ» (He produced), and this is the view of al-Fārisī, and «مِنْ» is attached to what governs the accusative of «اثنين».
The majority read «الضأن» with sukūn on the hamza, and it is the plural of ḍāʾin (masc.) and ḍāʾina (fem.), like tājir and tājira and tajr, ṣāḥib and ṣāḥiba and ṣaḥb, rākib and rākiba and rakb. al-Ḥasan, Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «الضَّأَن» with fatḥa on it; it is either a broken plural of ḍāʾin, as one says khādim and khadam, ḥāris and ḥaras, ṭālib and ṭalab, or a collective noun (ism jamʿ). It is pluralized as ḍaʾīn, as one says kalb and kalīb. He said:
2103 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . فبذَّتْ نَبْلَهمْ وكليبُ
(... so it surpassed their arrows, and Kalīb.)
It is also said: «الضَّئين» and «الكليب» are collective nouns, and it is said «ضِئين» with kasra on the ḍād, as though it were an assimilation to the kasra of the hamza, like «بِعير» and «شِعير» with kasra on the bāʾ and shīn because of the kasra of the ʿayn. «الضأن» is well known: it is the woolly kind of sheep, and the goat (maʿz) is the haired kind. Abān ibn ʿUthmān read «اثنان» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the preposition phrase before it as the khabar (predicate). Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «المَعَز» with fatḥa on the ʿayn, and the rest with sukūn; they are two dialectal forms in the plural of māʿiz. It was mentioned earlier that fāʿil is pluralized on faʿl at times and on faʿal at others, like tājir and tajr, khādim and khadam, and its verification has already been given. It is also pluralized as miʿzā, and Ubayy read it so. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
1104 - ألا إنْ لا تكن إِبِلٌ فمِعْزَى ... كأنَّ قُروْنَ جِلَّتِها العِصِيُّ
(Indeed, if there are no camels, then goats... as if the horns of their old ones were staves.)
«[Translator's note: the source prints the verse number as 1104, which breaks the sequence 2103, 2105; it is probably a misprint for 2104.]»
Abū Zayd said: it is pluralized as umʿūz, and he recited:
2105 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كالتَّيْبسِ في أُمْعوِزهِ المُتَرَبِّلِ
(... like the he-goat among his herd of goats, the well-fed one.)
It is also pluralized as maʿīz, and they recited for Imruʾ al-Qays:
1106 - ويمنحها بنو شَمَجَى بنِ جَرْمٍ ... معيزَهُمُ حنَانكَ ذا الحَنانِ
(And the sons of Shamajā ibn Jarm grant her their goats... Your compassion, O Possessor of compassion!)
«[Translator's note: the source prints 1106 here, again apparently for 2106.]»
«الإبل» is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own wording; rather its singular is jamal, nāqa or baʿīr. No noun on the pattern fiʿil has come, according to Sībawayh, other than it; others than Sībawayh added bikir, iṭil, wītid and mishit. More explanation of this will come in (Sūrat) al-Ghāshiya, if Allah wills. The relative adjective (nisba) to it is ibalī with fatḥa on the bāʾ, so that two kasras do not follow one another together with two yāʾs.
His saying: {ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ}: «الذَّكَرَيْن» is accusative by what follows it, and the reason for the hamza's being placed directly before it is what was mentioned earlier at His saying «أأنت قلتَ للناس». «أم» is a conjunction conjoining «الأُنْثَيَيْن» to «الذكرين»; likewise the second «أم» conjoins the relative «ما» to what precedes it, so its position is accusative, the implied form being "or that which the wombs enclose"; when the mīm, being sākin, met what follows it, assimilation became obligatory.

semin-durr:144-144.t: «أم» in His saying, the Exalted: {أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَآءَ}: is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), not a conjunction, because after it is a clause independent in itself; so it is implied as «بل» and the hamza, the implied form being: "Rather, were you witnesses?" «إذ» is accusative by «شهداء». He censured them for what they claimed and mocked them in ascribing to them presence at the time of the charge to do that. «بهذا» is a pointer to everything whose mention has preceded of the things forbidden in their view.

semin-durr:145-145.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مُحَرَّماً}: It is accusative by His saying «لا أَجِدُ», and it is an adjective of an omitted described noun, omitted because His saying «على طاعم يَطْعَمُه» indicates it, the implied form being: "I do not find forbidden food." «على طاعم» is attached to «محرَّماً», and «يَطْعَمُه» is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «طاعم». al-Bāqir read it, and Makkī reported it from Abū Jaʿfar, «يَطَّعِمُه» with shadda on the ṭāʾ; its origin is «يَطْتَعِمه», the ifʿitāl form from «الطعم», and the tāʾ was changed to ṭāʾ because it follows a ṭāʾ, for proximity, so assimilation became obligatory. ʿĀʾisha, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read «تَطَعَّمه» with tāʾ from above (second/third person feminine) and shadda on the ʿayn, as a past verb.
His saying {إِلاَّ أَن يَكُونَ}: it is accusative as an exception, and there are two aspects to it. One: that it is connected (muttaṣil). Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "An exception from the same kind, and its position is accusative, i.e. I find nothing forbidden except carrion." The second: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). Makkī said: "and it may be in the position of accusative as a disconnected exception." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "«وإلا أن يكون» is a disconnected exception, because it is an event (kawn) while what is before it is a substance; and its position may be accusative as a badal according to the dialect of Tamīm, and accusative as an exception according to the dialect of the Hijaz." He means that the disconnected exception has two dialects: one is the dialect of the Hijaz, which is the obligatory accusative absolutely; and the Tamīmīs treat it like the connected. If there is negation or something like it in the speech, the badal is preferred; and here the speech is negative, so for the Tamīmīs its being a badal is preferred over the accusative as exception, so its accusative is in two ways, while for the Hijazis its accusative is in one way. The apparent sense of the words of Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī is that it is connected, for he said: "«محرماً», i.e. forbidden food among the foods that you have forbidden, unless it is carrion", i.e. unless the forbidden thing is carrion. Ibn ʿĀmir read, in one transmission, «أوحَى» with fatḥa on the hamza and the ḥāʾ, as an active verb.
His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ آلذَّكَرَيْنِ}, His saying «نَبِّئوني», His saying again «آلذكرين» the second time, and His saying «أم كنتم شهداء» are parenthetical clauses between the enumerated items that came as the detailing of the eight pairs. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is the enumerated thing separated from part of it and not followed continuously? I say: a separator occurred between them as a parenthesis not foreign to the enumerated thing, namely that Allah, mighty and majestic, conferred a favour on His servants by producing the cattle for their benefit and by making them lawful to them, so He interposed an argument against those who forbade them; and the argument against those who forbade them is a confirmation and a rectification of the making-lawful; and parentheses in speech are brought only for emphasis."
Ibn ʿĀmir read «إلا أَنْ تكونَ ميتةٌ» with the feminine and the nominative of «ميتة», meaning "unless a dead animal exists"; so it is the complete (tāmma) for him; and it may be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) with an omitted khabar (predicate), the implied form being: "unless there is there a dead animal". It was mentioned earlier that this is reported from al-Akhfash in his saying the like of that in {وَإِن يَكُن مَّيْتَةً}.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is also read with «ميتة» nominative, on the basis that «تكون» is complete, and it is weak because the conjoined item is accusative." I say: how can he weaken a mutawātir reading? As for his saying "because the conjoined item is accusative", that is not necessary, because the accusative, according to the reading of the one who makes «ميتة» nominative, is a conjunction on the position of «أن تكون», which occurs as the excepted item, the implied form being: "unless there is a dead animal, and unless poured-out blood, and unless the flesh of swine." Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: "Abū Jaʿfar read «إلا أن تكون» with the tāʾ, «ميتةٌ» nominative", then said: "It would be necessary for Abū Jaʿfar to read «أو دمٌ» in the nominative, and likewise what follows it." I say: this is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, which he ascribed to Abū Jaʿfar Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ al-Madanī, the teacher of Nāfiʿ; it is possible. His saying "it would be necessary for him", to the end, has the meaning of what Abū l-Baqāʾ used to weaken this reading, and the reply to that has been given. It happens that Ibn ʿĀmir reads «وإن تكنْ ميتةٌ» with the feminine and the nominative, and here too.
Ibn Kathīr and Ḥamza read «تكون» with the feminine, «ميتةً» in the accusative, on the basis that the ism (subject) of «تكون» is a latent pronoun referring to a feminine, i.e. "unless the thing eaten is dead"; and it is possible that the pronoun of «تكون» refers to «محرَّماً», the verb being made feminine only because of the femininity of the khabar, like His saying {ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن} [al-Anʿām: 23], where he puts «فتنتهم» in the accusative and makes «تكن» feminine. The rest read «يكون» in the masculine, «ميتة» accusative, and the ism of «يكون» refers to His saying «مُحَرَّماً», i.e. "unless that forbidden thing is carrion". Abū l-Baqāʾ, Makkī and others implied it: "unless the thing eaten is" or "that is carrion".
His saying: «أو دماً»: «دماً», on the reading of the common people, is conjoined to the khabar of «يكون», namely «ميتة»; on the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Jaʿfar it is conjoined to the excepted item, which is «أن يكون», and the verification of this has been given earlier. «مسفوحاً» is an adjective of «دماً». «السَّفْح» is pouring; it is also said: flowing, which is close to the first. «سفح» is used both intransitively and transitively; one says «سَفَحَ زيدٌ دمعه ودمه», i.e. he shed it, and "he himself poured out", except that the difference between them occurs through the difference of the maṣdar: in the transitive one says «سَفْح», and in the intransitive «سُفُوح». Of the transitive is His saying, the Exalted, {أو دماً مسفوحاً}, for the complete passive participle is formed only from a transitive verb. Of the intransitive is what Abū ʿUbayda recited for Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
2107 - أقول ودَمْعي واكفٌ عند رسمها ... عليك سلامُ الله والدمعُ يَسْفَح
(I say, with my tears streaming at her ruined abode... "Upon you be the peace of Allah," as the tears flow.)
His saying: «أو فِسْقاً»: there are three aspects. One: that it is also conjoined to the khabar of «يكون», i.e. "unless it is a transgression (fisq)".
«أُهِلَّ» is in the position of accusative because it is an adjective of it, as if it had been said: "or a transgression proclaimed for other than Allah"; he made the forbidden thing itself the very transgression, for intensification, or on the omission of a muḍāf, and what preceded of His saying explains it: {وَلاَ تَأْكُلُواْ مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسم الله عَلَيْهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ} [al-Anʿām: 121]. Second: that it is accusative by conjunction to the position of the excepted item, i.e. "unless it is carrion or unless a transgression". His saying «فإنه رجْسٌ» is a parenthesis between the two conjoined items. Third: that it is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), the governor in it being His saying «أُهِلَّ», which precedes it, so that this object of purpose separates between the conjunction, namely «أو», and the conjoined item, namely the clause «أُهِلَّ»; and its parallel, in the preceding of the object of purpose before its governor, is his saying:
2108 - طَرِبْتُ وما شوقاً إلى البيض أطربُ ... ولا لَعِباً مني وذو الشيب يَلْعَبُ
(I was moved, though not from longing for the fair ones do I get moved... nor in play on my part, for one with grey hair does not play.)
According to this iʿrāb «أُهِلَّ» is conjoined to «يكون», and the pronoun in «به» refers to what the latent pronoun in «يكون» refers to; its verification has been given. So said al-Zamakhsharī. But the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) followed him up on that, saying: "This is an extremely forced iʿrāb, and a construction on this iʿrāb is outside eloquence, and is impermissible on the reading of the one who reads {إِلاَّ أَن يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً} with the nominative, leaving the pronoun in «به» with nothing to refer to; and it is not permissible to force an omitted word so that the pronoun may refer to it, the implied form being 'or something proclaimed for other than Allah', because the like of this is not permitted except in poetic necessity." I say: by that he means that the described noun is not omitted when the description is a clause, unless the partitive «مِنْ» is in the speech, as in their saying «منا ظَعَنَ ومنا أقام», i.e. "among us a group departed and among us a group stayed"; if «مِنْ» is not in it, it is a necessity, as in his saying: 2109 - تَرْمي بكفَّيْ كان مِنْ أرمى البشَرْ (You shoot with the two hands of one who was among the best shots of mankind.) that is, "with the two hands of a man". This is the opinion of some; as for others, they say: whenever evidence indicates the described noun, it is omitted absolutely; so it is possible that al-Zamakhsharī held this opinion.
His saying: «فإنه»: there is disagreement about the hāʾ in it. The apparent is that it refers to «لحم» which is annexed to «خنزير». Ibn Ḥazm said: "It refers to «خنزير» because it is the nearest mentioned." The first was preferred in that the flesh is what is spoken about, and the swine came by incidental annexation to it; do you not see that if you say «رأيت غلام زيد فأكرمته» ("I saw Zayd's boy and honoured him"), the hāʾ refers to the boy, because he is the one spoken about and intended in the report, not to Zayd, who is not intended. The second was preferred in that the prohibition attached to the swine is not restricted to its flesh; rather its fat, hair, bone and hoof are the same, so if we return the pronoun to «خنزير» it is complete for this purpose, and if we return it to «لحم» there would be in the verse no reference to the prohibition of what is other than flesh of what was mentioned. It was answered that flesh is mentioned rather than the others, although the others are also intended in the prohibition, because it is the most important thing in it and what is mostly sought from it is flesh, as with other animals; and on this there is no implication (mafhūm) in singling out flesh for mention, and even if it were conceded, it would be of the category of mafhūm al-laqab (implication of the title), which is very weak. His saying «فإنه رِجْسٌ»: either for intensification, in that it is made the very filth itself, or on the omission of a muḍāf, and it has parallels.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَكَذَّبْتُم بِهِ}: There are two aspects regarding this clause. One: it is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), brought to report that. The second: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and in that case, is it necessary to imply «قد» or not? The hāʾ in «به» may return to «ربي», which is the apparent. It was also said: to the Qurʾān, because it is as if mentioned. It was said: to «بَيِّنَة», because it has the meaning of «البيان». It was also said: because the tāʾ in it is for intensification, and the meaning is "upon a clear matter from my Lord"; «من ربي» is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «بينة».

His saying: {يَقُصُّ الحق}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read «يقص» with an undotted ṣād, doubled, with ḍamma; this is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās. The rest read with a dotted ḍād, light, with kasra, and these two are among the mutawātir readings. ʿAbd Allāh, Ubayy, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Nakhaʿī, al-Aʿmash and Ṭalḥa read «يقضي بالحق», from «القضاء». Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid read «يقضي بالحق وهو خير القاضين». As for the reading «يقضي», it is from «القضاء» ("judging"). It is supported by His saying «وهو خير الفاصلين», since «الفصل» (deciding) suits «القضاء»; and it was written only with ḍād, as if the yāʾ was dropped in writing as it was dropped in pronunciation due to the meeting of two quiescents, as it was dropped in {فَمَا تُغْنِ النذر} [القمر: 5], and as the wāw was dropped in {سَنَدْعُ الزبانية} [العلق: 18] and {وَيَمْحُ الله الباطل} [الشورى: 24], for the reason given.

As for the accusative of «الحق» after it, there are four aspects. The first: it is accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "He judges the true judgment." The second: that «يقضي» is made to include the meaning of «يُنْفِذ» ("carries out"), and for that reason it is made transitive to a direct object. The third: that «قضى» has the meaning of "made", so it is transitive by itself without inclusion; and what indicates that is the saying:

193 - 6- وعليهما مَسْرُودتان قضاهُما ... داودُ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Upon the two of them were two coats of mail, Dāwūd made them ...)

i.e. made them. The fourth: that it is by removal of the preposition, i.e. "He judges by the truth"; when it was omitted, its genitive noun became accusative, along the lines of the saying:

193 - 7- تمرُّون الدِّيار فلم تَعْوجوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(You pass by the abodes and do not turn aside ...)

This is supported by the reading with this original form.

As for the reading «يَقُصُّ», it is from «قَصَّ الحديث» ("he related the account") or from «قصَّ الأثر», i.e. he followed the trace. The Exalted said: {نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ القصص} [يوسف: 3]. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ preferred the first reading because of «الفاصلين», and it was reported from him that he said: "Is it «يَقُصُّ الحقَّ» or «يقضي الحقَّ»?" They said: "«يقصُّ»." He said: "If it were «يقص» he would have said «وهو خير القاصِّين». Does anyone read it so? And since He said {وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الفاصلين}, deciding occurs only in judging." It is as if «وهو خير القاصِّين» as a reading had not reached Abū ʿAmr. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī answered what Ibn al-ʿAlāʾ mentioned and said: "Here «القصص» has the meaning of speech, and «الفصل» has also come in speech. The Exalted said: {إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلٌ فَصْلٌ} [طارق: 13], and the Exalted said: {كِتَابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ} [هود: 1], and the Exalted said: {وَنُفَصِّلُ الآيات} [التوبة: 11]. So «الفصل» has been applied to speech and used with it as it has come with judging; therefore «الفاصلين» does not necessarily mean that «يقضي» is the determined reading."

«Translator's note: the source text of Abū ʿAmr's question repeats «يقضي الحق» twice; translated once. The source also reads «ابن العلاء» for ابن العلاء and spells «قُرْقُرر» etc. elsewhere as written.»

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والله أَعْلَمُ بالظالمين}: This is an instance of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, to draw attention to their deserving that by the attribute of wrongdoing; for had it come in the original form, He would have said: «والله أعلمُ بكم» ("and Allah knows best about you").

«Translator's note: the source reads «أعملُ» (apparently a misprint for «أعلمُ»); translated as «أعلمُ».»

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَفَاتِحُ}: There are three statements about it. The first: it is the plural of «مِفْتح» with kasra on the mīm and a short form, which is the instrument with which one opens, like «مُنْخُل» (sieve), pl. «مَناخل». The second: it is the plural of «مَفْتَح» with fatḥa on the mīm, which is a place; this is supported by the explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās: they are the treasuries of rain. The third: it is the plural of «مِفتاح» with kasra on the mīm and an alif, which is also the instrument, except that there is weakness in this, in that the alif of the singular should have been turned into yāʾ, so that it would be said «مفاتيح» like «دنانير». But it has been reported in the plural of «مصباح» as «مصابح», in the plural of «مِحْراب» as «مَحارِب», and in the plural of «قُرْقُر» as «قراقِر». This is just as they brought the yāʾ in the plural of what has no long vowel in its singular, as in their saying «دراهيم» and «صياريف» for the plural of «دِرْهَم» and «صَيْرَف». He said:

193 - 8- تَنْفي يداها الحصى في كل هاجِرَةٍ ... نَفْيَ الدارهيمِ تَنْقادُ الصَّياريفِ
(Her forelegs throw off the pebbles in every midday heat, as the money-changers' hands throw off the dirhams when tested.)

and they said «عيِّل» and «عَياييل». He said:

193 - 9- فيها عياييلُ أُسودٌ ونُمُرْ ...
(In it are many lions and leopards ...)

The original is «عيايل» and «نمور»; he added in this one and subtracted from that one.

«مفاتيح» has also been read with yāʾ, and it supports that «مفاتح» is the plural of «مفتاح» whose long vowel was dropped. Al-Wāḥidī allowed that «مفاتح» be the plural of «مَفْتَح» with fatḥa on the mīm, as a maṣdar. He said, after discourse he related from Abū Isḥāq: "On this, «مفاتح» is the plural of «المَفْتح» in the sense of «الفتح»," as if the meaning were: "with Him are the openings of the unseen," i.e. He opens the unseen to whomever He wills of His servants. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«مفاتح» is the plural of «مَفْتَح», and «المَفْتَح» is the treasury; as for that with which one opens, it is «المفتاح», and its plural is «مفاتيح», and «مَفْتح» has also been said." End of quotation. He means the plural of «مَفتح», i.e. with fatḥa on the mīm. His saying "it has also been said «مَفْتح»" means that it is a rare dialectal form for the instrument, while the common form for it has the long vowel; he should have clarified his wording, for it is misleading, which is why I explained it.

His saying: {لاَ يَعْلَمُهَآ إِلاَّ هُوَ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «مفاتح», and the governor in it is the "settling" (istiqrār) which the preposition includes by occurring as a predicate. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "the very adverbial phrase, if you make «مفاتح» nominative by it", i.e. if you make it raise it as an agent, according to the opinion of al-Akhfash. Its including the istiqrār is necessary on every view, so there is no difference between making it raise the agent or making it a predicate.

His saying: {مِن وَرَقَةٍ}: the agent of «تَسْقُط», and «مِنْ» is redundant for the inclusion of the entire genus. His saying {إِلاَّ يَعْلَمُهَا} is a ḥāl from «ورقة», and the ḥāl came from an indefinite because of its reliance on a negation, the implied meaning being: "No leaf falls except that He knows it", like your saying «ما أكرمْتُ أحداً إلا صالحاً». In my view it is also permissible that the clause be an adjective of «ورقة». And since they allowed in His saying {إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ} [الحجر: 4], in His saying {وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ} [الحجر: 4], that it is an adjective of «قرية» despite its having the wāw, and they excuse the redundancy of the wāw, then allowing that here is more fitting. In that case it may be in the position of genitive by the form, or nominative by the position.

His saying: {وَلاَ حَبَّةٍ}: conjoined to the form of «ورقةٍ»; had it been read with nominative, it would be by the position. «في ظلمات» is an adjective of «حبة». His saying {وَلاَ رَطْبٍ وَلاَ يَابِسٍ} are also conjoined to the form of «ورقة», and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read them with nominative, by the position, and this is the apparent. They may also be two subjects, the predicate being His saying {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ}.
