Al-Zamakhsharī reported that the nominative applies to the three, I mean His saying «ولا حبةٍ ولا رطبٍ ولا يابسٍ», and mentioned the two aspects of the nominative mentioned earlier, and compared the second aspect to your saying «لا رجلٌ منهم ولا امرأة إلا في الدار».

His saying: {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ}: There is obscurity in this exception. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "His saying {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ} is like a repetition of His saying {إِلاَّ يَعْلَمُهَا}, because the meaning of «إلا يعلمها» and the meaning of «إلا في كتاب مبين» is one, and the Book is the knowledge of Allah, or the Tablet." The Shaykh put it in wording close to this and said: "This exception runs in the manner of emphasis (tawkīd), because His saying «ولا حبةٍ ولا رطب ولا يابس» is conjoined to «مِنْ ورقة», and the first exception extends over them, as you say «ماجاءني من رجلٍ إلا أكرمته ولا أمرأةٍ», the meaning being «إلا أكرمتها»; but when the discourse became long, the exception was repeated by way of emphasis, and its being a verse-ending (fāṣila) makes it good." End of quotation. The author of al-Naẓm made the discourse complete at His saying {ولا يابس}, then began another predicate with His saying {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ}, meaning "and it is also in a clear Book." He said: "Because if you attached His saying {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ} to the first discourse, the meaning would be corrupted, and the explanation of its corruption is in a long section we mentioned in Sūrat Yūnus in His saying «ولا أصغرَ من ذلك ولا أكبرَ إلا في كتاب مبين»." End of quotation. I say: the meaning was corrupt only because he believed it to be another independent exception, and how its corruption would arise will come; but had he made it an exception emphasizing the first, as Abū al-Qāsim said, the meaning would not be corrupted. And how can the completion of the discourse be imagined at His saying {وَلاَ يَابِسٍ}, with a start by «إلا»? And how does «إلا» occur in this way?

Abū al-Baqāʾ moved toward something of what al-Jurjānī said, for he said: "«إلا في كتاب مبين» means «إلا هو في كتاب مبين», and it cannot be an exception that «يعلمها» works on, because the meaning would become: 'No leaf falls except He knows it, except in a Book', so its meaning turns to affirmation, i.e. 'He does not know it, in a Book'; and if it is not except in a Book, He must know it in the Book. So then the second exception is a substitute (badal) for the first, i.e. 'No leaf falls except it is in a Book, and He knows it.'" End of quotation. The answer to it is what preceded, of making the exception an emphasis. This will be established, if Allah wills, in Sūrat Yūnus, since it has its own discussion.

«Translator's note: the source prints «ماجاءني» (without space) and «أمرأةٍ» (for «امرأة»), and «الاستثاءُ» for «الاستثناءُ»; translated as intended.»

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بالليل}: attached to what precedes it as an adverbial for it, and the bāʾ comes with the meaning of «في»; I have presented a good deal of this earlier. Abū al-Baqāʾ said here: "That is permissible because the bāʾ is for attachment (ilṣāq), and that which is attached to time and place is present in them." He means that this relation is what permits the figurative use; on this there is no need for one particle to stand in place of another; rather we say: it is here for attachment figuratively, along the lines of what they said regarding «مررت بزيد». He ascribed the taking (tawaffī) here to His holy Self because it is not repugnant here, as what is meant by it is rest and repose, and he ascribed it to another in His saying, the Exalted: {تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنَا} [الأنعام: 61] and {يَتَوَفَّاكُم مَّلَكُ الموت} [السجدة: 11] because it is repugnant, as what is meant by it is death.

His saying: {مَا جَرَحْتُم}: Apparently it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), although its being a relative noun is more common; it may also be an indefinite noun described by what follows it. The returning pronoun, on both of the latter two assumptions, is omitted, and likewise according to al-Akhfash and Ibn al-Sarrāj on the first view. «بالنهار» is like {بالليل}. The pronoun in «فيه» returns to «النهار»; this is the apparent. The Shaykh said: "It returns to it in wording," the meaning being "on another day", as you say «عندي درهم ونصفه» ("I have a dirham and half of it"). I say: apparently there is no need for it to return to the like of what was mentioned, since its returning to what was mentioned has no objection; as for something like «درهم ونصفه», it is because of the necessity of avoiding awkwardness in speech. They said: because when you say «عندي درهم» it is known that you have half of it necessarily, so your saying «ونصفه» after that forces its returning to the like of what you have, unlike what we are discussing. It was also said: it returns to the night. It was also said: it returns to the taking (tawaffī), which is sleep, i.e. "He wakes you in the course of sleep." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Then He raises you from the graves, in the matter of that in which you spent your lives, of sleeping at night and earning sins in the day." End of quotation. It is good.

He singled out the night for the taking and the day for earning, though one may sleep in the latter and earn in the former, with regard to the predominant circumstance. He put the taking in the night first because it is stronger in favour upon them, particularly according to those who restrict «الجَرْح» to the earning of evil rather than good.

His saying: {ليقضى أَجَلٌ}: The majority read «لِيُقْضَى» as passive, with «أجلٌ» nominative by it. There are two possibilities for the omitted agent: one, that it is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted; the second, that it is the pronoun of the addressees, i.e. "so that you complete", that is, fulfil your terms. Abū Rajāʾ and Ṭalḥa read «ليقضي» as active, the agent being Allah the Exalted, with «أجلاً» a direct object and «مُسَمَّى» an adjective; so it is nominative on the first and accusative on the second. A disagreement among the reciters follows from that regarding the imāla of its alif, which I have clarified in Sharḥ al-Qaṣīd. The lām in «لِيُقْضَى» is attached to what precedes it, of the two verbs together, i.e. "He takes you and then raises you for that purpose."

semin-durr:146-146.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَعَلَى الذين هَادُواْ}: It is attached to «حرَّمْنا», and according to some, such as al-Zamakhsharī and al-Rāzī, it gives the sense of specification; al-Rāzī stated this explicitly here, I mean the preposing of the object-of-government before its governor.
In «الظفر» there are five dialectal forms, the highest of which is ẓufur, and this is the reading of the common people; ẓufr with sukūn on the ʿayn, which is a lightening of the form with ḍamma, and al-Ḥasan read it so in one transmission, as did Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and al-Aʿraj; ẓifir with kasra on the ẓāʾ and the fāʾ, which al-Wāḥidī ascribed to Abū l-Sammāl as a reading; ẓifr with kasra on the ẓāʾ and sukūn on the fāʾ, which is a lightening of the one with kasras, and people also ascribed it to al-Ḥasan as a reading; and the fifth dialectal form is uẓfūr, which was not read, as far as I know. On that they recited the poet's saying:
2110 - ما بين لُقْمَتِها الأولى إذا انحدَرَتْ ... وبين أخرى تليها قِيْدُ أُظْفورِ
(Between her first morsel when it goes down and another following it is the length of a fingernail.)
The plural of the triliteral is aẓfār, and the plural of uẓfūr is aẓāfīr, which is the regular form, and aẓāfir without the lengthening, which is not regular; and this is like his saying:
2111 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . العينين والعواوِرِ
(... the two eyes and the ʿawāwir.)
Its verification has already been given at His saying «مفاتح الغيب».
His saying: «ومن البقر»: there are two aspects. One: that it is conjoined to «كل ذي», so «مِنْ» is attached to the first «حرَّمنا», not the second; the second clause was brought only as an explanation of what was left vague in the partitive «مِنْ» of what was forbidden, so He said: «حَرَّمْنا عليهم شحومهما». The second: that it is attached to the later «حرَّمْنا», the implied form being: "and We forbade to those who were Jews, of the cattle and sheep, their fats"; so here it is not obligatory to put the word with «مِنْ» before the verb, but it may be put after it as was said before; yet it may not be put after the object of the verb, so that one would say: «حرَّمنا عليهم شحومَهما من البقر والغنم», lest the pronoun return to something later in both word and rank. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible that «مِن البقر» be attached to the second «حَرَّمنا»." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "It is as though he imagined that the return of the pronoun prevents the attachment, since the rank of the word governed by «مِنْ» is to be last; but last after what? After the verb, conceded; after the object, not conceded." He means that if he intends that the rank of the saying «من البقر» is to come after «شحومهما», so that the implied form becomes «حرَّمْنا عليهم شحومهما من البقر», it is not conceded. Then the Shaykh said: "And if we concede that its rank is to come after the verb and the object, it is still not prohibited, but permitted, as «ضرب غلامَ المرأة أبوها» ('Her father struck the woman's boy') and «غلامَ المرأة ضرب أبوها» are permitted, even though the rank of the object is to be last; here it is obligatory to put it first because of the return of the pronoun in the agent, whose rank is to be first, to it. How then with the object, which is in the same rank as the word governed by the preposition? I mean in that both are supplementary (faḍla), so it does not matter which of the two you put before the other. The poet said:
2112 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وقد رَكَدَتْ وسطَ السماء نجومُها
(... when its stars had stood still in the middle of the sky.)
He put the adverbial first obligatorily because of the return of the pronoun attached to the agent to the word governed by the adverbial." I say: someone could say that we do not concede that Abū l-Baqāʾ forbade that only for what he mentioned, so as to be bound by what you bound him with; rather he may have forbidden it for a reason of meaning.
The annexation in His saying «شحومهما» gives an indication of emphasis on the specification and the link, for had the speech come with «من البقر والغنم حرَّمْنا عليهم الشحوم» it would have sufficed in indicating that only the fats of cattle and sheep are meant. This is the Shaykh's statement and is an elaboration of what al-Zamakhsharī said, for he said: "«ومن البقر والغنم حَرَّمْنا عليهم شحومهما» is like your saying 'Of Zayd I took his property'; by the annexation you intend an additional link."
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا}: «ما» is a relative in the position of accusative as a connected exception from «الشحوم», i.e. He did not forbid the fat carried on the back. Then, if you wish, you may make this relative an adjective of an omitted word, i.e. "except the fat which their backs carry"; so the Shaykh implied it, and there is something to consider in it, because he himself stated that one does not describe by the relative «ما», though one describes by «الذي», and he himself rejected others on that point in the like of this implication. Or, if you wish, you may make it described by an omitted «شيء», i.e. "except that which their backs carry of fat"; and this preposition phrase is a semantic description, not a technical one, for if it were overt as that its iʿrāb would be a ḥāl.
His saying «ظهورهما» may be of the category of {فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا} [al-Taḥrīm: 4], in relation to the pronoun of cattle and sheep, without regard to their plurality in meaning; and it may be that he made «الظهور» plural because the muḍāf ilayhi is plural in meaning, so it is like «قَطَعْت رؤوس الكبشين» ("I cut off the heads of the two rams"), for the dual in the like of this is impermissible.
His saying: {أَوِ الحوايآ}: there are three aspects to its position in the iʿrāb. First, which is the view of al-Kisāʾī: that it is in the position of nominative, conjoined to «ظهورهما», i.e. "and except what the intestines carry of fat, for that too is not forbidden"; and this is the apparent. Second: that it is in the position of accusative, conjoined to «شحومهما», i.e. "We forbade them the intestines also, or what is mixed with bone", so the intestines and the mixed are both forbidden; their explanation will come. A small group held this, and «أو» in it is like the one in His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِماً أَوْ كَفُوراً}, by which is meant the negation of what it enters upon, individually, as you say: «هؤلاء أهلٌ أن يُعْصَوا فاعصِ هذا أو هذا» ("These are worthy of being disobeyed; so disobey this one or that one"); the meaning: He forbade them this and that. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أو» is in the position of what it is in their saying «جالس الحسن أو ابن سيرين» ('Sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn')."
The Shaykh said: "The grammarians said «أو» in this example is for permission, so he may sit with both or with one of them; and the better in the verse, if we say that «الحوايا» is conjoined to «شحومهما», is that «أو» in it is for detailing, by which He detailed what He forbade them of cattle and sheep."
I say: this expression that al-Zamakhsharī mentioned was preceded by Abū Isḥāq, for he said: "A group said: the fat membranes (al-thurūb) were forbidden to them, and what the backs carry was made lawful for them, and 'the intestines or what is mixed with bone' became a conjunction on what He forbade, not on the exception; and the meaning, on this view: their fats were forbidden to them, or the intestines, or what is mixed with bone, except what the backs carry, for that is not forbidden; and «أو» was brought in the manner of permission, as the Exalted said {وَلاَ تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِماً أَوْ كَفُوراً} [al-Insān: 24], the meaning being: each of these is worthy of being disobeyed, so disobey this one or disobey that one; and «أو» is eloquent in this meaning, because if you say «لا تُطع زيداً وعمراً» ('Do not obey Zayd and ʿAmr'), it is possible that you forbade me to obey both together in one state, so if I obey Zayd by himself I would not be disobedient; but if you say «لا تُطع زيداً أو عمراً أو خالداً», the meaning is that each of these is worthy of not being obeyed, so do not obey any one of them nor the group; and the like of it is «جالس الحسن أو ابن سيرين أو الشعبي»: the meaning is not that I command you to sit with one of them, so that if you sit with one of them you are right, and if you sit with the group you are right." As for his saying "the better is that «أو» in it be for detailing", Abū l-Baqāʾ preceded him to that, for he said: "«أو» here has the meaning of «و» for detailing their schools or for the difference of their places, and we have mentioned it at His saying {كُونُواْ هُوداً أَوْ نصارى} [al-Baqara: 135]." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, rejecting this view, I mean the view that «الحوايا» is a conjunction on «شحومهما»: "On this the intestines enter into the prohibition, and this is a view that neither the wording nor the meaning supports; rather they reject it", but he did not explain the aspect of rejection in them. Third: that «الحوايا» is in the position of accusative by conjunction to the excepted item, namely «ما حَمَلَتْ ظهورُهما», as though it were said: "except what the backs carry, or except the intestines, or except what is mixed"; Makkī reported it, and Abū l-Baqāʾ began with it then said: "It is also said that it is conjoined to the fats." al-Wāḥidī reported from al-Farrāʾ that he said: "It is permissible that it be in the position of accusative on the implication of the omission of the muḍāf, meaning 'or the fats of the intestines', so he omits the fats and suffices with the intestines, as the Exalted said {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82], meaning its people." Ibn al-Anbārī related from Abū ʿUbayd that he said: I said to al-Farrāʾ: It is in the position of the poet's saying:
2113 - لا يَسْمعُ المرءُ فيها ما يُؤَنِّسُهُ ... بالليل إلا نئيمَ البُوْمِ والضُّوَعا
(A man hears in it nothing that comforts him at night... except the wailing of owls and the ḍuwaʿ.)
He said to me: Yes, he takes «الضوع» as conjoined to «النئيم» and not conjoined to «البوم», just as «الحوايا» is conjoined to «ما» and not conjoined to «الظهور». I say: what the report of Ibn al-Anbārī requires is that «الحوايا» be a conjunction on the excepted «ما», and in the meaning of that there is evident unease.
This is what relates to its iʿrāb. As for what relates to its referent, it is said that they are the mabāʿir (the ruminants' paunches); it is said: the guts and intestines; it is said: everything that the belly contains, which is gathered and rounded; it is said: it is the dawwāra (the coiled bowel) which is in the belly of the sheep. There is disagreement about the singular of «الحوايا». It is said: ḥāwiya, like ḍāriba; it is said: ḥawiyya, like ṭarīfa; it is said: ḥāwiyāʾ, like qāṣiʿāʾ. al-Fārisī allowed that it be a plural of each of the three, meaning that it is suitable for that. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: it is ḥawiyya and ḥāwiya, and he did not mention ḥāwiyāʾ. Ibn al-Sikkīt mentioned the three, saying: "One says ḥāwiya and ḥawāyā like zāwiya and zawāyā, rāwiya and rawāyā"; some of them say ḥawiyya and ḥawāyā, like the ḥawiyya that is placed on the back of the camel and ridden upon; and some of them say for its singular «ḥāwiyāʾ», and he recited the saying of Jarīr:
2114 - تَضْغُو الخَنانيصُ والغُول التي أكلَتْ ... في حاوِيَاءِ رَدُومِ الليل مِجْعارِ
(The piglets squeal, and the ghoul that ate... in the coil of the night's [...]) «[Translator's note: the second half-verse is obscure in the source; the gloss is tentative.]»
And Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī recited:
2115 - كأنَّ نقيق الحَبّ في حاويائه ... فحيحُ الأفاعي أو نقيقُ العقارب
(As if the croaking of the grain in its coils were the hissing of vipers or the clicking of scorpions.)
If its singular is ḥāwiya, its pattern is fawāʿil, like ḍāriba and ḍawārib, and its counterpart among the weak roots: zāwiya and zawāyā, rāwiya and rawāyā; the origin is ḥawāwī like ḍawārib, so the wāw which is the ʿayn of the word was changed to hamza because it follows two letters of lengthening that flank the long vowel of mafāʿil; a hamza with kasra was found heavy, so it was changed to yāʾ; the kasra on the yāʾ was found heavy, so it was made a fatḥa; then the weak letter, namely the yāʾ which is the lām of the word, being moved after a fatḥa, was changed to alif, so it became ḥawāyā. If you wish you may say: the wāw was changed to a hamza with fatḥa, so the yāʾ was moved with what is before it open, so it was changed to alif, and the hamza with fatḥa came between two alifs resembling it, so the hamza was changed to yāʾ. The verification of this has been given at His saying {نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 58], with the disagreement of the people of morphology on it. Likewise, if we say its singular is «ḥāwiyāʾ», its pattern is also fawāʿil, like qāṣiʿāʾ and qawāṣiʿ, rāhiṭāʾ and rawāhiṭ, and the origin is also ḥawāwī, so what was done to what is before it was done to it. If we say that its singular is ḥawiyya, its pattern is faʿāʾil like ṭarāʾif, and the origin is ḥawāʾī, so the hamza was changed to a yāʾ with fatḥa, and the yāʾ which is the lām was changed to alif, so the wording again became ḥawāyā; the wording is the same and the process differs.
His saying «أو ما اختلط بعظم»: what was said about «حوايا» applies to it, and al-Farrāʾ held that it is accusative by conjunction on the excepted «ما» in His saying «إلا ما حَمَلَتْ ظهورهما»; what is meant is the fat tail (al-alya); and it is said: it is every fat in the flank, the eye, the ear and the legs.
His saying: {ذلك جَزَيْنَاهُم}: there are several aspects to it. One: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter is that"; so said al-Ḥawfī, Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ. The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is what follows it, the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) being omitted, i.e. "that We recompensed them with it"; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, and there is weakness in it, in that he omitted the accusative returning pronoun, and what there is in that was mentioned in (Sūrat) al-Māʾida at His saying {أَفَحُكْمَ الجاهلية يَبْغُون} [verse 50]; and also he implied the returning pronoun as attached, whereas it should be implied only as detached, but its omission is problematic, and its verification was given at the beginning of al-Baqara.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«ذلك» is in the position of nominative", and he did not state on which of the two preceding aspects, and it should be taken as the first, because of the weakness of the second. The third: that it is accusative as a maṣdar, and this is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words, for he said: "That recompense We recompensed them with, and it is the forbidding of good things." However, this may be scratched by what Ibn Mālik reported, namely that when a maṣdar is pointed to, it is obligatory that the maṣdar follow «ذلك» as an appositive, so one says «ضربت ذلك الضرب» and «قمت هذا القيام», and if you said «ضربت زيداً ذلك» or «قمت هذا» it would not be permissible. He mentioned that in rejecting the one who answered concerning the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
2116 - هذي بَرَزْتِ فَهِجْتِ رسيسا ... ثم انصرفْتِ وما شَفَيْتِ نسيسا
(This one, you appeared and stirred a lingering passion... then you turned away and healed not a breath.)
For they accused al-Mutanabbī of a solecism in that he omitted the vocative particle from the demonstrative, since the original is «يا هذي»; so they answered for him that we do not concede that «هذي» is vocative, but it is a pointer to the maṣdar, as though he said: «برزتِ هذي البَرْزة». Ibn Mālik rejected this answer, saying that a demonstrative is not accusative as pointing to the maṣdar unless it is followed by the maṣdar. If this is conceded, the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's saying "it is accusative as a maṣdar" is rejected by what the answer about Abū l-Ṭayyib's verse was rejected with; except that Ibn Mālik's rejection is not sound, because a demonstrative has occurred pointing to the maṣdar without being followed by it. The poet said:
2117 - يا عمرُو إنك قد مَلِلْت صَحابتي ... وصحابَتيك إخالُ ذاك قليلُ
(O ʿAmr, you have grown weary of my companionship... and your companionship, I think that, is small.)
The grammarians said: «ذاك» is a pointer to the maṣdar of «خال» (I think), confirming it, and he himself recited it for that.
The fourth: that it is accusative as a second object preposed before its governor, because «جزى» takes two objects, the implied form being: "We recompensed them with that forbidding". Abū l-Baqāʾ and Makkī said that it is in the position of accusative by «جَزَيْناهم», and they did not state in which aspect it is accusative: whether as the second object or the maṣdar.
His saying {لَصَادِقُونَ}: its object-of-government is omitted, i.e. "truthful in the completion of their recompense in the hereafter", for it is an allusion to their lying, since they said: "we follow Israel in forbidding these things"; and the meaning: "truthful in our report about them of that"; and no object-of-government is implied for it, i.e. "it is our nature to be truthful". The pronoun in «كذَّبوك»: the apparent is that it refers to the Jews, because they are the nearest mentioned. It is also said that it refers to the polytheists, because the speech with them preceded in His saying {نَبِّئُونِي بِعِلْم} [al-Anʿām: 143] and {أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَآء} [al-Anʿām: 144].

semin-durr:147-147.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {ذُو رَحْمَةٍ}: This clause was brought nominal, and His saying {وَلاَ يُرَدُّ بَأْسُهُ} verbal, to draw attention to the intensity of the vastness of the mercy, because the nominal clause indicates permanence and emphasis more than the verbal. His saying: {عَنِ القوم المجرمين} may be a placing of the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, to draw attention to the recording of this against them; the original being: "and His might is not turned back from you". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«فإن كَذَّبوك» is a condition (sharṭ), its apodosis (jawāb) being «فقل ربكم ذو رحمة واسعة», and the implied form: 'say: He pardons you by delaying the punishment'." This is an explanation of meaning, not of iʿrāb.

semin-durr:148-148.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ آبَاؤُنَا}: It is conjoined to the attached nominative pronoun, and here no emphasis by a detached nominative pronoun was brought, nor any separator between the two conjoined items, it being sufficient that the redundant «لا» for emphasis is present as a separator between the conjunction and the conjoined item; and this is according to the rules of the Basrans. As for the Kufans, they do not stipulate anything of that. The mastery of this question has already been given.
In this verse the pronoun is not emphasized, whereas in the verse of al-Naḥl he emphasized it, the Exalted saying: {مَا عَبَدْنَا مِن دُونِهِ مِن شَيْءٍ نَّحْنُ ولا آبَاؤُنَا} [al-Naḥl: 35]. There also he said «من دونه» twice, whereas here he said it once. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "Because the word 'worship' can be ascribed to singling out Allah in it, and this is not objectionable; rather what is objectionable is the worship of other than Allah or of something alongside Allah, so it was fitting here to mention «من دونه» with worship. As for the wording «ما أشركنا», association (ishrāk) indicates the affirmation of a partner, so the wording «من دونه» is not compounded with this verb; if the construction, outside the Qur'an, were «ما أشركنا مِنْ دونه», the meaning would not be sound. As for the second «من دونه», association indicates the prohibition of things and the making-lawful of things, so it had no need of the wording «من دونه»; whereas the wording of worship does not indicate prohibition of anything as the wording «أشرك» does, so he restricted it by His saying «من دونه». And when he omitted «مِنْ دونِه» here, it was fitting to omit «نحن» so that the construction would be consistent in lightening." I say: in this statement there is a consideration which is not hidden. His saying «من شيء»: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) on the object, i.e. "we forbade nothing", and «مِنْ دونه» is attached to «حرَّمْنا», i.e. "we forbade nothing without His permission to us in that". «كذلك» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "like the denial pointed to in His saying «فإن كَذَّبوك»". «كَذَب» is also read, without shadda.
And His saying: {حتى ذَاقُواْ}: He brought it for the extension of the denial or the lying. His saying «مِنْ علم»: it may be a mubtadaʾ with «عندكم» as a preposed khabar, or an agent (fāʿil) of the adverbial because it relies on the interrogative, and «مِنْ» is redundant on both implications. al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Wathāb read «إن يتَّبعون» with the yāʾ of the third person; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is an irregular reading, weakened by His saying {وَإِنْ أَنتُمْ إَلاَّ تَخْرُصُونَ}", meaning that after it the second person came, so the third person is far from it. It may be answered that this is of the category of iltifāt (shift of person).

semin-durr:149-149.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ}: Between «قل» and «فلله» there is something omitted. al-Zamakhsharī implied it as a condition whose apodosis is «فلله». He said: "If the matter is as you claim, namely that you are upon the will of Allah, then to Allah belongs the argument." Others implied it as a nominal clause, the implied form being: "Say: You have no argument for what you claimed; so to Allah belongs the conclusive argument against you."

semin-durr:150-150.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ هَلُمَّ شُهَدَآءَكُمُ}: «هلمَّ» here is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) with the sense of "bring", and «شهداءَكم» is the direct object (mafʿūl bihi), since a verbal noun governs as its named verb does, in transitivity and intransitivity. Know that there are two dialects of «هلمَّ», the dialect of the Hijazis and the dialect of the Tamīmīs. As for the dialect of the Hijaz, it has a single form whether it is addressed to a singular, dual, plural or feminine, as in: «هلمَّ يا زيد، يا زيدان، يا زيدون، يا هند، يا هندان، يا هندات»; in this dialect it is a verbal noun according to the grammarians because it does not change, and the Arabs adhered to the fatḥa of the mīm in this dialect, and it is a vowel of indeclinability (binā'), made indeclinable on fatḥa for lightness. As for the dialect of Tamīm, which al-Layth ascribed to Banū Saʿd, pronouns are attached to it as they are attached to all verbs, so one says: «هلمَّا، هلمُّوا، هلمِّي، هَلْمُمْن». al-Farrāʾ said: "One says «هَلُمِّين يا نسوة»", and in this dialect it is a genuine verb, not conjugated. This is the view of the majority; some have disagreed about its being a verb in this dialect, but it is nothing. The Arabs also adhered, in the Tamīmī dialect, to the fatḥa of the mīm when it is addressed to a singular masculine pronoun, and they did not allow in it what they allowed in «ردَّ» and «شدَّ» of ḍamma and kasra.
The grammarians disagreed about it: is it simple or compound? Then those who say it is compound disagreed about what it is compounded of. The majority of the Basrans hold that it is compounded of «ها», which is for alerting, and of «المم», an imperative of «لَمَّ يَلُمُّ»; so when the two were compounded, the alif of «ها» was dropped because of frequent use, and the hamzat al-waṣl dropped because it was dispensed with by the vowel of the mīm moved to it for the sake of assimilation, and the mīm was assimilated into the mīm, and it was made indeclinable on fatḥa. It is also said: rather the vowel of the mīm was moved to the lām, so the hamza dropped as it was dispensed with; then when «ها» for alerting was brought, two sākin letters met, the alif of «ها» and the lām of «لَمَّ», because it is sākin in implication, and they did not count this vowel because the vowel of transfer is incidental; so the alif of «ها» was dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters in implication. It is also said: rather the alif of «ها» was dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters, namely that when it was brought with the mīm, the hamzat al-waṣl dropped in connected speech, so two sākin letters met, the alif of «ها» and the lām of «المم», so the alif of «ها» was dropped, leaving «هَلْمُم», and the vowel of the mīm was moved to the lām and assimilated. Some held that it is compounded of «ها» for alerting as well and of «لَمّ», an imperative of «لَمَّ الله شَعْثَه», i.e. "He gathered it", and the meaning, in «هلم», is based on that, because it has the sense of "gather yourself to us"; so the alif of «ها» was dropped because of frequent use. This is very easy, since there is in it only one operation, the dropping of the alif of «ها», and it is the school of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. al-Farrāʾ held that it is compounded of «هل», which is for rebuke, and of «أمّ», an imperative of «الأَمّ», which is intending; there is in it only one operation, namely moving the vowel of the hamza to the lām of «هل». Each of these schools has been rejected with arguments whose mention would lengthen the book without benefit. «هَلُمَّ» is transitive with the sense of "bring", and intransitive with the sense of "come forward"; whoever makes it transitive takes it from «اللَّمّ», which is gathering, and whoever makes it intransitive takes it from «اللَّمَم», which is drawing near and closeness.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَيُرْسِلُ}: There are five aspects in it. The first: it is conjoined to the active participle that occurs as the ṣila (relative clause) of the definite article «أل», because it has the meaning of a verb, the implied meaning being: "and He is the One who subdues His servants and sends." So the verb is conjoined to the noun because it is in its interpretation. Similar to it, according to some, is {إِنَّ المصدقين والمصدقات وَأَقْرَضُواْ} [الحديد: 18]; they said: «وأقرضوا» is conjoined to «مصدقين» which occurs as the ṣila of «أل», because it means "those who gave charity and lent". This is nothing, because it necessitates separation between the parts of the ṣila by a foreigner: «وأقرضوا» is a completion of the ṣila of «أل» in «المصِّدِّقين», and His saying «المصدقات», which is a foreigner, has been conjoined to the relative. It has been established more than once that nothing is attached to the relative except after the completion of its ṣila. As for His saying, the Exalted: {فَوْقَهُمْ صَافَّاتٍ وَيَقْبِضْنَ} [الملك: 19], «يقبضن» is in the interpretation of a noun, i.e. "and folding (their wings)". And among the conjoining of a noun to a verb because it is in the interpretation of a noun is His saying, the Exalted: {يُخْرِجُ الحي مِنَ الميت وَمُخْرِجُ الميت} [الأنعام: 95] and the saying:

194 - 0- فأَلْفَيْتُه يوماً يُبيرُ عدوَّهُ ... ومُجْرٍ عطاءً يستخفُّ المعابرا
(I found him one day destroying his enemy, and a giver of bestowals, making light of the passers-by.)

The second: it is a verbal clause conjoined to a nominal clause, namely His saying {وَهُوَ القاهر}. The third: it is conjoined to the ṣila and what was conjoined to it, namely "He takes you" and "He knows" and what follows, i.e. "and He is the One who takes you and sends." The fourth: it is the predicate of an omitted subject, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). As to its owner there are two aspects, the more apparent being that it is the latent pronoun in «القاهر». The second: that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the adverbial phrase; so said Abū al-Baqāʾ, who reported it from the Shaykh and said: "This aspect is the weakest of the i'rabs." As to their saying "the pronoun in the adverbial phrase", there is no adverbial phrase here from which this ḥāl might be imagined to be from a pronoun in it except His saying «فوق عباده»; but by what means does this adverbial phrase carry a pronoun? The answer is that it was mentioned in the verse similar to this that «فوق عباده» has five aspects, three of which carry a pronoun, namely its being a second predicate, or a substitute for the predicate, or a ḥāl. We were compelled to imply a subject before «يُرْسِلُ» only because an affirmative imperfect, when it occurs as a ḥāl, is not accompanied by the wāw; its explanation has gone before more than once. The fifth: it is resumptive, brought to report that, and this aspect is in meaning like the second.

His saying: {عَلَيْكُم} admits three aspects, the most apparent being that it is attached to «يرسل», and from it are {يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُمَا} [الرحمن: 35], {فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ} [الأعراف: 133] and {وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْراً} [الفيل: 3], and so on. The second: it is attached to «حَفَظَة». One says «حَفِظْتُ عليه عمله», so the implied meaning: "He sends guardians over you." The Shaykh said: "i.e. they preserve for you their deeds, as He said: {وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ} [الانفطار: 10], as you say «حَفِظْتُ عليك ما تعمل»." His saying "as He said: 'Indeed over you are guardians'" is a comparison in meaning, not that «عليكم» is attached to «حافظين»; for «عليكم» is the predicate of «إن» and so is attached to an omitted word.

The third: it is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from «حفظة», since if it were postponed it could be an adjective of it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «عليكم» has two aspects: one, that it is attached to «يرسل»; the second, that it is in the intention of postponement, and in it are two aspects: one, that it is attached to «حفظة» itself and the object is omitted, i.e. "He sends over you those who preserve your deeds"; the second, that it is an adjective of «حفظة» that was fronted and so became a ḥāl. End of quotation. His saying "the object is omitted" means the object of «حفظة», but it gives the impression that the implying of the object is specific to the aspect he mentioned, and it is not so; rather it must be implied in every aspect, and «حَفَظَة» works on that implied object only because it is an adjective of an omitted noun, the implied meaning: "He sends over you angels, guardians", because it does not work except under conditions of which this is one, I mean its relying on a described noun.

«حَفَظَة» is the plural of «حافظ», and it is regular for every adjective on the pattern fāʿil with sound lām, for a rational masculine, like «بارّ» and «بَرَة», «فاجِر» and «فَجَرة», «كامل» and «كَمَلة», and it is rare for non-rational beings, as in their saying «غراب ناعق» and «غربان نَعَقَه». The like of His saying «حتى إذا جاء» has been mentioned earlier.

His saying: {تَوَفَّتْهُ}: The majority read {توفَّتْه} as a past verb with the feminine tāʾ because of the feminine plural. Ḥamza read {توفَّاه} without the feminine tāʾ, which admits two aspects, the more apparent being that it is a past verb and the feminine tāʾ was omitted for two reasons: one, that the feminine is figurative; the second, the separation between the verb and its agent by the object. The second: that it is an imperfect, its original being «تتوفاه» with two tāʾs, one of which was dropped, with disagreement as to which, like «تَنَزَّلُ» and its type. Ḥamza follows his rule in the imāla of an alif like this. Al-Aʿmash read {يتوفَّاه} as an imperfect with the yāʾ of the third person, taking into account that the feminine is figurative or for the separation; so it is like Ḥamza's reading in the first aspect in that the verb is masculine, and like his reading in the second aspect in that he brought it as an imperfect. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "{تتوفَّاه} was read irregularly, in the future," and did not mention it with yāʾ or tāʾ.

His saying: {وَهُمْ لاَ يُفَرِّطُونَ}: This clause admits two aspects, the more apparent being that it is a ḥāl from «رسلنا». The second: that it is resumptive, brought to report about them with this attribute. The majority read «يُفَرِّطون» with doubling, and its meaning is "they do not fall short". ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and al-Aʿraj read «يُفْرِطون» light, from «أفرط», and there are two interpretations of it. One: that it means they do not exceed the limit in what they have been commanded. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Tafrīṭ is slackness and delay beyond the limit, and ifrāṭ is exceeding the limit, i.e. they do not diminish what they have been commanded, nor do they add." The second: that its meaning is they do not go ahead of the command of Allah; this requires a report that «أفرط» has the meaning of «فَرَّط», i.e. went ahead. Al-Jāḥiẓ said something close to this, for he said: "The meaning of «لا يُفْرِطون» is: they do not leave anyone to slip away from them, i.e. get ahead of them and escape them." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is also read light, i.e. they do not add to what they have been commanded," which is close to what has preceded.

«Translator's note: the source reads «مصدر على غير الصدر» and «الاية» in this passage; translated as written/intended.»

semin-durr:62-62.t: His saying, the Exalted: {مَوْلاَهُمُ الحق}: two attributes of Allah. Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read «الحقَّ» in the accusative, which has two interpretations, the more apparent being that it is a cut-off adjective (naʿt maqṭūʿ). The second: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they were returned the true return, not the false". {رِدُّوا} was also read with kasra on the rāʾ, and its derivation has been given in full earlier. The pronoun in «مولاهم» has three aspects, the more apparent being that it refers to the servants in {فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ}; so His saying {وَيُرْسِلُ عَلَيْكُم} is an iltifāt (shift of person), since the original would be "and He sends over them", and the benefit of this shift is alerting and awakening. The second: that it refers to the angels meant by «رسلنا», meaning that they die as the children of Ādam die, and are returned to their Lord. The third: that it refers to «أحد» in {إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَكُمُ الموت}, since what is meant by it is the plural, not the singular.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ مَن يُنَجِّيكُمْ}: The Seven read this one with doubling; {قل الله ينجيكم}: the Kufans and Hishām ibn ʿAmmār from Ibn ʿĀmir read it with doubling like the first; and Ḥumayd ibn Qays, Yaʿqūb and ʿAlī ibn Naṣr from Abū ʿAmr read both with the light form, from «أنجى». The result is that the Kufans and Hishām double in both places, that Ḥumayd and those with him lighten in both, and that Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Dhakwān from Ibn ʿĀmir double the first and lighten the second. The readings are clear, as they derive from «نجَّى» and «أنجى», and the doubling and the hamza both serve to make the verb transitive; the Kufans and Hishām kept to transitivity by doubling, Ḥumayd and his group kept to it by the hamza, and the others combined both forms of transitivity, combining the two dialects, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَمَهِّلِ الكافرين أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْداً} [الطارق: 17]. The interrogative is for affirmation and reproach. There is an omitted muḍāf in the discourse, i.e. "from the perils of the darknesses" or "from their terrors"; the darknesses are a figure for hardships.

His saying: {تَدْعُونَهُ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the object of «ينجيكم», which is the apparent, i.e. "He saves you while you call upon Him", or from its agent, i.e. "while called upon by you."

«Translator's note: the source reads «مَدْعُوَّاً مِنْ جتهكم» (apparently «من جهتكم»); translated as "by you".»

His saying: {تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً}: Two aspects are permissible for them. One: that they are two maṣdars in the position of ḥāl, i.e. "you call upon Him humbly and secretly." The second: that they are two maṣdars from the meaning of the governor, not from its wording, like "I sat sitting". The majority read {خُفْية} with ḍamma on the khāʾ. Abū Bakr read it with kasra, and they are two dialects, like «العُدوة» and «العِدوة», «الأُسوة» and «الإِسوة». Al-Aʿmash read {وخيفة} like the one in al-Aʿrāf, which is from «الخوف», the wāw being turned into yāʾ because the preceding letter has kasra and it is quiescent. On this reading it would appear to be an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), were it not for what «تضرُّعاً» refuses of the meaning.

His saying: {لَّئِنْ أَنجَانَا}: Apparently this oath clause is an explanation of the supplication before it, and it may also be accusative in position by an implied "saying", and that saying would be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «تَدْعُونه», i.e. "you call upon Him saying that." You already know from what has gone before, more than once, how the condition and the oath combine. The Kufans read «أَنْجانا» in the third person, in keeping with {تَدْعُونَهُ}, and the rest «أَنْجَيْتنا» in the second person, relating their address in the state of supplication. Each read according to what is written in his codex, for in the codices of Kufa it is «أنجانا» and in the others «أَنْجَيْتنا».

His saying: {مِنْ هذه}: attached to the verb before it; «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range, and «هذه» refers to the darknesses, since they run in the manner of a single feminine; likewise «منها» returns to the darknesses for the reason given.

semin-durr:64-64.t: His saying: {وَمِن كُلِّ كَرْبٍ}: conjoined to the genitive pronoun by repeating the preposition, which is obligatory according to the Basrans, and it has been mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying: {عَذَاباً مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ}: The adverbial phrase may be attached to «نبعث», and it may be attached to an omitted word as an adjective of «عذاباً», i.e. "a punishment coming from these two directions."

His saying: {أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ}: conjoined to «يَبْعَث». The majority read «يَلْبسكم» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and there are two aspects in it. One: that it means "He mixes you up as divided factions of different inclinations, each faction following an imām"; the meaning of their mixing is the outbreak of fighting among them, so that they are mixed in the heat of battle, as in the saying of the author of the Ḥamāsa:

194 - 1- وكتيبةٍ لَبَّسْتُها بكتيبةٍ ... حتى إذا التبسَتْ نَفَضْتُ لها يدي
فَتَرَكْتُهمْ تَقِصُ الرماحُ ظهورَهم ... ما بين مُنْعَفِرٍ وآخرَ مُسْنَدِ
(Many a squadron I mingled with another squadron, until when they were intermixed I shook my hand free of them; I left them with the lances breaking their backs, some rolled in the dust, others propped up.)

This is al-Zamakhsharī's wording, so he made it from «اللَّبس» which is mixing, and with this fine explanation the transitivity of «يلبس» to an object becomes clear. «شيعاً» is accusative as a ḥāl. It is the plural of «شِيْعة», like «سِدْرة» and «سِدَر». It was also said: «شيعاً» is accusative as a maṣdar from the meaning of the first verb, i.e. a maṣdar not from the same root, like "I sat sitting". The Shaykh said: "To make it a maṣdar requires a report from the language." On this too it may be a ḥāl, like «أتيته ركضاً», i.e. "running" or "with running". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The majority read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, i.e. 'He confuses your affairs for you', so the preposition and the object were omitted; the better is for the implied form to be 'or He confuses your affairs', with the muḍāf omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place." All this is unnecessary, because of what you know of al-Zamakhsharī's statement.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Madanī read «يُلبسكم» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from the quadriliteral «ألبس», and there are two aspects in it. One: that the second object is omitted, the implied form being "or He clothes you with discord"; «شيعاً» on this is a ḥāl, i.e. "He clothes you with discord while you are divided and scattered." The second: that «شِيعاً» is the second object, as if He made the people clothe one another figuratively, as in the saying:

194 - 2- لَبِسْتُ أناساً فَأَفْنَيْتُهمْ ... وأَفْنَيْتُ بعد أُناسٍ أُناسا
(I lived among people and saw them pass away, and after people I saw other people pass away.)

«الشيعة» are those by whom a person is strengthened, and the plural is «شِيَع» as mentioned and «أشياع»; so said al-Rāghib. The apparent is that «أشياعاً» is the plural of «شِيَع», like «عِنَب» and «أعناب», «ضِلَع» and «أضلاع», and «شِيَع» is the plural of «شِيْعة», so it is a plural of a plural.

His saying: {وَيُذِيقَ}: conjoined to «يَبْعَث». «الإِذاقة» ("causing to taste") is a metaphor, and it is common: {ذُوقُواْ مَسَّ سَقَرَ} [القمر: 48], {ذُقْ إِنَّكَ} [الدخان: 49], {فَذُوقُواْ العذاب} [الأنعام: 30]. He said:

194 - 3- أَذَقْناهُمْ كؤوسَ الموت صِرْفاً ... وذاقوا من أَسِنَّتنا كؤوسا
(We made them taste the cups of death unmixed, and they tasted cups from our spearheads.)

Al-Aʿmash read {ونذيق} with the nūn of grandeur, which is an iltifāt whose benefit is magnifying the matter and warning of His might.

«Translator's note: the source reads «الجهيتن» in the first paragraph and «ملاحكم» (for «ملاحم») in the second; translated as intended.»

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {وَكَذَّبَ بِهِ}: The hāʾ in «به» refers back to the punishment mentioned before in His saying {عَذَاباً مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ}; so said al-Zamakhsharī. It was also said: it refers to the Qurʾān. It was said: it refers to the warning included in these preceding verses. It was said: to the Prophet ﷺ, and this is remote because the address with the kāf follows immediately, so had it been so, He would have said «وكذَّب به قومك»; and the claim of an iltifāt (shift of person) in it is more remote. It was also said: an adjective must be omitted here, i.e. "and your people, the obstinate, or the disbelievers, denied it", because not all his people denied him, like His saying: {إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ} [هود: 46], i.e. of those saved. The omission of the adjective with the described noun remaining is very rare, unlike the opposite. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read {وكَذَّبَتْ} with the feminine tāʾ, like His saying, the Exalted: {كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ} [الشعراء: 105] and {كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ} [القمر: 33], taking the group into account.

His saying: {وَهُوَ الحق}: There are two aspects in this clause, the apparent being that it is resumptive. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «به», i.e. "they denied it while it is the truth", which is more serious in ugliness.

His saying: {عَلَيْكُمْ}: attached to what follows it, and it is an emphasis, fronted for the sake of the verse-endings. It may also be a ḥāl from His saying «بوكيل», because if it were postponed it could be an adjective of it; this is according to those who allow the ḥāl to precede its owner when the latter is governed by a preposition, which is the choice of a group, and they recited as evidence the verse:

194 - 4- غافلاً تُعْرَضُ المَنِيَّةُ للمَرْ ... ءِ فيُدْعَى ولات حين إباءُ
(Death is presented to a man while he is heedless, and he is called, when there is no time for refusal.)

So he fronted «غافلاً» before its owner, which is «المرء», and before its governor, which is «تُعرض»; this is therefore more fitting. And from it:

194 - 5- لَئِنْ كان بَرْدُ الماءِ هَيْمانَ صادياً ... إليَّ حبيباً إنها لحبيبُ
(If the coolness of water is dear to me, thirsty and parched, then she is dear indeed.)

i.e. "dear to me, thirsty and parched"; and similarly:

194 - 6- فإن يك أذوادٌ أُصِبْنَ ونسوةٌ ... فَلَنْ يذهبوا فَرْغاً بقتل حبالِ
(If camels and women were taken, they will not go in vain for the killing of Ḥibāl.)

«فرغاً» is a ḥāl from «بقتل», and «حبال» with undotted ḥāʾ is the name of a man; and the preposition here is redundant, so its permissibility is more fitting than what we mentioned.

«Translator's note: the source text has «وكذِّبَتْ» with kasra on the dhāl in the printed vocalization; the phrase is translated as the reading with feminine tāʾ. The source also has «الجماعمة» for «الجماعة».»

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لِّكُلِّ نَبَإٍ مُّسْتَقَرٌّ}: «نبأ» may be nominative as a subject, its predicate being the preposition and its genitive noun before it; or as an agent according to al-Akhfash, by the preposition and its genitive noun before it. «مستقر» may be a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar), i.e. "settlement", or a place or a time.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ}: «إذا» is accusative by its apodosis, which is «فأعرضْ», i.e. "turn away from them at this time". «رأيت» here may be that of sight, which is the apparent, and for that reason it takes one object. The Shaykh said: "A ḥāl must be implied as omitted, i.e. 'when you see those who plunge into Our verses while they are plunging into them', that is, 'when you see them engaged in plunging into them'." End of quotation. I say: there is no need for that, because His saying «يخوضون» is an imperfect and the preponderant view is that it is a ḥāl; also, «الذين يخوضون» is in the force of "the plungers", and the active participle is literally for the present without disagreement, so this is taken in its literal sense, and there is no need to imply this ḥāl which he supplied, and which is a confirmatory ḥāl. It may also be that of knowledge, which the Shaykh weakened by saying that it requires omission of the second object, and its omission is either for brevity by limiting (iqtiṣār) or by abridgement (ikhtiṣār); if the first, it is prohibited by agreement, and if the second, the correct view is prohibition, to the point that some grammarians prohibited that.

His saying: {غَيْرِهِ}: There are two aspects regarding the hāʾ in it. One: that it refers to the verses, and it returned as singular masculine because the verses are in the meaning of "the discourse" and "the Qurʾān". It was said: it refers to the plunging, i.e. what is indicated by the verb, as in the saying:

194 - 7- إذا نُهِي السَّفيهُ جرى إليه ... وخالف والسفيهُ إلى خلافِ
(When the fool is forbidden, he runs to it and opposes, and the fool goes toward opposition.)

i.e. "he ran to foolishness", which the adjective indicated, as the verb indicates its maṣdar; i.e. "until they plunge into a discourse other than the plunging."

His saying: {يُنسِيَنَّكَ}: The common reading is «يُنْسِيَنَّك» with light sīn, from «أنساه», as in His saying: {وَمَآ أَنْسَانِيهُ إِلاَّ الشيطان} [الكهف: 63] and {فَأَنْسَاهُ الشيطان} [يوسف: 42]. Ibn ʿĀmir read it with doubling of the sīn, from «نَسَّاه». Transitivity has come in this verb sometimes by the hamza and sometimes by doubling, as mentioned for «أنجى» and «نجَّى», «أمهل» and «مهَّل». The second object is omitted in both readings, the implied form being: "and if Satan makes you forget the reminder or the truth." It is better to imply what suits the meaning, i.e. "and if Satan makes you forget what you were commanded, of leaving the sessions of the plungers, after your being reminded, then do not sit with them afterwards." He brought them out as overt nouns only to record against them the attribute of wrongdoing. The first condition came with «إذا» because their plunging into the verses is certain, and the second with «إنْ» because Satan's making him forget is not a certain matter; it may occur and may not, and he is protected from it.

No maṣdar has come on the pattern fiʿlā other than «ذكرى». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«وإمَّا» is a condition, and the heavy nūn is usually required with it, though it is not always required, as in the saying:

194 - 8- إمَّا يُصيبْكَ عدوٌّ في مُنَاوَأَةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If an enemy afflicts you in a contest ...)"

What he mentioned about the necessity of the emphasis is the position of al-Zajjāj, while people hold otherwise; they recited what Ibn ʿAṭiyya recited and other verses which I mentioned in Sharḥ al-Tasḥīl, such as the saying:

194 - 9- إمَّا تَرَيْني اليومَ أمَّ حَمْزِ ...
(If you see me today, Umm Ḥamz ...)

I have gathered many of the aspects of this question at the beginning of al-Baqara, except that no one said its emphasis with the heavy form rather than the light is required, even if the apparent wording of Abū Muḥammad is that.

«Translator's note: the source reads «انفاقاً» (for «اتفاقاً») and «ح‍َذْفُ»; translated as intended. Abū Muḥammad is Ibn ʿAṭiyya.»

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا عَلَى الذين}: It is permissible to take «ما» as the Ḥijāzī one, so that «من شيء» is its subject (ism), with «من» added in it to confirm inclusiveness, and {عَلَى الذين يَتَّقُونَ} is its predicate according to those who allow it to work with the predicate fronted absolutely, or who see that in the adverbial phrase and its equivalent. {مِنْ حِسَابِهِم} is a ḥāl from «شيء», because if it were postponed, it would be an adjective of it. It may also be non-working, either on the dialect of Tamīm or on the dialect of the Ḥijāz, owing to the loss of a condition, namely the fronting of its predicate, even if it is an adverbial; the verification of that is in what preceded in His saying: {مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ} [الأنعام: 52].

His saying: {ولكن ذكرى}: four aspects. The first: it is accusative as a maṣdar by an implied verb; some implied it as a command, i.e. "but remind them with a reminder", and some implied it as a report, i.e. "but they remind them with a reminder". The second: it is a subject whose predicate is omitted, i.e. "but upon them is a reminder", or "upon you is a reminder", i.e. reminding them. The third: it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "it is a reminder", i.e. the prohibition of sitting with them and abstaining from it is a reminder. The fourth: it is conjoined to the position of «شيء» which is genitive by «مِنْ», i.e. "nothing of their account is upon the God-fearing, but upon them is a reminder", so it is a conjoining of single terms; whereas according to the previous aspects it is a conjoining of clauses. Al-Zamakhsharī rejected this fourth aspect, and the Shaykh rejected him in turn, so their two statements must be cited. Abū al-Qāsim said: "It is not permissible that it be conjoined to the position of «من شيء», like your saying «ما في الدار من أحد ولكن زيد», because His saying «من حسابهم» refuses that."

The Shaykh said: "It is as if he imagined that in the conjunction the restriction in the conjoined-to term is necessarily carried over, namely «من حسابهم», which is a restriction in «شيء»; so according to him it is not permissible that it be a conjoining of single terms conjoined to «من شيء» by position, because the implied meaning for him would become: 'but a reminder of their account', and the meaning is not so. What he imagined is nothing; what he mentioned is not necessary in conjunction with «ولكن». You say: «ما عندنا رجل سوء ولكن رجلُ صدق», and «ما عندنا رجل من تميم ولكن رجل من قريش», and «ما قام من رجل عالم ولكن رجل جاهل». So on what we have established, it may be a conjoining of clauses as mentioned earlier, or a conjoining of single terms, the conjunction being by the wāw, and «لكن» being brought for the correction (istidrāk)."

I say: his saying "You say: «ما عندنا رجل سوء ولكن رجل صدق»", and so on to the end of the examples he mentioned, does not refute al-Zamakhsharī, because al-Zamakhsharī and others among the people of the language and the legal theorists say: conjunction is apparently for sharing; so if there is a restriction in the conjoined-to term, the apparent is that the conjoined term is bound by that restriction, unless a diverting indication comes, to which the matter is then referred.

So if you say: «ضربت زيداً يوم الجمعة وعمراً», the apparent is that ʿAmr shares with Zayd in the beating restricted to Friday; if you say «وعمراً يوم السبت», he does not share his restriction. The noble verse is of the first kind, i.e. no indication is brought with the conjoined term to take it out; so the apparent is that it shares with the first in its restriction, and if it shared with it in its restriction, what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned would follow. As for the examples he brought, the conjoined term is restricted by a restriction other than that by which the first was restricted. He should have brought examples like these, saying: «ما عندنا رجل سوء ولكن امرأة», and «ما عندنا رجل من تميم ولكن صبي»; the apparent from this is that the meaning is: "but an evil woman" and "but a boy of Quraysh". And al-Zamakhsharī's saying "conjoined to the position of «من شيء»", rather than saying "conjoined to its form", has a fine benefit that is hard to recognize: it is that «لكن» is a particle of affirmation, so if what follows it were conjoined to the genitive noun of «مِنْ» by form, «من» would necessarily be redundant in an affirmative context, and most of the Basrans hold that it is not redundant in that. What indicates that affirmation is considered in «لكن» is that when they conjoin after the predicate of the Ḥijāzī «ما», they invalidate the accusative, because it does not work when the negation is broken by an exception; and «بل» is like «لكن» in what I have told you.

«Translator's note: the source prints «اي» for «أي», «ماعندما» for «ما عندنا», and «انفاقاً»-type misprints in this passage; translated as intended.»

semin-durr:151-151.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ}: There are three aspects to this «ما». The most apparent: that it is a relative meaning «الذي», with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "that which He has forbidden", and the relative is in the position of accusative as a direct object. The second: that it is maṣdariyya, i.e. "recite the prohibition of your Lord"; but the prohibition itself is not recited; rather it is a maṣdar standing in the place of the direct object, i.e. "recite what your Lord has forbidden, which He forbade". The third: that it is interrogative, in the position of accusative by the «حرَّم» after it, and it suspends (muʿallaqa) «أتل», the implied form being: "recite what thing your Lord has forbidden"; and this is weak, because only verbs of the heart, and what is carried on them, are suspended. As for «عليكم», there are two aspects. One: that it is attached to «حَرَّم», and this is the choice of the Basrans. The second: that it is attached to «أَتْلُ», and this is the choice of the Kufans; meaning that the question belongs to the chapter of iʿmāl (competition of two governors), and you have learned that the choice of the Basrans is to give effect to the second governor and the choice of the Kufans is to give effect to the first.
His saying: {أَلاَّ تُشْرِكُواْ}: there are several aspects. One: that «أَنْ» is explicative (tafsīriyya), because what has the sense of saying, not its letters, precedes it; and «لا» is prohibitive and «تشركوا» is jussive by it. This is an apparent aspect and is al-Farrāʾ's choice; he said: "It is possible that it be jussive by «لا» as a prohibition, as you say: «أمرتك أَنْ لا تذهب إلى زيد», with accusative and jussive. Then he said: The jussive in this verse is dearer to me, like His saying, the Exalted, {أَوْفُواْ المكيال والميزان} [Hūd: 85]." I say: he means that the conjunction of this imperative clause strengthens that what precedes it is a prohibition, so that the two ends of the speech correspond. It is also al-Zamakhsharī's choice, for he said: "«أَنْ» in «أن لا تشركوا» is explicative and «لا» is for prohibition." Then he said after some speech: "If you say: if you make «أن» explicative of the verb of reciting, which is suspended on «ما حرم ربكم», it is necessary that what follows be entirely forbidden and prohibited, like the association and what follows it that the particle of prohibition has entered; so what will you do with the imperatives? I say: when these imperatives came along with the prohibitions, with the verb of prohibition preceding them all, and they shared in entering under its rule, it is known that the prohibition goes back to their opposites, namely mistreatment of the parents, short-changing in measure and scales, abandoning justice in speech, and breaking the covenant."
The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "That these things shared in entering under the rule of the prohibition, and that the prohibition goes back to the opposites of the imperatives, is very remote and a riddle in blindness, and no necessity calls for it." I say: what he considered remote is not remote, and where is the riddle and blindness in this statement that he should hurl it at him? Then the Shaykh said: "As for the conjunction of these imperatives, it admits two aspects. One: that they are conjoined not to the prohibitions before them, which would require the prohibition to extend to them since they would be within the scope of the explicative «أن», but rather they are conjoined to His saying {تَعَالَوْاْ أتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ}; He commanded them first with a command on which the mention of prohibitions depends, then commanded them second with imperatives; and this is a clear meaning.
The second: that the imperatives are conjoined to the prohibitions and enter under the explicative «أن»; this is sound on the implication of an omitted word of which «أن» is explicative, and of the uttered word before it that indicated its omission, the implied form being «وما أمركم به» ("and what He commanded you"); «وما أمركم به» was omitted because «ما حَرَّم عليه» indicates it, for the meaning of «ما حرم ربكم» is «ما نهاكم ربكم عنه» ("what your Lord has forbidden you"), so the meaning: come, I shall recite what your Lord forbade you and what He commanded you. And when the implied form is thus, it is sound for «أن» to be explicative of the verb of prohibition which the prohibition indicates and of the omitted verb of command; do you not see that you may say «أمرتك أن لا تكرم جاهلاً وأكرم عالماً» ('I commanded you not to honour an ignorant man, and honour a learned one'), since it is permissible to conjoin command to prohibition and prohibition to command, as he said:
2118 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يقولون لا تَهْلِكْ أسىً وتجمَّلِ
(... they say: do not perish of grief, and bear up with grace.)
and we know of no disagreement on this, unlike clauses that differ in report, interrogative and performative, where there is disagreement about the permissibility of the conjunction." End of his words.
The second: that «أَنْ» is the one that puts the following verb in the accusative, and it and what is in its scope are in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) for «ما حرم». The third: that it is also the accusative-governing one, and it and what is in its scope are a badal for the omitted returning pronoun, since the implied form is «ما حَرَّمه»; and in meaning it is like the preceding. «لا», on these two aspects, is redundant (zāʾida) lest the meaning be spoiled, like its redundancy in His saying, the Exalted, {أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 12] and {لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ} [al-Ḥadīd: 29]. The Shaykh said: "This is weak because the generality of what is forbidden is confined to association, since the command that follows is not within the forbidden, nor what follows the command in which it is not possible to claim the redundancy of «لا», given that it is evident that «لا» in it is for prohibition." When Makkī mentioned that it is a badal for «ما حرم», he did not draw attention to the redundancy of «لا», though it is indispensable. al-Zamakhsharī prevented it from being a badal for «ما حرم», saying: "If you say: why do you not say it is the one that puts the verb in the accusative, and make «أن لا تشركوا» a badal for «ما حرم»? I say: it is necessary that «أن لا تشركوا ولا تقربوا ولا تقتلوا ولا تتبعوا السبل» be prohibitions, because the imperatives turn back upon them, and they are His saying «بالوالدين إحساناً», for the implied form is: 'and treat the parents with kindness', 'and fulfil', 'and when you speak, be just', 'and fulfil the covenant of Allah'. If you say: what will you do with His saying {وَأَنَّ هذا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيماً فاتبعوه} [al-Anʿām: 153] for one who reads it with fatḥa? Its conjunction to «أَنْ لا تشركوا» is straight only if you make «أن» the accusative-governing one, so that the meaning is: 'I recite to you the negation of association, and I recite to you that this is My straight path'? I say: I make His saying «وأن هذا صراطي مستقيماً» a reason for following, with an implied lām, like His saying {وَأَنَّ المساجد لِلَّهِ فَلاَ تَدْعُواْ مَعَ الله أَحَداً} [al-Jinn: 18], meaning: 'and because this is My straight path, follow it'; and the proof is the reading with kasra, as though it were said: 'and follow My path because it is straight', or 'and follow My path, for it is straight'."
The Shaykh objected to him after the first question and its answer, namely "If you say: why do you not say it is the accusative-governing one," up to {وَبِعَهْدِ الله أَوْفُواْ}, saying: "It is not necessary that all the imperatives be conjoined to what «لا» has entered, because we have shown the permissibility of conjoining «وبالوالدين إحساناً» to «تعالَوا», and what follows it is conjoined to it, and His saying «وبالوالدين إحساناً» would not be conjoined to «أن لا تشركوا»."
The fourth: that «أَنْ» is the accusative-governing one and it and what is in its scope are accusative by incitement (ighrāʾ) with «عليكم», and the first speech is complete at His saying «ربكم», then He began and said: «عليكم أن لا تشركوا», i.e. "keep to the negation of association and its absence". This, although a group mentioned it as Ibn al-Anbārī reported, is weak because of the disjointing of the construction from its apparent form, and because it does not come to mind.
The fifth: that it and what is in its scope are in the position of accusative or genitive on the omission of the lām of reason, the implied form being: "recite what your Lord has forbidden you so that you do not associate". This is reported from Abū Isḥāq, except that some found it remote in that what follows is a command conjoined by wāw and prohibitions conjoined by wāw also, so it is not fitting that it be a clarification of what He forbade; as for the command, in respect of meaning, and as for the prohibitions, in respect of the conjunction.
The sixth: that it and what follows it are in the position of accusative by an implied verb, the implied form being: "I charge you not to associate", because His saying «وبالوالدين إحساناً» is carried on "I charge you to treat the parents with kindness"; this is also the school of Abū Isḥāq.
The seventh: that «أَنْ» and what is in its scope are in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the forbidden is that you not associate", or "the recited is that you not associate", except that the implication with something like "the recited" is better, because it does not require the redundancy of «لا», whereas the implication with "the forbidden" requires its redundancy lest the meaning be spoiled.
The eighth: that it is also in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the preceding preposition phrase as the khabar, the implied form being: "upon you is the absence of association", the pause being at His saying «ربكم», as was said in the aspect of incitement. This is a school of Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī, for he said: "It may be in the position of nominative by «على», as you say: «عليكم الصيام والحج»."
The ninth: that it is in the position of nominative as an agent (fāʿil) of the preposition phrase before it, and this is the apparent sense of Ibn al-Anbārī's preceding statement, the implied form being: "the absence of association is incumbent upon you". The result for the position of «أن لا تشركوا» is three aspects: nominative, accusative and genitive. The genitive is in one way, namely on the omission of the preposition according to the school of al-Khalīl and al-Kisāʾī; the nominative in three ways; the accusative in six ways; so the total of that is ten aspects whose verification has been given.
«شيئاً» has two aspects. One: that it is a direct object. The second: that it is a maṣdar, i.e. ishrākan, that is: "anything of association".
And His saying {وبالوالدين إِحْسَاناً}: its verification was given in al-Baqara.
His saying: {مِّنْ إمْلاَقٍ}: «مِنْ» is causal, attached to the verb that is prohibited, i.e. "do not kill your children because of imlāq". «الإملاق» is poverty, in the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās. It is also said: hunger, in the dialect of Lakhm; Muʾarrij reported it. It is also said: extravagance; «أَمْلق» means he was extravagant in his spending; so said Muḥammad ibn Naʿīm al-Tirmidhī. It is also said: spending; «أملق مالَه» means he spent it; so said al-Mundhir ibn Saʿīd. «الإملاق» is also ruination, so said Shamir; he said: "«أَمْلَقَ» is both intransitive and transitive: «أَمْلَقَ الرجل» when he became poor is intransitive; and «أملق ما عنده الدهر» means time ruined what he had." On that al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl recited the saying of Aws ibn Ḥajar:
2119 - ولمَّا رأيت العُدْمَ قَيَّد نائلي ... وأملق ما عندي خطوبٌ تَنَبَّلُ
(When I saw that destitution had fettered my giving... and calamities that carry off wealth had ruined what I had.)
That is: «تَنَبَّلُ» means they take away the wealth; «تَنَبَّلَتْ بما عندي» means it went off with what I had.
In this noble verse {نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ}, He put those addressed first, while in al-Isrāʾ He put the pronoun of the children before them, saying {نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُم} [al-Isrāʾ: 31]. It is said: for variety in eloquence. Better than that is to say: the apparent of His saying «من إملاق» is that the imlāq has occurred for the father, not that it is expected and feared, so He began first with the promise of providing for the fathers as glad tidings to them of the removal of the imlāq they were in; whereas in the verse of Subḥān (al-Isrāʾ), its apparent sense is that they were well-off and only feared that poverty would come about, hence He said «خَشْيَةَ إملاقٍ» (fear of imlāq), and it is only anticipated matters that are feared, so it began there with the guarantee of their provision, so there is no sense in your killing them. So this verse gives the prohibition to fathers against killing children even if they are afflicted with poverty, and the other gives it against killing them even if they are well-off but fear that poverty will occur; and giving a new meaning is preferable to claiming that the two verses have one meaning for emphasis.
His saying {مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ}: in the position of accusative as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) for «الفواحش», i.e. "do not approach its overt and its hidden", as you say: «ضربْتُ زيداً ما ظهر منه وما بطن»; and it is possible that «ما» be a badal of part from whole. «منها» is attached to an omitted word because it is a ḥāl from the agent of «ظهر». «منها» was omitted after His saying «بطن» because His saying «منها» in the first indicates it.
His saying {إِلاَّ بالحق}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «تقتلوا», i.e. "do not kill them except in a state of being with the right"; and it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a killing accompanied by the right", which is that the killing be for retaliation, or for apostasy, or for adultery, with its conditions, as has come explained in the Sunna. His saying «ولا تَقْتلوا» is similar to the mention of the specific after the general, out of concern for its importance; because the abominations (fawāḥish) include the killing of a soul, so this was set apart from them as a mark of its gravity and to make it dreadful, and because an exception was made from it in His saying «إلا بالحق»; had He not mentioned this specific, the exception from the generality of abominations would not have been sound; had it been said outside the Qur'an «لا تَقْرَبوا الفواحشَ إلا بالحق», it would not have been anything.
His saying {ذلكم وَصَّاكُمْ}: there are two views on its position. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is the verbal clause after it. The second: that it is in the position of accusative by an implied verb from the meaning of the verb that follows it, and the question belongs to the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation), the implied form being: "He enjoined on you" or "charged you with that", and «وصَّاكم به» is explicative of this implied governor, like His saying, the Exalted, {والظالمين أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذَاباً أَلِيماً} [al-Insān: 31]. His saying here «لعلكم تعقلون» was fitting, because the intellect is the locus of obligation and of the charge with these things mentioned.

semin-durr:152-152.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ بالتي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ}: An emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), i.e. "do not approach it except with the finest quality"; so it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be an adjective of a maṣdar. He used the elative form to draw attention to the fact that one should strive in that and do the finest, and not be satisfied with the good.
His saying: {حتى يَبْلُغَ}: This is a limit (ghāya) in respect of meaning, for the meaning is: "guard his property until he reaches his maturity"; and if we made it a limit for the wording, the implied form would be: "do not approach it until he reaches, then approach it", and that is not intended.
«الأَشَدُّ»: the grammarians disagreed about it in five views. It is said: it is a plural with no singular, and this is the view of al-Farrāʾ, for he said: "The singular of «الأشدّ» would, by analogy, be «شَدّ», but I have not heard a singular for it." It is said: it is a singular, not a plural; Ibn al-Anbārī reported that from some of the people of the language, and that it is in the position of «الآنُك» (lead); and the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) reported from him that this aspect is his choice among others, then said: "It is not the choice, for the pattern afʿul is absent from singulars by original formation." It is said: it is a plural of «شِدَّة», fiʿla being pluralized as afʿul, like niʿma and anʿum; so said Abū l-Haytham, and he said: "It is as though the hāʾ in «الشدة» and «النعمة» were not in the word, since it is additional, the origin being niʿm and shidd, which were pluralized as afʿul as they say rajul and arjul, qadaḥ and aqdaḥ, ḍirs and aḍrus." It is said: it is a plural of shudd with ḍamma on the shīn; Ibn al-Anbārī reported it from some Basrans, who said: "like your saying «هو وُدٌّ» and «هم أَوَدّ»." It is said: it is a plural of shadd with fatḥa, and this is possible. What is meant here by reaching maturity is reaching puberty (ḥulum), in the opinion of most, because it is the presumption of that. It is said: it is the attainment of men in resourcefulness and knowledge. It is said: it is reaching fifteen to thirty. It is said: reaching thirty-three. It is said: forty. It is said: sixty; and these do not suit this verse; they suit only His saying, the Exalted, {حتى إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً} [al-Aḥqāf: 15]. «الأَشَدُّ» is derived from «الشِدَّة», which is strength and hardiness, and al-Farrāʾ recited:
2120 - قد ساد وهو فتىً حتى إذا بلغت ... أَشُدُّهُ وعلا في الأمر واجتمعا
(He became a chief while still a youth, until, when his full strength was reached... and he rose in affairs and came together [in maturity].)
It is said: its origin is from rising, from «شَدَّ النهارُ» when it rose and became high. ʿAntara said:
2121 - عهدي به شَدَّ النهار كأنما ... خُضِبَ البَنانُ ورأسُه بالعِظْلِمِ
(My last meeting with him was at the height of the day, as though his fingertips and his head were dyed with indigo.)
«الكَيْل والميزان»: these are the instrument with which things are measured and weighed; the original of «الكيل» is the maṣdar, then it was applied to the instrument. «الميزان» is a mifʿāl from «الوَزْن» for this instrument, like «المصباح» and «المقياس» for that by which one lights a lamp and by which one measures; the origin of «ميزان» is miwzān, and what was done to «ميقات» was done to it, and this was given in al-Baqara.
«بالقسط» is a ḥāl from the agent of «أَوْفوا», i.e. "fulfil both, being just (muqsiṭīn)", that is, accompanied by justice; and it may be a ḥāl from the object, i.e. "fulfil the measure and the scale accompanied by justice", that is, complete. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«الكَيْلُ» here is a maṣdar in the sense of «المكيل» (the measured), and likewise «الميزان». It may also have an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being: 'the measured of the measure and the weighed of the scale'." There is no need for what he claimed of the maṣdar's standing in the place of the passive participle, nor of the implication of the muḍāf, because the meaning is sound without them; and «ميزان» is not a maṣdar. However, what al-Wāḥidī said supports his saying; he said: "«والميزان», i.e. the weighing of the scale, because what is intended is completing the weighing, not completing the scale, just as He said «وأَوْفوا الكيل» and did not say «المِكْيال», so it is of the category of omitting the muḍāf." End. The apparent is that there is no need for that, and it is as though he did not know that «الكيل» is applied to the measuring vessel itself, so that he says "and He did not say «المكيال»".
His saying {لاَ نُكَلِّفُ}: a parenthesis among these imperatives. His saying «ولو كان»: i.e. "even if the one spoken to and the one spoken against is a kinsman". A counterpart of this construction was given repeatedly. His saying «وبعهدِ الله» may be of the category of annexing the maṣdar to its agent, i.e. "with that which Allah covenanted with you"; and it may be annexed to its object, i.e. "with that which you covenanted with Allah", like His saying {صَدَقُواْ مَا عَاهَدُواْ الله عَلَيْهِ} [al-Aḥzāb: 23], {بِمَا عَاهَدَ عَلَيْهِ الله} [al-Fatḥ: 10]; and the annexation may be merely explicative, annexed to Allah in that He is the one who commands its preservation; and what is meant by it is the covenant that occurs between the two verses.
