This one was sealed with remembrance (tadhakkur), because the four before it are subtle and need the exercise of thought and reflection so that the one who deals with them may come to know justice, so remembrance suited them; whereas the five matters (above) are apparent in terms of their being understood and comprehended, and therefore they were sealed with the verb «تعقلون» (reason). «تَذَكَّرون», wherever it occurs, is read by the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Ḥafṣ with a light (unshadded) form, and the rest with shadda; the origin is «تتذكرون»; whoever lightened it omitted one of the two tāʾs, and is it the tāʾ of the imperfect or the tāʾ of tafaʿʿul? There is a well-known disagreement. Whoever made it heavy assimilated the tāʾ into the dhāl.
His saying {وَأَنَّ هذا}: The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «إنّ» with kasra, as a resumption, and «فاتبعوه» is a clause conjoined to the clause before it. This resumptive clause gives the reason for His saying «فاتبعوه», and therefore al-Zamakhsharī cited it for that, as was mentioned; so on this the discussion of the fāʾ in «فاتَّبِعوه» is as in the reading of others, and will come.
Ibn ʿĀmir read «وأَنْ» with fatḥa on the hamza and a light nūn, and the rest also with fatḥa and shadda. As for the reading of the group, it has four aspects. One, which is the apparent: that it is in the position of accusative by conjunction on «ما حرم», i.e. "recite what He forbade and recite that this is My path"; the speaker meant is the Prophet ﷺ, because his path is the path of Allah, mighty and majestic; and this is the view of al-Farrāʾ, who said: "with fatḥa on «أن» because «أتلُ» falls upon it", meaning: "I recite to you that this is My straight path". The second: that it is also accusative in position by conjunction on «أن لا تشركوا» if we say that «أَنْ» is maṣdariyya and that it and what follows it are a badal for «ما حَرَّم»; so said al-Ḥawfī.
The third: that it is on the dropping of the lām of reason, i.e. "and because this is My straight path, follow it", like His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنَّ المساجد لِلَّهِ فَلاَ تَدْعُواْ} [al-Jinn: 14] «[Translator's note: the source gives verse 14; the verse is al-Jinn 72:18, as cited earlier in this entry.]». Abū ʿAlī (al-Fārisī) said: "For the one who reads «أنَّ» with fatḥa, the analogy of Sībawayh's view is that he carried it on «فاتَّبعوه», the implied form being: 'because this is My straight path, follow it', like {وَأنَّ هذه أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً} [al-Muʾminūn: 52]. Sībawayh said: 'meaning: and because this is your community'; and he said of His saying, the Exalted, «وأن المساجد لله»: 'meaning: and because the mosques'." Some said: this lām has been stated explicitly in a counterpart of this construction, such as His saying, the Exalted: {لإِيلاَفِ قُرَيْشٍ إِيلاَفِهِمْ. . . فَلْيَعْبُدُواْ} [Quraysh: 1]; and the fāʾ on this is like the one in your saying «زيداً فاضرب» and «بزيد فامرر». Its explanation has been given in al-Baqara. al-Fārisī said: "The analogy of Sībawayh's view in the fatḥa of the hamza is that the fāʾ is redundant, like the one in «زيد فقائم»." I say: Sībawayh does not allow its redundancy in the like of this predicate; what Abū ʿAlī meant by its counterpart is merely the redundancy, even if he does not say it, though others do. The fourth: that it is in the position of genitive by conjunction on the genitive pronoun in «به», i.e. "that is what He enjoined on you with, and with 'that this is...'"; and this is also the view of al-Farrāʾ. Abū l-Baqāʾ rejected it for two reasons. One: conjunction on the genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition. The second: the meaning would become 'He charged you with the straightness of the path', and this is invalid." I say: both reasons are rejected. As for the first, this is not of the category of conjunction on the pronoun without repeating the preposition, because the preposition here is as good as pronounced, and was omitted only because its omission is regular with «أنّ» and «أنْ» on account of their length with the ṣila; hence the school of the majority is that they are in the position of genitive after its omission, because it is like what is present; and what I have said is indicated by what al-Ḥawfī said: "The bāʾ was omitted because of the length of the ṣila and it is intended, and there is no conjunction of an overt on a pronoun in this, because it is intended." As for the second, the meaning is sound, not invalid; because the meaning of our being charged with the straightness of the path is that we not engage in what takes us out of the path, so our being charged with its straightness is an intensification in following it.
As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, they said: «أنْ» in it is lightened from the heavy, and its ism is the pronoun of the matter and the affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), i.e. «وأنَّه», like His saying, the Exalted, {أَنِ الحمد للَّهِ} [Yūnus: 10] and his saying:
2122 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أنْ هالكٌ كلُّ مَنْ يَْحفَى ويَنْتَعِلُ
(... that perishing is everyone who goes barefoot or wears sandals.)
Then in it are the four aspects mentioned for the heavy one. «مستقيماً» is a ḥāl, its governor being either the «ها» of alerting or the demonstrative. In the codex of ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) it is «وهذا صراطي» without «أنَّ», and it is the reading of al-Aʿmash, by which the reading with kasra, which signals resumption, is supported.
His saying: {فَتَفَرَّقَ}: it is accusative by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ in the answer to a prohibition. The majority read «فتفرق» with a light tāʾ, and al-Bazzī with shadda on it; whoever lightened dropped one of the two tāʾs, and whoever shadded assimilated, as was mentioned recently at {تَتَذَكَّرُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 80]. «بكم» may be a direct object in meaning, i.e. "so that it separates you", and it may be a ḥāl, i.e. "while you are with them (the paths)", like his saying:
2123 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَدُوس بنا الجماجمَ والتَّرِيبا
(... trampling with us the skulls and the breastbones.)
He sealed this one with piety (taqwā), which is guarding against the Fire, for its fitness to the command to follow the path, for whoever follows it protects himself from the Fire.

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {اتخذوا دِينَهُمْ لَعِباً وَلَهْواً}: «اتخذوا» admits two aspects. One: that it is transitive to one object, with the meaning "they acquired and made", and «لهواً ولعباً» on this is an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), i.e. "they acquired it for the sake of amusement and play." The second: that it is the one transitive to two objects, the first being «دينهم» and the second «لعباً ولهواً». The Shaykh said: "It appears from some of al-Zamakhsharī's statement and from Ibn ʿAṭiyya's that «لعباً ولهواً» is the first object and «دينهم» the second object. Al-Zamakhsharī said: 'i.e. their religion, which they ought to have taken up, as play and amusement; that is, their worship and what they were upon, of slitting the ears of the baḥīra camels and setting free the sāʾiba camels, belongs to amusement and play and following the desire of the self and to what is of the kind of jesting, not seriousness; or they took what is play and amusement, from the worship of idols, as a religion for themselves; or they took their religion that they were charged with, which is the religion of Islam, as play and amusement, in that they mocked it.' He said: so the apparent form of his second implied reading indicates what we mentioned."

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He annexed the religion to them in the sense that they made play and amusement a religion; and it may be that the meaning is: they took their religion, which they ought to have had, as play and amusement; his first explanation is what we mentioned from him." End of quotation. I say: what the two mentioned they only mentioned as an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab. How could they make the indefinite the first object and the definite the second object without any reason, though they are among the greatest authorities in this field? And look how they made what they called the first object appear as definite and what they called the second as indefinite in the structure of their statement, in order to ... [see note] the speech of the Arabs; so how can it be supposed of them that they make the indefinite the subject-of-report and the definite the report, in the speech of Allah the Exalted?

«Translator's note: the source reads «ليَخِدوا على كلام العرب» (apparently a misprint; the intended wording is unclear), and «تبحير البحائر», «وأو اتخذوا», «معفولاً»; I have translated the sense and left the unclear clause marked above.»

His saying: {وَذَكِّرْ بِهِ}: i.e. by the Qurʾān, which is indicated by His saying: {فَذَكِّرْ بالقرآن مَن يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ} [ق: 45]. It was said: it refers to their account. It was said: to «الذين». It was also said: this is a pronoun explained by what follows it, and its clarification will come.

His saying: {وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الحياوة} admits two aspects. One: that it is resumptive. The second: that it is conjoined to the ṣila of «الذين», i.e. "who took ... and who were deceived by ...". The meaning of «الغرور» has been given at the end of Āl ʿImrān. It was also said here: «غَرَّتهم» is from «الغَرّ» with fatḥa on the ghayn, i.e. it filled their mouths and satiated them, and on this is the poet's saying:

195 - 0- ولمَّا التَقَيْنا بالحُلَيْبَةِ غَرَّني ... بمعروفِهِ حتى خرجْتُ أفوقُ
(When we met at al-Ḥulayba, he stuffed me with his generosity until I left gasping.)

His saying: {أَن تُبْسَلَ}: There are two aspects regarding this. The well-known one, indeed the consensus, is that it is an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), the implied meaning being "for fear that it be given up to destruction", or "in dislike that it be given up", or "that it not be given up". The second: the Shaykh said, after reporting the agreement on the object of purpose: "In my view it may be in the position of genitive as a substitute (badal) for the pronoun, the pronoun being explained by the substitute, and the giving-up (ibsāl) being implied for the magnification inherent in implying, as they implied the pronoun of the matter and the case, the implied meaning being: 'and remind by the pledging of souls and their confinement for what they earned', as they said: «اللهم صلِّ عليه الرؤوفِ الرحيمِ» ('O Allah, bless him, the Compassionate, the Merciful')." Sībawayh allowed that, saying: "If you say «ضربت وضربوني قومك», you put it in the accusative, except in the speech of one who says «أكلوني البراغيث», or you take it as a substitute for the pronoun."

He also said: "If you say «ضربني وضربتُهم قومُك», you put it in the nominative on the basis of fronting and postponing, unless you take the substitute here as you took it in the nominative." End of quotation. The saying has been transmitted:

195 - 1-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . فاستاكَتْ به عُودِ إسْحِلِ

with genitive «عُود» as a substitute for the pronoun. I say: as for explaining a non-nominative pronoun by a substitute, it is the statement of al-Akhfash, who recited this second half-verse as evidence, whose first half is:

إذا هي لم تَسْتَكْ بعودِ أراكةٍ ... تُنُخَّلَ فاستاكَتْ به عودِ إسحلِ
(When she did not use a stick of arāk to clean her teeth, one was selected for her, and she cleaned them with it, a stick of isḥil.)

The verse is by Ṭufayl al-Ghanawī. It is transmitted with nominative «عود», which is the well-known form among the grammarians, its nominative being by giving effect to the first verb, which is «تُنُخِّل», and ignoring the second, which is «فاستاكَتْ», to which he gave its pronoun; had he given effect to it, he would have said «فاستاكَتْ بعود إسحل», which is not possible because it would break the meter. The other transmission, which he used as evidence, is very weak and unknown to most of the i'rab scholars. Had he cited as evidence what is not disputed, like the saying:

195 - 2- على حالةٍ لو أن في القوم حاتِماً ... على جوده لضَنَّ بالماءِ حاتمِ
(In a state in which, had Ḥātim been among the people, despite his generosity, Ḥātim would have been stingy with water.)

with genitive «حاتم» as a substitute for the hāʾ in «بجوده», and the rhyme-letters being in the genitive, it would have been better. «الإِبسال» is pledging, and one says «أَبْسَلْتُ ولدي وأهلي», i.e. I pledged them. He said:

195 - 3- وإبسالي بَنِيَّ بغير جُرْمٍ بَعَوْناه ولا بدمٍ مُراق
(And my pledging of my sons without a crime we committed, nor for blood shed.)

«بَعَوْنا» means "we committed", and «البَعْو» is the crime. It was also said: «الإِبسال» is a man's giving himself up to destruction.

Al-Rāghib said: "«البَسْلُ» is gathering a thing and withholding it. Because of its including the sense of gathering, it was borrowed for the frowning of the face, so it is said «باسل» and «مُتْبَسِلُ الوجه»; and because of its including the sense of withholding, the forbidden and the pledged are called «بَسْلٌ»." Then he said: "The difference between the forbidden (ḥarām) and the basl is that the ḥarām is general for what is withheld by compulsion and by ruling, while the basl is what is withheld by compulsion. Courage is called «بسالة» either because of the frowning of the face with which the brave man is described, or because he is forbidden to his peers, or because he withholds what is in his possession and under his hand from his enemies. «البُسْلَةُ» is the wage of the one who recites a charm, taken from the reciter's saying «أَبْسَلْتُ زيداً», i.e. I made him forbidden to Satan or I made him brave and strong in defending himself; and «بَسَل» has the meaning of «أَجَلْ» and «بَسْ»," i.e. it is a particle of response like «أجل», and a verbal noun meaning "enough" like «بس».

His saying {بِمَا}: attached to «تُبْسَل», i.e. "by reason of"; «ما» is a maṣdar or has the meaning of the relative, or is indefinite, and its matter is clear.

His saying: {لَيْسَ لَهَا}: This clause has three aspects. One, the apparent: it is resumptive, brought to report that. The second: it is in the position of nominative as an adjective of «نفس». The third: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «كسبت».

His saying: {مِن دُونِ}: There are two aspects regarding «مِنْ», the more apparent being that it is for the beginning of the range; the second: that it is redundant, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported with something. If it is for the beginning of the range, there are two aspects as to what it is attached to. One: that it is a ḥāl from «وليّ», because if it were postponed it would be an adjective of it, so it is attached to an omitted word which is the ḥāl. The second: that it is the predicate of «ليس», so it is attached to an omitted word that is the predicate of «ليس»; and on this «لها» is attached to an omitted word by way of explanation (bayān). Parallels have gone before. In {مِن دُونِ الله} there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "other than His punishment and recompense".

His saying: {كُلَّ عَدْلٍ}: accusative as a maṣdar because «كل» takes its sense from what it is annexed to; this is the well-known view. It may also be accusative as a direct object, i.e. "even if she ransoms with all that one ransoms with, it will not be accepted". The pronoun in «لا يُؤْخَذُ» on the first view, the Shaykh said, "returns to that which is given in exchange, understood from the course of the discourse, and does not return to the maṣdar, because taking is not ascribed to it; as for {وَلاَ يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ} [البقرة: 48], its meaning is the thing ransomed with, so it is sound." End of quotation. That is, he ascribed taking explicitly to «عدل» in al-Baqara only because what is meant is not the maṣdar but the thing ransomed with; and on the second view it returns to «كل عدل», because it is not a maṣdar, so it is like the verse of al-Baqara.

His saying: {أولئك الذين أُبْسِلُواْ}: It is permissible that «الذين» be the predicate and «لهم شراب» a second predicate, and that «لهم شراب» be a ḥāl: either from the pronoun in «أُبْسِلوا» or from the relative itself, with «شرابٌ» an agent because the preposition and its genitive noun before it relies on the owner of the ḥāl. «لهم شراب» may also be resumptive; so these are three aspects for «لهم شراب». It is also permissible that «الذين» be a substitute for «أولئك» or an adjective of them, in which case it is necessary that the clause «لهم شرابٌ» be a predicate of the subject. So three aspects are obtained for the relative as well: its being a predicate, a substitute or an adjective; so, with what precedes, six aspects in this verse.

«شراب» may be nominative in two ways: as a subject, and as an agent according to al-Akhfash, and also according to Sībawayh, on the basis that «لهم» is the predicate of the subject, or a ḥāl where we made it a ḥāl, with «شراب» nominative by it because it relies on what precedes. «من حميمٍ» is an adjective of «شراب», so it is in the position of nominative and attached to an omitted word.

«شراب» is on the pattern faʿāl with the meaning of mafʿūl, and faʿāl with the meaning of mafʿūl, like «طعام» meaning "food eaten" and «شراب» meaning "drink drunk", is not regular; one does not say «أَكال» meaning «مأكول», nor «ضَراب» meaning «مضروب». The reference by «ذلك» in the statement of al-Zamakhsharī and al-Ḥawfī is to those who took (their religion as play), so he brought the plural form; and in the statement of Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ it is to the confinement understood from His saying «أن تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ», since what is meant by it is souls in general, so it is referred to in the plural.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَنَدْعُواْ}: an interrogative of reproach and denial. The clause is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying. «ما» is the object of «ندعو», and it is a relative or an indefinite noun with a description. «مِنْ دون الله» is attached to «ندعو». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It cannot be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَنْفَعنا», nor governed by «ينفعنا», because it precedes «ما», and the ṣila and the description do not work on what precedes the relative and the described noun." His saying "from the pronoun in «ينفعنا»" means the nominative one returning to «ما», and his saying "do not work on what precedes the relative and the described noun" means that «ما» does not depart from these two categories. But it is permissible that «من دون» be a ḥāl from «ما» itself, according to his own statement, since he did not make the preventing factor, in making it a ḥāl from its pronoun in «ينفعنا», other than a technical one, not a semantic one; and there is no difference between the overt noun and its pronoun, in the sense that if it may be a ḥāl from an overt noun, it may be a ḥāl from its pronoun, unless a preventer prevents.

His saying: {وَنُرَدُّ}: There are two aspects in it, the more apparent being that it is conjoined to «ندعو», so it falls within the scope of the interrogative over which the saying has authority. The second: that it is a ḥāl, with an implied subject, i.e. "and we are being returned". The Shaykh said, after reporting from Abū al-Baqāʾ: "It is weak, because of the implying of the subject, and because it would be a confirmatory ḥāl." There is something to examine in its being confirmatory, because the confirmatory is that whose meaning is understood from the first, and it is as if he says that turning back on the heels is inherent in calling on something "other than Allah".

His saying: {على أَعْقَابِنَا}: two aspects. One: it is attached to «نُرَدُّ». The second: it is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun of «نُرَدُّ», i.e. "we are returned going back on our heels", or "turning back", or "lagging behind"; so he implied it, and this is an explanation of meaning, since what is implied in the like of it is a general "being"; and it can be said of this that it is a confirmatory ḥāl. «بعد إذ» is attached to «نُرَدُّ».

His saying: {كالذي استهوته}: There are two aspects in this kāf. One: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "we are returned a return like the return of the one who ...". The second: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun of «نرد», i.e. "we are returned resembling the one whom the devils lured". So whoever permits multiple ḥāls makes it a second ḥāl if he makes «على أعقابنا» a ḥāl; and whoever does not permit that makes this ḥāl a substitute for the first ḥāl, if he does not make «على أعقابنا» a ḥāl but attached to «نُرَدُّ».

«Translator's note: the source reads «ألم يجعل» here; the sense requires "if he does not make", which I have translated.»

The majority read «اسْتَهْوَتْهُ» with the feminine tāʾ, and Ḥamza «استهواه», following his rule of imāla; the two aspects are known from what preceded in {تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنَا} [الأنعام: 61]. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Aʿmash read «استهوَتْه الشيطان», with the verb feminine and «الشيطان» singular. Al-Kisāʾī said: "And it is so in the codex of Ibn Masʿūd." The justification of this reading is that it interprets the masculine as a feminine, as in their saying «أتته كتابي فاحترقها», i.e. my sheet; and parallels have preceded. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «الشياطون», and they made it a solecism, but it does not reach solecism; it is a poor minor dialect. It has been heard: "around the garden of so-and-so are «بساتون»", and "he has «سلاطون»". It is related that when the reading of al-Ḥasan was reported, some called it a solecism, and al-Farrāʾ said: "Yes, by Allah, they call the Shaykh a solecist, and they cite as evidence the saying of Ruʾba." By my life, al-Farrāʾ spoke truly in denying that. «الذي» is meant as a genus, and it may be meant as the single individual.

His saying: {فِي الأرض}: four aspects. One: it is attached to His saying {استهوته}. The second: it is a ḥāl from the object of «استهوته». The third: it is a ḥāl from «حَيْران». The fourth: it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «حيران». «حَيْران» is a ḥāl: either from the hāʾ of «اسْتَهْوَتْه», on the basis that it is a substitute for the first, or according to the one who permits multiple ḥāls; or from «الذي», or from the latent pronoun in the adverbial phrase. «حيران» has the feminine «حَيْرى», and for that reason it is a diptote. The verb is «حار يحار حَيْرةً وحَيَراناً وحَيْرورة».

His saying: {لَهُ أَصْحَابٌ}: a clause in the position of accusative as an adjective of «حيران»; it may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «حيران», and it may be resumptive. «إلى الهدى» is attached to «يَدْعُونه». In the codex of Ibn Masʿūd and in his reading it is «أتينا» in the past form, and «إلى الهدى» on this reading is attached to it; on the reading of the majority, the imperative clause is in the position of accusative by an implied saying, i.e. "they say: Come to us", and the implied saying is in the position of an adjective of «أصحاب», and likewise «يدعونه».

«Translator's note: the source prints «محصل نصب» for «محل نصب» here; translated as "position of accusative".»

His saying: {لِنُسْلِمَ}: There are several statements regarding this lām. The first, which is the position of Sībawayh: that this lām after volition, command and the like is attached to an omitted word as the predicate of a subject, and that subject is the maṣdar of that preceding verb; so if you say «أردْتَ لتقوم» or «أمرت زيداً ليذهب», the implied meaning is "the volition is for standing" and "the command is for going". So the Shaykh reported that from Sībawayh and his companions, and there is weakness in it which I presented in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ at His saying: {يُرِيدُ الله لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ} [الآية: 26]. The second: that the object of the command and volition is omitted, and its implied form is: "and we were commanded to sincerity so that we submit". The third: al-Zamakhsharī said: "It gives a reason for the command, meaning: 'We were commanded, and it was said to us: submit, in order that we submit.'" The fourth: that the lām is redundant, i.e. "we were commanded to submit". The fifth: that it has the meaning of the bāʾ, i.e. "with the submitting". The sixth: that the lām and what follows is the object of the command, occurring in the place of «أن», i.e. the two alternate, so you say «أمرتُك لتقومَ» and «أن تقوم»; this is the position of the Kufans. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The position of Sībawayh is that «لنُسْلِمَ» is in the position of the object, and that your saying «أُمِرْت لأقومَ» and «وأَنْ أقومَ» run the same; and the poet said:

195 - 4- أُريد لأَنْسى حبَّها فكأنَّما ... تَمثَّلُ لي ليلى بكل طريقِ
(I want to forget her love, but it is as if Laylā appears to me in every path.)

This is not the position of Sībawayh; his position is what preceded, and the verification of this question has gone before in the sūra indicated earlier.

semin-durr:154-154.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ آتَيْنَا}: The basic sense of «ثم» is a delay in time, and it may come for a delay in reports. al-Zajjāj said: "It is conjoined to «أتل», the implied form being: recite what He forbade, then recite «آتينا»." It is also said: it is conjoined to «قل», on the implication of «قل», i.e. "then say: We gave". It is also said: its implied form is "then I inform you: We gave". al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is conjoined to «وصَّاكم به»." He said: "If you say: how is it sound to conjoin it to that with «ثم», when the giving was long ages before the charge with it? I say: this charge is ancient; every community has constantly charged one another with it on the tongue of its prophet, so it is as though it were said: 'That is what He charged you with, O children of Adam, anciently and recently; then, greater than that, We gave Mūsā the Book.'" It is also said: it is conjoined to what preceded before the half of the sūra, namely His saying {وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ} [al-Anʿām: 84]. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its delay is in the ordering of the speech which Muḥammad ﷺ was commanded to utter, as though He said: 'then, of what We charged him with, that We gave Mūsā the Book'; and what calls to that is that Mūsā, peace be upon him, is earlier in time than Muḥammad, peace be upon him." Ibn al-Qushayrī said: "There is an omitted word in the speech, the implied form being: 'then We had given Mūsā the Book before Our sending down of the Qur'an upon Muḥammad, blessings and peace upon him'." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "What should be done is that it be used for conjunction like the wāw without considering a delay, and some grammarians said so." I say: this is a resort to ease; also, the absence of delay does not entail the absence of order, so he should have said "without considering order or delay", given that the supposition in this verse is the absence of order in time.
His saying: {تَمَاماً}: five aspects are allowed in it. One: that it is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the completion of Our favour". The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الكتاب», i.e. "in the state of its being complete". The third: that it is accusative as a maṣdar, because it has the sense: "We gave it a giving of completeness, not deficiency". The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "completing [it]". The fifth: that it is a maṣdar accusative by an implied verb of its own wording, and it is a maṣdar with the augments dropped, the implied form being: "We completed it completely".
{عَلَى الذي} is attached to «تماماً» or to an omitted word as an adjective; this when it is not made a confirmatory maṣdar; if it is made one, making it an adjective is necessary.
{أَحْسَنَ} has two aspects, the more apparent being that it is a past verb occurring as the ṣila of the relative, its agent being a latent pronoun referring to Mūsā, i.e. "completeness upon the one who did well"; so «الذي» is an expression for Mūsā. It is also said: every one who did well. It is also said: «الذي» is an expression for what Mūsā did and perfected, i.e. "completeness upon that which Mūsā did well". The second: that «أحسن» is a noun on the pattern afʿal, like afḍal and akram, and the description of the relative sufficed in place of its ṣila; for whenever the relative is described by a definite, as in «مررت بالذي أخيك», or by what is close to definite, as in «مررت بالذي خيرٍ منك وبالذي أحسن منك», that is permissible and it dispenses with its ṣila; this is the school of al-Farrāʾ, and he recited:
2124 - حتى إذا كانا هما اللَّذيْنِ ... مثلَ الجَدِيْلَيْنِ المُحَمْلَجَيْنِ
(Until, when the two of them became the two... like two well-twisted plaits.)
with «مثل» accusative as the ṣila of «اللذين», which is accusative as the khabar of kāna. It is also possible that «الذي» be maṣdariyya, with «أحسن» a past verb as its ṣila, the implied form being: "completeness upon his doing well", i.e. Allah's doing well to him and Mūsā's doing well to them; this is the opinion of Yūnus and al-Farrāʾ, as in his saying:
2125 - فَثَبَّتَ اللهُ ما آتاك مِنْ حَسَنٍ ... تثبيتَ عيسى ونصراً كالذي نُصِرُوا
(May Allah make firm what He gave you of good... with the firming He gave ʿĪsā, and with victory like theirs.)
Its verification has already been given for you.
The fatḥa on the nūn of «أحسن» is the reading of the common people. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with ḍamma, and there are two aspects to it. The more apparent: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "upon that which is best", the returning pronoun having been omitted, though the ṣila is not long, so it is irregular from that side; this was given with its proofs at His saying {مَّا بَعُوضَةً} [al-Baqara: 26], for the one who reads «بعوضة» in the nominative. The second: that «الذي» stands in the place of «الذين», and the origin of «أَحْسن» is «أَحْسَنوا» with the wāw of the pronoun, the wāw being dropped content with the vowel before it; so said al-Tibrīzī, and he recited:
2126 - فلو أنَّ الأَطِبَّا كانُ حولي ... وكان مع الأطباء الأُساةُ
(If the physicians had been around me... and with the physicians the healers.)
«[Translator's note: «كانُ» appears to be for «كانوا», the wāw dropped, as the author's argument requires.]»
And another's saying:
2127 - إذا ما شاءُ ضرُّوا مَنْ أرادوا ... ولا يألوهُمُ أحدٌ ضِرارا
(When they wish, they harm whom they want... and no one spares them harm.)
And another's saying:
2128 - شَبُّوا على المجد وشابوا واكتهلْ
(They grew up upon glory, and grew grey, and [reached] middle age.)
meaning «اكتهلوا»; he dropped the wāw and made the letter before it sākin. Other verses like this have been given in the course of this compilation, but the majority of the grammarians restrict this to poetic necessity.
His saying: «وتفصيلاً» and what is conjoined to it are accusative according to what was mentioned for «تماماً».

semin-durr:155-155.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وهذا كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ}: It is possible that «كتاب», «أنزلناه» and «مبارك» are all predicates of the demonstrative, according to those who allow multiple predicates absolutely, or by interpretation according to those who do not allow that. It is also possible that «أنزلناه» and «مبارك» are two descriptions of «كتاب», according to those who allow the preposing of a non-explicit description before an explicit one. The verification of that was given in the sūra before it at His saying {بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ} [al-Māʾida: 54]. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Had «مباركاً» been read in the accusative as a ḥāl, it would have been permissible." There is no need for the like of this. The description of sending down was put first because the speech is with those who deny that Allah sends down a book to humans and sends a messenger; as for describing it with blessing, that is a matter remote from them. The attribute of sending down was brought as a verbal clause in which the verb is assigned to the pronoun of the One who magnifies Himself, for intensification in that, unlike had it been brought as a singular noun.

semin-durr:156-156.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن تقولوا}: There are two aspects to it. One: that it is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose). The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "Its governor is an implied «أنزلناه» indicated by the uttered «أنزلناه» itself, the implied form being: 'We sent it down lest you say'." He said: "It is not permissible that the uttered «أنزلناه» govern it, so as not to require separation between the governor and its governed item by a foreigner, which is that «مبارك» is either an adjective or a khabar and is a foreigner in either implication." This which he forbade is the apparent sense of the words of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ. The second: that it is a direct object, its governor being «واتقوا», i.e. "and fear your saying such and such"; and His saying «لعلكم ترحمون» is a parenthesis running in the manner of a reason. On its being a mafʿūl min ajlihi, its implied form, according to the Basrans, is on the omission of a muḍāf, namely "out of dislike that you should say"; and according to the Kufans its implied form is "that you not say", like {رَوَاسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ} [al-Naḥl: 15], i.e. "that it not shake with you"; and this is regular with them in this kind, and it has been mentioned more than once. The majority read «تقولوا» with the tāʾ of address; Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يقولوا» with the yāʾ of the third person.
His saying: {وَإِنْ كُنَّا}: «إنْ» is lightened from the heavy one according to the Basrans, and here it is inoperative; hence the verbal clause follows it; its verification has been given, and that the Kufans make it have the sense of the negative «ما», and the lām the sense of «إلا», the implied form being: "we were only heedless of their study". al-Zajjāj said the same, taking the way of the Kufans. Quṭrub said: «إنْ» has the sense of «قد» and the lām is redundant. al-Zamakhsharī, after establishing the school of the Basrans as I presented it, said: "The original is «إنَّه كنا عن عبادتهم»", so he implied for it an omitted ism, which is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), as the grammarians imply that for «أَنْ» with fatḥa when it is lightened; and this contradicts their texts, for they stated that «إنْ» with kasra, when lightened and followed by an abrogating verbal clause, has no operation, neither on an overt nor a latent word. «عن دراستهم» is attached to the khabar of «كنا», namely «غافلين», and in it is an indication of the invalidity of the school of the Kufans in their claim that the lām has the sense of «إلا»; for what follows «إلا» may not govern what precedes it, so likewise what has its meaning.
The Shaykh said: "They may make «عنها» attached to an omitted word." The disagreement of Abū ʿAlī was also given earlier, that this lām is not the lām of inception (ibtidāʾ) but another lām; "and it also indicates that the lām is a lām of inception made obligatory for distinction, so it is permissible for its governed item to precede it, since it occurred in a place that is not its original place, as that was permissible in «إنَّ زيداً طعامَك لآكل», where it occurred in a place that was not its original one, and that was not permissible for it when it occurred in its original place, which is its entering upon the mubtadaʾ." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The lām in «لغافلين» is a compensation or a distinguisher between «إنْ» and «ما»." I say: his saying "compensation" is a strange expression; what is most often said is that it is a compensation for the shadda that went from «إنَّ», and it is nothing.

semin-durr:157-157.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {فَقَدْ جَآءَكُمْ}: It is the apodosis of an implied condition. al-Zamakhsharī implied it: "If you are truthful in what you used to count upon from yourselves, then there has come to you...", and it is among the finest of omissions. Another implied it: "If you are as you claim, that if a book were sent down to you you would be better guided than the Jews and Christians, then there has come to you...". The verb is not made feminine, because the feminine is figurative, and because of the separation by the object. «من ربكم» may be attached to «جاءكم», and may be attached to an omitted word as an adjective of «بيِّنة». His saying «وهدىً ورحمةً»: «من ربكم» is omitted after both.
And His saying: {فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ}: the apparent is that it is an independent clause. Some said: it is the apodosis of an implied condition, the implied form being: "If you deny, then there is none more unjust than you."
The majority read «كذَّب» with shadda, and «بآيات الله» is attached to it. Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «كَذَبَ» without shadda, and «بآيات الله» may be an object and may be a ḥāl, i.e. "he lied while he had the signs of Allah with him". The object of «صَدَفَ» is omitted, i.e. "and he turned others away from them". The explanation of that has already been given.

semin-durr:158-158.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {أَوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ}: It was mentioned earlier that this is on the omission of a muḍāf. The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read {إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِيهُمُ الملائكة} with the dotted-from-below yāʾ (masculine), because the feminine is figurative, and it is a counterpart of {فناداه الملائكة} [Āl ʿImrān: 39]. Abū l-ʿĀliya and Ibn Sīrīn read: «يوم تأتي بعض» with the feminine, like His saying {تَلْتَقِطْه بعضُ السيَّارة} [Yūsuf: 10].
His saying: {يَوْمَ يَأْتِي}: The majority read «اليومَ» accusative, and its governor is what follows «لا»; this is according to one of three views about «لا»: that the governed item of what follows it may precede it absolutely; that it may not precede absolutely; and the third is distinguished: between its being the answer to an oath, in which case it is impermissible, and otherwise permissible. Zuhayr al-Furqubī read «يومُ» in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the clause after it as the khabar (predicate), the returning pronoun from it to it being omitted, i.e. "in which it does not benefit".
The majority read «ينفع» with the yāʾ from below (masculine). Ibn Sīrīn read «تنفع» with the tāʾ from above (feminine). Abū Ḥātim said: "They mentioned that it is an error." I say: that is because the verb is assigned to a masculine; and the answer is that when it acquired the feminine by annexation, it was given its rule, as in his saying:
2129 - وتَشْرَق بالقول الذي قد أَذَعْتَهُ ... كما شَرِقَتْ صدرُ القانةِ من الدم
(And she chokes on the word you had spread... as the breast of the spear-shaft chokes with blood.)
You were given the verification of this at the beginning of the sūra, and Sībawayh recited on that:
2130 - مَشَيْنَ كما اهتزَّتْ رماحٌ تسفَّهَتْ ... أعاليهَا مَرُّ الرياحِ النَّواسمِ
(They walked as lances sway, whose upper parts the passing of the gentle winds has made unsteady.)
It is also said: because faith (īmān) has the sense of creed, so it is like their saying «أتته كتابي فاحتقرها» ("my book came to him and he despised it"), i.e. my page and my message. al-Naḥḥās said: "In this there is a subtle point that Sībawayh mentioned, namely that faith and the soul (nafs) each include the other, so he made faith feminine since it is from the soul and by it." And Sībawayh recited "مَشَيْن كما اهتزَّت", the verse. al-Zamakhsharī said of this reading: "because faith is annexed to the feminine pronoun which it is part of, as in their saying «ذهبت بعض أصابعه» ('some of his fingers went')." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "This is an error, because faith is not part of the soul." I say: what bears witness to the soundness of this expression has just been given from al-Naḥḥās's words reporting from Sībawayh: "namely that faith and the soul each include the other, so he made faith feminine since it is from the soul and by it"; so there is no difference between these two expressions, i.e. no difference between saying "it is from it and by it" or "it is part of it", and what is intended in both expressions is figurative.
His saying: «لم تكنْ آمَنَتْ»: in this clause there are three aspects. One: that it is in the position of accusative because it is an adjective of «نفساً», and the agent, namely «إيمانها», separates between the adjective and its described noun because it is not a foreigner, since the described noun, which is the object, and the agent share in the governor; on this it is permissible: «ضرب هنداً غلامُها القرشية» ("Her boy struck Hind, the Qurashī woman"). His saying «أو كسبت» is conjoined to «لم تكن آمنت».
In this verse there are fine discussions related to the science of Arabic, and on them questions of the foundations of religion are built. The Muʿtazilī says: mere sound faith is not sufficient; rather it must be joined to an action that accompanies it and confirms it, and he cited the apparent sense of this verse. That is as al-Zamakhsharī said: "«لم تكنْ آمَنَتْ من قبلُ» is an adjective of His saying «نفساً», and His saying «أوكسبت في إيمانها خيراً» is conjoined to «آمنت». The meaning: when the portents of the Hour come, and they are compelling, coercive signs, the time of obligation passes with them, so faith does not then benefit a soul that did not advance its faith before the appearance of the signs, or advanced its faith but earned no good in its faith. So, as you see, he did not distinguish between the disbelieving soul that believes at a time that is not the time of faith, and the soul that believed in its time but earned no good, so that it be known that His saying {الذين آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصالحات} is a joining of two companions, one of which should not be separated from the other, so that their possessor may succeed and be happy; otherwise there is wretchedness and perdition." People have answered this apparent sense by saying that the meaning of the noble verse is: when some of the signs come, the faith which a disbelieving soul then performs does not benefit it, and a soul's having advanced its faith without earning good in it does not benefit it either; so He made the benefit of the negation of faith depend on one of two descriptions: either the negation of advancing faith only, or its advancing together with the negation of earning good; and its implication (mafhūm) is that earlier faith alone benefits, or earlier faith together with good; and the implication of the description is strong, so the verse is cited for the school of Ahl al-Sunna; thus they turned their proof into a proof against them.
The judge Nāṣir al-Dīn ibn al-Munayyir answered al-Zamakhsharī's words, saying: "Aḥmad said: He seeks to prove that the disbeliever and the disobedient are equal in eternity (in the Fire), in that the verse equates them in the non-benefit of what they make up after the signs appear; but that is not complete, for this speech in rhetoric is called 'lafff' (rolling up); its original is: 'on the day some of your Lord's signs come, faith will not benefit a soul that had not been a believer before its faith afterwards, nor a soul that had not earned good before what it earns of good afterwards'; so He rolled up the two statements and made them one statement for brevity and eloquence; and it becomes apparent by this that it does not contradict the school of truth: after the appearance of the signs, earning good does not benefit, while earlier faith does benefit with respect to eternity; so it is more fitting for the verse to refute his school than to indicate it."
The second: that this clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun, so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, meaning from the «ها» in «إيمانها». The third: that it is resumptive. Abū l-Baqāʾ began with this and put the ḥāl second, and made the adjective weak, as though he sensed what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned and fled from making it an adjective; the Shaykh made the ḥāl remote and the resumptive more remote than it.
